tips: The full forms јесам/јеси/јесте are used in questions (јеси ли), in a short answer («јесам»), when the verb stands alone, and for emphasis: мачак јесте био мртав - the cat really was dead.
The short yes-answer in the 3rd person is јесте (not «јест»): Да ли је то за вас? - Јесте. «Јест» survives only in the phrase «то јест» (i.e.).
forms: сам, си, је, смо, сте, су; нисам; fut. бићу

examples.en: I'm a student from Novi Sad.
Where were you yesterday?
The weather will be nice tomorrow.
Yes, I understand.
I want to go home.
I think he's right.

note: «да» + present tense replaces the infinitive: хоћу да идем

forms: full: себе; dat. себи; instr. собом

examples.en: My name is Marko.
See you tomorrow!
He only thinks of himself.

note: «се» goes in second position in the clause, not after the verb: Ја се зовем...

examples.en: I don't know where he is.
No, thanks, I'm full.

examples.sr: [Не] брини, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

note: written as one word with some verbs: нисам, немам, нећу

examples.en: That man is my neighbor.
That's my sister.
Who is that girl?
Ana and Marko came.
I love you too.
I live in Belgrade.
We're going to the movies.
See you at five o'clock.

note: «у» + loc. - where; «у» + acc. - where to

forms: gen./acc. тебе, те; dat. теби, ти; instr. тобом

examples.en: You're my best friend.
I love you more than anything.
What's your name?

tips: The question word «what» is шта: Шта могу да кажем? Not «што могу да кажем».
forms: gen. чега; dat. чему; var. што

examples.en: What are you doing tonight?
I don't know what to say.
What are you talking about?

note: «шта» - what (question); «што» - why, which

tips: In songs and in speech што often means «зашто» (why). So when you ask someone to repeat, don't say «што?» - a Serbian will hear "why?". Say «молим?» (pardon?).
In a question it often equals «зашто» (why): «Што си покисао?» - why are you so down? Colloquial.

examples.en: I'm glad you came.
Why are you so sad?
Come as soon as possible.

note: «што пре» - as soon as possible

forms: gen./acc. мене, ме; dat. мени, ми; instr. мном

examples.sr: [Ја̑] сам Ана, а ово је мој брат.
examples.en: I'm Ana, and this is my brother.
Wait for me in front of the building.
I don't like that.

tips: "They don't want to know" is «неће да знају»; «не хоће да» and «не хоћу да» are wrong. «Неће знати» means something else: they won't know (future).
«Хоћу» and «нећу» can be a reply on their own: «Назови Ивана! - Хоћу» - I will. «Нећу» means both "I don't want to" and "I won't".
The 1st person singular is хоћу, нећу (not «хоћем», «нећем»). Exceptions to the -м ending: хоћу, нећу, могу (not «можем»).
forms: хоћу, хоћеш; short: ћу, ћеш; нећу

examples.en: Do you want some coffee?
I'll call you tomorrow.
I don't want to go there.

note: ћу + infinitive = future tense: радићу, ићи ћу

forms: gen./acc. њега, га; dat. њему, му; f. она, n. оно

examples.en: He works at a bank.
I saw him in town yesterday.
Tell him to call me.

forms: gen./acc. нас; dat. нама, нам; instr. нама

examples.en: We're from Serbia.
They're waiting for us at the restaurant.
Come see us on Saturday.

note: «ми» is also the short form of «мени» (to me): дај ми

examples.en: The book is on the table.
In July we're going to the seaside.
I keep thinking about you.

note: мислити на + acc. - to think of someone

tips: Моћи means ability or permission: «могу да дођем сутра». Knowing facts is «знати», knowing how to do something is «умети».
The 1st person singular is могу, not «можем» (можемо is "we can"). An exception to the -м ending.
The verb is irregular: могу, можеш, може (not «можем»). Past: ја сам могао / могла.

examples.en: Can you help me?
I can't sleep.
May I have a coffee?

forms: var. с; + instr. (with whom); + gen. (from where)

examples.en: I'm going to the movies with a friend.
I drink coffee with milk.
He fell off the bicycle.

tips: In speech - a hesitation pause like "uh, well": «Па не знам, овај... треба размислити». Often continued with «овај, како се зове» - "uh, what's it called".
In conversation it is often a filler word like "um, you know": «Овај... не знам шта да кажем». Not to be confused with the demonstrative "this".
In speech «овај» can also be a filler like "this, what's-it": «Дај ми нож, овај, не нож, него вилицу».

examples.en: This car is new.
This is my brother.
What do you think of this idea?
This is a gift for you.
See you in an hour.
We were sitting at the table.

note: за + acc. of time - in: за пет минута

examples.en: Are you hungry?
Do you know where the post office is?

note: colloq. «је л'» = је ли: Је л' то истина?

tips: Знати is for facts and information: «знам где је продавница». A skill is «умети», possibility or permission is «моћи».

examples.en: I don't know where he is.
Can you swim?
He knows three languages.

tips: The negation is written together with the verb: «немам, немаш, нема», not «не имам». Often with the genitive: «имати среће, дара, разума».
Impersonal «има» - there is (+ gen.): «има хлеба». With time and distance: «има 80 километара», «колико година има?» - how old is he. «Имаш да радиш» - you have loads of work to do.
Има + да - must (има да ћути); има + gen. - amount, age, height (има два метра, има тридесет година); impersonal - there is (има лавова у Африци).

examples.en: I have two brothers.
Is there any bread?
How old are you?

note: «имам» = I have; «има» = there is

examples.en: I'm tired, but happy.

examples.sr: Хтео сам да дођем, [а̏ли] нисам могао.
examples.en: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
Everything is fine.
Everyone came to the party.
All the children were playing outside.

forms: gen./acc. вас; dat. вама, вам; instr. вама

examples.en: Where are you from?
Can I help you?
We've been waiting for you for an hour.
This is my brother.
My mom cooks great.

tips: Који asks about a choice from a set: Који ауто је твој? (which of the cars); какав asks about quality: Какав је твој ауто? (what kind of car do you have).

examples.sr: Човек [ко̀јӣ] стоји тамо је мој отац.
examples.en: The man standing over there is my father.
What's your favorite movie?
What year were you born?

tips: In speech the parenthetical «мислим» works like "I mean": «Не знам шта да ти кажем, мислим, нисам упућен». It is not always "I think".
мислити на + acc. - to think of someone, to have them in mind: мислим на тебе. Мислити о + loc. - to think about something: мислити о будућности. Мислити да - to think that.
«Мислити» is followed by «да» (that), not «шта» (what): «Мислим да то није добро за тебе».

examples.en: I think you're right.
What do you think about it?
I keep thinking about you.

note: мислити на некога - to think of someone

tips: It can also mean "simply": «само уради како су ти рекли» - just do as you were told.

examples.en: I only have five minutes.
Just a little, please.
How are you? - Fine, thanks.
Okay, see you tomorrow.
She speaks Serbian well.

tips: Рећи has no usable present tense: "I say" is кажем (казати). The future and the past exist: рећи ћу, рекао сам. «Рекнем» is also heard in speech.

examples.en: What did you say?
Tell me the truth.
It's hard to say what will happen.

note: in the present tense «кажем» (from казати) is more common than «речем»

examples.en: This letter is from my mother.
I've been working here since January.
My brother is older than me.

note: in comparisons: старији од мене - older than me

examples.en: I'm from Belgrade, and you?
He works, and she studies.
I have to go.
You don't have to come.

note: «не морати» means "don't have to", not "must not"

forms: f. оне; n. она; gen./acc. њих, их; dat. њима, им

examples.en: They live downtown.
I saw them yesterday.
Tell them to come.
How are you?
What's your name?
I don't know how this is done.
We talked about you.
What do you think about it?

tips: A biaspectual verb: «видети» means both "to see" and "to catch sight of, to spot". The aspect is clear from context: «Нисам видео ниједну грешку» - I didn't spot a single mistake.

examples.en: See you tomorrow!
Do you see that ship?
I haven't seen you in years.

tips: It is also used for travelling by transport: «Идем аутобусом кући», «Идете ли летос у Црну Гору?». For regular trips there is возити се.
One verb covers going, walking and travelling. Transport takes the instrumental without a preposition: ићи аутобусом, возом, колима, бициклом; on foot - ићи пешке.
«Ићи» is also used for a trip: «идемо бусом», «ишли смо авионом». Note that «дошао сам» means "I came", whether on foot, by vehicle or by plane.

examples.en: I'm going home.
How is work going?
Come on, let's go!

note: ићи also means "to travel": идем у Београд возом

examples.en: If you want, come tomorrow.
Call me if you need anything.

tips: If a verb follows, use the impersonal «треба да»: «Треба да учим». If you need a thing, use personal forms: «Требају ми књиге». «Требам да учим» is heard in speech but is not standard.

examples.en: I need your help.
You should study more.
What do you need?

note: impersonal: треба ми = I need

examples.en: Happy birthday to you!
What would you like to drink?
I'd like to meet you.

tips: In speech it is also a marker like "sort of, like": «Ја као: хајде да свратимо на кафу». It softens a phrase or introduces someone's words, not only "as".
Colloquially «као» also means "supposedly": «Он је као болестан» - he's supposedly sick. In fast speech it shortens to «ко».
Also a filler like "like": «И она као: Мени је то много значило». «Мислим» at the start of a phrase means "I mean".

examples.en: White as snow.
He works as a waiter.
You look like you haven't slept.

note: ради као конобар - he works as a waiter

examples.en: I've lived here for five years.
It's really nice here.

tips: Besides "to work": «ради се о...» - it is about..., «не ради ми се» - I don't feel like working, «сат ради» - the clock is running, «радити домаћи» - to do homework, «на своју руку» - in one's own way.

examples.en: Where do you work now?
What are you doing tonight?
Why are you so sad?
That's right, you're right.
Apples, pears and so on.

tips: «Човек» means both "person" and "man". For traits of character people say особа or личност: она је оптимистична особа (not «оптимистичан човек»).
The plural comes from a different stem: «један човек - два човека, али много људи». The form «човеци» is archaic and sounds bookish or jocular.

examples.en: He's a good person.
There were a hundred people in the hall.
Man, this is great!

note: pl. «људи»; «човече!» - colloq. address: buddy, man

examples.en: Is this your phone?
I like your dress.

tips: Before an adverb or an adjective only «много» is used: много добро, много лепо. Before a verb or a noun both «много» and «пуно» work: «хвала пуно» and «хвала много» are both fine.

examples.en: I have a lot of work.
Thank you very much!
He doesn't work here anymore.

note: много + gen.: много људи

tips: A conjunction: "and, then, so" (Каснили смо, па смо узели такси). Also a filler interjection "well...", often drawn out: «Па… видећемо».
In dialogue - "well": «Па, добро» - well, okay; «Па шта онда?» - so what then? Also in lists: «прво Нови Сад, па Београд, па Суботица».
When thinking or answering evasively: «Па... можда дођем» - "Well... maybe I'll come". Opening with «па» softens the reply and makes speech livelier.

examples.sr: Прво ћемо ручати, [па] ћемо у шетњу.
examples.en: First we'll have lunch, then we'll go for a walk.
She was sick, so she didn't come.
Well, of course I do!

note: at the start of a phrase - "well": па добро - well, okay

examples.en: Everyone has their own opinion.
Take your bag.
Do you want something to drink?
I have to tell you something.

examples.sr: Чекали смо [не̏што] више од сат времена.
examples.en: We waited a little more than an hour.

forms: gen./acc. кога; dat. коме; instr. ким

examples.en: Who is that?
Who are you waiting for?
Who were you with last night?
Why are you late?
I don't know why she left.
I have no time.
No problem.
He isn't at home.

note: нема + gen.: нема хлеба - there is no bread

examples.en: Would you like some more coffee?
He still isn't here.
I still work at the same company.

note: још увек - still

tips: Not the color: «у реду» means "all right, okay" («Дама је у реду» - she's fine). «Ред» is also a queue, a row, a line: «чекати у реду».
«У првом реду» - first of all, «реда ради» - for form's sake, «ред вожње» - timetable, «дневни ред» - agenda, «у реду је» - fine (when paying: keep the change).

examples.en: Everything is in order.
We've been waiting in line for half an hour.
We sat in the first row.

note: у реду - all right, okay

examples.en: What do you say to that?
Tell me what happened.
Who told you that?

note: in the present tense «кажем» usually replaces «речем»

tips: To avoid repeating «добар»: одличан, сјајан, диван, изврстан, савршен, фантастичан, феноменалан. To intensify, add the prefix: предобар.

examples.en: He is a good man.
Good afternoon, how are you?
Where do you live?
Where were you last night?
I don't know where my keys are.
When does the film start?
Call me when you arrive.

examples.sr: [Ка̏д] бих имао новца, купио бих стан.
examples.en: If I had money, I would buy an apartment.

note: кад бих... - if I were to...

tips: «Дођи!» - "come here" (to children, animals). Pairs: доћи - отићи (come - leave), ући - изаћи (go in - go out).
One verb for both "come" and "arrive", by any means of travel: «Дошао сам пешке / колима» - I came on foot / by car.

examples.en: Come to my place tonight.
When did you arrive?
The bus will arrive in ten minutes.

tips: «Хвала вама» - thank you too (in reply to thanks). «Молим» - you're welcome, «Нема на чему» - don't mention it.

examples.en: Thanks a lot!
Thank you for everything.

note: хвала на + loc.: хвала на помоћи - thanks for the help

examples.en: I'm from Russia.
Take the keys out of the bag.
It might rain.
Maybe you're right.
Do you want tea or coffee?

examples.sr: [И̏ли] ћеш ти доћи, или ћу ја.
examples.en: Either you'll come, or I will.

tips: Дати гол = to score a goal. Do not confuse «гол» (goal) with «гол» (naked, f. гола).

examples.en: Give me some water, please.
Mom gave me the money.
Can you give me your number?
Wait a little.
I have little time.
Eat fewer sweets.
Breakfast first, then work.
See you tomorrow, then.
Where do you work now?
I'll tell you in a moment.
Now I know the truth.

tips: «Колико је сати?» asks the time; «Какво је време данас?» asks about the weather. Context decides.
«Лепо време» - nice weather, «радно време» - working hours, «с времена на време» - from time to time, «у право време» - just in time.

examples.en: I have no time for that.
What's the weather like today?
Now it's time for lunch.

note: «време» is both "time" and "weather"

tips: Also a reply to «хвала»: «Ништа!» - don't mention it. After a refusal: «Ништа, хвала» - oh well, thanks. When someone is ignored: «ти ништа» - and you said not a word.
A reply to «извините» and «хвала»: «ма ништа» (it's nothing, never mind). Not to be confused with «молим», which answers «хвала» in shops and formal settings.

examples.en: I don't understand anything.
What are you doing? - Nothing special.

note: double negative: ништа не знам - I know nothing

tips: «Зар» opens a question that shows surprise: «зар се нисмо упознали?» - haven't we met? «зар је тешко?» - is it that hard?

examples.en: Didn't you know?
Are you leaving already?
Pack your things.
That's a different matter.
He is actually right.

note: у ствари - in fact, actually

examples.en: I work until five o'clock.
Sit next to me.
Goodbye!
Good day!
I'll stay for three days.
I go to work every day.
Give me the other knife.
This is my second attempt.

note: also "second": други спрат - the second floor

tips: Indefinite words start with «не-»: неко, нешто, негде, некад, неки. Negative ones start with «ни-» and still need «не» before the verb: «нико није дошао» - nobody came.

examples.en: Someone is knocking at the door.
Does anyone speak Russian?
Are you waiting for someone?
What did you do?
I have to do it today.

tips: «Молити се» (with «се») - to pray: молити се Богу; without «се» - to ask: «молим те», «молити за помоћ».
«Молим» in speech: "please" and "how can I help?" (on the phone); «молим?» - "pardon?"; «молим?!» - disbelief: «Молим?! Како то мислиш?» - Excuse me?! What do you mean?

examples.en: Please help me.
One coffee, please.
Pardon? I didn't hear you.

note: молим - please; pardon?; you're welcome

examples.en: This is our house.
Our son goes to school.

tips: Often without the first letter: «ајде». Used for an invitation («Ајде да идемо на кафу!»), agreement («Ајде, долазим!»), parting («Ајде, чујемо се») and "okay, fine" («Ајде, добро»).

Forms: хајде (to one person), хајдемо (we), хајдете (you, plural); also ајде, ајмо. From Turkish; the first letter is often dropped in speech. «Ајмо кући!» - let's go home. «Хајде» often nudges someone into action.

examples.en: Let's go to the movies!
Let's go, it's late.
Come on, don't be angry.

note: хајде да + present - let's...: хајде да једемо - let's eat

tips: «Година» is a year as a period, and also age: «Имам 35 година». Year of birth is «годиште»: «Које си годиште?» Adults are usually asked that; «Колико имаш година?» sounds like a question to a child.
«Преступна година» - leap year, «проста» - ordinary year, «берићетна» - a fruitful year (in wishes). «Година» is also a year of study at university; the plural «године» means age: «у тим годинама».

examples.en: Happy New Year!
I'm thirty years old.
Last year we were in Greece.
Is this your passport?
Thank you for your help.

tips: Strengthens a negative, often like "even": «Нисам те ни питао» - I didn't even ask you. In an affirmative sentence "too" is «и»: «И ја долазим» - I'm coming too.

examples.en: I didn't say a single word.
I don't know either.
There is neither bread nor milk.

note: ни ја - me neither

examples.en: Who is there?
I'm going there tomorrow.
I have to leave.
She left an hour ago.
Let's go for a drink.

tips: Means "some, a certain" and "some (people)": «неки пут» - sometimes; before a number - "about" («неких двадесет година»); as a reproach: «Баш си неки!» - you're a strange one!

examples.en: Some man called you.
Some people don't like coffee.
We've been waiting for some time already.
I was late because of the traffic jam.
I did it for you.
I'll give you the money back tomorrow.
I came back from Vienna yesterday.
When will you get back home?

note: вратити се - to come back

tips: A biaspectual verb: both imperfective and perfective. Доручковати, ручати, вечерати and verbs in -овати, -исати, -ирати behave the same.
«Чуј!» opening a remark is an ironic echo of the other person: «Чуј два!» - "two, he says!"; «чуј не могу!» - "can't, you say? Of course I can!"
«Чујемо се!» - we'll be in touch, «Чуј га!» - just listen to him (ironic), «Нећу ни да га чујем» - I won't even hear of him, «Нисам добро чуо» - I didn't hear properly.

examples.en: Can you hear me?
I heard you're getting married.

tips: The plural «послови» means duties, operations (кућни, банкарски послови). In set phrases the plural is «посла» - affairs: «српска посла», «мешати се у туђа посла».
Stress on the first syllable: пОсао. Fleeting а: посао, посла, послу. "Where (at)?" - «на послу», "where to?" - «на посао». «На послу» is not a mistake but the locative.

examples.en: I'm looking for a new job.
I go to work at eight.
That's none of your business.
I can't find my keys.
Let's meet at six.

note: наћи се - to meet up

examples.en: I'm here, don't be afraid.
Stay right here!
I love you.
Do you like coffee?
I would like to go to Paris.

note: волео бих - I would like to; љубити - to kiss

examples.en: He wanted to kill him.
If I'm late, Mom will kill me!
That's life.
I've lived here all my life.

tips: In everyday speech simply "to speak": «не прича руски» - he doesn't speak Russian, «причамо српски» - we speak Serbian.

examples.en: What are you talking about?
Tell me about yourself.

note: colloquially «причати» = to speak, to chat

examples.en: This is his house.
Do you know his number?

note: declines like an adjective: његова сестра

examples.en: She is always late.
I still love you.

note: још увек - still

tips: The short form (велик) comes after the verb («Јелен је велик») and for something mentioned for the first time; the long form (велики) is for a specific, already identified thing: «тај велики јелен».

examples.en: They have a big house.
That's a big problem.
My apartment is bigger than yours.

tips: The compliment «Лепо (ми) изгледате!» - you look nice; informal: «Лепо изгледаш!». The particle «ми» adds warmth and suits a colleague, a mother-in-law, a mom.

examples.en: You look great!
It looks like it's going to rain.

note: изгледа да... - it looks like..., it seems that...

examples.en: God, how beautiful!
Do you believe in God?
Thank God, everyone is alive.

note: хвала богу - thank God

examples.en: I'm really sorry.
Really? I don't believe it.

tips: Besides "exactly, just" («баш сад» - right now) it often replaces «врло, јако» - "very": «Баш волим овај бенд», «Баш је топло». A colloquial intensifier.
Meanings: exactly, just («баш сад»), really, very («баш тежак дан»); in a negative sentence - "not particularly". In conversation also "really": «баш лепо» - really nice, not only "exactly".

examples.en: That's exactly what I wanted to say.
That's really nice of you.
I couldn't care less.

note: colloq. «баш ме брига» - I couldn't care less

examples.sr: Не могу да дођем [је̏р] сам болестан.
examples.en: I can't come because I'm sick.

examples.sr: Остао сам код куће [је̏р] је падала киша.
examples.en: I stayed home because it was raining.
That woman works in a bank.
This is my wife Ana.

tips: "To call someone" takes the accusative: зовем Ану. The verb телефонирати, on the contrary, takes the dative: телефонирам Ани.
«Звати» - to call, to phone, to invite: «Звала ме је да би ме позвала на рођендан» - she called me to invite me to a birthday party. «Позван сам на рођендан» - I've been invited to a birthday party.
«Звати» + accusative: «зови ме» - call me, «звати на телефон». There is no separate "call back": «зваћу те касније», «звати поново».

examples.en: What's your name?

examples.sr: [Зва̏о] сам те јуче, ниси се јавио.
examples.en: I called you yesterday, you didn't pick up.
Mom is calling you.

note: звати - also "to phone": звао сам те - I called you

examples.en: We walked around the city.
I'm going to get bread.
In my opinion, that's not true.

note: ићи по + acc. - to go and get: идем по децу - I'm going to pick up the kids

examples.en: I was sick, so I didn't come.
Because I love you.

note: зато што - because

tips: Two meanings: "already" («Већ знам одговор») and "but" after a negative («Не желим кафу, већ чај»). Both can occur in one sentence: «Нисам још ручао, већ сам појео бурек».

The construction «не X, већ Y»: «Личим не на мајку, већ на бабу» - I take after my grandmother, not my mother. The negation stands before the right element or before the predicate. «Није Ана, већ Марија» - it's not Ana, but Marija. More bookish than «него».

examples.en: It's already late.
Have you already had dinner?
It's not him who's to blame, but me.

note: не ..., већ ... - not ..., but ...

examples.en: Wait for me in front of the cinema.
Who are you waiting for?
I've been waiting for you for an hour.
I don't believe you.
Do you believe in God?

note: веровати + dat.: верујем ти - I believe you

tips: An adverb that does not change; a noun after it is in the genitive: «колико година имаш?». The adjective «колики» does decline: «колика је штета?»

examples.en: How much does this cost?
How old are you?
You know how much I love you.

tips: Perfective: помогнем; imperative «помози!» or «помогни!»; past помогао, помогла: «Нико неће да ми помогне» - nobody wants to help me.

examples.en: Can you help me?
Help!
She helped me a lot.
Good afternoon, sir!
That gentleman is waiting for you.
Ladies and gentlemen!

note: pl. господа: даме и господо - ladies and gentlemen

tips: The plural «деца» declines like a feminine singular (gen. деце, dat. деци), but the verb and adjective are plural: «деца су мала», «децо, долазите!».
«Деца» is a collective noun with a plural verb: «деца су дошла». There is no plural «дета». With numbers: «двоје/троје деце».

examples.en: They have two children.
The children are playing in the park.
He is still a child.

note: pl. «деца» declines like a feminine singular: мала деца

examples.en: Wash your hands before eating.
I was there two years ago.
Why didn't you say so earlier?

note: пре две године - two years ago

tips: «Право» means "straight" («иди право»), not "to the right": that is «десно».
«Право» is also law as a subject («студирам право») and a legal right: «људска права» - human rights; «бити у праву» - to be right, «с којим правом» - by what right.

examples.en: You have the right to remain silent.
You're right, sorry.
Go straight, then left.

note: у праву си - you're right; adv. право - straight

tips: «Пут» is a road and a journey («на путу сам» - I'm on my way) and also "time": први пут, овог пута, прошли пут, више пута, два пута, пет пута дневно, «неки други пут».
Besides "road", «пут» means "time": сваки пут - every time, овај пут - this time, први пут - the first time.

examples.en: Have a good trip!
I've been there three times.
What's the shortest way to the center?

note: «пут» also means "time": први пут, два пута

tips: Not only "to get": добити утакмицу - to win a match; добити сина/ћерку - to have a son/daughter; добити позив - to be invited or called; «нисам те добио» - I couldn't reach you by phone.

Also: to get a shot (добити ињекцију), to win (добити на лутрији - to win the lottery), «добити корпу» - to be turned down, and to get through by phone («добили сте погрешан број» - you've dialed the wrong number).

examples.en: I got a new job.
Our team won the match.

tips: Means "but" when the first part is negative: «Нисам гладна, него сам уморна». Also «него шта?» - what else!; «није само…, него и…» - not only..., but also...; in comparisons - "than".

examples.en: He is older than me.
Better late than never.
He drinks not tea, but coffee.
Wait until I come.

examples.sr: [До̏к] је он радио, она је спавала.
examples.en: While he was working, she was sleeping.

note: док не + perfective verb - until

examples.en: I drink coffee without sugar.
I can't do without you.

tips: The filler «значи» is a verbal tic: «значи, ја сам...» = "so, I...". Serbs also say «па», «овај», «дакле»: much like "well", "um".
As a discourse word «значи» = "so, that is, well": «Значи, видимо се у шест.» Often just a filler in colloquial speech.

examples.en: What does this word mean?
That means a lot to me.
So, we'll see each other tomorrow?
Of course I'll come.
Can you help me? - Of course!
Take an umbrella, it's raining.
Who took my phone?
Is this seat free?

examples.sr: Ово је моје омиљено [ме̏сто] у граду.
examples.en: This is my favorite place in the city.
In your place I wouldn't go.
I go to work every day.
Everyone has the right to make a mistake.

note: свако - everyone: свако то зна - everyone knows that

examples.en: My father is a doctor.
You look a lot like your father.

note: gen. оца, voc. оче

meanings: what kind of, what sort of

examples.en: What is your new boss like?
What's the weather like in Belgrade?
What a beautiful dress!
Do you see that ship?
Give me those red apples.

note: овај - near me, тај - near you, онај - far from both

examples.en: Do you speak English?
Don't talk nonsense.
What are you saying?
Mom is making lunch.
I called Mom yesterday.

tips: Besides "to look for" it means "to ask for, to demand": цариник тражи пасош - the customs officer asks for your passport. Not to be confused with питати (to ask a question).
Both "to look for" and "to ask for, to demand": тражим кључеве - I'm looking for my keys, тражим помоћ - I ask for help, тражим новац - I demand money.

examples.en: What are you looking for?
I'm looking for a job.
He asked me for money.

note: тражити од некога - to ask someone for something

examples.en: I bought a new phone.
Happy New Year!
What's new?
Do you watch soccer?
What are you watching?
Watch where you're going!

tips: «Код» + genitive: at a person's («идем код доктора» - I'm going to the doctor's, «код фризера сам» - I'm at the hairdresser's), or by an object («чекам те код банке»). For buildings and places use «у» and «на».
«Код куће» - at home, but «у кући» - inside the house. To people we go «код» (код лекара), to institutions «у» (у школу). Also: «код мене је кључ» - I have the key.

examples.en: Tonight I'm sleeping at my brother's.
I'll wait for you by the post office.
Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor.

note: код куће - at home; идем код лекара - I'm going to the doctor

examples.en: I'm sorry, I didn't know.

examples.sr: Било ми је [жа̏о] што ниси дошао.
examples.en: I was sorry that you didn't come.

note: жао ми је - I'm sorry

examples.en: She has blue eyes.
Close your eyes and rest.

note: pl. очи is feminine: плаве очи

tips: The plural of the noun «око» is «очи» (feminine, gen. «очију»): лепе очи. The form «ока» is rarer. «Лош вид» - poor eyesight, «на левом оку» - in the left eye.
Plural: очи: плаве очи, боле ме очи. One eye - око: лево и десно око, «Боли ме десно око» - my right eye hurts.

examples.en: We sat around the table.
I'll come around eight.
Don't worry about that.
He is my best friend.
I went out with friends.
Hi, how are you?
Bye, see you!

note: used both to greet and to say goodbye

examples.en: We live in a small apartment.
This is my little brother.

tips: Negative pronouns need a double negative: «нико није дошао», «нигде нисам био» - I haven't been anywhere.

examples.en: Nobody came.
I don't trust anyone.

note: with a preposition it splits: ни са ким - with no one

examples.en: Can I ask you something?
Ask Mom.
I asked him where he lives.

note: in speech also used as a perfective: «питао сам» - I asked

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
Sorry for being late.

note: извинити се - to apologize

examples.en: I've never been to Paris.
I will never forget you.

note: double negative: никад нисам... - I have never...

examples.en: This is my first job.
We live on the second floor.
I was first in line.

note: први спрат - the floor above the ground floor (приземље), i.e. the second floor in the US

tips: Masculine, but declines like «мама»: «код мог тате, о мом тати». Adjectives in the plural take feminine endings: «наше тате», «нашим татама».

examples.en: Dad works at a factory.
Ask Dad.

note: masculine, but declines like a feminine noun: тату, тати

examples.en: Look at this!
Let's watch a movie.
Stay a bit longer.
How long will you stay in Belgrade?
Nothing was left.
Listen to me carefully.
I like to listen to music.
Children don't obey their parents.
I don't understand what you're saying.
Do you understand Serbian?

tips: «Проблем» is masculine, not «проблема»; plural «проблеми», gen. pl. «проблема»: «Немам проблема», «Имам проблеме».

examples.en: We have a big problem.
Thanks! - No problem.

note: masculine: велики проблем

tips: Prefixes change the meaning: преживети - to survive, to live through; оживети - to come alive; заживети - to start living, to settle in; доживети - to experience; уживети се - to settle into a place.

examples.en: Where do you live?
I lived in Russia for five years.
Cheers!

note: живели! - a toast: cheers!

examples.en: Are you sure?
This is a safe place.
I worked all day.
He ate a whole pizza.

tips: «Девојка» - a girl, a young woman and a girlfriend; «девојче» - a little girl, also an affectionate "girl"; «девојчица» - a little girl. Not to be confused with «жена» (woman, wife).

examples.en: Who is that girl?
This is my girlfriend Jelena.

note: моја девојка - my girlfriend

examples.en: What's your name?
I forgot his name.

tips: «Кући» answers "where to": home («вратио се кући»); «код куће» answers "where": at home («код куће сам»); «кући сам» is wrong. The adjective is «кућни»: кућни љубимац - pet, кућни ред - house rules, кућне папуче - slippers.

examples.en: Our house is near the sea.
I'm going home, I'm tired.

note: «идем кући» - I'm going home

examples.en: What did I do to you?
I'll do everything for you.

note: a bit more formal than «урадити»

examples.en: I baked a cake.
I made a mistake.
Let's take a break.

tips: Many meanings: to release, to let in, to put on («пусти песму»), to grow («пустити браду»), to spread a rumor, to let out paint or water. «Пусти ме» - leave me alone.
Besides "to release": to play a song, a film, cartoons: «Пусти музику!», «Пусти ми цртаће».
meanings: to let in, to let through

examples.en: Let me go!
Let me through.
Put on some music.

note: пусти! - leave me alone

examples.en: I want to travel around the world.
You're the best mom in the world.
There were lots of people at the concert.

tips: Singular only, neutral and fit for documents. The colloquial «паре» exists only in the plural, is a Turkish loanword, and is not used in official texts.

examples.en: I have no money.
How much money do you need?

note: singular, masculine: новац је на столу - the money is on the table

meanings: to be there, to be available

examples.en: Is there another way?
There is no such word.

tips: Also a romantic relationship: «У вези сам» - I'm in a relationship; «љубавна веза» - a love affair. In memes «нема везе» plays on two meanings - "no connection" and "never mind".
Colloquial: «преко везе» - through connections, «немати везе» - to have no clue, «без везе» - pointless, nonsense, «нема везе» - never mind.
Also a connection as a link («телефонска, интернет веза»), a link between phenomena («веза између језика и културе») and a bunch of greens («веза першуна, младог лука»).

examples.en: Sorry! - Never mind.
They've been together for two years.
He got the job through connections.

note: нема везе - never mind, it doesn't matter

examples.en: Leave me alone.
Where did you leave the keys?
She left him after five years.
Wash your hands before eating.
Give me your hand.

tips: «Момак» - a guy, a young man; also a bachelor («остати момак» - to stay single) and a boyfriend. «Дечко» - a boy, a guy; «младић» - a young man.

examples.en: Who is that guy?
She has a boyfriend.
My mother is a teacher.
I bought flowers for my mom.
He comes every Friday.
Coming!
Where are you from?

tips: «Сат» is a clock or watch (ручни, џепни сат) and an hour as a unit: «сат времена» - an hour, «сат и по» - an hour and a half. Telling time: «Колико је сати?», «у пет сати». Also a meter: «електрични сат».
«Сат» - both hour and clock (the device); a school lesson is «час». The words «сат» and «минут» are often dropped: «пола шест» - half past five, «пет до дванаест» - five to twelve.

examples.en: What time is it?
I've been waiting for you for an hour.
I bought a new watch.

note: колико је сати? - what time is it?

examples.en: This is her car.
Do you know her address?

note: declines like an adjective

examples.en: How do you feel?
I feel much better.

note: осећати се - to feel (well, ill...)

examples.en: This is an old house.
How old are you?
My older brother lives in Niš.

note: колико си стар? - how old are you?

examples.en: They have a son and a daughter.
Son, come here!

tips: Ево - here (close by), ето - there (near the listener or in general), ено - over there (far): «ево је», «ето је», «ено је».
«Ево га/је/ме» - here he/she/I am: «Где ми је телефон? - Ево га». Said when showing or handing something.
With short pronouns: ево ме, ево те, ево га, ево је, ево нас, ево вас, ево их. To «Где си?» one answers «Ево ме!» - here I am.

examples.en: Here I am, I've arrived.
Here are your keys.

note: ево - here (near me), ето - there (near you), ено - over there

tips: Without «се»: «почети» means both "to begin" (something) and "to start" (by itself): «час почиње у осам». Not «почети се».

examples.en: The film has already started.
Let's begin.
I started learning Serbian.
Today is Monday.
What are you doing today?

tips: The wish is «лаку ноћ» (literally "a light night"), used for "good night".

examples.en: Good night!
He worked all night.
His grandfather died last year.

examples.sr: Мислио сам да ћу [у̀мре̄ти] од страха.
examples.en: I thought I would die of fear.
Is it far to the center?
He lives far from the city.
What do we do next?
We need to talk.
Who were you talking to?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.
She takes care of the children.

note: бринути о + loc. - to take care of

examples.en: Come at once!
I'll be right back.

tips: The person it happens to is in the dative: «шта ти се десило?», «шта му се десило?» (what happened to him).

examples.en: What happened?
It can happen to anyone.
She has a kind soul.
Darling, where are you?

note: душо - an affectionate form of address

tips: A very versatile word: «лепо се понашати» - to behave well, «лепо замолити» - to ask nicely, «лепо пише» - it's written clearly; also «хвала лепа», «молим лепо».

examples.en: She sings beautifully.
Thank you very much!
It's nice to see you again.
Even he doesn't know.
Everyone came, even Grandma.
The fish is dead.
I'm dead tired.
I take the kids to school.
Who runs the company?
Where does this road lead?
Have you finished the work?
The film ended at midnight.
She graduated from university.
Hold my hand.
Where do you keep the keys?
Why are you so late?
Don't drink so much.
That's enough about that.

tips: «Нека» + noun - "some": «нека жена те тражи» - some woman is looking for you. «Нека» + verb - "let": «нека иде», «нека каже истину».

examples.en: Let him in.
Let it be as you say.
No need, thanks, I'll do it myself.
I lost my keys.
Our team lost.
I don't want to lose you.
This is very important.
Very nice to meet you.
I have one question.
That's not a question of money.

tips: Don't mix up the forms: «сам» - I am (урадио сам), «сам/сама» - alone, by oneself, and «само» - only. «Урадио сам то сам» - I did it myself.
«Сам сам» - I'm alone: the first is «alone», the second is «am» from бити. «Могу сама» - I can manage on my own. Само мало - just a second; само што нису стигли - they're about to arrive.

examples.en: I live alone.
She did it herself.
Don't leave me alone.

note: not to be confused with «сам», a form of бити (to be)

examples.en: Stop! Don't go any further.
The bus stopped in front of the school.
I care about you.

note: стало ми је до + gen. - I care about, ... matters to me

tips: In slang «крај» is the neighborhood where you live: «у мом крају» - in my neighborhood, «у крају» - somewhere nearby, in the area.

examples.en: This is the end of the movie.
I live in this neighborhood.
In the end, I agreed anyway.
Stop it, please!
The rain has stopped.
I quit smoking.
Don't drive so fast!
Come as soon as you can.
I left my keys at home.
Don't forget to call me.
He's that kind of person.
I've never seen such a house.
Are you late again?
It's raining again.

tips: Exactly, precisely: «управо тај аутомобил желим», «управо сам разговарао са комшијом» - I was just talking to the neighbor.
It strengthens «exactly, precisely»: «управо тај аутомобил» - that very car. With the past tense it means «just now»: «управо сам разговарао».

examples.en: I've just arrived.

examples.sr: То је [у̏право] оно што ми треба.
examples.en: That's exactly what I need.

note: управо сам... - I have just...

examples.en: There must be another way.

examples.sr: Не свиђа ми се његов [на́чин] говора.
examples.en: I don't like his way of speaking.
In a way, you're right.

tips: Country is земља or држава; «страна» means side or page.
Земља means earth (soil, the planet) and country: «страна земља» - a foreign country. Don't confuse it with «страна» (side) or «страница» (page).
Земљина кугла - the globe; Земљина оса, кора, језгро - the Earth's axis, crust, core. Земљиште - soil, ground, or a plot of land.

examples.en: Serbia is a beautiful country.
He fell to the ground.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.

note: земља also means «country»

examples.en: He will surely come.
Will you come? - Of course!
Take an umbrella, just in case.
The police are investigating the case.
Under no circumstances!
Go to your room.
I booked a room at the hotel.

tips: Истина is the truth of a fact; «правда» means justice, fairness. «Жива истина» - the plain truth.

examples.en: Tell me the truth.
That's not true.
This is the most beautiful part of the city.
That's part of my job.
Come in, it's open.
May I come in?
Are you ready?
Dinner is ready.
I've only been there once.
Someday you'll understand me.
I go to the gym once a week.

tips: Брат is not only a biological brother: the word can be used for any male relative (uncle, cousins). Affectionately, a boy you don't know is «бато», a girl «сека».
The plural is the collective «браћа»: моја браћа, браћа су дошла.
The address «брате!» is closest to «bro» or «man»: friendly. Don't confuse it with «бре», a particle that only adds emotion.

examples.en: I have an older brother.
These are my brothers.
What's up, bro?

note: pl. браћа takes feminine singular agreement: моја браћа

examples.en: Belgrade is a big city.
We're going downtown for a coffee.
It hailed yesterday.
I have a headache.
Read the first chapter.
Whatever you do, I'll love you.
Whoever comes, let them wait.
Come whenever you want.

note: ко год - whoever; шта год - whatever

examples.en: I'm very cold.
The wind is blowing hard.
Press harder.

tips: Always with «се» and the genitive: «сећам се детињства», «сећам се тебе». Pf. pair - «сетити се» (to recall, to think of), impf. - to remember in general.
forms: сећам се, сећају се; pf. сетити се

examples.en: Do you remember me?
I don't remember his name.

note: сећати се + gen.: сећам се тога

tips: Takes the dative: «надати се нечему» (to hope for something). Common «надам се да...» - I hope that... The noun is «нада».

examples.en: I hope you'll come.
Let's hope for the best.

tips: After пуно comes the genitive: пуно воћа, пуно људи (not «пуно воће»). The same holds for мало, довољно, много.

examples.en: Thank you very much!
I have a lot of work.

note: colloq.; пуно + gen.: пуно људи

examples.en: I'm trying to fall asleep.
What are you trying to say?
Send me a message.
I sent you a package.
See you after work.
I'll call you later.
The police found the car.
We have to find a solution.

tips: Страна means both side and page: «с горње стране» - from above, «са стране» - from the side, «на све стране» - in all directions, «шалу на страну» - joking aside. Don't confuse it with «земља» (country).
Besides «side» it also means «page»: «на страни 10». The adjective «страни» means foreign: «страни језик».

examples.en: Cross to the other side of the street.
Open your books to page ten.
You're always on my side.

note: страни means «foreign»: страни језик

examples.en: I want to become a doctor.
It has gotten cold.

note: постати + nom.: постао је лекар

tips: «Проћи на испиту» - to pass an exam, «проћи на аудицији» - to get through an audition, «Добро си прошао!» - you got off easy, «прошло је лето» - summer is over.

examples.en: A lot of time has passed.
How did you do on the exam?
Let me through.
We have enough time.
That's enough, thank you.
See you tomorrow.
I'm leaving on a trip tomorrow.

tips: «Месец» is both a month (on the calendar) and the moon: «Мој омиљени месец је мај», «Месец је данас прелеп».

examples.en: I was in Greece last month.
Tonight there's a full moon.

note: месец also means «moon»

tips: Impf. - a state, a habit: «мени се свиђа овај град». Pf. «свидети се» - a moment: «свидео ми се ресторан», «свидеће ти се». The pronoun comes before the verb: «мени се свиђа».
The structure is reversed: the thing liked is the subject: «свиђаш ми се» - I like you (literally, you please me), «свидео си ми се», «свидело ми се». Synonym - «допадати се».
The thing liked is the subject, the person who likes is in the dative: Свиђаш ми се - I like you; Свиђа ми се песма - I like the song. Synonym: допадати се.
forms: свиђа ми се; pf. свидети се

examples.en: I like this city.

examples.sr: Да ли ти се [сви̏ђа] моја хаљина?
examples.en: Do you like my dress?

note: the thing liked is the subject: свиђа ми се песма - I like the song

examples.en: It's already late.
I'll call you later.

tips: «Чинити се» + dat. - «to seem»: «Чини ми се да је касно» - it seems to me that it's late; «чинило се немогућим» - it seemed impossible. Without «се» - simply «to do, to make».

examples.en: I think it's raining.
Good deeds make the world a better place.

note: чини ми се - it seems to me

tips: Broader than «beautiful»: «лепа идеја» - a good idea, «леп мирис» - a pleasant smell, «лепа жена» - a beautiful woman, «хвала лепо» - thank you very much.
Not only «beautiful»: лепо време - fine weather, лепо мирише - smells nice, лепа реч - a kind word, леп посао - a good job, Лепо! - Great!

examples.en: She's a beautiful girl.
What a nice day!
What happened?

examples.sr: Таква несрећа може да се [до̀годи] свакоме.
examples.en: Such a misfortune can happen to anyone.
Let's have lunch together.
We've been living together for three years.
I haven't seen you for a long time.
How long are you staying?
Some guy was looking for you.
He's not my type.

note: colloq. «тип» - a guy, a dude

tips: A very broad verb: put, place, add (шећер у кафу), apply (крему), put on (наочаре, минђуше), pose (питање). Impf. стављати.

For accessories instead of «обући»: ставити/скидати наочаре (glasses), шешир (hat), качкет (cap), минђуше (earrings), прстен (ring), сат (watch), шминку (makeup), крему (cream), кармин (lipstick), каиш (belt). «Ставити под кључ» - to lock up.
«Ставити кафу» - to put the coffee on (to brew it for a guest or oneself): «Ставићу кафу, седи». A common hospitable phrase.

examples.en: Put the book on the table.
Where did you put my phone?
Get out of the room!
Do you want to go out tonight?

tips: «Реч» is a word («његове речи»); «слово» means a letter of the alphabet.
A speech or talk is «говор» or «обраћање».
Реч - «word»; a speech is говор, говор у јавности (public speaking).

examples.en: What does this word mean?
I give you my word.

tips: Покушати да + present: «Покушаћу да дођем на време». «Немојте покушавати код куће!» - don't try this at home. «Покушај убиства» - attempted murder.

examples.en: Try again.
I'll try to come.
That's enough!
I have quite a lot of work.

note: доста + gen.: доста времена

tips: By phone: «Позовите ме сутра у 8» - call me tomorrow at 8. To call back - «узвратити позив» or «позвати касније»; to get through - «добити телефоном».

examples.en: Call me tomorrow.
We were invited to a wedding.
Call the waiter, please.

note: позвати also means «to phone»

examples.en: We live in the same building.
You're all the same!
I have an important meeting.
The important thing is that you're alive.

tips: Always neuter plural, even for a single door: ова врата су дрвена, затвори врата.
Plural only: «door» is врата (n. pl.), «gate» is капија. With на: куцати на врата, на вратима. Collective numerals: једна врата, двоја врата, петора врата.

examples.en: Close the door, please.
Someone is knocking at the door.

note: plural only: ова врата су отворена - this door is open

examples.sr: Драго ми је што смо се [упо̀знали].
examples.en: Nice to have met you.
I want to introduce you to my parents.

tips: Takes the accusative: користим ову апликацију - I use this app.

examples.en: Can I use your phone?
That won't help us.
Forgive me, please.
Excuse me, where is the post office?
This is their house.
I know their son.

note: declines like an adjective

examples.en: Where are the others?
I'll tell you the rest tomorrow.
We were walking toward the town.
He was very nice to me.
According to the forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
Get out of here!
How far is it from here?
This is the last train.
When did you last see him?
What are you carrying in your bag?
She always wears black.
Come here!
Bring it here.

note: овамо - motion (to here), овде - place (here)

examples.en: This is very important.
She was very kind.
It's the struggle between good and evil.
I don't wish you any harm.

tips: «Драго ми је!» is not only "nice to meet you": in reply to good news, or when a guest praises the meal («Баш ми је пријало!» - I really enjoyed that), it means "I'm so glad!"

examples.en: Nice to meet you.

examples.sr: Било ми је [дра̑го] што сам те видео.
examples.en: I was glad to see you.

note: драго ми је - nice to meet you

tips: Породица is the family in the narrow sense (mom, dad, me), «фамилија» is the wider circle: grandparents, aunts and uncles, cousins. «Фамилија» is not a «family name»: a surname is «презиме».

examples.en: I have a big family.
I spend weekends with my family.

note: фамилија means the extended «family», not a surname (that is презиме)

examples.en: Go to sleep, it's late.
Did you sleep well?
I need your help.
You don't need to come.
We have to go.
The train started moving.
Follow me.
Open the window, it's hot.
Who opened the door?
Show me the photos.

examples.sr: Можете ли ми [пока́зати] пут до станице?
examples.en: Could you show me the way to the station?
The cat is under the table.
He put the box under the bed.

note: also a noun «под» - floor: на поду

examples.en: He's very dear to me.
Dear friends, welcome!

note: драг - dear; «expensive» is скуп

tips: Not «to make it in time» but «to manage, to succeed»: «успео сам да решим». For «to catch a train» you need the verb «стићи».
«Успети» - to work out, to manage; «Јеси ли успео?» - did you manage it? Not just «to make it in time».

examples.en: We did it!
I didn't manage to find him.

note: успети - to manage, to succeed; not «to be in time»

examples.en: They're a lovely couple.
I'll be back in a couple of minutes.

note: colloq. «пар» - a few: пар дана

examples.en: Try again.

examples.sr: Драго ми је што те [по̏ново] видим.
examples.en: I'm glad to see you again.

tips: It means «hard, difficult»: «Тешко ми је». Not «трудно»: «трудна» means pregnant.

examples.en: It's hard for me without you.
Serbian isn't hard to learn.
It's even harder for me now.

tips: More emotional than «па»: «Ма дај!», «Ма немој!», «Ма пусти то» - come on, no way, forget it. «Па не знам» - well, I don't know, «Ма не знам!» - how should I know?
An intensifier in dialogue: «Ма шта кажеш?» - what are you saying?!, «Ма иди!» - get out of here, no way!; «ма важи» - ironic: yeah, sure.
At the start of a reply, «come on, no way»: «Ма, свака част!» - hey, well done. It adds feeling and softens a refusal.

examples.en: Oh, come on, no way!
Oh, come on, it's nothing.

note: colloq.

examples.en: That's a great idea!
You look great.

tips: Past m.: «јео» (not «јел»), јела, јело, јели. Present: једем, једеш, једе, једемо, једете, једу.

examples.en: What are we going to eat tonight?
I don't eat meat.

tips: With time spans: кроз две недеље - in two weeks (in the future), кроз цео дан - through the whole day. Not for means: not «кроз стихове» but «стиховима»; not «кроз представнике» but «преко представника».

examples.en: We walked through the park.
He was looking out the window.
See you in a week.

tips: «Заиста» - really, actually: «заиста не знам» - I really don't know; in a question: «да ли заиста мислиш тако?».

examples.en: I'm really sorry.
Is that really true?
Wait a moment.
I'm not at home at the moment.

tips: Time words: вечерас (this evening), јутрос (this morning), ноћас (tonight), синоћ (last night). Not «данас увече».

examples.en: What are you doing tonight?
Tonight we're going to the theater.
Call the police!
The police arrived quickly.
He has a weak heart.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
I feel bad.
Not bad!
Today it's even worse.

note: comp. горе - worse (also «горе» = up, above)

tips: «With love» is «с љубављу»: the instrumental of a feminine noun ending in a consonant takes -ју.

examples.en: Everyone is looking for love.
He wrote her letters full of love.

note: љубити means «to kiss», not «to love»

examples.en: The children go to school.
We learn English at school.
You drank too much.
That's too expensive.
I'll stay for a few days.
I have a few questions.

tips: Games and sports take the accusative with no preposition: играм тенис, играмо фудбал. For a musical instrument use свирати: свирам гитару.

examples.en: The children are playing football.
Do you want to play cards?

note: играти + acc. without a preposition: играти шах; also «to dance»

examples.en: You're a true friend.
That was the right decision.
He's afraid of death.
After his death she moved away.
Go on, I'm listening.
We'll continue the conversation tomorrow.
You're my only friend.
That's our only chance.

tips: It means both «Sunday» and «week»: «данас је недеља» - today is Sunday; «за недељу дана» - in a week. The meaning is clear from context.
A seven-day week is both «недеља» and «седмица». «Седмица» has only this meaning, so people often say «сваке седмице» (every week) to avoid confusion with Sunday.
«Недељом» - on Sundays (like «понедељком», «суботом»). «Сваке недеље» means every week or every Sunday, depending on context.

examples.en: On Sunday we're going to grandma's.
See you in a week.

note: недеља means both «Sunday» and «week»

examples.en: What's going on?
That happens to everyone.

tips: Besides «number» («број телефона») it also means a size of clothing or shoes: «Имате ли већи број?» Physical dimensions are «димензије».
Besides number, figure - also a shoe size: «ципеле без броја» - shoes without a size (from a children's song). Also «бројити» - to count.
Also a number and a shoe or clothing size: «Треба ми број 37» - I need a size 37. What size do you wear? - Који број носите?

examples.en: Give me your phone number.
What shoe size do you wear?
I have to go to the doctor.
Doctor, what's wrong with me?
Do it like this.
It can't go on like this.
See you next week.
Who's next?

tips: Masculine: минут (pl. минути, but after 2-4 «минута»): један минут, пет минута.

examples.en: I'll be there in five minutes.
Wait one minute.

note: m. (var. f. минута): пет минута

examples.en: My sister lives in Novi Sad.
Nurse, could you help me?

tips: A cry for help: «У помоћ!». In Serbia: ambulance 194, police 192, fire brigade 193, roadside assistance 1987.

examples.en: Thank you for your help.
Call an ambulance!

note: f.; хитна помоћ - ambulance

examples.en: I have an idea!
That's not a very good idea.
I bought new shoes.
What should I buy for dinner?

tips: Схватити means «to understand» (ја сам схватио), not to grab physically: that is «ухватити, зграбити».

examples.en: I finally got it.

examples.sr: Да ли си [схва̀тила] шта сам рекао?
examples.en: Did you understand what I said?

tips: Правити - to create something material («правим торту»); радити - to do work («радим домаћи»); чинити - to do deeds («чиниш добро дело»).
Правити = to make, prepare: кафу, ручак, колаче, буку, проблеме. «Правити се + adj.» - to pretend: правити се луд, паметан. «Правити слику» - to take a picture.

examples.en: Mom is baking cakes.
Don't make noise!
I bought a new car.
Where did you park the car?

note: masculine: мој ауто

tips: Pf. of «знати»: to find out, learn something new: «сазнао сам где је библиотека». «Знам где је» - I know where it is in general, I'm already aware.

examples.en: How did you find that out?
I want to find out the truth.
We all think alike.
Me too.
After lunch we go for a walk.
He came back after two years.

note: more formal than «после»

examples.en: I'm waiting for you downstairs.
Come down!
First we'll have lunch.
Who arrived first?
I'm against it.
Tomorrow we're playing against Croatia.
Hi, how are you?
Bye, see you tomorrow!

note: colloq.; both a greeting and a farewell

examples.en: My whole body hurts.
The police found the body.

tips: Брод is a ship, a vessel: «трговачки брод» - a merchant ship. The nave of a church is also «брод». A ford (a shallow river crossing) is «газ».

examples.en: We traveled by ship.
The ship is sailing down the Danube.
Do you know Marko?
I've known him since school.

note: of people: познајем га - I know him

examples.en: I had a bad day.
That's not a bad idea.

note: comp. гори - worse

tips: «Из тог разлога» - for that reason, «из ког разлога» - for what reason. Don't confuse it with «разлаз» (parting, divergence).

examples.en: What's the reason?
There's no reason to worry.
Come inside, it's cold.
What's inside?
Happy birthday!
I'm so happy!
Everyone came except Marko.
Besides that, there's nothing new.
Exactly right!
I arrived at eight o'clock sharp.
A beautiful painting hangs on the wall.
Send me a picture.

related.en: to paint, to draw; to photograph

tips: «Шанса» is feminine: добра шанса.

examples.en: Give me one more chance.
We have no chance at all.

note: feminine: последња шанса

examples.en: It will probably rain.
He's probably asleep.
This is my boyfriend.
Hey, young man, come here!

note: colloq.; мој дечко - my boyfriend

tips: «Особа» is used for qualities: оптимистична особа (an optimistic person), rather than «оптимистичан човек».

examples.en: She's a wonderful person.
A table for two, please.

note: feminine, also of a man: он је добра особа

examples.en: It's only a game.
I like board games.
Wash your face with cold water.

examples.sr: Видео сам му на [ли̑цу] да лаже.
examples.en: I could see from his face that he was lying.

tips: «Преко реда» - out of turn, cutting in line: «Не може преко реда!» - no cutting in line.
Colloquially «преко» also means abroad: отићи преко - to go abroad to work or live.

examples.en: Cross the street.
I waited for more than an hour.
Take me home.
The taxi driver took us to the airport.

tips: Пазите! - careful!; пазити на + acc. - to take care of, look after someone or something (на децу, на ствари).

examples.en: Watch out! A car!
Look after the kids until I get there.

note: пазити на + acc. - to look after

examples.en: The police caught the thief.
Catch the ball!

tips: To arrive, to get there: «стићи кући», «стићи на време». Also «стићи» + infinitive - to have time to: «нисам стигао да погледам».
Also «to make it in time» («не стижем» - I can't make it, «стигао сам на воз» - I made the train) and «to catch up with» («не могу да га стигнем»). «To be in time» can only be said with «стићи».
Стићи also means «to have time to»: «Нисам стигао да вечерам» - I didn't have time to eat dinner. Impf. - «стизати».

examples.en: We arrived in Belgrade.
I won't make it on time.
So, what do we do now?
So you didn't know.
You've changed a lot.
I need to change jobs.

tips: «Платити» is broader than the English «to pay»: to pay for something, pay off, repay, compensate: «платити дуг» (pay a debt), «платити казну» (pay a fine).

examples.en: I'll pay for lunch.
Can I pay by card?

note: платити + acc. without «за»: платити ручак

examples.en: What's the plan for the weekend?
I have a good plan.
When are you coming home?
He always returns books on time.

note: враћати се - to come back

examples.en: You're still young.
My younger brother goes to school.

note: млада (noun) - bride

examples.en: That's easy.
It's easy for you to talk.

tips: Бар / барем - «at least, at a minimum»: «треба ми бар пет минута». The intensifier «чак» - «as many as, even»: «попио је чак три чаше».
The variant «барем» (at least) is the same, both words are equal. Close in meaning: «макар», «најмање» (at the very least), «у најмању руку».

examples.en: Call at least once.
At least try.

note: also a noun «бар» - a bar (pub)

examples.en: I'll call you tomorrow.
They named their son after his grandfather.

note: назвати - often «to phone»

tips: Not only «to follow»: пратити моду, пратити некога = to follow someone, to be subscribed to them. The object is in the accusative without a preposition: не пратим моду.
A broad word: to accompany (пратити до школе), to follow the news, and on social media - to follow: пратим те на инстаграму.
Запратити - to start following on social media; «пратити причу» - to follow a story; «пратити своје срце» - to follow your heart. Don't confuse it with «прати» (to wash).

examples.en: Someone is following us.
Follow me, I know the way.

tips: In conversation it can be a compliment: «луд си!» - you're wild, you're awesome.
«Луд за + instr.» - crazy about something: «Она је луда за музиком».

examples.en: Are you crazy?
I'm crazy about him.

tips: One word for both «happiness» and «luck»: «имати среће» - to be lucky, «срећно!» - good luck. From it comes «срећка» - a lottery ticket; the slogan «Огреби срећу!» is a play on words.
One word for both happiness and luck: «Срећа је да смо отишли на време» - it's lucky we left in time. «Срећом» - luckily, «несрећа» - misfortune, accident.
«Срећа» - happiness and luck: «Имам среће» - I'm lucky, «Немам среће» - I'm out of luck, «Срећа прати храбре» - fortune favors the brave.

examples.en: I wish you lots of happiness!
You were lucky.

note: срећа means both «happiness» and «luck»

examples.en: He's a real man.
There were two men in the room.
Allow me to introduce myself.
Mom didn't let me go.
There's blood on the floor.
I gave blood at the hospital.

note: feminine

tips: Besides «with»: next to (уз прозор), up (уз брдо), accompanied by (уз музику), with the help of (уз помоћ), as an accompaniment to a dish or an outfit, support. Always + acc.

examples.en: I drink tea with breakfast.
I was by your side all the time.
There's no reason to worry.
I couldn't care less!

note: брига ме - I don't care

examples.en: I get up early.
Why didn't you come earlier?

tips: After бојати се comes the genitive: бојим се мрака, воде, висине (afraid of the dark, water, heights). The particle се stays next to the verb: Не бојим се змија.

examples.en: I'm afraid of dogs.
Don't be afraid, I'm here.

note: бојати се + gen.: бојим се мрака

tips: To put in order: «средити папире», «средити ормар». The opposite is пореметити, to disrupt the order.
«Средити се» - to get oneself together, to be transformed: «баш си се средила!» - what a transformation (you look great).

examples.en: I need to tidy up the room.
Don't worry, I'll sort it out.

tips: The difference is in the means: «довести» - to bring (leading on foot), «довезти» - to bring by vehicle. Impf.: «доводити» / «довозити».

examples.en: Bring the kids tomorrow.
Who brought you here?
Good morning!
I drink coffee every morning.
My wallet is gone.
The power went out.

tips: Рат за независност - war of independence, ослободилачки рат - war of liberation, крсташки рат - crusade, грађански рат - civil war.

examples.en: The war lasted five years.
My grandfather was in the war.

note: masculine: велики рат

examples.en: I'm reading an interesting book.
What does it say in that book?

tips: The past tense of «писати» is built from the infinitive stem: «писао/писала». The form «пишао» belongs to another verb, пишати (to pee, colloq.). Don't mix them up.

examples.en: I'm writing a letter to my mom.
What does it say here?

note: шта пише? - what does it say?

examples.en: Check whether the door is locked.
I need to check my mail.
Actually, I'm not hungry.
What actually happened?

tips: As a noun, «dream» in the sense of an ambition is «сан»: «Сан ми се остварио» - my dream came true. «Машта» (imagination) does not work for this.

examples.en: I had a strange dream.

examples.sr: Мој [са̏н] је да путујем по свету.
examples.en: My dream is to travel the world.

note: gen. сна (the vowel «а» drops out)

tips: Also «to keep, not go bad»: «Малине дуго не стоје» - raspberries don't keep long.
The verb's stem changes: стајати - стојим, стоје (the suffix «-а-» becomes «-о-»). «Стајати» - to stand, and also to suit, of clothes: «лепо ти стоји».

examples.en: Why are you standing? Sit down.
The car is parked in front of the house.

note: present: стојим, стојиш

examples.en: Are you leaving already?
The train departs at eight.
This is my husband.
Her husband works as a doctor.
The ship's captain is an experienced sailor.
Understood, captain!
Bring me a glass of water.
I made a decision.

tips: A homonym: пас - a dog (gen. «пса») and a belt («пас око струка»).
An adult dog - «пас» (имам пса, немам пса; the accusative equals the genitive for animate nouns), a puppy - «штене»/«куче», affectionately - «куца».
Kinds of dogs: пас луталица - stray dog, ловачки пас - hunting dog, пас чувар - guard dog. Пас is the neutral word; куче - puppy, куца - affectionate, кер - mutt, pejorative.

examples.en: We have a dog and a cat.
The neighbor's dog barks all night.

note: masculine

examples.en: It's half past four now.
I ate half of the pizza.

note: пола пет - 4:30 (literally «half of five»)

tips: The adjective филмски: филмска уметност (cinematography), филмски фестивал, филмска пројекција (film screening), филмска екипа (film crew). A cartoon - цртани филм.

examples.en: Let's watch a movie.

examples.sr: У овом [фѝлму] глуми мој омиљени глумац.
examples.en: My favorite actor stars in this movie.
What are you thinking about?
I've been thinking about your offer.
Tell me a story.
It's a long story.
Good afternoon, madam!
Mrs. Jovanović is waiting for you.
I learned Serbian in a year.
Who taught you to cook?
I'll come anyway.

examples.sr: Био је уморан, али је [и̏па̄к] отишао.
examples.en: He was tired, but he went all the same.
My leg hurts.
He broke his leg skiing.
The dog ran away from the yard.
You can't run away from the truth.
How are you? - Great!
She cooks superbly.
It costs a hundred dollars.
I'm exchanging dollars for dinars.

tips: «Возим аутобус» - I'm a bus driver; «возим се аутобусом» - I'm riding a bus as a passenger. Without «се» the meaning is different!

examples.en: Do you know how to drive?
I drive the kids to school.

note: возити се - to ride: возим се аутобусом

tips: The stress falls on the second syllable: теле́фон (English puts it on the first).

examples.en: Your phone is ringing.
I talked to him on the phone.

tips: Pf. - «слагати» (to tell a lie): «слагала сам га» - I lied to him. Don't confuse it with «слагати» (to fold, put together) and «слагати се» (to agree).

examples.en: Don't lie to me.
He lies all the time.

tips: Храна is ordinary food, the neutral word. «Нафака» is bookish, of Turkish origin: sustenance as one's share allotted by fate; you don't buy «нафака» at a market.

examples.en: This food is excellent.
We have no food in the fridge.
The car is behind the house.
Who's behind it?
I hate Mondays.
I can't be bothered to get up.

note: мрзи ме - I can't be bothered

tips: «Јавити се» - to get in touch, including by phone: «Јавићу ти се сутра» - I'll get in touch tomorrow. Impf. «јављати се».
With «се»: to answer a call or in class, to get in touch («јавићу ти се сутра»), to respond to a job ad, to make itself felt («јавио ми се бол у леђима» - back pain showed up).
Јавити се - to make contact, to say hello or goodbye: «Јави ми се!» - call me, let me know; «Морам да се јавим Драгани» - I have to get in touch with Dragana. Impf. - јављати.

examples.en: Let me know when you arrive.

examples.sr: Звао сам те, што се ниси [ја̏вио]?
examples.en: I called you, why didn't you answer?

note: јавити се - to pick up the phone; to get in touch

tips: With a number «скоро» means «almost»: «скоро 50 година». Age is expressed with «имати»: «имам скоро 50 година», not «ја сам 50».

examples.en: I'm almost ready.
I saw him recently.

note: скоро - usually «almost» or «recently»

examples.en: I sent you a message.
Leave a message after the tone.
Put down your weapon!
He doesn't have a license for the weapon.
I leave the house at eight.
They've been dating for a year.
Sit down, please.
I sit at the computer all day.

note: седи! - «sit down!» or «sit!»

examples.en: My boss is very strict.
I need to ask the boss.
We have to fight.
He fought for his rights.
Come back!
We're going back home.
I left my keys somewhere.
Let's go out somewhere.

tips: Also «crooked» (крива линија). «Крив сам» - I'm to blame, «Ко је крив?» - who is to blame?

examples.en: It's not your fault.
The picture on the wall is crooked.
The fire destroyed the house.
You ruined my life!

tips: The word also means «constipation» in medical contexts: «Имам затвор».
Useful phrases: лежати у затвору - to be in prison, одлежати робију - to serve a sentence, пустити из затвора - to release from prison, побећи из затвора - to escape from prison.

examples.en: He ended up in prison.
They let him out of prison.

tips: «Такође» - also, too: «волим кафу, такође и чај». Do not confuse it with «исто» (the same) and «слично» (similar).
In everyday speech «и» is more common: «И ја.» «Доћи ћемо и следеће године.» «Такође» sounds more bookish and is rare in conversation.

examples.en: Me too.
He also works here.

tips: Of a child, «жив» means lively, active, not only «alive».

examples.en: Thank God he's alive!
I like live music.
I wasn't expecting you.
What do you expect from me?
I've just arrived.
We won't see each other until Monday.

note: «тек» of time: тек сада - only now, not before

examples.en: I decided to stay.
You decide.

tips: «Постеља» - bedding, bed linen; «пресвући постељу» - to change the sheets. Кревет is the bed itself.

examples.en: It's time for bed.
I lie in bed all day.
Close the door!
The store closed at eight.
It's simply impossible.
Explain it to me simply.
Try this cake!
Can I try on these pants?
He sat between us.
There's nothing between us.

note: Takes the genitive: између нас

examples.en: I don't understand at all.
Were you even listening to me?

tips: Set phrases: пун месец - full moon, пун пара - flush with money, пун пунцат - chock-full. «Пуно» means «a lot» and also works as an intensifier, «very».

examples.en: The glass is full.
The bus was full of people.

note: пун + gen.: пун људи

examples.en: I have a meeting at ten.
This is our first date.
That's a stupid question.
I'm not stupid!

tips: Set phrases: «бацити се на нешто» - to throw oneself into something, «бацити удицу» - to cast a fishing line, «бацити се некоме под ноге» - to throw oneself at someone's feet.

examples.en: Throw that in the trash.
He threw the ball over the fence.
The police stopped me.
We have to stop him.

related.en: to stop, to come to a halt

examples.en: The police uncovered the truth.
Who discovered America?

tips: The noun «лак» (m., gen. лака) means varnish, polish: «лак за нокте» - nail polish, «лак за косу» - hairspray, «лак за дрво» - wood varnish. It differs from the adjective in gender and declension.

examples.en: This bag is light.
The exam was easy.
You saved my life.
The doctors managed to save him.
I have good news.
I watch the news on TV.

note: Feminine; «вести» is also the news (broadcast)

examples.en: My parents live in Niš.
Every parent worries about their children.
Leave me alone!
We all want peace.

tips: «Ускоро» means soon (in the future), while «скоро» means «almost» or «recently»: «Скоро сам стигао» - I arrived recently.

examples.en: See you soon.
Winter is almost here.
The police are investigating the murder.
He was charged with murder.

tips: «Беба» is a baby up to a year old, «новорођенче» a newborn (up to 40 days); «малишан», «клинац» - a little kid, «клинци» - kids.

examples.en: The baby is asleep, keep it down.
They had a baby.

tips: It means not only «done» but also «almost»: «готово два сата» - almost two hours, «готово цео дан» - almost all day. Often with a hint of exaggeration.
«Готово!» - There, it's done. «Готово?» - Is that all? «Није готово» - not finished yet.
More «almost»: «готово никад не излазимо заједно» - we almost never go out together, «то је готово бесплатно» - it's almost free. Related: «готов сам» - I'm done for.

examples.en: I've almost finished.
It's all over.
She's a real lady.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome!
You're completely right.
I forgot completely.
Everything is possible.

examples.sr: Да ли је [мо̏гӯће] да је то истина?
examples.en: Is it possible that it's true?
I lived in Belgrade then.
We haven't seen each other since then.

note: од тада - since then

tips: «Не смем да једем шећер» - I'm not allowed to eat sugar (e.g. on doctor's orders), while «не могу да једем» - I can't eat (physically, or it doesn't work out).

examples.en: Smoking is not allowed here.
May I come in?

note: не сме - must not, is not allowed

examples.en: Calm down!
I tried to calm her down.

note: смирити се - to calm down

examples.en: Do you want something to drink?
We're going for a drink after work.
That sounds good.
You sound tired.
You have no evidence.

examples.sr: Ово је [до̏ка̄з] да је био ту.
examples.en: This is proof that he was here.
He always gives me good advice.
What's on TV?

note: «шта дају?» - what's on?

examples.en: We walked toward the river.
He turned toward me.

note: To a person use «код»: идем код лекара

examples.en: He's constantly late.
I think about you all the time.
Wait for me here.
Can you wait a minute?

tips: More than «to fall»: пасти на испиту - to fail an exam, пасти на памет - to come to mind, пасти у очи - to catch the eye, «плата ми је пала» - my pay has come in.
Colloquial: «пасти на нешто» - to fall for something, «пао је» - he got caught by the police, «пасти у несвест» - to faint.

examples.en: I fell off my bike.
Be careful not to fall.

note: пасти на испиту - to fail an exam

examples.en: What are you drinking?
I don't drink alcohol.
Sometimes I go to the movies.
Sometimes I miss you.

tips: «У улици» is used of a specific street («живим у улици Иве Андрића»), «на улици» means in the open air, outside (close to «напољу»).

examples.en: I live on this street.
Cross the street carefully.

note: «у улици» - on a given street (address); «на улици» - outside

examples.en: Put the gun down!
He had a pistol in his pocket.

tips: «Слатка вода» is plain still water, «кисела вода» is sparkling or mineral water. Not «sweet» and not «sour».

examples.en: A glass of water, please.
The water in the sea is warm.
He'll probably come.
You'd know better, I suppose.

note: Colloquial; expresses an assumption

tips: People answer the phone with «Хало!» or «Молим!». If you are the caller, greet after «Хало» and say who you are: «Добар дан, Марија је на телефону» - good day, this is Marija.

examples.en: Hello, who is this?
Hello, can you hear me?
He was like a brother to me.
I like cities like Vienna.

tips: Takes the genitive: «плашити се мрака». Without «се» it means to scare: «плашити дете». A synonym is «бојати се».
Other reflexive verbs that take the genitive: «сећати се дана» (to remember the day), «стидети се грешке» (to be ashamed of a mistake), «чувати се ватре» (to beware of fire).
forms: плашим се, плаше се; pf. уплашити се

examples.en: I'm afraid of the dark.
Don't scare me like that!

note: плашити се + gen.; without се - to scare

examples.en: Really? I don't believe it.
You have to take it seriously.
I thought you were sick.
Who would have thought!
What's going on here?
Things like that happen.
Do you understand what I'm saying?
Now I understand why she left.
That's strange.
Why are you looking at me so strangely?
He pulled a wallet out of his pocket.
You won't get away with it this time.

note: извући се - to wriggle out of it

examples.en: This is the main street.
Who's in charge here?

tips: Чувати - to keep, protect, guard, look after (a child, a sick person): «Чувај се!» - take care, «пас чува кућу» - the dog guards the house. Past «чувао сам» - not to be confused with «чуо сам» (I heard).
Also to babysit: «хвала што нам чуваш дете» - thanks for looking after our child; «чувати стоку» - to keep livestock.

examples.en: Take care of yourself!
Grandma looks after the children.

note: «чувај се!» - take care!

tips: «Ужина» is a light snack, e.g. in the afternoon: «ужинати» means to have a snack, not dinner.

examples.en: What's for dinner?
He invited me to dinner.
I suppose you're hungry.
Where do you suppose he is?

tips: Not only physical: «повредио си је» - you hurt her. It is also said of feelings: «повредити некога» - to hurt, offend someone.

examples.en: I hurt my leg.
I didn't mean to hurt you.

tips: Three senses: opportunity, chance; occasion, pretext; circumstances and conditions (економске прилике, plural). «Одлична прилика да скијамо» - a great occasion to go skiing.
«Стицај прилика» - a coincidence of circumstances; «прилике» in the plural - circumstances, conditions.

examples.en: This is a good opportunity.
Take the chance!

tips: «Кола» is a neuter plural: «Нова кола су лепа», «Где су ми кола?»; the singular is «ауто» (m.). There is also «кола» (f. sg.) - cola: «Ова кола је хладна».
Not «wheels»: a wheel is «точак», pl. точкови. Also «спаваћа кола» - sleeping car, «Велика кола» - the Big Dipper.

examples.en: Whose car is this?
I drive to work.

note: «кола» (pl.) - car; «коло» - round dance, wheel

tips: The plural «избори» means elections (plural only): «Избори су заказани за јесен» - the elections are scheduled for the fall.

examples.en: I have no choice.
Who will win the elections?

tips: The structure is reversed: the person missed is the subject (nominative), the one who misses is in the dative: «недостајеш ми» - I miss you, «недостајем ти» - you miss me. Colloquially also «фалиш ми».
meanings: to be missing, to be lacking

examples.en: I miss you.
We're short of money.

note: недостајеш ми - I miss you

examples.en: Is that clear?
I can't see clearly without glasses.
Our team won.
Who will win the elections?
My father is in the hospital.
They took him to the hospital.
Don't shoot!
Someone is shooting at us!
Come with me.
In the morning we set off on a trip.
He quit his job.
We have to leave the building.

tips: Поред = 1) next to, 2) in addition to (поред тога - besides that), 3) compared to (поред њега изгледаш као џин - next to him you look like a giant), 4) despite (поред свега труда - despite all the effort). Always with the genitive.

examples.en: Sit next to me.
The store is next to the post office.

tips: «Никакав» declines like an adjective («никакву идеју», «никаквог разлога») and goes with a negation: «немам никакву идеју» - I don't have any idea.

examples.en: I don't have any plan.
There's no difference.
He was quite tired.
The restaurant is fairly expensive.
I'm waiting for you in front of the house.
A long road lies ahead of us.
Run!
Why are you running away from me?

note: бежати - to run away; plain «to run» is трчати

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
This is some kind of game.

note: нека врста - a kind of, sort of

examples.en: I keep losing my keys.
Don't waste your time on him.

tips: «Решити се» + genitive without a preposition: to get rid of something («Решио сам се ненужних ствари»). «Решити се да» + present: to make up one's mind: «Решио се да оде».

examples.en: We have to solve this problem.
I decided to stay at home.

tips: Takes the dative, with no preposition: «смејемо се његовој шали» - we laugh at his joke.
«Осмехнути се» - to smile. «Шта се смејеш?» - what are you laughing at? «Није смешно» - it's not funny. «Смејем се, а плакао бих» - I laugh, but I feel like crying.
forms: смејем се, смеју се; pf. насмејати се

examples.en: Why are you laughing?
Everyone laughed at his joke.

note: смејати се + dat. - to laugh at

examples.en: Have you ever been to Paris?

examples.sr: Ово је најбоља пица коју сам [и̏када] јео.
examples.en: This is the best pizza I've ever eaten.
I rented an apartment downtown.

examples.sr: Наш [ста̑н] има три собе и терасу.
examples.en: Our apartment has three rooms and a terrace.
The king lived in a large palace.
He acts as if he were a king.
Where are those damn keys of yours?
They say this house is cursed.

tips: Not just «slowly» but a way of life: calmly, without rushing. «Полако!» - take it easy, don't rush.

examples.en: Drive slowly, the road is slippery.
Take it easy, we have plenty of time.

note: «Полако!» - easy, no rush

examples.en: My brother is strong as a bull.
