This coffee is too strong.
I live near the school.
The store is very close.
I wrote her a long letter.
Can you write down the address for me?
That boy is my nephew.

examples.sr: Кад сам био [дѐча̄к], живео сам на селу.
examples.en: When I was a boy, I lived in the country.
Where are you from?
I don't know where he came from.
I've never seen a car like this.
I don't like weather like this.
A police officer stopped us on the road.
My brother is a police officer.
The victim was taken to the hospital right away.

examples.sr: Родитељи су поднели велику [жр̑тву] за нас.
examples.en: Our parents made a great sacrifice for us.

tips: With «са» + instrumental it means «to get along»: «Да ли се добро слажете у породици?». Without a preposition - «to agree».
forms: слажем се, слажу се; pf. сложити се

examples.en: I completely agree with you.
My brother and I get along well.

note: Not to be confused with «слагати» (pf. of «лагати») - to lie

forms: украдем, украду; past украо; impf. красти

examples.en: Someone stole my wallet.
Thieves stole a car in front of the building.
He's out of town this week.
The situation is completely out of control.

examples.sr: У суботу идемо на [за̀баву] код Марка.
examples.en: On Saturday we're going to a party at Marko's.
Children love fun and games.

tips: Also a hundredth part of a dinar, like a cent: «99 динара и 99 пара». The coins are long gone, but the word appears in prices. Singular пара - small change, plural паре - money. Synonym: «новац».
The plural «паре» is colloquial but not slang: «пун пара» (rich), «тврд на пари» (stingy), «ни пребијене паре» (not a penny).

examples.en: I don't have the money for a new phone.
Steam is coming out of the pot.

note: паре - money (colloq.)

tips: «Паметан» also means knowing about something: «нисам паметан» - I can't make sense of it, «имам паметнија посла» - I have better things to do.

examples.en: She's a very smart girl.
That wasn't very smart.
The film starts at eight.
Every day I start with coffee.
The attack took place late at night.
He had a panic attack on the plane.
I have no idea where he is.
Freedom is a very broad concept.

note: «немам појма» - I have no idea

examples.en: Can you explain this to me?
I explained everything to her from the beginning.
This is my last attempt.
Sit in the back seat.
This suitcase is too heavy.
We had a hard day.
Last night we were at the movies.
Where were you last night?

note: one word for «yesterday evening»

examples.en: Keep the change.
The police detained him at the border.
That was a big mistake.
Sorry, my mistake.
The city has almost a million inhabitants.
Thanks a million!

forms: појавим се, појаве се; impf. појављивати се

examples.en: He suddenly appeared in the doorway.
She didn't show up for work.

forms: проведем, проведу; past провео; impf. проводити
meanings: to lead through, to show around

examples.en: We spent the summer at the seaside.

examples.sr: Желим да [про̀ведем] више времена с децом.
examples.en: I want to spend more time with the kids.
Stop that right now!
She broke up with her boyfriend.

note: прекинути с неким - to break up with someone

examples.en: We spent a wonderful day at the lake.
She's a wonderful person.

note: An adjective, not a piece of furniture

examples.en: Yes, what would you like?
Here you go, this is for you.

note: «изволите» - polite «here you are» or «may I help you?»

examples.sr: Хтео сам да дођем, [но̑] нисам могао.
examples.en: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
The house is small but comfortable.

note: Bookish; in speech «али» is more common

examples.en: Can you keep a secret?
That's our little secret.

examples.sr: Кажу да у тој кући живи [ду̏х].
examples.en: They say a ghost lives in that house.
There's a good spirit in our team.

tips: «Важи!» - deal. «Ма важи» - ironic: yeah, sure. The basic meaning is to be valid («лична карта важи до...»); «важити за» - to be regarded as something.
In conversation: «Видимо се у пет? - Важи.» Literally «it holds». «Важи за све» - it applies to everyone, «важи до петка» - valid until Friday.

examples.en: Deal, see you at eight!
This ticket is valid for a month.

note: colloq. «Важи!» - deal, okay

tips: Takes «у» + locative, and the preposition is required: «Уживам у музици», «Уживајте у овом граду!», «уживам у лепом времену, у спорту».

examples.en: Enjoy your vacation!
I'm really enjoying this music.

note: уживати у + loc. - to enjoy

tips: Many figurative uses: црно вино - red wine, црни лук - onion, црни петак - Black Friday (a sale) or a bad day, црне бриге - heavy worries. «Какав црни...!» - what on earth...!

examples.en: She bought a black dress for the celebration.
Our cat is completely black.

related.en: to turn black; to get tanned

examples.en: Anyone can make a mistake.
This music isn't for everyone.

note: свако - everyone (people); сваки - each + noun

examples.en: In the evening I like to read in bed.
I've read that book twice.
Are you free tomorrow evening?
Is this seat free?
He hit me for no reason.
I banged my head on the door.
Damn, I'm late again!
Go to hell with your advice!

note: colloq., a bit rude

examples.en: Let me know as soon as you arrive.
As soon as he walked in, everyone went quiet.
This is only the beginning.
Let's start from the beginning.

tips: Also «водити рачуна» - to be careful, to take into account: «Води рачуна!» - be careful, take care.
It means both a bill and a receipt; a current account is «жиро-рачун». A payment slip is «уплатница», a receipt for payment is «признаница».
«Отворити рачун» - to open a bank account. The score of a match is «резултат», not «рачун».

examples.en: Waiter, the check, please!
I transferred the money to your account.

note: водити рачуна о + loc. - to take care of, to look after

examples.en: Hurry up, the train is leaving!

examples.sr: Морамо да [по̀журимо] ако хоћемо да стигнемо.
examples.en: We have to hurry if we want to make it.
Wake me up at seven, please.
I woke up very early this morning.
Go straight ahead.
Sit in front next to me.
He works as a real estate agent.
The secret agent followed the suspect.
I'm still waiting for an answer from them.
Do you know the answer to this question?
I have no more strength for this.
The wind blew with great force.
She has a sharp mind.
What's on your mind?

note: имати на уму - to keep in mind

tips: Of a person it means a fool: «Не буди коњ, размисли мало». Vocative - «коњу».

examples.en: My grandfather had two horses.
She learned to ride a horse.
That's not funny at all.
You look funny in that hat.

tips: «Напоље» is a direction, «out, outside» («изаћи напоље» - to go out); «напољу» is a place, «outdoors, outside the house».

examples.en: Get out!

examples.sr: Деца су истрчала [на̏поље] да се играју.
examples.en: The kids ran outside to play.

note: напоље - motion (out); напољу - location (outside)

examples.en: Our plane takes off at six.
We flew to London.

tips: «Скинути» - to take off (clothes, shoes, glasses) and to undress someone: «скини дете»; «скини се» - to get undressed. Imperfective - «скидати».
Also: to download («скинути песму са интернета»), to cross off a list («скинути са листе»), to copy someone's voice or manner. Context decides.

examples.en: Take off your coat and sit down.
I downloaded the new app.
This is my favorite song.
She memorized the poem.

examples.sr: Да ли вам [сме̏та] ако отворим прозор?
examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
Music distracts me while I work.

note: + dat.: смета ми - it bothers me

examples.en: The police are still looking for the killer.
The killer escaped through the window.

note: Masculine, but declined like words in -а

tips: Almost always in set phrases: «без обзира на» (regardless of), «с обзиром на» (considering), «узети у обзир» (to take into account), «не долази у обзир» (out of the question), «имати обзира» (to show consideration for someone).

examples.sr: С [о̏бзиром] на кишу, остали смо код куће.
examples.en: In view of the rain, we stayed home.

examples.sr: Ни под којим [о̏бзиром] не отварај врата.
examples.en: Under no circumstances open the door.

note: с обзиром на - considering; без обзира на - regardless of

examples.en: That's against the law.

examples.sr: Нови [за́кон] ступа на снагу у јануару.
examples.en: The new law comes into force in January.
The cat is sleeping under the table.
The temperature fell below zero.

note: испод + gen.: испод стола

examples.en: Give me a little time to think.
Think carefully before you decide.
They have a son and two daughters.
My daughter is in first grade.
She has a very beautiful voice.
Don't raise your voice at me!
We'll manage somehow.
You look kind of sad today.
Where did I leave my keys?
Persistence is the key to success.
Guess who's here!
The bullet hit him in the leg.

tips: «Карта» - any ticket (plane, bus, match, concert): «Имам две карте». An admission ticket specifically is «улазница».
Besides a ticket, «карта» is also a map and a playing card. For a concert or theater ticket «улазница» is more common, though «позоришна карта» is also said.

examples.en: I bought two tickets for the concert.
Look at the map to see where we are.
Last year we were in Greece.
We saw each other last weekend.

tips: In military and official contexts «позив» is a summons, a call-up («позив за војску»); in everyday speech it is more often a call or an invitation.

examples.en: You have one missed call.
Thanks for the invitation!

examples.sr: Имам лош [о̏сећа̄ј] у вези с тим.
examples.en: I have a bad feeling about it.
He lost feeling in his fingers.

tips: «Готова ствар» - a done deal, the matter is settled. «Готова јела» - ready meals (from a shop). «Готов новац» - cash.

examples.en: Lunch is ready!
If they catch us, we're done for.

tips: Also «after» («пошто је завршио»), «since, seeing that» («пошто тако кажеш») and, colloquially, «how much»: «Пошто су јабуке?» - «По сто педесет динара кило» (150 dinars a kilo).
For «why» use «зашто» (colloquially «што»), not «пошто».

examples.en: Since it's raining, we'll stay home.
How much are the apples?

note: «Пошто је ово?» - how much is this?

tips: «Познат по» + locative - known for something: «Србија је позната по специјалитетима», «Нови Сад је познат по фестивалу».

examples.en: He's a famous actor.
This face looks familiar to me.

examples.sr: Синоћ сам изашао са [дру̏штвом] у град.
examples.en: Last night I went out on the town with friends.
We live in a modern society.
It was a hard struggle.
His fight against the illness has lasted for years.

tips: Broader than «to be friends»: to socialize, to spend time together («дружим се са породицом»), also to be on good terms with something («дружити се са природом», «са телефоном»).

examples.en: I like to socialize with my colleagues.
Who do you hang out with at school?
Don't come in without knocking!
The guests come in through the main entrance.
I got a letter from my grandmother.
Cyrillic is the Serbian script.
Choose what you want.
They elected him president of the club.
Imagine you're on the beach.

examples.sr: Не могу да [за̀мислим] живот без тебе.
examples.en: I can't imagine life without you.
I'm waiting for you in front of the building.
The car is parked in front of the house.
Put the gun down!
He put the suitcase down on the floor.
She has long blond hair.

examples.sr: Био је то [ду̏г] и тежак дан.
examples.en: It was a long, hard day.

note: As a noun, «дуг» means debt

tips: The imperfective of «помоћи»: помажем, imperative «помагај!»: «Нико ми не помаже» - nobody helps me, «нико ти није помагао» - nobody helped you.

examples.en: He always helps the neighbors.
I help Mom in the kitchen.
Where is the post office?
He always finds some excuse.

tips: «Дивна» also fits a person's character: «ти си дивна особа» - you're a wonderful person. For looks, «прелепа жена» (a beautiful woman) is stronger.

examples.en: You look wonderful tonight!
We had a wonderful time at the seaside.
Only you understand me.
I work every day, except Sundays.
To err is human.
That's human nature.
He disappeared without a trace.
The police found traces of blood.
He still hasn't replied to my message.
Answer me honestly.
Good evening, may I help you?
We spent a lovely evening together.

note: Neuter: «добро вече»; «вечера» is dinner

examples.en: Many people work on weekends too.
He has visited many countries.

tips: «Иако» introduces a concession: «Иако је касно, идемо». Not to be confused with «као» (like, as).

examples.sr: [И̏ако] је болестан, дошао је на посао.
examples.en: Although he is sick, he came to work.
We went out even though it was raining.
The situation is under control.
I found myself in an awkward situation.

tips: «Контрола» is feminine: «строга контрола».
«Имати контролу над» + instrumental: «над ситуацијом», «над емоцијама».

examples.en: Don't worry, everything is under control.
The driver lost control of the vehicle.
The brain uses a lot of energy.
Use your brain a little!

meanings: to set off, to start moving

examples.en: We set off early tomorrow morning.
The Earth moves around the Sun.
I need a little more information.

examples.sr: Где могу да добијем [информа̀ције] о возовима?
examples.en: Where can I get information about the trains?
We sold the old car.
Will you sell me your bike?
I'm interested in history.
That doesn't interest me at all.

note: занима ме - I'm interested (literally, it interests me)

examples.en: Did you get my message?
He was accepted to the university.
Let's have a coffee.
Last night I drank too much beer.

tips: Colloquially also a traffic light: «код другог светла скрените лево» - turn left at the second light (more often «семафор»).

examples.en: Turn off the light, please.
Wait for the green light.

note: «светло» - light; «свет» - world

examples.en: She accepted his invitation to dinner.
We have to accept the truth.

tips: Usually singular: «Коса ми је дуга» - my hair is long. The same word also means a scythe.

examples.en: She has long black hair.
How often do you wash your hair?

note: коса (sg.) - hair on the head

tips: «Кафа» is feminine: «јака кафа», «моја кафа», «добра кафа».
When ordering, «Може кафа?» has the coffee in the nominative (not «кафу»). The accusative «кафу» is needed after «молим» and «желим».

examples.en: Would you like a coffee?
Let's go for coffee after work.

note: Feminine: «једна кафа»; «кафић» - a café

examples.en: The president gave a speech.
He was elected president of the club.
We traveled in a large group.
What's your favorite band?
I'm just kidding, don't be mad!
You must be joking?

forms: pl. будале; of a man: тај будала

examples.en: Don't act like a fool!
What a fool I am!

note: Of a man it takes masculine agreement: «тај будала»

examples.en: That makes no sense.
He has an excellent sense of humor.
We had a long conversation.
This is a private conversation.
Can I ask one question?
Mom set the table for dinner.

note: поставити сто - to set the table

examples.en: Wait a second!
The race lasted ten seconds.
Turn around so I can look at you.

examples.sr: [О̀кренуо] сам број, али се нико не јавља.
examples.en: I dialed the number, but nobody answers.
My grandfather was a soldier.
The soldiers guarded the bridge.
The Serbian people love music.
A lot of people came to the concert.
Behave politely!
Why are you behaving like that?

tips: The 3rd person plural is «боле», not «болу»: «боли ме, боле ме ноге». «Болу» sounds childish.
«Боли ме глава/нога/леђа/грло/стомак»; «Боли ме уво за њих» - I couldn't care less about them.
meanings: to hurt, to ache (a body part)

examples.en: My head hurts.
Where does it hurt?

note: the person is in acc.: боли ме глава - my head hurts

tips: The perfective verb means remembering at a particular moment («сетио сам се њеног имена»). Its imperfective pair «сећати се» means to remember in general («сећам се детињства»).
To remember someone or something takes the genitive without a preposition: сетила сам се лепих тренутака. «Подсетити некога на + acc.» means to remind: подсети ме на договор.
forms: сетим се, сете се; impf. сећати се

examples.sr: Не могу да се [се̏тим] његовог имена.
examples.en: I can't remember his name.
I remembered that I had a meeting.

note: + gen.: сетити се нечега

examples.en: This costs two thousand dinars.
Thank you a thousand times!
The car is in excellent condition.
His condition is stable.

note: бити у стању - to be able to

examples.en: That's not important now.
This is an important decision for us.
The boss is in his office.
Our office is in the city center.
You promised you would come!
Promise me you'll be careful.
The banking system has crashed.
We have to change the way we work.
Thank you for your attention.
Pay attention to the signs.

related.en: to watch out, to look after

examples.en: People don't talk about sex in front of children.

examples.sr: У филму има превише [се̏кса] и насиља.
examples.en: There is too much sex and violence in the film.
He got into serious trouble.
A friend in need is a friend indeed.
Don't take my things without asking.
I take my medication twice a day.
Have you read that book?
Read the contract carefully.
I felt a sharp pain in my back.

examples.sr: [О̀сетила] сам да нешто није у реду.
examples.en: I sensed that something was wrong.

tips: A broad verb: to learn something, to teach someone (учим странце српском), to study. For years of schooling use школовати се, for university studies - студирати.
Prefixes: научити - to learn thoroughly, подучити - to teach a little, изучити - to study in depth, обучити - to train in a skill, учити се - to learn something by effort («учим се стрпљењу»).
No «се» is needed to say «I'm learning»: Учим српски.

examples.en: I've been learning Serbian for a year.
Mom taught me how to cook.

note: учити means both to learn and to teach

tips: The state of being married: «удата» (a woman only), «ожењен» (a man only): «она је удата», «он је ожењен».
To marry someone: за + acc.: «Удала сам се за Милоша». The state: «удата сам», «у браку сам».
forms: удам се, удају се; impf. удавати се

examples.en: My sister got married last year.
She wants to marry him.

note: of a woman: удати се за + acc.; of a man - оженити се

examples.en: He's a bit strange.
At night we heard a strange sound.
I drink tea instead of coffee.
You go instead of me.

forms: сретнем, сретну; past срео; impf. сретати

examples.en: I ran into him in town by chance.

examples.sr: Драго ми је што смо се [сре̏ли].
examples.en: I'm glad we met.

tips: «Услужно» does not mean free of charge, but offered as a (paid) service: услужно печење - they roast the meat or fish you bought, услужно пеглање веша - ironing laundry as a service. «Самоуслужна» means self-service.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми учиниш једну [у̏слугу]?
examples.en: Can you do me a favor?
The service in this restaurant is excellent.
The sky is full of stars tonight.
She is a big movie star.
That's a good sign.
Give me a sign when you're ready.

tips: «Ето» is not only «there»: it also means «well, I told you so» («Ето видиш...») and a hesitant «well»: «- Како си? - Ето, добро.» «Ево» is used when handing something over, «ето» when it is near the listener, «ено» when it is far away.

examples.en: There, everything is done.
See, I wasn't lying.

note: ево - here (near me), ето - there (near you), ено - over there

examples.en: His work is highly valued.
I'm writing a term paper on history.

note: рад (adj.) means glad: рад сам да помогнем

forms: побринем се, побрину се; impf. бринути се
meanings: to take care of, to see to

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll take care of everything.
Who will take care of the dog?

note: побринути се за + acc. - to take care of someone or something

forms: поједем, поједу; past појео; impf. јести

examples.en: Who ate my chocolate?
Eat everything on your plate.
That was a difficult decision.
I've made the final decision.

note: донети одлуку - to make a decision

forms: родим, роде; part. рођен; impf. рађати

examples.en: I was born in Novi Sad.
She gave birth to a healthy baby girl.

note: «рођен сам» - I was born

examples.en: I often go for a walk along the river.
How often do you work out?
The sun is very hot today.
We sat in the sun all afternoon.
It's a pity you didn't come.
The storm did a lot of damage.

note: «Штета!» - What a pity!

examples.en: The kitchen is completely clean now.
I need a bit of fresh air.
My daughter loves animals.
What's your favorite animal?
Where is the bus stop?
They took him to the police station.
You've finally arrived!
The question has been settled once and for all.

tips: Of a person or a child it means cute, adorable: «какво слатко дете».

examples.en: This cake is too sweet.
What a cute puppy!
My brother is in the army.
The army entered the city.
I think it's a mistake.
Everyone considers him a hero.
He admitted that he had lied.
Admit that you like her!
We stayed at a hotel near the beach.
I booked a hotel for the weekend.
I usually get up at seven.
What do you usually do on weekends?
I won't say anything without a lawyer.
My lawyer will call you.
We lit a fire on the beach.
Don't play with fire!
Oh, you scared me!

examples.sr: Немој да се [у̀плашиш], то је само пас.
examples.en: Don't be scared, it's just a dog.
Do you speak English?
I love English literature.

note: говорити енглески - to speak English

examples.sr: [Већѝна] људи ради од девет до пет.
examples.en: Most people work from nine to five.
In most cases that's true.
Hang the picture on the wall.
This wall needs to be whitewashed.
I'm staying home tonight.
How long are you staying in Belgrade?
Nobody knows what the future will bring.
In the future I'll be more careful.
You're late again!
The train is half an hour late.

tips: «Дом» is the place where a person lives and feels at home (Овде ми је дом). A building is called «кућа». Also «Дом здравља» - a health center.

examples.en: This is your home now.
I live in a student dormitory.

note: a building is usually кућа; дом здравља - health center

tips: It can also mean a bow: «поклонити се» - to bow. «Поклон-бон» is a gift voucher.

examples.en: I bought her a gift for her birthday.
Thank you for the gift!
That's an excellent idea!
He is an excellent student.

tips: «Избацити» means to throw out garbage (смеће) or to expel someone from a club. Of an ATM: «избацио је картицу» (spat out the card) and «није ми избацио паре» (did not give me my money). Imperfective - избацивати.

examples.en: He was thrown out of the club.
Throw out that old junk.
It's obvious that he's lying.
He obviously doesn't know what he's doing.

forms: нападнем, нападну; past напао; impf. нападати

examples.en: The dog attacked a child in the park.
We were attacked from an ambush.
I see it differently.
Everything is different now.
She put on a red dress.
The driver went through a red light.
I won't let anyone hurt you.
Allow me to introduce myself.
Sorry, I'm busy right now.
This seat is taken.
They've been married for twenty years.
Their marriage wasn't happy.
He has nothing to do with drugs.
The police found drugs in the car.
What is the price of this jacket?
Prices have gone up again.
We live in a new apartment building.
That building has twenty floors.
Are you taking any medicine?
This is the best remedy for a cold.

note: лекар - doctor

tips: «Девојчица» is a little girl, usually a daughter: «Како је твоја девојчица?» asks about a child. A girlfriend is «девојка».

examples.en: They have a little girl.
The girl is playing in the yard.

tips: With «се» it means to surrender (предати се непријатељу); without it, to hand over or hand in (предао је домаћи).
meanings: to hand over, to pass on

examples.en: Hand this letter to the director.
Never give up!

tips: Besides «to answer»: «одговарати некоме» (dat.) means to suit («термин ми одговара»); «одговарати за» + acc. - to be responsible for one's actions; «одговарати стварности» - to correspond to reality.
It also means to bear responsibility («одговарам за своје дете») and to fit in size or convenience («не одговара ми овај прслук», «одговара ми термин»).
In a shop: «Одговара ми величина» - the size fits me; «Не одговара ми величина» - it does not; «Да ли имате већи/мањи број?» - do you have a bigger/smaller size?; «другу боју?» - another color?

examples.en: Why don't you answer the phone?
Does five o'clock suit you?

note: одговара ми - it suits me

examples.en: This stays between us.
He sat among friends.

tips: An attempt on someone's life is «атентат» («покушај убиства» also works).

examples.en: He succeeded on the first attempt.
This is my last attempt.
Smile for the camera!
The cameras filmed the thief.

tips: Names of the fingers: палац - thumb, кажипрст - index finger, средњи прст - middle finger, домали прст - ring finger, мали прст - little finger. On the foot, the second toe is «други прст» or «прст до палца».
forms: gen. прста; pl. прсти; gen. pl. прстију

examples.en: I cut my finger with a knife.
Don't point your finger at people!
I bet he'll be late again.

examples.sr: Колико си се [кла̏дио] на ту утакмицу?
examples.en: How much did you bet on that match?

tips: In youth slang «риба» is also a girl, usually an attractive one. Be careful: the tone can sound rude.
In youth slang «рибе» means girls: «гледају га рибе» - the girls are checking him out (not fish!).
Slang: «риба, рибица, рибетина» - a girl (not necessarily a beauty). Of a real beauty: «риба је као авион» - she's a stunner.

examples.en: On Fridays we usually eat fish.
My dad likes to go fishing.

note: slang: риба - an attractive girl

examples.en: See you in court!
Who will wash the dishes?

note: судови means both courts and dishes

examples.sr: Данас не идем на посао, [бо̏лестан] сам.
examples.en: I'm not going to work today, I'm sick.
She takes care of her sick mother.
We went to a club last night.
I support a football club from Belgrade.
Don't be an idiot!
I behaved like an idiot.
I promise I'll come back.

examples.sr: Он стално [обѐћава], а ништа не уради.
examples.en: He keeps promising, but never does anything.
I got up very early this morning.
I saw him in the shop this morning.

note: a single word meaning this morning

examples.en: I will love you forever.
He left forever.
Smoking kills.
This heat is killing me.

tips: «Покупити дете из вртића» - to pick up a child from kindergarten. «Покупити нешто» - to pick something up.

examples.en: I'll pick you up in front of the building at eight.
Pick your things up off the floor.
This is a serious problem.
Are you serious?
I barely made the train.
I can't wait for the weekend!

note: једва чекам - I can't wait

tips: «Добити боју» - to get a tan: «Добила си боју!» - you got a tan. A tan (complexion) is «тен», to tan - «препланути», «поцрнети».
«У боји» means in color: фотографија у боји, штампач у боји. The adjective «обојен» means only dyed or painted, not «in color».

examples.en: What's your favorite color?
We bought paint for the walls.

meanings: to use, to make use of

examples.en: Take advantage of this opportunity!
He just used you.

tips: For groups of only men: двојица, тројица, четворица. For children and mixed groups: двоје, троје, четворо, петоро. For only women, ordinary numbers: две девојке.

examples.en: Two men are waiting outside.
I saw two men in front of the building.

note: двојица - for men; двоје - for a mixed group

examples.en: I'm dying of hunger!
The plant is dying without water.
The dog faithfully waits for its master.
He is the master of his fate.
My brother is very tall.
Prices here are too high.
I feel a sharp pain in my chest.
This pill will ease the pain.
Open the window, it's hot.
He looked out the window.
Excuse me, miss, is this yours?
Miss Petrović is our new teacher.
That little guy is a real devil.
Go to the devil!
The operation went well.
He has knee surgery tomorrow.
That's just plain stupidity.
Don't talk nonsense!
He is not my enemy.
The enemy attacked at night.
All the passengers survived the accident.
I won't survive another day like this.

tips: «Леђа» - the back (plural): «Боле ме леђа» - my back hurts. The spine is «кичма»: «зеза ме кичма» - my spine is giving me trouble.
A plural-only word, so the verb is plural too: «боле ме леђа» (my back hurts), not «боли». Like наочаре, панталоне.

examples.en: My back aches from sitting.

examples.sr: Лежао је на [лѐђима] и гледао у небо.
examples.en: He lay on his back looking at the sky.

note: plural only: леђа ме боле

examples.en: Pack warm clothes for the weekend.
I usually buy clothes at the sales.
Why are you crying?
The baby cried all night.
This is especially important.
We'll pay separately, if that's possible.
Did you notice anything strange?
Nobody noticed that I had left.
I'll definitely come to your birthday party.
Can you help me? - Of course!
I spent the rest of the day in bed.
Finish the rest of the pizza.
You look tired today.

examples.sr: Лек почиње да [де̏лује] после пола сата.
examples.en: The medicine starts working after half an hour.

tips: It joins negations: Не зовеш ме нити се дружиш са мном (you neither call me nor hang out with me). The double form: Нити је био Аустријанац, нити је одрастао у Бечу (he was neither Austrian nor did he grow up in Vienna).
«Нити... нити...» means neither... nor...: «нити пијем, нити пушим». The verb takes no extra «не».

examples.en: He neither drinks nor smokes.

examples.sr: Нисам га видео, [ни̏ти] сам чуо за њега.
examples.en: I haven't seen him, nor have I heard of him.

note: нити... нити - neither... nor

examples.en: What are you planning for the weekend?

examples.sr: [Пла̀нирамо] да се преселимо у Нови Сад.
examples.en: We're planning to move to Novi Sad.

tips: «Час» means a lesson («даје часове»), but also a moment: «у згодан час» - at the right time, «за час» - in no time, «у последњем часу» - at the last moment. The conjunction «час... час» means now... now....
«Претчас» is a zero period before classes begin.

examples.en: I have an English class at five.
Wait, I'll be back in a moment.

note: час - lesson, moment; an hour is «сат»

examples.en: Everything went perfectly.
He speaks Serbian perfectly.
She is my best friend.
I went into town with a friend.

examples.sr: Нико те не може [на̀терати] да то урадиш.
examples.en: Nobody can make you do that.

examples.sr: [На̀терао] ме је да чекам сат времена.
examples.en: He made me wait for an hour.
One cold beer, please.
Shall we go for a beer after work?
Tell me what happened.
He told us a funny story.
What kind of music do you like?
I listen to music while I work.

tips: In colloquial speech it is an intensifier meaning very: страшно висок, страшно ми се свиђа. So are ужасно, јако.

examples.en: It was terribly cold.
It's scary in the forest at night.

tips: Not only «otherwise»: a colloquial discourse word meaning «by the way, in general»: «Како сте иначе?» - how are you, in general?, «Иначе, можемо попити пиво» - by the way, we could have a beer.
As an aside it means «actually, by the way»: «Иначе, он је из Ниша.» (By the way, he's from Niš.) Not to be mixed up with «иначе» meaning «or else».

examples.en: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
By the way, where are you from?

tips: Also «to have time to»: «Не стижем све» - I can't get everything done, «Стижеш ли?» - can you make it? To arrive: стићи у град.

examples.en: The train arrives at five.
I can't manage to do everything.

note: «Стижем!» - I'm coming!

examples.en: I need to make a phone call.
I got all my errands done this morning.
What's in that box?
I bought her a box of chocolates.
It was a lot of fun last night.
What's so funny about that?
The police freed the hostages.
Try to get rid of stress.

tips: To marry someone takes the instrumental: «Оженио сам се Јеленом». The common mistake «оженио сам Јелену» means «I got Jelena married (to someone)», as in «кум је оженио сина» (the best man married off his son).
forms: оженим се, ожене се; impf. женити се

examples.en: My brother got married last summer.
Do you want to marry her?

note: of a man: оженити се + instr.; of a woman - удати се

tips: «Част» means honor and respect, and also a treat (hospitality).

examples.en: It's an honor to meet you.
I give you my word of honor.

tips: «Уста» - the mouth, plural only (neuter): у устима, по устима. Not to be confused with «усне» (lips). Expressions about speech and eating: из уста у уста, на сва уста, вода на уста.
Plural in form, but it means one mouth: «отвори уста». «Очи» - eyes (more literary than the plural of «око»).

examples.en: Don't talk with your mouth full!
Open your mouth, please.

note: plural only: уста су

examples.en: He is my business partner.
He lives with his partner in Belgrade.
What's for lunch?

examples.sr: Позвали су нас на [ру́чак] у недељу.
examples.en: They invited us to lunch on Sunday.
He didn't commit that crime.
The crime scene has been cordoned off.

meanings: to get up, to stand up

examples.en: Get up, you're late for school!
I got up at five this morning.

examples.sr: Бог је [ство̏рио] свет за шест дана.
examples.en: God created the world in six days.
We've created an excellent team.
Who's paying for dinner?
I pay rent every month.
This is already his third book.

examples.sr: Ово ти је [тре̏ћӣ] пут да касниш.
examples.en: This is the third time you're late.
She hired a private detective.
The detective examined the crime scene.
That's my ex-boyfriend.
I met my ex-wife on the street.
I completely forgot about the meeting.
That's perfectly normal.

forms: повучем, повуку; past повукао; impf. повлачити

examples.en: Pull the door, don't push!
The army withdrew from the city.
People don't change.
Where can I exchange money?
I work at the seaside during the summer.
He called you during the meeting.
She wore a long white dress.
A glass of white wine, please.

note: m. бео, but f. бела: бео хлеб, бела кућа

tips: «Обући» means to put on clothes or to dress a child: обучем, обуче, обуку (they); обукао сам дукс; «обући се» - to get dressed. For shoes use «обути».
One verb covers both putting on and dressing: обуци капут! (put on a coat), обукао сам, обући се - to get dressed. For shoes: обути: обуј ципеле! (past обуо сам).
forms: обучем, обуку; past обукао; impf. облачити

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
She got dressed quickly and went out.
We once lived in Niš.
Sometimes I miss my old job.
Nobody is perfect.
This is a perfect day for the beach.

tips: «Бака» is affectionate, «баба» neutral, «бабетина» disrespectful.

examples.en: On weekends we go to Grandma's.
My grandma makes the best cakes.

tips: Годишњи одмор - annual leave; распуст - school holidays; «лепо се проведите!» and «уживајте на одмору!» - wishes to someone on vacation.
At school: «велики одмор» - the long break (30 minutes), «мали одмор» - a short one, 5 minutes.

examples.en: I need a little rest.
Where are you going on vacation this year?

tips: «Клинац» is a little guy, a kid. Sometimes used sarcastically of young people (a naive kid with his head in the clouds). The plural «клинци» means children: «Где су вам клинци?» - where are your kids?

examples.en: The kids are playing in the yard.
I was still a kid then.

note: colloq.

examples.en: The general issued an order.
His grandfather was a general.
I went to the doctor yesterday.
Where were you yesterday afternoon?
The government passed a new law.
People are protesting against the government.
Honestly, I don't like it.
Tell me honestly what you think.
I get loads of messages every day.

examples.sr: Наш тим увек [добѝја] на домаћем терену.
examples.en: Our team always wins at home.

tips: At the moment, currently: «тренутно радим на пројекту». Not the same as «привремено» - temporarily.

examples.en: I'm not at home at the moment.
The medicine works almost instantly.
This house belongs to my father.
I feel that I belong here.

tips: A serious, solemn farewell; in everyday life people more often say «довиђења» or «ћао».
Farewell with a sense of forever or solemnity. In daily life people say: довиђења, ћао, пријатно.

examples.en: Farewell, we won't see each other again.
She said goodbye to him at the station.

note: a solemn farewell; everyday «bye»: ћао, здраво

examples.en: I study French at school.
I like French cheese.

tips: «Куда» is the standard «where to»; in colloquial speech «где» is often used instead: Куда ћемо на ручак? / Где ћемо на ручак?

examples.en: Where did you set off to?
I don't know where to go.

note: in speech often «где» instead: Где идеш?

examples.en: I'm afraid of heights.
He was trembling with fear.

tips: Mostly used in the 3rd person: «тиче се» + gen.: «Ово се тиче свих» (this concerns everyone). «Што се тиче...» - as for..., «то ме се не тиче» - that doesn't concern me.
meanings: to concern, to have to do with

examples.en: That doesn't concern you.

examples.sr: Што се мене [ти̑че], можеш да идеш.
examples.en: As far as I'm concerned, you can go.

note: што се тиче + gen. - as for, regarding

tips: In an invitation «венчање» can mean a church ceremony, a civil ceremony or the reception. Check the time and place in the invitation; «скуп сватова» - the gathering of the wedding guests.

examples.en: We've been invited to a wedding.
The wedding is on Saturday in the church.
The baby has started to walk.
I like walking in the rain.

note: ходати - to walk; «to go somewhere» is ићи

examples.en: The room has a view of the sea.
At first glance he seemed decent.

tips: «Рупа од стана» - a tiny, shabby flat: a hole rather than a home. «Мишја рупа» - a mouse hole.

examples.en: You have a hole in your sock.
There's a big pothole in the road.
The police arrested the thief.
Arrest that man!
Can you prove it?
He proved that he was not guilty.
I live in the very center of the city.
Are we going downtown tonight?
Enter your personal data.
This data is incorrect.

tips: «Банка» is a bank: «ићи у банку». A glass jar is «тегла», a tin can - «конзерва».
forms: dat. банци; pl. банке; gen. pl. банака

examples.en: My sister works at a bank.
I need to go to the bank.

note: dat./loc. банци: у банци - at the bank

examples.en: They have a huge house in the country.
That's a huge problem.
I'm watching the film with subtitles.
This translation isn't very good.

tips: «Особе са посебним потребама» - people with special needs (with disabilities). «Посебно» also means separately or in particular: «посебно бих хтео да се захвалим» - I would especially like to thank.

examples.en: Today is a special day.
We have a separate room for guests.

tips: From the root «нос» (to carry): однос (relation), ношња (costume), понос (pride), пренос (broadcast), унос (input), износ (amount).

examples.en: We have a very good relationship.
What is your relationship with your parents like?
Serbia is a small country.
The state pays for schools.
It's raining outside.
The kids keep falling off their bikes.

note: пада киша/снег - it's raining/snowing

meanings: to have a chat, to talk

examples.en: Can we talk in private?
Let's talk tomorrow.

tips: Senses: to decline («одбио сам позив»), to reject («одбили су моју пријаву»), to deflect («голман је одбио лопту» - the goalkeeper deflected the ball), to refuse entry («одбили су му улаз»).

examples.en: She turned down his offer.

examples.sr: Ако ти понуде посао, немој да [о̀дбијеш].

This church is five hundred years old.
Which line goes to the center?
Draw a line under the text.

Don't break my heart.
Where is the women's restroom?
This store sells women's clothing.

tips: Of things and ideas it means allowed, appreciated: «Кућни љубимци су добродошли» (pets are welcome), «Савети су добродошли» (advice is welcome). The reply to «Добро дошли!» is «Боље вас нашли!».

examples.en: Welcome to Serbia!
You're always welcome at our place.

note: agrees with the person: добродошао (m.), добродошла (f.), добродошли (pl.)

examples.en: Tonight we're watching an American movie.
He has American citizenship.

tips: «Славити рођендан» - to celebrate a birthday, «Колико година пуниш?» - how old are you turning?, «Које си годиште?» - what year were you born?, «Лепо се проведите!» - have a good time!

examples.en: Happy birthday!
What do you want for your birthday?

note: written as one word

forms: шаљем, шаљу; past слао; pf. послати

examples.en: I'm sending you the address in a message.

I reserved a table for two.

note: сто (gen. стола) - table; сто is also the number 100

examples.en: That's impossible!
It's impossible to find an apartment in the center.

tips: For «outdoors, in the open air» use напољу: Да седнемо напољу или унутра? (Shall we sit outside or inside?)

examples.en: The children are playing outside.
It's very cold outside.

note: напољу - location; напоље - direction (out)

tips: Besides «to lie» it means to fit (of clothes): «ова хаљина ти лепо лежи» (this dress fits you nicely). Often paired with «стајати».

examples.en: I lay in bed all day.
The book is on the table.

tips: In colloquial speech «лик» is a guy, a type: «неки лик»; «ликуша» - a girl or woman (about someone unknown).
In youth slang «лик» is simply a guy, a dude: «Знаш ли оног лика?» - do you know that guy? A colloquial word, not to be mixed up with the literary sense of image, face.

examples.en: The main character in the film is a detective.
Who's that guy by the door?

forms: придружим се, придруже се; impf. придруживати се

examples.en: Do you want to join us?
He joined the army at eighteen.

note: + dat.: придружити се коме

examples.en: We have a math test tomorrow.
The pregnancy test is positive.

Everyone has their own needs.
None of them came.
I don't have a single free evening this week.
Where did you hide the keys?
She hid behind the door.
Words don't matter, deeds do.
This painting is the work of a great artist.

note: for work as a job, use «посао»

examples.en: Our flight is delayed by two hours.
Have a pleasant flight!

note: «лет» is a flight; «лето» is summer

forms: кунем се, куну се; pf. заклети се

examples.en: I swear I'm telling the truth.

note: «клети» (without «се») means to curse

«Љута паприка», «љута чорба» are spicy; of a person, «љут сам на тебе» means «I'm angry at you». The context tells which.

examples.en: Why are you angry at me?
This pepper is very hot.

examples.en: That's unbelievable!
She was incredibly beautiful.
There was an accident on the highway.
Unfortunately, I wasn't at home.
Don't wake the baby!
I wake up at six every day.
It's getting colder and colder.
He gets nervous before an exam.
Everyone came except him.
Besides that, there's no news.
I need a little change.

examples.sr: У фирми је дошло до великих [про̏мена].
examples.en: Big changes have taken place at the company.
She sings very nicely.
Let's sing together!
The bomb exploded at noon.
This cake is a real knockout!
I made dinner for everyone.
Get ready, we're leaving in five minutes!
I need to tell him that personally.
Personally, I think you're wrong.
Are you hungry?
The kids are hungry, let's eat.
How long is the movie?
Nothing lasts forever.

On weekends we visit Grandma and Grandpa.

note: masculine, but declines like words in -а

examples.en: How much do I owe you?
I owe you an apology.

forms: пређем, пређу; past прешао; impf. прелазити

examples.en: Cross the street on green.
Today we covered three hundred kilometers.
Your life is in danger.
There's no danger, everything is fine.
How many languages do you speak?
The doctor told me to stick out my tongue.

forms: договорим се, договоре се; impf. договарати се

examples.sr: [Догово̀рили] смо се да се нађемо у осам.
examples.en: We agreed to meet at eight.
Let's agree on it.

tips: The perfective for a one-time «liked it»: «свидела ми се презентација», «свидеће ти се филм». For a lasting «like», use «свиђати се».
forms: свидим се, свиде се; impf. свиђати се

examples.en: Did you like the movie?
I think she liked me.

note: + dat.: «свидело ми се» - I liked it

examples.en: I have a meeting with a client at ten.
The customer is always right.
Give me a sheet of paper.
All the papers are in order.

forms: gen. метка; pl. меци; gen. pl. метака

examples.en: The bullet hit him in the shoulder.
I have no more rounds left.
Take one step forward.
We're learning the language step by step.
Go out for a bit of fresh air.
The air in the city is polluted.
What's the difference between these two?

examples.sr: За [ра̏злику] од брата, он је миран.
examples.en: Unlike his brother, he's calm.

note: «за разлику од» + gen.: unlike

tips: With files it means «to download»: «преузети фајл». In everyday speech «скинути» is more common: «скини слику на рачунар».
meanings: to take over, to take on

examples.en: I'll take responsibility.
Download the app for free.
I have a pile of work.
A crowd of people gathered in the square.
Make a wish and blow out the candles!
His greatest wish came true.

tips: «Набавити» is to buy or get hold of a thing: «карте», «оружје». It doesn't go with experience: say «стећи искуство», not «набавити».

examples.en: Where did you get the tickets?
I need to get a new phone.

tips: A musical instrument takes the accusative with no preposition: «свирам гитару», «свира клавир».
A band or club takes «у» + loc.: «свира у групи», «у клубу».
In traffic «свирати» means to honk: «Шта ми свираш, видиш да је црвено!» - why are you honking, it's red.

examples.en: Do you play the guitar?
The band plays every Friday.

note: «свирати гитару» (acc.): to play the guitar

examples.en: You misunderstood me.
You spelled my name wrong.

tips: «Личити на» + acc.: «Личим на оца» - I look like my father. «Већ» sets up the contrast: «Не личим на оца, већ на деду» - I don't look like my father but like my grandfather.

examples.en: You look a lot like your mother.
That's not like him at all.

note: «личити на» + acc.: to resemble

examples.en: Forget the past.
That's in the past now.
Don't lose hope!
He is our last hope.

tips: «Фин» also means well-mannered, decent, pleasant: «фина особа», «фин мирис», «фин момак». English needs different words depending on the noun.

examples.en: He's a very nice guy.
This cake is really delicious.

examples.en: I usually eat eggs for breakfast.
Boil me an egg.
We got on the wrong train.
That was a wrong decision.

tips: «На селу» means in the countryside in general. For one particular village, use «у селу» («у свом селу»).

This is a small village in the mountains.

note: «на селу» - in the countryside

examples.en: He is the only witness of the accident.

Deal?
Stick to the agreement!

examples.en: Please sit down.

He kissed her goodnight.

examples.sr: Оклизнуо сам се и пао на [ду̏пе].
examples.en: I slipped and fell on my butt.
Get off your butt and help me!

note: colloq., a bit rude

forms: испаднем, испадну; past испао; impf. испадати

examples.en: My phone fell out of my pocket.
In the end everything turned out well.

forms: полудим, полуде; past полудео; impf. лудети

examples.en: Have you lost your mind?
Mom will go crazy when she sees the room.
I run in the park every morning.
Don't run in the hallway!
I have to finish the report by Friday.
I read the police report.
I'm very tired after work.
You look tired today.
He's a perfectly ordinary man.
It was an ordinary workday.

tips: «Роба добро пролази» - the goods sell well; «пролази рок» - the deadline is running out. It can also mean to get away with something.

examples.en: The bus passes here every half hour.
Time passes quickly.
It was a pleasure!
I'll gladly help you.

tips: Kinds of teeth: «млечни» (baby), «стални» (permanent), «секутићи» (incisors), «очњаци» (canines), «преткутњаци» (premolars), «кутњаци» (molars), «умњак» (wisdom tooth). The tooth fairy is «Зубић вила».

examples.en: I've had a toothache for two days.

We walked through the forest.

tips: Red wine is usually called «црно вино» (not «црвено»), white wine «бело вино».

«Црно вино» is literally «black wine». Mulled wine is «кувано вино».

examples.en: A glass of red wine, please.

note: «црно вино» - red wine

tips: Slang: the exclamation «Пакао!» means awful, a nightmare.

examples.en: My life has become a real hell.

What do you sell here?
The neighbor is selling an apartment in the center.

tips: The pattern «честитати» + dat. + acc.: «Честитам ти Нову годину». It sounds a bit more formal than «Срећна Нова година!».

«Честитка» is a greeting card, «позивница» an invitation. «Хвала на лепим честиткама!» - thanks for the kind wishes.

examples.en: Congratulations on the new job!

tips: главна улога - lead role, споредна улога - supporting role; играти улогу - to play a role.

examples.en: She got the lead role in the film.
Money plays no role here.
We signed the contract yesterday.
That wasn't in the contract.
It suddenly started to rain.
Don't eat it all at once!
Understood, Sergeant!
The sergeant gave an order.
Breathe deeply and calm down.
I can't breathe!

tips: Slang, does not decline: баш је кул, кул тип, скроз кул. The verb «искулирати» means to chill out, to not care.

examples.en: Your new phone is really cool.
Everything's cool, don't worry.

note: colloquial, indeclinable

tips: Of a woman, «згодна» means having a nice figure («витка» is slim); «Каква ти је линија!» - what a figure you have!
Of a person it means well-built, more often of men: «згодан момак». The opposite «незгодан» means awkward, hard to deal with.

examples.en: Your brother is really good-looking.
This is a good opportunity to talk.

note: of a person: good-looking

examples.sr: Да ли је [и̏ко] видео моје наочаре?
examples.en: Has anyone seen my glasses?
I love you more than anyone.

note: in questions and comparisons; in a statement use неко

examples.en: The plane is flying over the city.
The lamp hangs above the table.
The witch turned him into a frog.
We converted the attic into a room.

note: претворити у + acc. - to turn into something

examples.en: I speak a little Serbian.
I'm a bit tired.
We met completely by chance.

examples.sr: Да ли [слу̏ча̄јно] знаш где је пошта?
examples.en: Do you happen to know where the post office is?
How much does this shirt cost?
It will cost you dearly.

tips: Упалити/угасити - to turn a light or fire on/off: «упали светло», «угаси ватру». For devices «укључити» and «искључити» are more usual.
meanings: to light, to set on fire

examples.en: Turn on the light, please.
The car won't start.

note: colloquial: «упалило је!» - it worked!

examples.en: He fell after the first blow.

examples.sr: То је био тежак [у̀дарац] за њега.
examples.en: That was a heavy blow for him.

tips: Most often an appliance or a machine tool: веш-машина, машина за судове.

examples.en: Turn on the washing machine.
This machine runs day and night.
Look at this old photo.
My grandmother is in the photo.
I've been waiting for you for a whole hour!
I spent my whole childhood in the countryside.

note: also unharmed: вратио се читав

examples.en: That is my duty.
The policeman was on duty.
It's very cold outside.
He gave me a cold look and left.

note: «хладно ми је» - I'm cold

tips: To be surprised is «изненадити се»: «Он се изненадио». The state of being surprised is «бити изненађен»: «Она је била изненађена».
Изненадити некога + instr.: «мама нас је изненадила ненајављеним путовањем». The imperfective is изненађивати.

examples.en: Your call surprised me.
Let's surprise Mom!
That's an order!
I'm just following orders.

tips: In farming «поље» is the general word; professionally people distinguish ливада (meadow), пашњак (pasture), ораница (plowland), њива (field), виноград (vineyard), воћњак (orchard).

examples.en: Corn grows in the field behind the house.
He's an expert in his field.
There's no phone signal here.
Wait for my signal.
I'm madly in love with her.
We had a blast.
I respect your decision.
Everyone must follow the rules.
The mailman brings us packages.
He makes all the decisions in the house.

note: доносити одлуку - to make a decision

examples.en: His father is in the military service.
The church service starts at nine.
There's a secret passage behind the wardrobe.
They had a secret affair.
How much did you earn last month?
I want to earn enough for an apartment.

tips: «Зезати се» is slang for to hang out and goof off; «зезати некога» is to tease someone.
«Зезнут» means in an unpleasant situation, in a mess. Colloquial, not for formal speech.
To kid or prank someone (Зезаш ме! - You're kidding me!); to act up (Нешто ме зеза телефон - my phone is acting up). Зезати се: to joke or to relax in company: Добро смо се зезали.
meanings: to joke around, to goof off (reflexive)

examples.en: Don't mess with me, I'm serious!
I'm just kidding, relax.

note: colloquial; зезнути also means to cheat, to let down

tips: A synonym of свиђати се, a bit more bookish: Допада ми се твој стан. The person who likes is in the dative (ми, ти), the thing liked is the subject.
forms: допадам се, допадају се; pf. допасти се
meanings: to appeal to, to be liked

examples.en: I like your dress.
Do you like Belgrade?

note: works like «to appeal to»: допада ми се - I like it

examples.en: This passport is fake.
It was a false alarm.

examples.sr: Не брини, [иона̀ко̄] сам хтео да идем.
examples.en: Don't worry, I was going to leave anyway.
There's no point in waiting anyway.
There isn't enough room in the apartment.
I need a bit of space.
The wedding was a big event.
He told us about that incident.

tips: Подићи пошиљку - to pick up a parcel at the post office or a parcel locker; подићи новац - to withdraw money from an account.

examples.en: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
I have to withdraw money from the bank.

note: подићи новац - to withdraw money

examples.en: Have fun tonight!
The clown entertained the children.
Silence, please!
I love the quiet of the forest.
I have great respect for him.
Sincerely, Marko Petrović.

tips: As an answer to «како је било?» it means so-so, nothing special: «Онако, ништа посебно».
meanings: just so, for no particular reason

examples.sr: Урадио сам то [она̀ко̄] како си рекао.
examples.en: I did it the way you said.
I'm just asking, out of curiosity.
I don't feel like doing it.
He did it against his will.

note: «добре воље» - in a good mood

examples.en: I accept your offer.

examples.sr: Добио сам [по̀нуду] за посао у Берлину.
examples.en: I got a job offer in Berlin.
They found his fingerprints on the gun.
A footprint was visible in the sand.

note: отисак прста - fingerprint

examples.sr: Могу ли да вас замолим за [пле̑с]?
examples.en: May I have this dance?
She goes to dance classes.
There he is, coming!

examples.sr: Где су ми кључеви? - [Е̏но] их на столу.
examples.en: Where are my keys? - There they are, on the table.

note: ево - here it is (near), ено - there it is (far)

examples.en: Turn off the TV, it's time for bed.
He was expelled from school.
Pass me the salt, please.
I have something else to add.

note: «додај ми» - pass me

examples.en: We sat in a circle around the fire.

examples.sr: Возимо се у [кру̑г] већ сат времена.
examples.en: We've been going around in circles for an hour.

tips: Also a store promotion: «акција на дечије мајице» - a sale on kids' T-shirts. Not only «operation» or «action».
Among hikers it means an outing: «Идемо у акцију», «пријавити се за акцију». Тура is a route or tour, једнодневни излет a day trip.

examples.en: The operation starts at midnight!
Coffee is on sale this week.
Do you want to dance with me?
I don't know how to dance.
A series of strange things happened.
We went down the stairs.
His father is a military doctor.
That is a military secret.
Dad, you're my hero!
He returned home a hero.
You won't believe what happened!
Nobody believed me.

tips: Путничко возило - passenger car, теретно возило - freight vehicle. Одјава возила - deregistration of a vehicle, регистарске таблице - license plates.

examples.en: Get out of the vehicle!
This vehicle has been stolen.
There is no doubt that he is guilty.
Suspicion fell on the neighbor.

tips: From памет comes the adverb напамет: «знати напамет» - to know by heart. «Пасти на памет» - to come to mind.

examples.en: Have you lost your mind?
He's smart, but lazy.
We have different tastes.
The brothers are completely different.
Could you repeat that, please?
This won't happen again.

tips: «Добити утакмицу» - to win a match, «изгубити утакмицу» - to lose it. «Прећи у други клуб» - to move to another club (of a player), «пребацити у други клуб» - to transfer someone to another club.

examples.en: We're watching the match tonight.
Who won the match?
I really appreciate your help.
Everyone respects him as a person.
She is different from other girls.
I thought it would be different.
In summer we swim in the river.
Belgrade lies on two rivers.
I've lost faith in people.
What religion is he?

tips: A colloquial intensifier, totally or absolutely, with verbs and adjectives: «скроз сам сигуран». The name of a bakery, «Скроз добра пекара», is a pun.

examples.en: You're absolutely right.
I got soaked to the skin.

note: colloquial

tips: In youth slang: «морам да палим» - I have to go; «палити» - to leave quickly.
Палити светло - to turn the light on, гасити светло - to turn it off: Упали / угаси светло. Also палити кола - to start the car.
Colloquial: «палим» - I'm off («Палимо одавде!» - Let's get out of here!); «то не пали» - that doesn't work; «палити се на некога» - to fall for someone. Basic meaning: to burn, to light.

examples.en: Don't turn on the light, the kids are asleep.
The neighbor is burning leaves in the yard.

note: colloquial: «пали!» - get lost!, scram!

examples.en: The fridge is empty again.
The streets were empty.
Do you smoke?

examples.sr: Престао сам да [пу̏шим] пре две године.
examples.en: I quit smoking two years ago.
The drive to the sea takes five hours.
Thanks for the ride!
He's my best friend.

examples.sr: Играо сам се са [друга́рима] из краја.
examples.en: I played with the kids from my neighborhood.
Our tomcat is too fat.
Put on a thick sweater, it's cold.
I just wanted to protect you.
This cream protects your skin from the sun.

tips: Of a woman: good-looking, well-groomed, attractive («права мачка»). Not to be confused with «риба», which in slang is just a woman or a girl.
Мачка is a loanword from Hungarian; the male is мачак. «Окотити се» means to give birth, of cats and some other animals.

examples.en: Our cat sleeps on the bed.
Do you have a dog or a cat?
Children are playing with a ball in the park.
Pass me the ball!
The police used force.
I can't force you.

note: силом - by force

tips: To pay by card: платити картицом (instr.); in cash - готовином. A common question: Може ли картицом?

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
I lost my credit card.

tips: Убацити реч - to slip in a word, убацити картицу - to insert a card, «убацити некога у фирму» - to get someone a job at a firm. «Убацивати се» - to butt in: «Немој да се убацујеш!»
meanings: to toss in, to throw in

examples.en: Insert a coin into the machine.
Toss the stuff in the trunk.
What time are you coming?
Autumn is my favorite time of year.

note: годишње доба - season

examples.en: Why are you so nervous?
She was nervous before the exam.
I heard some strange sound.
Turn up the volume, I can't hear anything!
Listen to me carefully.
Drive carefully, the road is slippery.
The wound heals quickly.
First I need to clean the wound.

tips: Also a fairy-like creature of South Slavic mythology, something between a fairy and a nymph, not only a villa.
In Serbian mythology, a beauty of the mountains, forests and waters. She can help and heal, but an angry вила is best left alone: she brings storms and illness.

examples.en: He lives in a big villa on a hill.
The fairy granted him three wishes.

note: виле also means a pitchfork

examples.en: The water level in the river is rising.
Your Serbian is at a high level.
Mars is the red planet.
We must take care of our planet.
Your hands are dirty, wash them.
I put the dirty laundry in the machine.
Speak more quietly, the baby is sleeping.
She went quietly into the room.

tips: By the school rule, «захваљујем» without «се» means yes, thank you, while «захваљујем се» means no, thank you (in reply to «Хоћете ли кафу?»). Not everyone keeps the distinction in real life.

examples.en: Thank you for the invitation.
Thanks to you, everything is fine.

note: захваљујући + dat. - thanks to someone

examples.en: You're a real angel.
The baby sleeps like an angel.
His grandfather was killed in the war.
Two people died in the accident.

tips: Expresses indifference: «њему је свеједно». Vivid synonyms: «баш га брига», «боли га уво» (literally: his ear hurts).

examples.en: It doesn't matter to me, I don't care.

examples.sr: Био је уморан, али је [свејѐдно] дошао.
examples.en: He was tired, but he came anyway.

note: «свеједно ми је» - I don't care

tips: Свемир is outer space: путовања у свемир - space travel. Свемирски брод - spaceship. Васиона - universe.

examples.sr: Као дете сам желео да летим у [све̏мӣр].
examples.en: As a child I wanted to fly into space.
How big is the universe?

tips: «Детаљ» is masculine: мали детаљ.

examples.en: Tell me all the details.
I don't remember every detail.
Is there a pharmacy nearby?
We live near the school.

note: у близини + gen. - near, close to

examples.en: This is private property.
That's my personal business.
He threw a stone into the water.
The house is built of stone.
Congratulations on the victory!
This is a big victory for us.
It's dangerous to swim here.
You drive too dangerously.

examples.en: Since when do you smoke?
Since he moved away, I rarely see him.
This is my favorite song.
What's your favorite movie?

Move over a bit!
He represents our company.
This is a big problem.

note: представљати се - to introduce oneself

tips: Speech as a public talk or a manner of speaking; also a dialect or local way of speaking.

examples.en: He gave a lovely speech at the wedding.
The child has a speech problem.

She is a very responsible person.

note: одговоран за + acc. - responsible for

examples.en: I share a room with my sister.
We don't share the same opinion.
I've been learning German for two years.
He drives a German car.

tips: A children's rhyme for brushing teeth: «Киша пада» (rain falls) - the upper teeth, brushing down; «трава расте» (grass grows) - the lower teeth, brushing up.

examples.en: It's raining outside.
Take an umbrella, it's going to rain.

note: feminine; «пада киша» - it's raining

examples.en: New goods arrive tomorrow.
This store has quality goods.

tips: Издајица - a traitor (f.); издати некога - to betray someone. But also издати књигу - to publish a book, издати стан - to rent out an apartment.

examples.sr: Веровао сам ти, а ти си ме [ѝздао]!

He wants to rent the apartment out to students.
I swear I'm innocent!
Innocent people suffered.

tips: Besides a shop it means the plot of a film or book (радња филма/књиге) and an action (рефлексна, инстинктивна радња). «Радња ради до девет» - the shop is open until nine.

examples.en: He opened his own shop downtown.
The plot of the film is boring.
On weekends I like to walk in nature.
It's in his nature.
He is a calm and quiet man.
I wish you a peaceful night.

tips: The result of thinking: «моје мишљење је да ...» - my opinion is that.... The process of thinking itself is «размишљање».

examples.en: What is your opinion?
I changed my mind.

note: по мом мишљењу - in my opinion

examples.en: He claims he is innocent.
I'm not claiming that I'm right.
I have no money on me.
Be careful when driving.
Who is your leader?
They arrested the gang leader.

note: masculine, but declines like a feminine noun: наш вођа, вођу

examples.en: Comrades, let's begin the meeting.
He was my comrade in the army.

note: a friend is usually «пријатељ»

tips: «Ћути!» - Be quiet!, «Ћутим» - I'm silent. Do not confuse with «чути» (to hear) and «чувати» (to keep, to guard): three similar verbs with different meanings.

examples.en: Why are you silent?
Be quiet and listen!
This is too expensive for me.
I'm too tired to go out.
I have a theory about that.

examples.sr: У [тѐорији] то ради, у пракси не.
examples.en: It works in theory, but not in practice.
Did you lock the door?
Don't forget to lock the car!
He bought her a ring for the engagement.
He wears a wedding ring.
I live on the fifth floor.

examples.sr: Ово ми је [пе̑тӣ] пут у Београду.
examples.en: This is my fifth time in Belgrade.
Your behavior is unacceptable.
I'm sorry for my behavior.
I mostly work from home.
People here are mostly polite.
Who is the owner of this car?
He owns the restaurant.
Hundreds of people are waiting in line.
Lend me a hundred dinars.
He has his own company.
I saw it with my own eyes.
The actors come out on stage.
Don't make a scene in front of everyone!

This is terrible news.

examples.sr: Ко ће га [заме́нити] док је на одмору?
examples.en: Who will replace him while he is on vacation?
I mistook you for your brother.
He was naked to the waist.
The child is running around naked on the beach.

note: m. го, f. гола; гол (m.) is a goal in football

examples.en: Where do you buy bread?
Don't buy anything else, we have everything!
We walked along the seashore.
We crossed to the other bank of the river.
He started his career as a waiter.
This scandal will ruin his career.
I have a personal problem.
I lost my ID card.

note: лична карта - ID card

examples.en: Call a taxi, it's late.
I came by taxi.

note: masculine and declined: таксија, таксијем

examples.en: Don't film me, I'm not ready!
Where is that movie being shot?
This cake is really good!
Ask him nicely and he'll agree.

note: colloquial: «фино!» - delicious!

examples.en: For God's sake, what happened to you?
Let me go, for God's sake!
Just behave normally.
Are you coming? - Of course!

note: colloquial: «нормално!» - of course!

examples.en: I work at a small company.
He opened his own company.

This island is a real paradise.
Good people go to heaven.
I filmed everything with my phone.
Can you take a picture of us?
Who won the race?
This is a race against time.
We drank water from the spring.
Who is your source of information?
Return the seat to an upright position.
He holds a high position in the company.

related.en: to put, to lay; to pass (an exam)

examples.en: This isn't funny!
He told a funny joke.
Turn left at the traffic light.
The post office is to the left of the bank.

tips: «Наљутити се» is to get angry or take offense (once), «љутити се» is to be angry: «Немој се љутити!» - Don't be angry, don't take offense.

examples.en: Don't be angry with me.
You know that makes me angry.

note: љутити се на + acc. - to be angry at

examples.en: A police car is parked in front of the house.
They took him to the police station.
Someone kidnapped his daughter.
He snatched the bag out of my hands.
He bought a new car.
The car is parked in front of the building.
Pack the camping gear.
This equipment is very expensive.

tips: Intensifies emotion: «Шта радиш, бре?» - What the heck are you doing?; «Дођи, бре!» - Come here, man!; «Где си, бре?» - anything from reproach to joy at meeting.
Placed at the end of an emotional remark, it intensifies any emotion - surprise, anger, joy: «Где си, бре!» (when meeting), «Носи се, бре!» (get lost).
Strengthens tone and emotion: «Хајде, бре, касниш!» - come on, you're late; «Браво, бре!» - well done, you. Together with «брате»: «Ма дај, бре, брате!». It cannot be translated literally.

examples.en: What are you doing, man?
Come on, hurry up!

note: colloquial, a typically Serbian particle

examples.en: The director is waiting for you in his office.
He is the school principal.
I came, although I didn't have time.
Although he is sick, he goes to work.
He cheated me out of money.
Did she cheat on you?
I think much the same.
Something similar has happened to me before.
The evil witch put a spell on the princess.
She dressed up as a witch for the masquerade.
Don't move, police!
The dog is wagging its tail.

note: colloquial

examples.en: Don't open the window, it's cold.
The store opens at eight.
The cake is heart-shaped.
Water can be in a solid form.

The dentist pulled my tooth.
You have beautiful eyes.
It was a gorgeous sunny day.
Excuse me, where is the exit?
There is no other way out.
A period goes at the end of a sentence.
This is our starting point.

note: «и тачка!» - and that's final!

examples.sr: [Ни̏ка̄ко] не могу да запамтим његово име.
examples.en: I just can't remember his name.
You must not tell Mom under any circumstances!
I didn't recognize you with a beard!
Can you identify this man?

note: to recognize a person; to find out news is «сазнати»

examples.en: Where is the men's room?
Act like a man!
We crossed the bridge on foot.
The Sava flows under the bridge.
That depends on you.
Everything depends on the weather.

note: зависити од + gen.

examples.en: I've been waiting for the bus for half an hour.
I go to work by bus.
This week I'm working the night shift.
We went to a nightclub.

note: ноћна мора - nightmare

examples.en: Kids, it's time for bed!
I need eight hours of sleep.

Sales dropped this month.

Follow me and don't ask anything.

Sit still!
The night passed peacefully.
Give me a glass of cold water.
Why are you so cold toward me?

That was a very long time ago.
Long time no see!
Goodbye, and thanks for everything!

Kids, we're going to the beach!

note: feminine: на плажи

tips: Kinds: путно осигурање - travel insurance, осигурање од ауто-одговорности - third-party car liability insurance, осигурање куће или стана - home insurance, осигурање моторних возила - motor vehicle insurance.

examples.en: Do you have health insurance?

We live under the same roof.

This coffee is too weak.

note: not to be confused with врата (pl.) - door

examples.en: You hurt her feelings.

examples.sr: Имам чудно [о̀сећа̄ње] у вези с тим.
examples.en: I have a strange feeling about it.
The film is based on real events.
It was a real danger.
He works for a state-owned company.
