There is no point in waiting.

note: «нема сврхе» - there is no point

examples.en: It's always clean at their place.
I'm asking purely out of curiosity.

tips: Written as one word: нажалост. The two-word «на жалост» is a common mistake.

examples.en: Unfortunately, I can't come.
Unfortunately, he is right.
Some people are waiting for you at the door.
I heard some noise.

tips: Грешити is also the everyday verb for to be wrong, with no religious tone: «често грешим» - I often make mistakes.

examples.en: I think you're wrong.
We all make mistakes sometimes.
See you on Friday.
We always go out on Fridays.

note: masculine; петком - on Fridays

examples.en: Grandpa raises pigs in the village.
You eat like a pig!
Where are you spending the summer?
He spends a lot of time on the phone.

tips: Свратити means to drop in on the way: «Свратићу до тебе после посла» - I'll stop by your place after work.

examples.en: Stop by my place after work.
I have to pop into the store.

note: свратити код некога - to drop in on someone

examples.en: Look in the top drawer.
I need to seek help.
My son is afraid of the dark.
It's already dark outside.

tips: Used only of a woman. «Difficult» is тежак or напоран.

examples.en: My wife is pregnant.
She was six months pregnant.
Help! Somebody call the police!
Someone shouted «Help!» from the water.
She got a short haircut.
Life is short.
She won a gold medal.
He has a heart of gold.
We live outside the city.
That is beyond my control.
The guard wouldn't let us in.
He works as a night watchman.

tips: Цвеће is a collective neuter noun used in the singular: «цвеће је лепо». A single flower is цвет.

examples.en: I bought her flowers.
Don't forget to water the flowers.

note: collective, singular: «цвеће је лепо» - the flowers are beautiful

tips: There is also the one-word form «послеподне». Written as two words, «после подне» is an adverbial phrase (after noon). As one word it is a noun: «лепо послеподне».

examples.en: See you tomorrow afternoon.
I slept all afternoon.
We live in the twenty-first century.
I've been waiting for you for ages!
I can't take it anymore!
Hang in there a little longer!

note: impf. издржавати also means to support (a family)

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми [прѐведеш] ово писмо?
examples.en: Can you translate this letter for me?
He translated the book into Russian.
We set out to look for him.
The search has been going on for three days.

note: у потрази за + instr. - in search of

examples.en: The power went out last night.
A strong current caught us.

note: «нема струје» - there is no power

examples.en: Put down the gun!
Grandpa had a hunting rifle.
We are all waiting for your return.

examples.sr: По [по̀вратку] с мора почео сам да радим.
examples.en: After coming back from the seaside, I started working.

tips: Странац means a foreigner, but also simply a stranger. A foreign language is «страни језик».

examples.en: Many foreigners come to Belgrade.
Don't talk to strangers.

note: both foreigner and stranger

examples.en: We must prevent an accident.
Nobody will stop me from leaving.

tips: For cooking food, «спремати храну»: «Волим да спремам» - I like cooking. «Кувати» is to boil, or to cook on the stove.

examples.en: Mom is making lunch.
I'm getting ready for an exam.
I trust you.
He lost my trust.

note: поверење у + acc. - trust in

examples.en: I take full responsibility.
A child is a big responsibility.
Turn right at the intersection.
The bank is to the right of the post office.
Children grow so fast.
Prices keep rising.

tips: Радо means gladly, willingly: Радо ћемо доћи - We'll gladly come. The opposite is нерадо.

examples.en: I'll gladly help you.
Do you want coffee? - Gladly!
Grandpa goes hunting every autumn.
The hunt for the killer began.

note: colloq. «лова» (f.) - money, dough

tips: «Имам поздрав од ...» - I have regards for you from ... To congratulate someone on a holiday, use «честитати», not «поздравити».

examples.en: Give my regards to your parents.
Greetings to everyone from Novi Sad!
You look really sexy tonight!
She put on a sexy dress.
I drink coffee with milk.
Buy a liter of milk.
What's for breakfast?
After breakfast we go for a walk.
Take these plates to the kitchen.
The storm blew the roof off.
I like your style.
That's not my style.
My daughter wants to be a princess.
Good morning, princess!
I can't control my emotions.
Who controls this territory?
He was accused of theft.
He is charged with murder.

note: оптужити за + acc. - to accuse of

examples.en: Don't judge people by their looks.
Judging by everything, he won't come.
The police burst into the apartment.
Did you get into trouble again?
Stop hitting him!
The rain is beating against the window.
The bus driver was polite.
He is an excellent driver.
The ship is entering the port.
The hotel is near the harbor.

note: not to be confused with лук (m.) - onion

examples.en: It's obvious that he's lying.
He was clearly angry.
What do you intend to do?
I don't intend to apologize.
It's too late for that now.
We arrived too late.
Our coach is very strict.
He works as a coach at a football club.
Get out of there right now!
My grandmother is from there.
Where do you put the keys?
Don't put your feet on the table!
The price includes breakfast.
Everyone came, including him.

note: укључујући - including

examples.en: Thank you for your support.
I need your support right now.

tips: Floors are counted from the ground floor (приземље): «први спрат» is the second floor in the US sense, «трећи спрат» the fourth. For a ground-floor apartment, look for «приземље».

examples.en: I live on the third floor.
The building has ten floors.

note: counted above приземље: трећи спрат - the 4th floor (US)

examples.en: Are you happy with your new job?
The boss was not satisfied.

note: задовољан + instr.: задовољан послом

tips: Colloquially of a person, «он је опасан» often means sharp and savvy, not as simple as he looks. It can sound like a compliment.
Colloquially of a person: «опасна правница» - a formidable, sharp lawyer; «Баш сте опасни!» - you've got some nerve!
Jokingly of a woman, «опасна Рускиња» means a femme fatale who could steal someone's husband, not just a dangerous woman.

examples.en: That man is dangerous.
This is a dangerous game.

examples.sr: [Ра̑дно] време је од девет до пет.
examples.en: Working hours are from nine to five.
Tomorrow is a workday.
Do you believe in magic?
That was real magic!

tips: Правда is justice or fairness: борба за правду - the fight for justice. Truth is истина.

examples.en: There is no justice in this world.
I'm fighting for justice.
I don't want you to suffer because of me.
He suffers from insomnia.

note: патити од + gen. - to suffer from

examples.en: The police caught the thief.
Thieves broke into our apartment.
The players are coming out onto the field.
I was out in the field all day.

note: «на терену» - out in the field, on site

examples.en: We swam in the lake.
The cottage is by the lake.
I have to work one more hour.
You did a good job with it!

note: colloq.

examples.en: Can you confirm the reservation?
The witness confirmed his story.

tips: «Бити свестан чега/да...» - to be aware: «Свестан сам да сам погрешио». Spelling: свестан, but свесна, свесно (the т drops out). «Несвесно» means unconsciously, unintentionally.

examples.en: Are you aware of what you've done?
The patient is still conscious.

note: бити свестан + gen. - to be aware of

tips: As a noun, «слатко» (n.) is a traditional fruit preserve that custom says is served to a guest on a spoon, with a glass of cold water.
«Слатка вода» - fresh water (not salt), «слатке речи» - sweet words, «слатка вуна» - cotton candy.

examples.en: Good night, sleep tight.
She smiled sweetly.

note: «слатко» (n.) - fruit preserve served to guests

examples.en: She is a nurse.
You need medical help.
Thank you for your visit!
We're going to visit Grandma.

note: ићи у посету - to go visiting

examples.en: My aunt lives in Niš.
Say hello to your aunt for me!
I warned you, but you didn't listen!
We must warn them about the danger.

note: упозорити на + acc. - to warn about

tips: Чаша covers a glass of water or of wine; a shot of ракија is also «чаша ракије». In Serbian «бокал» is a carafe or pitcher, not a wine glass, and beer comes in a «кригла» (mug).

examples.en: Give me a glass of water, please.
We each had a glass of wine.
We had a wonderful vacation.
You look wonderful in that dress.
How much is that in pounds?
The ticket costs ten pounds.

note: feminine: једна фунта

examples.en: That's against the rules.
You must follow the rules.

note: по правилу - as a rule

examples.en: The ring fell to the bottom of the lake.
The keys are at the bottom of the bag.
Let's change the subject.
What topic are you talking about?
What will you order?
We ordered pizza for dinner.
Turn on the TV, the match is starting.
I want to include you in the project.

tips: Рок means a deadline or time limit (рок за пријаву - application deadline), not only music; in an older sense, fate.

examples.en: The application deadline is Friday.
My dad listens to old rock.

tips: Склонити се means to step away: «Склоните се у страну» (step aside); «Склони се с пута» - get out of the way (ruder).
meanings: to take cover, to get out of the way (reflexive form)

examples.en: Get out of the way!
Take those things off the table.
We have a little house in the country.
The baby is still very little.

note: affectionate; the neutral word is мали

tips: Besides «to chase»: to hunt for (јурити везу - hunt for a connection), to strive for (јурити упис - chase admission), to run after girls. Јурити за ким is to pursue; бежати is to flee.

examples.en: The police are chasing a thief.
Where are you rushing off to like that?
I'll buy bread on the way.
By the way, have you seen Marko?
I can't sleep at night.
He works at night and sleeps during the day.
Let's start the meeting.
He started a new life in Belgrade.
Who acts in that movie?
Don't pretend you're sick!
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
He's still in the bathroom.

tips: «Викнути» is to give a shout, and also to call someone: «Викни ме кад будеш спреман» - call me when you're ready.

examples.en: Don't yell at me!
Why are you shouting? I can hear you.

note: викати на + acc. - to yell at

examples.en: Don't make me choose!
The shepherd drives the sheep to pasture.

note: терати некога да + pres. - to make someone do

examples.en: Fasten your seat belts, please.
They tied his hands.
If you have any questions, call us.
If he doesn't come, we'll go without him.

note: bookish; = ако

examples.en: Journalists are waiting in front of the building.
My brother is a journalist.

tips: Always plural and feminine: читам новине, ове новине су старе.

examples.en: I read the newspaper with my morning coffee.
It was written in the newspaper.

tips: Славски колач is a special ceremonial bread for the slava (a family's patron saint's day), not a sweet cake.

examples.en: Mom is baking cakes for the slava.
Would you like a piece of cake?
That's unbelievable!
I had an unbelievable dream.

examples.sr: Шта имате да кажете у своју [о̀дбрану]?
examples.en: What do you have to say in your defense?
Our team has a strong defense.
I can't start the car.
We launched a new project.
I'm working on a study.
The results of the research are interesting.

examples.sr: Његова смрт је велики [губи́так] за нас.
examples.en: His death is a great loss for us.
The company had big losses.

note: «губитак времена» - a waste of time

forms: f. pl.; gen. груди; dat. грудима

examples.en: My chest hurts.
The dog jumped onto his chest.

note: plural only: груди су

examples.en: What position do you play?
We're in a bad position now.
Listen to this song!
I should have listened to you.
I don't have internet access.
We need a new approach to the problem.

examples.sr: Не могу да [би̏рам], свиђају ми се оба.
examples.en: I can't choose, I like both.
Choose your friends carefully.
This light bothers me.
Plants need sunlight.

note: «свет» means world, not light

tips: Also to suit, to look good on: «Та боја ти лепо пристаје». Пристати на + acc. - to agree to: «Пристајем!» - I agree!

examples.sr: Да ли је [прѝстао] на наш предлог?
examples.en: Did he agree to our proposal?
The ship docked in the port.

note: пристати на + acc. - to agree to

examples.en: Try the local food.
We listen to the local radio.
Let's split the bill.
He divided the cake into four parts.
Do you really think so?
I'm truly sorry.

tips: The plural колеге takes feminine agreement: Моје колеге су дошле. Although the word is masculine in the singular (мој колега), its plural agrees as feminine.

examples.en: This is my colleague from work.
Tomorrow I'm going to lunch with my colleagues.

note: masculine, but declines like a feminine noun: колегу, колеге

examples.en: Who broke the window?

examples.sr: Пао ми је телефон и [ра̀збио] се.
examples.en: My phone fell and broke.
Our team won the championship.
How did you win her heart?
Why are you so sad?
That's a very sad story.
My computer broke down again.
He sits at the computer all day.
Show me a card trick!
That's an old trick.
Are you cheating on me?

examples.sr: Ако ме сећање не [ва̏ра], био је ту.
examples.en: If my memory doesn't fail me, he was here.
Drive in the right lane.
She tied her hair with a red ribbon.
See you on Saturday.
On Saturdays I go to the market.

note: суботом - on Saturdays

examples.en: The fishermen are pulling in the net.
There's no network coverage here.
Children play on the grass.
I have to mow the grass.
He persuaded me to stay.
Don't try to convince me.

tips: Storm, thunderstorm. To mean specifically a thunderstorm, say «олуја са грмљавином». Related words: невреме, оркан.

examples.en: There was a strong storm last night.
The ship was caught in a storm.

tips: «Сместити се» means to settle in, to find a place: «лепо смо се сместили у соби» - we settled into the room nicely; also to take one's seat: «сместили смо се у авион» - we got settled on the plane.
«Сместите се удобније» - make yourselves more comfortable; «Све се може сместити у ормар» - everything can fit in the wardrobe.

examples.en: They put us up in a small hotel.
Somebody framed me!
She has big green eyes.
The light is green, go!
The trial starts tomorrow morning.
He testified at the trial.

meanings: to fold, to put in order

examples.en: I have to agree with you.
Put the clothes away in the wardrobe.

note: сложити се са + instr. - to agree with

examples.en: Last night we watched a scary movie.
He's an amazing guy!

note: colloq. can mean amazing

examples.en: I'm going to the store, do you need anything?
The store is open until nine.
The prisoner sits alone in his cell.
The body consists of billions of cells.
Don't throw trash in the street!
The kids are throwing stones into the river.
Understood, Major!
My father is a major in the army.
The pirates buried treasure on the island.
Lucky you, you're going to the seaside!

note: «благо теби!» - lucky you!

examples.en: We all have our demons.
The priest drove out the demon.
What a lovely smell of coffee!
I smell smoke.

related.en: to smell, to give off a smell

note: usually a pleasant smell; an unpleasant one is смрад

examples.en: Why do you keep defending him?
Mom won't let me go out.

note: бранити некоме - to forbid someone

tips: Ујак (also ујка) is the maternal uncle, стриц the paternal one. «Мамин син» means a mama's boy.

examples.en: My uncle lives in Canada.
Aunt and Uncle are coming for lunch.

note: mother's brother; father's brother is стриц

examples.en: Be careful on the road!
She is a very careful driver.
See you tomorrow evening.
In the evening we usually watch a movie.

meanings: to let in, to let go

examples.en: Don't let him in!
Who is playing this music?
Data processing takes a long time.
This is a cover of an old song.
The police took his statement.
The minister gave a statement to the media.
I watched a new episode last night.
What happened in the last episode?

note: feminine: нова епизода

examples.en: She is still waiting for her prince.
The Little Prince is my favorite book.

tips: «Јави ми се» in modern speech often means message me, let me know (on Viber or in a messenger), not only call. «Јавићу се телефоном» - I'll call.
meanings: to get in touch, to answer the phone (reflexive form)

examples.en: Why don't you answer the phone?
Keep in touch more often!

note: јавити се - to call, to get in touch

examples.en: As you wish, Your Majesty.
Her Majesty the Queen arrives tomorrow.
A young man was looking for you.
Your son has become a real young man.
Come closer, don't be afraid.

examples.sr: На улици ми је [при̏шао] непознат човек.
examples.en: A stranger came up to me on the street.
Call me on my cell.
I bought a new mobile phone.
We have a mutual friend.
It's our joint project.
Careful, this is a trap!
The fox fell into a trap.

tips: «Срамота ме је!» - I'm ashamed; «Срам те било!» - shame on you; «осрамотио сам те» - I disgraced you. Adjectives: срамотан - shameful, срамежљив - shy.

examples.en: What a disgrace!
I'm ashamed to say.

note: «срамота ме је» - I'm ashamed

examples.en: In summer the kids go to camp.
We set up camp by the river.
I totally forgot!
This is total madness.

note: colloq.

examples.en: Knowledge is power.
I need a better knowledge of the language.

tips: Гас is also the gas pedal of a car: «притиснути гас» - to step on the gas.

examples.en: I smell gas.
Step on the gas, we're late!
The tourist season is starting.
I'm watching the second season of the series.

note: feminine: нова сезона

tips: Стомак (also трбух) is the stomach or belly; живот means life only: «боли ме стомак» - my stomach hurts, «живот је леп» - life is beautiful.

examples.en: My stomach hurts.
Don't swim on a full stomach.
I'll wait for you at the corner of the street.
We put the table in the corner.
What caused the fire?
He challenged me to a duel.

examples.sr: Из [одрѐђених] разлога не могу да дођем.
examples.en: For certain reasons I can't come.
We have no specific plan.
Today is a special day.
He served in a special unit.
A prisoner escaped last night.
The guards counted the prisoners.
What size are you?
Do you have this in a smaller size?

tips: In slang «провалити» means to figure out, to get it: «давно сам провалила да му се свиђаш». The basic meaning is to collapse, to cave in.
Colloquially, besides «to break in», it means to get to the bottom of something: «нисам провалио шта хоће» - I didn't get what he wants.
meanings: to see through, to figure out (colloq.)

examples.en: Someone broke into our apartment.
I've got you figured out, don't lie!
What do you suggest?
I suggest we leave right away.

meanings: to get off, to get out (of a vehicle)

examples.en: Come down, a taxi is waiting for you.
We got off the bus downtown.
This area is dangerous at night.
That's not my field of work.
I love modern art.
Cooking is a real art.

note: not to be confused with «искуство» - experience

tips: Serbs say «на аеродрому», not «у аеродрому»: at the airport.

examples.en: I'll take you to the airport.
I'll wait for you at the airport.
I have a feeling someone is watching us.
I like to watch the stars.
You deserve a rest.
She didn't deserve such treatment.

examples.sr: Мој први [у̀читељ] је био веома строг.
examples.en: My first teacher was very strict.

examples.sr: Он ради као [у̀читељ] у основној школи.
examples.en: He works as a teacher in a primary school.

note: in the upper grades the usual word is «наставник»

examples.en: I demand an explanation!
This job requires patience.
I agree, but on one condition.
What are the working conditions like?

examples.sr: Требало му је много [хра̏брости] да јој то каже.
examples.en: It took him a lot of courage to tell her that.
Pluck up your courage and call her.

tips: Figuratively: a stupid person, an idiot, not just a monkey.
Said to a man, it is a serious insult; the word is masculine («велики мајмун»), vocative «мајмуне!». «магарче!» and «коњу један!» are just as insulting. For an animal at the zoo it is neutral.

examples.sr: Деца воле да гледају [ма̀јмуне] у зоолошком врту.
examples.en: Children love to watch the monkeys at the zoo.
You climb trees like a monkey.

tips: «Мука ми је» - I feel sick. The word on its own also means «suffering»: «са муком» - with difficulty.
«Мука ми је од …» - I'm fed up with ...

examples.sr: Много [му̏ке] сам имао са тим папирима.
examples.en: I had a lot of trouble with those papers.
Bus rides make me sick.

note: «мука ми је» - I feel sick

examples.en: Do you have a cigarette?
He smoked a cigarette on the terrace.
Last night I fell asleep in front of the TV.
I can't fall asleep because of the noise.
He was fired from his job yesterday.
If you're late again, I'll fire you.

note: «добити отказ» - to get fired; «дати отказ» - to quit, or (of a boss) to fire someone

tips: «Налог за плаћање» - payment order, «налог за хапшење» - arrest warrant. «Кориснички налог» - user account.
Also an account: направити налог - to create an account, пословни налог - business account. In the legal sense - an order, a warrant.

examples.en: The police have a search warrant.

examples.sr: Направи [на́лог] на сајту и пријави се.
examples.en: Create an account on the site and log in.
It's another ten kilometers to the city.

examples.sr: Возио је сто осамдесет [киломѐтара] на сат.
examples.en: He drove a hundred and eighty kilometers an hour.
I have fond memories of my childhood.

examples.sr: Тај дан ми је остао у [сѐћању].
examples.en: That day stayed in my memory.
I found the recipe on the internet.

examples.sr: Код куће немамо [и̏нтернет] већ два дана.
examples.en: We haven't had internet at home for two days.

note: «на интернету» - on the internet

examples.sr: [Сачу̀вај] документ пре него што затвориш програм.
examples.en: Save the document before you close the program.
We managed to save the old house.

note: «Боже сачувај!» - God forbid!

examples.en: My husband is very jealous.
Are you jealous of her?

note: «љубоморан на» + acc.: jealous of someone

examples.en: Allow me to introduce my wife.
He introduced himself as a doctor.
He put on a new suit for the wedding.
This suit looks good on you.

note: «одело» is a suit; clothing in general is «одећа»

examples.sr: Потписао ми је [че̏к] на хиљаду евра.
examples.en: He wrote me a check for a thousand euros.
Can you pay by check?

note: colloq. «чек!» - hold on (from «чекај»); a till receipt is «рачун»

tips: «Раме» is the shoulder as the top of the body between the neck and the arm. The upper arm is «надлактица», the forearm «подлактица».
The plural is «рамена»: «Има широка рамена» - he has broad shoulders.

examples.en: My left shoulder hurts.
He put his hand on my shoulder.

note: «слегнути раменима» - to shrug one's shoulders

examples.sr: [Увѐрио] сам га да је све у реду.
examples.en: I assured him that everything was fine.
See for yourself!
The newspapers published his interview.
The government announced new measures.
We haven't seen each other for a long time.
I've known him for a long time, since school.
She has a gift for music.
They brought gifts for the newlyweds.

note: in everyday speech a present is more often «поклон»

examples.en: I have no intention of giving up.
He had good intentions.
What is this strange creature?
Poor thing, it's completely soaked.

examples.sr: Мој брат студира на [ко̀леџу] у Америци.
examples.en: My brother studies at a college in America.
We met back in college.

note: usually an American-style college; a Serbian university faculty is «факултет»

examples.en: You've finally arrived!
The rain has finally stopped.
Are you still awake?
I was awake all night.

note: «будан сам» - I'm awake

examples.en: They found his DNA on the knife.

examples.sr: [ДНК] тест је показао да је он отац.
examples.en: The DNA test showed that he is the father.
Now it's your move.
That was a very smart move.

note: «повући потез» - to make a move

examples.en: I fell and scraped my knee.

examples.sr: Клекнуо је на [ко̀лена] и запросио је.
examples.en: He got down on his knees and proposed to her.

tips: «Венчати се» - to get married: «Венчали су се у јуну». Used for both a church and a civil wedding.

examples.en: We got married last summer.

examples.sr: Свештеник их је [вѐнчао] у старој цркви.
examples.en: The priest married them in the old church.

tips: «Запослити се» - to get a job: «Запослила сам се у продавници». «Запослити некога» - to hire someone.

examples.en: The company hired ten new workers.
I finally got a job!
I read your file.
The police already have a file on him.
The bank robbery lasted five minutes.
These prices are a real rip-off!
My grandfather was a brave soldier.

examples.sr: Буди [хра̏бра], све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Be brave, everything will be fine.
The knight drew his sword.
They fought with swords until dawn.
My grandfather was a passionate hunter.
The hunters searched for the wolf all day.

tips: «Вредан» means both «hardworking, diligent» and «valuable». The noun «вредност» is «value».
«Вредна ученица» - a diligent pupil. The sense «valuable» depends on context.

examples.en: This ring is very valuable.
She is a diligent student.
Fill the glass with water, please.
I have to charge my phone.
The sheriff arrested the thief.
Call the sheriff, quick!

tips: «Сликати» also means to photograph: «сликати се» - to have one's picture taken, «слика» is both a painting and a photo. «Желим да се сликам за пасош».
Other ways to say it: правити фотографије, фотографисати. «Волим да сликам» - I like taking pictures.

examples.en: She has been painting landscapes for years.
Let's take a picture of ourselves by the fountain.
Our whole plan fell through.
The company went under after two years.
Which way is the train station?
You're going the wrong way.
Someone is stealing our newspapers from in front of the door.
It's not nice to steal from friends.

examples.sr: Та странка је дошла на [вла̑ст] пре две године.
examples.en: That party came to power two years ago.
The authorities closed the border.
He grew up on a farm in Vojvodina.
His parents have a cattle farm.

meanings: to treat (someone to food or drink)

examples.en: What do you offer us for dessert?

examples.sr: [Ну̀дили] су ми добар посао у Београду.
examples.en: I was offered a good job in Belgrade.
There must be some other solution.
I received a decision on my pension.
On what grounds do you claim that?
There are no grounds for such suspicion.

note: «на основу» + gen.: on the basis of

tips: In an address the entrance of an apartment building is «2. улаз», but in a long building each entrance usually has its own house number.

examples.en: I'm waiting for you at the entrance to the building.
Where is the entrance to the museum?

tips: The preposition is «у»: «у пошти» - at the post office. But «на интернету» - on the internet.

examples.sr: Морам да одем у [по̏шту] да платим рачуне.
examples.en: I have to go to the post office to pay the bills.
Has the mail come today?

note: «ићи у пошту» - to go to the post office

examples.en: I'm not interested in politics at all.
We don't talk about politics at the table.

meanings: to turn to, to apply to (reflexive)

examples.en: Please go to window number three.
Nobody paid any attention to him.

note: «обратити пажњу на» + acc.: to pay attention to

examples.en: My keys are in my pocket.
I pay for everything out of my own pocket.
He is the best player on the team.
There are eleven players on the field.
The elevator got stuck between floors.
We were stuck in traffic for an hour.

note: colloq. «заглавити у затвору» - to land in prison

examples.en: Let's take a short break.
We drink coffee during the break.
The police are still investigating the case.
Scientists are researching a new drug.

tips: Historically a mercenary on the Austro-Hungarian border with the Ottoman Empire; in slang, a policeman.

examples.en: Run, the cops are coming!

examples.sr: Његов брат је [па̀ндӯр] у Новом Саду.
examples.en: His brother is a cop in Novi Sad.

note: slang for a police officer

examples.en: I urgently need to talk to you.
The patient was rushed to the hospital.
The police arrested the whole gang.
He was a member of a street gang.
My brother is a medical student.
There are a lot of students in Novi Sad.

tips: It can mean the night just past or the coming one. To avoid confusion, say «синоћ» (last evening) and «вечерас» (this evening).

examples.en: I didn't sleep at all last night.
Where will you sleep tonight?

note: «ноћас» - both the night just past and the coming night

tips: «Ђубре» is garbage and, as an insult, a scoundrel; «ђубриво» is fertilizer. Same root, different meanings.

examples.en: Take out the trash, please.
He's a total scumbag!

note: said of a person, a rude insult

examples.en: I'm inviting you to lunch on Sunday.
Why do you keep calling me at night?

examples.sr: [Сигу́рно̄ст] деце нам је на првом месту.
examples.en: Our children's safety comes first.
He spoke with great confidence.
He works in the sales department.
Mom is in the surgical ward.
He jumped into the water from the bridge.
Prices have shot up again.
He never picks up the phone.
Get up, you'll be late!

note: «дизати телефон» - to pick up the phone

examples.en: I don't want to take a risk.

examples.sr: [Ризѝковао] је живот да би је спасао.
examples.en: He risked his life to save her.
He lives a few miles from here.
We were driving sixty miles an hour.

forms: заљубим се, заљубе се; impf. заљубљивати се

examples.sr: Мислим да сам се [заљу̀био] у тебе.
examples.en: I think I've fallen in love with you.

examples.sr: Први пут се [заљу́била] са петнаест година.
examples.en: She first fell in love at fifteen.

note: «заљубити се у» + acc.: to fall in love with someone

examples.sr: Наш син ће ове године у трећи [ра́зред].
examples.en: Our son will start third grade this year.
We were in the same class.
You look awful, are you sick?
I feel terrible about it.
My pay is two months late.
He has a good salary at the bank.

tips: Also «good for you»: здрава навика - a healthy habit, Поврће је здраво. A wish: «Да си ми здрав!». Idioms: «здрав као дрен» - healthy as a horse, «здрав и прав» - safe and sound.

examples.en: Thank God, we are all healthy.
I try to eat healthy food.
He wants revenge for his brother's death.
Revenge is not a solution.
Stop interrupting me all the time!
Sorry for interrupting the meeting.
My feet hurt from walking.
The baby has tiny feet.

tips: Garlic is «бели лук» (literally white onion), plain «лук» is the ordinary onion. Do not mix them up at the market.
The ordinary onion is «црни лук», garlic is «бели лук». Other kinds: «црвени лук» - red onion, «млади лук» - spring onion.

examples.en: Chop the onion into small pieces.
The hunter drew his bow.

note: «бели лук» - garlic, «црни лук» - onion

tips: «Мешати се» - to meddle: «Немој се мешати!». Related: «То вас се не тиче» - it's none of your business, «Остави ме на миру» - leave me alone.

examples.en: Stir the soup so it doesn't burn.
Don't meddle in other people's business.

note: to hinder, to disturb is «сметати»

examples.sr: Ћерка се по цео дан игра [лу̏ткама].
examples.en: My daughter plays with dolls all day.
Hi, babe, how are you?
We live in the southern part of the city.

examples.sr: [Ју̏жна] Србија је позната по доброј храни.
examples.en: Southern Serbia is known for good food.
We keep the wine in the cellar.
Go down to the cellar for some potatoes.
The doctor sees patients from eight o'clock.
Do you accept cards?
Turn right at the traffic light.

examples.sr: Покушао је да [скрѐне] разговор на другу тему.
examples.en: He tried to steer the conversation to another topic.

note: «скренути пажњу на» + acc.: to draw attention to

examples.en: This is my buddy Marko.
They were business partners.

note: colloq.

forms: допаднем се, допадну се; допао се; impf. допадати се

examples.en: I really liked that movie.
I think she liked you.

note: the one who likes is in the dat.: «допао ми се» - I liked him

examples.en: He is a very capable worker.

examples.sr: У овом стању ниси [спо̀собна] да возиш.
examples.en: In this state you are not fit to drive.
Throw that in the trash.
The trash can is full again.
He threatened me with a knife.
The city is threatened by a flood.

note: «претити» + dat.: to threaten someone

examples.en: Please wait a moment.
This is the right moment for it.
He brought a bottle of good wine.
Buy two bottles of water.
He died of lung cancer.
There are crayfish in this river.

meanings: to be good, to be of use

examples.en: This knife is no good at all.
What's wrong with you?

note: «не ваља» - bad, no good

examples.en: He used to get threats over the phone.
He is no threat to anyone.
Make a shopping list.
Your name isn't on the list.

note: «на списку» - on the list

examples.en: He kept his promise.
Please fill out this form.
Sit in the back, Mom is in front.
The kids are in the back of the car.
The rain keeps falling.
We'll continue after the break.
You've ruined my whole evening!
The rain ruined our outing.

examples.sr: Изгубили смо [би̏тку], али не и рат.
examples.en: We lost the battle, but not the war.
This is a fight for life.
The concert will be held on Saturday.
He kept his word.

note: «одржати се» - to take place

examples.en: He didn't mention that he was married.
Nobody mentioned your name.
I'm watching a show about animals.
That show is on every Sunday evening.
He is the world tennis champion.

examples.sr: Деда је учествовао у Другом [све̏тском] рату.
examples.en: My grandfather took part in the Second World War.
We stayed with them only a short time.
He got a very short haircut.

examples.sr: Који ти је омиљени [пре́дмет] у школи?
examples.en: What's your favorite subject at school?
They found a strange object in the box.
You're making good progress in Serbian!
The disease is progressing very fast.
Let me know when you arrive.
Nobody informed us about it.
This is a public parking lot.
He is a well-known public figure.
Repeat after me.
I don't like to repeat the same things.
Every morning he takes the child to kindergarten.
Why do you bring strangers into the house?
Don't create problems out of nothing.
The artist creates in his studio.
This is a pedestrian zone.
We entered a restricted zone.

tips: «Узбуђен због нечега»: «узбуђена сам због путовања». It covers both «worked up, nervous» and «excited» (looking forward to something).

examples.en: The kids are excited about the trip.
I was too excited to fall asleep.
Play fair!
We ate until we were full.
We walked along a narrow path through the forest.
The bike path runs along the river.
A fire broke out in the building.
The firefighters quickly put out the fire.
What model of phone is this?
She works as a model in Milan.
My brother is a pilot for an airline.
The pilot landed the plane safely.
You need to see a doctor.
My father is a general practitioner.

note: «ићи код лекара» - to go to the doctor (код + gen.)

examples.en: The saleswoman was very kind.
Thank you, you are very kind.
Quick, the house is on fire!
The light is still on in the kitchen.
Come closer, I want to tell you something.
We work very closely together.
You can use my computer.
He used the wrong word.
We moved the things in a van.
A white van is parked in front of the house.
Smoking is prohibited inside the building.
We'll sort it out within the family.

tips: «Панталоне» are trousers; underwear is «гаће».

examples.en: I bought new pants.
These pants are tight on me.
The priest blessed our house.
His father was a priest.
Grandpa always wears a black hat.
Take your hat off in the house!
Send me the restaurant's location.
The apartment has an excellent location.
Everyone wore masks at the masquerade.
Take off the mask, I know who you are.

tips: An owner of a business or property; colloquially, a person who is in control and acts with authority; figuratively, a rich man.

examples.en: The landlord is asking for the rent.

examples.sr: Мој [га̏зда] ме је данас пустио раније.
examples.en: My boss let me leave early today.

note: masculine despite the ending -а: «наш газда»

examples.en: I get up at six every day.
Get up, we've arrived!

related.en: to get up, to stand up

tips: «Пребацити» covers: to move («пребаци овај сто»), to transfer money («пребаци ми паре»), to reproach («немам шта да му пребацим»); «пребацити се» - to transfer to another faculty.

examples.en: Transfer the money to my account.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ме [прѐбациш] до станице?
examples.en: Can you give me a lift to the station?

note: «пребацити некоме нешто» - to reproach someone for something

examples.en: I have to clean the kitchen before dinner.
Clean your shoes before you come in.

tips: «Наздравље!» - bless you after a sneeze (to children - «Пис, мацо!»). On sick leave - «на боловању»; «Брзо оздравите!» - get well soon.

examples.en: Health is the most important thing.
Smoking is bad for your health.

note: «на здравље!» - bless you (after a sneeze); also cheers, or enjoy (with food and drink)

tips: «Рачунати на» + acc. - to count on someone: «Рачунам на тебе» means «I'm counting on you». To count items, «бројати» is used.
«Рачунати на некога» - to count on someone; «то се не рачуна» - that doesn't count; «рачунати да» - to assume that.

examples.sr: Дете већ зна да [рачу́на] до сто.
examples.en: The child can already count to a hundred.
You can always count on me.

note: «рачунати на» + acc.: to count on

examples.en: Why do you call me that?
This place is called Little Venice.
Before leaving, we all said goodbye.
His departure surprised us all.
The nurse took a blood sample.
Send us a sample of the fabric.
The doctor examined me carefully.
Check the text once more before sending.
He rejected all the accusations.
That is a very serious accusation.
The movie was a lot of fun.
He's a fun guy.
Life in the countryside has many advantages.
Pedestrians at a crossing have the right of way.
Move aside, I can't see anything!
Take your hands off me!

note: colloq.; neutral: «померити», «склонити»

examples.en: Turn off the light when you go out.
The firefighters quickly put out the fire.
You look wonderful tonight!
It was wonderful at the seaside.

tips: Mostly used in the plural «степенице» - stairs: «Где су степенице?», «идемо степеницама».

examples.en: He fell down the stairs.
Careful, the first step is slippery.

note: stairs - «степенице» (pl.)

examples.en: The car stopped in the middle of the road.
He called me in the middle of the night.

They show no mercy to anyone.
Mom was very worried.
Why are you so upset?

tips: The word is of Serbian origin; the best-known vampire of Serbian folklore is Sava Savanović from Glišić's story.

examples.en: I don't believe in vampires.

examples.sr: Реч [ва̀мпӣр] је дошла из српског језика.
examples.en: The word "vampire" came from the Serbian language.
She was a victim of sexual harassment.
The doctor spoke about sexual health.
Don't move, I'm going to take your picture.
The dog is lying there and not moving.

note: colloq.

examples.en: It's so boring here.
I was bored at the lecture.
The commander ordered a retreat.

examples.sr: Ко ти је [нарѐдио] да то урадиш?
examples.en: Who ordered you to do that?
The explosion was heard all over the city.
Nobody was hurt in the explosion.
What time do you finish work?
He is finishing university this year.

tips: «На базену» - at the pool as a place (била је гужва на базену); «у базену» - in the water (деца се брчкају у базену).

examples.en: In summer we go to the pool every day.
The hotel has a big pool.

note: «ићи на базен» - to go to the pool

examples.en: What an ugly building!
I had a bad dream last night.
The house is on top of the hill.
I have loads of work.
We moved recently.
I saw him in town recently.
Wait for me in the hallway.
The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The police found a body in the river.
Only over my dead body!
This stinks horribly.
He behaved disgustingly toward her.

tips: The missing thing is in the nominative: «Фали ми само 20 динара». Colloquially, to miss: «Фали ми породица»; «нешто ти фали» - something is wrong with you.
«Шта ти фали?» - what are you missing (often «what more do you want?»), «не фали ти ништа» - you have everything.
«Фали ми ...» - I lack ..., «фалиш ми» - I miss you. This is the colloquial variant of the standard «недостајати».

examples.en: I'm ten dinars short.
I miss you a lot.

note: colloq.; «фалиш ми» - I miss you

examples.en: Don't stand in the passage!
A secret passage leads to the cellar.
Her parents live in the north of the country.
A cold wind is blowing from the north.
The apartment has lost value.
To me, family is the greatest value.
Put the table in the middle of the room.
He found it hard to get used to the new environment.

note: «среда» is Wednesday; «средина» is the middle or the environment

examples.en: I am against any violence.
There is too much violence in the movie.
You have to bear the consequences of your decisions.
This will have serious consequences.
I put the keys over there, on the table.
Who is sitting over there in the corner?

note: bookish; in speech «тамо» is more common

examples.en: I don't drink alcohol.
He was driving under the influence of alcohol.
I can't sleep because of the noise.
Don't make noise, the baby is sleeping.
Would you like ice in your drink?
Watch out, there's ice on the road.
The committee rejected our proposal.
He is a member of the board of directors.

tips: Two opposite meanings: to borrow (позајмио сам новац од брата) and to lend (позајмио сам брату новац). The context makes it clear.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми [по̀зајмиш] хиљаду динара?
examples.en: Can you lend me a thousand dinars?

note: both «to lend» and «to borrow»

examples.en: Wait a little, I'll be right back.
Can you wait a minute?

The doctor looked at the lung scan.

related.en: to film, to record; to photograph

examples.en: I grew up in a small village.
When you grow up, you'll understand.
They met all our demands.
I submitted a visa application.
Do you get what I mean?
Honestly, I don't get any of it.

note: colloq.

examples.en: We're looking for a replacement for our sick colleague.
There is no substitute for experience.
Sorry, I'm in a hurry to get to work.
Don't hurry, we have plenty of time.
He needs time to regain his strength.

examples.sr: Мало је фалило да [по̀вратим] у аутобусу.
examples.en: I almost threw up on the bus.

note: both «to regain» and «to throw up»

forms: суочим се, суоче се; impf. суочавати се
meanings: to come face to face with

examples.en: You have to face the truth.
We came up against a big problem.

note: суочити се са + instr.: to face something

examples.en: He has devoted his whole life to science.

examples.sr: Модерна [на̀ука] то не може да објасни.
examples.en: Modern science can't explain that.

tips: The related verb «кукати» means to whine or complain: «Престани да кукаш!» (Stop whining!).
Literally «cuckoo», figuratively «coward». Also: кукавичлук (cowardice). «Не буди кукавица!» - Don't be a coward!

examples.en: Don't be a coward, give it a try!
A cuckoo can be heard in the forest.

note: feminine, but also used of a man: он је кукавица

examples.en: What's the point of all this?
You seem to have missed the point.
Knowing the language is a big plus.
Two plus two is four.

examples.sr: Деда је [у̀са̄мљен] откад је бака умрла.
examples.en: Grandpa has been lonely since Grandma died.

note: feminine: дивља звер - a wild beast

note: A class period is «час»; a lecture is «предавање».

examples.en: You're safe here, don't be afraid.
This is a safe neighborhood for children.

I'm as hungry as a wolf.

meanings: to move, to relocate (someone or something)

examples.sr: Прошле године смо се [прѐселили] у Београд.
examples.en: Last year we moved to Belgrade.

examples.sr: Код нас се ципеле [скѝдају] на улазу.
examples.en: In our country, shoes are taken off at the entrance.

note: у току - in progress; бити у току - to be up to date

examples.en: Something smells nice from the kitchen.

examples.en: Put on a warm sweater, it's cold outside.

I'm afraid of snakes.
Watch out, he's a real snake!

tips: Besides «dark», «таман» is also an adverb meaning «just right, a perfect fit»: «Ове патике су ми таман» - these sneakers fit me perfectly.
The colloquial «таман посла» means «no way» or «don't mention it».

examples.en: She has dark hair and blue eyes.
This room is too dark.

note: adverb «таман» - just in time: таман сам хтео да те зовем

examples.en: I drink coffee without sugar.

examples.sr: Деда има [шѐћер] и пази шта једе.
examples.en: Grandpa has diabetes and watches what he eats.

tips: The reflexive «хранити се» means to eat, to have a diet.
meanings: to eat, to have a diet (reflexive)

examples.sr: Ко [хра̏ни] пса док сте на путу?
examples.en: Who feeds the dog while you're away?
You need to eat healthier.
He gave me a clear answer.
Are the instructions clear?
I'm so damn tired.
This is damn hard.

note: colloquial, a bit rude

examples.en: We rented a boat on the lake.
The boat capsized because of the waves.
Wash your hands before eating.
I need to do the laundry.
The child has a fever.
Tonight the temperature will drop below zero.

meanings: to move aside, to put away
to get out of the way, to hide (reflexive)

examples.en: Get out of the way!
Don't look away when I'm talking to you.
The whole local community helped us.
They have been married for ten years.
Stop asking stupid questions.
Mom is setting the table for dinner.
My left leg hurts.
Drive in the left lane.

related.en: to the left, on the left

examples.sr: Пребаци на други [ка̀на̄л], ово је досадно.
examples.en: Switch to another channel, this is boring.
An old canal runs through the city.
He keeps refusing my help.
Why do you refuse to eat?
I wish you great success!
The film was a big success.

examples.sr: Он је [мо̏ћан] човек у овом граду.
examples.en: He's a powerful man in this town.
This is a very powerful computer.
He's an expert in this field.
It snows in the mountain regions.

note: feminine: у овој области

examples.en: My brother plays guitar in a band.
What's your favorite band?
I try to buy local products.
This item is currently unavailable.

tips: Навићи се на + acc.: навикла сам се на живот у Србији (I got used to life in Serbia).
forms: навикнем, навикну; навикао; var. навикнути; impf. навикавати

examples.sr: Брзо сам се [навѝкао] на нови посао.
examples.en: I quickly got used to the new job.
I got used to getting up early.

note: навићи се на + acc.: to get used to

examples.en: Whoa, I almost fell!
Wow, look who's here!
You don't have to explain anything to me.
The teacher is explaining the new lesson.
Never mention that name again!
She keeps mentioning her ex.
It's all God's will.
He's late every single blessed day.

tips: A particle of emphasis: «Дај ми макар једну јабуку» - at least one apple; «Он је макар истину рекао» - at least he told the truth. In speech it is often replaced by «бар»/«барем».

examples.en: Give me at least a little water.
I'll come, even if I'm late.
I admit that I made a mistake.
He never admits his mistakes.
In the summer we visited Tara National Park.
Tomorrow is a national holiday.
The knight killed the dragon.
The children are flying a kite in the meadow.
The driver sustained serious injuries.
That's a clear violation of the law.
We ran out of gas on the highway.
The price of fuel is rising again.
You look fantastic!
The vacation was incredibly nice.
I'm watching a new Turkish series.
This is the third series of tests.

note: A TV show is «серија»; a single episode is «епизода».

examples.en: You remind me of my brother.
I remind you that we start earlier tomorrow.

note: подсећати на + acc.: to remind of someone

examples.en: He didn't do it on purpose.
I was late on purpose.
Close the gate behind you.
I'm waiting for you in front of the gate.
Put the cap on the bottle so it doesn't leak.
The sink is clogged again.

note: rude: «зачепи!» - shut up!

examples.en: I like fruit, especially apples.
This applies especially to children.
He has the ability to learn languages quickly.
I believe in your abilities.
The mayor opened the new bridge.
I talked to the mayor.
The entire crew of the ship was rescued.

examples.sr: Капетан и [по̏сада] вам желе пријатан лет.
examples.en: The captain and crew wish you a pleasant flight.
We traveled in business class.
He's a world-class player.

note: A school class is «разред» or «одељење».

examples.en: The sun sets in the west.
Many young people are leaving for the West.

examples.sr: Немојте да се [гу̀рате], има места за све!
examples.en: Don't push, there's room for everyone!
He was pushing a stroller through the park.
He's the best student in the class.
The teacher has thirty pupils.

tips: Of a thing it means «boring, dull»: «досадан филм» - a boring film. Of a person it means «annoying».

examples.en: The movie was terribly boring.
Stop being so annoying!
She works at a travel agency.
We found the apartment through an agency.

examples.sr: Један [ста̏рац] седи на клупи у парку.
examples.en: An old man is sitting on a bench in the park.
He helped the old man cross the street.
That's a very interesting book.
How interesting, I didn't know that.

tips: Feminine: «ова торта», «добра торта». A plainer, everyday kind of cake is «колач».

examples.sr: Мама је испекла [то̏рту] за мој рођендан.
examples.en: Mom baked a cake for my birthday.
Would you like a piece of cake?
All the workers wear a uniform.

examples.sr: На улазу је стајао полицајац у [унѝформи].
examples.en: A policeman in uniform was standing at the entrance.
What do you want to achieve in life?
We finally reached an agreement.
The public has the right to know the truth.
The news quickly became public.
Give me a kiss.
You never forget your first kiss.
He threw the plate in a rage.
He couldn't hold back his anger.
Make me a copy of the contract.
This isn't the original, it's a copy.
The lieutenant gave an order.
Understood, Lieutenant!
Dad is furious with me.
He was bitten by a rabid dog.

note: бесан на + acc.: angry at someone

examples.en: A pipe burst in the bathroom.
He pointed the barrel of the pistol at him.

note: feminine; a musical trumpet is «труба»

examples.en: He keeps his money in a safe.

examples.sr: Лопови су отворили [се̏ф] за пет минута.
examples.en: The thieves opened the safe in five minutes.
I have a business meeting at three.
He went on a business trip.
You look a lot like your father.
I have a similar problem too.

note: сличан + dat.: сличан оцу - like his father

examples.en: Grandpa has two cows in the village.
The cow is grazing peacefully in the meadow.

tips: «Ајде да се скупимо» - let's chip in together (pool money), not only «let's get together».

examples.en: Gather your things and go.
We collected money for a present.

note: not to be confused with «скуп» (adj.) - expensive

examples.en: I like seafood.
The sea air does you good.
You need to rest a little.
We had a good rest by the sea.
The teacher punished him for being late.
The police fined me for speeding.
I've never seen such a crowd.
What do you need such a huge car for?
See you on Monday.
I have an English class on Mondays.

note: «понедељком» - on Mondays

tips: In Serbia «сок» covers not only fresh juice but also boxed juices and sweet sodas (cola, Fanta, Sprite); the Cedevita drink is also called «сок».

examples.en: Do you want orange juice?
The children drink juice instead of water.
A bird is flying high above us.
Their house is high up in the mountains.
He graduated from college two years ago.
She studies at the Faculty of Philology.

note: «завршити факултет» - to graduate from university

examples.en: All the goods are in the warehouse.
He works nights at a warehouse.
My father works at a factory.
The factory was closed ten years ago.
We're looking forward to your arrival.
Let me know your arrival time.

tips: «Висина» means both a person's height (он има два метра висине) and altitude (надморска висина - height above sea level).
To ask how tall a person is, say «Колико си висок?». «С које висине?» - from what height?

examples.en: What is the height of this building?
He's about my height.
She takes great care of her appearance.
What are our chances of winning?
Open your book to page ten.
Check out our website.
The children are playing in the yard.
We have a big yard behind the house.
I've already spent my whole salary.

examples.sr: Не желим да [потро̀шим] цео дан на то.
examples.en: I don't want to spend the whole day on it.
Look at the map to see where we are.
The documents are in the blue folder.
Children love chocolate ice cream.
Let's have an ice cream each.
He has been in trade for twenty years.
Trade with Russia has grown.

note: In Serbia a shop is «продавница».

examples.en: I couldn't see anything in the dark.
My son is afraid of the dark.
We always go to the seaside in summer.
It's very hot here in summer.

tips: It declines like a masculine noun: шоуа, шоуу, шоуом. In compounds it takes a hyphen: ријалити-шоу, ток-шоу, шоу-бизнис.

examples.en: Do you watch that show on TV?
He put on a real show at the wedding.

tips: Утицати на + acc.: «утичем на одлуку» - I influence the decision. Not to be confused with «утисак» (impression) and «утицај» (influence, a noun).

examples.en: The weather affects my mood.

examples.sr: Не дозволи да то [утѝче] на тебе.
examples.en: Don't let it affect you.

note: утицати на + acc.: to affect

examples.en: This is our old family house.
Every Sunday we have a family lunch.
Tonight we're celebrating his birthday.
Our family celebrates the feast of Saint Nicholas, our family patron saint.

note: «слава» - a family feast of the patron saint

examples.en: This is my friend from school.
She went out with her friends.
I read an interesting article in the newspaper.
She writes articles for a magazine.
I missed the train this morning.
Hurry up, we'll be late!

note: закаснити на + acc.: to be late for

examples.en: Grandpa likes to catch fish.
The cat catches mice in the basement.
The old buildings will be torn down next year.
The wind knocked down the tree.

forms: свађам се, свађају се; pf. посвађати се

examples.en: They're always arguing about money.
Kids, don't quarrel!
Birds fly south in the fall.
He was born in the south of Serbia.
All the passengers got out safely.

examples.sr: [Пу̑тнӣци] за Ниш, молимо вас на перон три.
examples.en: Passengers for Niš, please proceed to platform three.
Can we talk in private?
Leave us alone, please.
Put on a jacket, it's cold outside.
Where did you buy that jacket?

tips: «Отказати термин, преглед» - to cancel an appointment, a checkup.

examples.en: We had to cancel the trip.
His brakes failed on the downhill.

examples.sr: Мој деда је [сле̑п] на једно око.
examples.en: My grandfather is blind in one eye.
They say love is blind.

tips: Besides «to kiss», it is an affectionate sign-off or plea among close people: «љубим те, ћао».
«Љубити се» - to kiss each other; «пољубац» - a kiss. «Љуби ме!» - Kiss me!

examples.en: Mom kisses the child on the cheek.
Love you, see you tomorrow!

note: usually «to kiss»; «to love» is «волети»

examples.en: Shortly after that he left.
Soon you'll understand everything.

tips: To watch TV is «гледам телевизију»; the set itself is «телевизор»: «купили смо нови телевизор».

examples.en: What's on TV tonight?
He works as a journalist in television.
I made a cheese sandwich.
Take sandwiches for the trip.

tips: A coffin is «ковчег» or «мртвачки сандук». «Гроб незнаног јунака» - the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

examples.en: Every year we visit Grandpa's grave.
I'll take that secret to my grave.
Learning a language is a long process.
The trial against him begins in May.
Don't you recognize me?
I no longer recognize my city.
Tie your shoelaces so you don't fall.
They tied him to a chair.

tips: Slang for money: «кинта» (from Albanian «kindarka»), «лова» (Romani), «сом» - a thousand, «динђа» - a dinar. All colloquial.
«Ух, која лова!» - wow, what a pile of cash!

examples.en: I don't have the dough for that.
How much money is he asking for the car?

note: colloquial

examples.en: Wait a moment.
He vanished in an instant.

note: «у трену ока» - in the blink of an eye

examples.en: I live on the fourth floor.

examples.sr: Ово ти је већ [чѐтврта] кафа данас.
examples.en: This is already your fourth coffee today.
This is plain deception!
He was arrested for fraud.
The doctor forbade me to smoke.
Smoking is prohibited here.

tips: Also figurative: «остати у нечијој сенци» - to remain in someone's shadow. Cool shade can also be «хлад» or «хладовина».
«Сенка за очи» is eyeshadow: «купила сам нову сенку».

examples.en: We're sitting in the shade of a tree.
He's afraid of his own shadow.
Is it worth the effort?
She worked hard all day.

tips: Combinations: трговински ланац - retail chain, ланчана реакција - chain reaction, ланчани судар - pileup, планински ланац - mountain range, ланчић - small chain.

examples.en: The dog was tied up on a chain.
This store belongs to a big chain.
He owns three apartments downtown.
Do you hold a driver's license?
You drive like a maniac!
He's not crazy, he's just different.

tips: Not only a crush: a packed schedule («у гужви сам»), a crowd at the market, lots of people in town («гужва је у граду»), traffic jams («гужва је на путу», «каснимо»).

examples.en: On Saturdays there's a huge crowd downtown.
I'm late, I'm stuck in traffic on the bridge.

note: «гужва» - both a crowd and a traffic jam

examples.en: The hotel staff is very friendly.
The hospital lacks medical staff.
You owe me an explanation.
There must be a logical explanation.
He goes to therapy twice a week.
The doctor prescribed him a new treatment.
The enemy captured ten soldiers.

examples.sr: Два сата смо били [заро̀бљени] у лифту.
examples.en: We were trapped in the elevator for two hours.
Something here smells terrible.
Your socks stink!
Did I fill out the form correctly?
The device is working properly now.
After work go straight home.
Ask him directly, no beating around the bush.
What kind of mess is this?!

examples.sr: После утакмице је било [нѐреда] у граду.
examples.en: After the match there were riots in the city.
This week I have a lot of things to do.
You're not obliged to come.
Catch the ball!
I'm starting to get sleepy.
I'm very disappointed in you.
She was disappointed with the result.

note: разочаран + instr.: разочаран тобом - disappointed in you

examples.en: Scientists have discovered a new species of frog.
When I grow up, I'll be a scientist.
They got lost in the desert.

examples.sr: У [пу̀стињи] скоро никад не пада киша.
examples.en: It almost never rains in the desert.
We climbed up a tall rock.
He's solid as a rock.

tips: Plural: «греси» (the older, native form) or «грехови» (later); both are correct. The adjective is «грешан».

examples.en: It's a sin to throw away food.
He confessed his sins.
The child has too many toys.
Pick the toys up off the floor.
Don't eat so many sweets.
Children adore sweets.
I speak Russian and a little Serbian.
I like Russian literature.

note: говорим руски - I speak Russian

examples.en: I'm starving!

examples.sr: Многи у свету још пате од [гла̑ди].
examples.en: Many people in the world still suffer from hunger.

note: feminine: велика глад

examples.en: I've been to Paris twice.

examples.sr: Размисли [два́пут] пре него што нешто кажеш.
examples.en: Think twice before you say anything.
The guests are sitting in the living room.
What is the daily dose of this medicine?

note: дневна соба - living room

examples.en: What are you doing, for God's sake?
For God's sake, leave me alone!

tips: Slang: «запалити» - to bail, to run away («он ће да запали», «палимо кући»); also «палити» - to deceive, to string along. The basic meaning is to set on fire.

examples.en: He lit a cigarette on the terrace.
Someone set a car on fire last night.

note: colloquial «запалити» - to take off, to leave

examples.en: Son, come over here for a moment!
Listen, son, life isn't easy.

note: an older person addressing a boy or young man

examples.sr: Под овим [о̀колностима] не могу да помогнем.
examples.en: Under these circumstances I can't help.
It was an unfortunate set of circumstances.
I want to express my gratitude.
We gratefully accept your help.
The car is in the garage.
Park in the underground garage.

tips: A general schedule of tasks and classes («школски распоред» - school timetable). For transport it is «ред вожње», for flights «ред летова»; a schedule with exact times is «сатница».

examples.en: What's your schedule for tomorrow?
They changed the class schedule.

tips: «Порота» - the jury, «поротни суд» - a jury trial. Also: «судница» - courtroom, «оптужница» - indictment.

examples.en: The jury found him guilty.

examples.sr: Чланови [по̀роте] су се повукли на већање.
examples.en: The jury members retired to deliberate.
A guard stands in front of the palace.
Who's on guard duty tonight?
What material is this dress made of?
I'm collecting material for a new book.
This juice tastes disgusting.
He was vile to her.
The police took away his driver's license.

examples.sr: Ако од десет [оду̀змеш] три, остаје седам.
examples.en: If you subtract three from ten, seven remains.
He traveled all over the world.
The door was wide open.
They took him in for questioning.
The opinion poll shows something different.

tips: «Пријатно!» is not only «enjoy your meal» but also a parting «all the best», for example to a shopkeeper or waiter. Informally also «Уживај!».

examples.sr: Било ми је веома [при̏ја̄тно] код вас.
examples.en: I felt very comfortable at your place.
Lunch is on the table, bon appétit!

note: «Пријатно!» - enjoy your meal; also «all the best» when parting

examples.en: Passenger safety comes first.
Fasten your seat belts for your safety.
What you're doing is sheer madness.
The concert was insane!

examples.sr: На Земљи живи више од осам [милѝја̄рдӣ] људи.
examples.en: More than eight billion people live on Earth.
The new bridge cost a billion dinars.

note: feminine: једна милијарда

examples.en: We opened the champagne at midnight.
Would you like a glass of champagne?

note: masculine: хладан шампањац

examples.en: We were all at the funeral.
The funeral will be on Friday.

note: singular: «сахрана» - a funeral

examples.en: Health is the greatest wealth.
He inherited an enormous fortune.

tips: Spelled with т: претпоставити, претпостављам (not «предпоставити»); the prefix пред- becomes прет- before п.

examples.en: Let's suppose he's right.
I assumed you weren't at home.

note: «претпостављам» - I suppose, probably

examples.en: Look at yourself in the mirror.
The cat broke the mirror.
You look beautiful in that dress.
It was beautiful at the wedding.

tips: As a reply, «Свашта!» can also mean "nonsense, what rubbish", showing contempt for what was said. Similar words: «глупости», «бесмислица».

examples.en: All sorts of things happen in life.
Unbelievable! Who would have thought?

note: exclamation «Свашта!» - unbelievable!, what nonsense!

examples.en: This summer we're going to Greece.
Summer is my favorite season.

note: «лети» means in summer; years of age are «година», not «лета».

examples.en: Grandpa still listens to old records.

examples.sr: На зиду је [пло̏ча] са именима палих војника.
examples.en: On the wall there's a plaque with the names of fallen soldiers.
This is my future husband.

examples.sr: Морамо да сачувамо природу за [бу̀дуће] генерације.
examples.en: We must protect nature for future generations.

note: «будући да» means «since, given that»

examples.en: Grandpa's eyesight keeps getting worse.
This is a perfective verb.

note: «поглед» is the word for a view from a window

examples.en: There are rats in the basement.
He's a real rat!

tips: Гума is the tire, точак is the wheel: «Издувала ми се гума, морам да је напумпам» - my tire has gone flat, I need to pump it up.

examples.en: I got a flat tire on the road.
Do you have an eraser?

note: «гума за брисање» - eraser; «гума за жвакање» - chewing gum

examples.sr: Неко му је ставио [о̀тров] у пиће.
examples.en: Someone put poison in his drink.
This mushroom is pure poison.
Her eyes were full of tears.
We laughed until we cried.
What is your favorite dish?
Sarma is a traditional Serbian dish.

forms: попнем се, попну се; попео се; impf. пењати се

examples.en: We climbed to the top of the mountain.

examples.sr: [По̀пни] се на столицу и дохвати кутију.
examples.en: Climb up on the chair and reach the box.
It's snowing outside.
The kids are having a snowball fight in the snow.

examples.sr: После земљотреса у граду је владао [ха̏ос].
examples.en: After the earthquake, chaos reigned in the city.
My room is a complete mess.
The sun rises in the east.
We traveled east.
We don't have that many options.
Giving up is not an option.

examples.sr: Полиција мисли да је то било [самоуби́ство].
examples.en: The police think it was suicide.

examples.sr: Возити по овом снегу је право [самоуби́ство].
examples.en: Driving in this snow is real suicide.
Man is a social being.
All living beings deserve respect.

note: Not to be confused with «биће» - 'will be' (from бити)

examples.en: Slow down, you're driving too fast!
We need to slow the pace down a bit.
Turn off all electronic devices.
This device measures blood pressure.

related.en: to arrange, to put in order

examples.en: This is the last warning!
He paid no attention to the warnings.

tips: Usually used in the plural: «суве усне» (dry lips), «кармин на усне» (lipstick on the lips). The singular «усна» is one lip.

examples.en: She has nice full lips.
He bit his lip.
What happened? It's awful, just awful!
The party last night was awesome!

note: colloq. «страва!» can mean both «awful» and «awesome»

forms: предомислим се, предомисле се; impf. предомишљати се

examples.en: I changed my mind, I'm staying after all.
If you change your mind, let me know.
The bomb exploded in the city center.
My head is going to explode from work!
He kept his promise.

examples.sr: Не дај [обѐћања] која не можеш да испуниш.
examples.en: Don't make promises you can't keep.
Please hear me out.
The police will question the witnesses tomorrow.
Have you read today's newspaper?
Kids today are always glued to their phones.
The daughter adores her daddy.
Daddy will buy you an ice cream.

note: Masculine, although it ends in -а

examples.en: We're working on a new project.
The project has to be ready by Friday.
He is tall and strong.
A strong wind was blowing last night.
He has a great influence on her.
He was driving under the influence of alcohol.
You spend too much on clothes.
This car uses little fuel.
I'm too old for parties like that.

examples.sr: [Ма̀тори] ми не да ауто за викенд.
examples.en: My old man won't let me have the car for the weekend.

note: colloq.; «матори» - father, 'the old man'

examples.en: He ate half of the cake.
The second half of the movie is much better.
It's twenty degrees outside.
You're right to some extent.
Who runs this company?
He doesn't know how to steer a ship.

note: «управљати» + instr.: «управљати фирмом» (to run a company)

examples.en: I love Chinese food.
He has been studying Chinese for two years.
Anyway, do whatever you want.
It doesn't really matter, after all.
Don't worry, it's just a phase.
The project is in its final stage.
Our friendship has lasted twenty years.
He values friendship above everything.

In the evening we philosophized over wine.

Bring me one cup, please.

An old Fića is parked in front of the building.

note: a symbol of the Yugoslav era

examples.en: Put a Band-Aid on the wound.
Do you have a Band-Aid?

note: neutral word; people often say «ханзапласт», after the brand

examples.sr: Моја ћерка свира [фла̀уту] у школском оркестру.
examples.en: My daughter plays the flute in the school orchestra.
The sound of the flute is very gentle.

note: «фрула» - a folk shepherd's flute

I bought a small bottle of juice.

This detergent removes all stains.

note: colloquial, from German Fleck

examples.en: The working hours are flexible.
We have to be flexible.

Don't show off, everyone gets it.

note: youth slang, from English flex

This marker has dried out.
A seal is lying on the rock.
The children like the show with seals.
Surely we won't fall for that trick?
We're supposedly working.

note: colloquial; used as an adverb in the sense of «supposedly»

examples.en: Create a new folder on the desktop.

examples.sr: Све слике сам сместио у један [фо̏лдер].
examples.en: I put all the photos in one folder.
Cheap poser!
Now everyone knows what a faker you are.

examples.en: He's faking chest pains.

note: colloquial; with «се» - to put on airs: «не фолирај се»

meanings: to pretend, to put on airs (colloquial)

examples.en: Don't pretend.
He pretends to know everything.

note: slang

examples.en: This is a formal letter to the director.
He was very formal at the meeting.

note: adverb: формално; opposite: неформално

examples.sr: У мојој соби је дубока мека [фо̀теља].
examples.en: There is a deep, soft armchair in my room.
Grandpa is sleeping in the armchair.
I like to photograph nature.
Taking photos is not allowed here.

note: Bookish; in speech «сликати» is more common.

examples.en: You need a copy of your passport.
Where can I make a photocopy?

forms: gen. фреске; gen. pl. фресака / фреска

examples.en: There are beautiful frescoes in the monastery.
They restored the old fresco.
I booked an appointment with the hairdresser.
My hairdresser works on Saturdays.

note: Female: «фризерка».

examples.en: My hairdresser works downtown.
The hairdresser cut my hair short.
I work as a freelancer from home.
Freelancers look for clients on their own.
I fry French fries in a deep fryer.
We bought an air fryer.
My brother is a professional soccer player.
All the players came out onto the field.
The phone has a protective case.
She put her glasses in the case.

examples.sr: За десерт смо јели [ха̏лву] са орасима.
examples.en: For dessert we had halva with walnuts.
Grandma makes homemade halva.
The bandit chief led a band of outlaws.
My son is a real little rascal.

note: Affectionate, for a lively boy.

examples.en: There is salted herring on the table.
Frozen herring must be thawed.
Grandpa plays the accordion at weddings.
You can hear an accordion from the tavern.

We bought paper for the printer.

note: Formal; in daily use «папир» is more common; «тоалет-хартија» is toilet paper.

examples.en: She has been playing the harp for ten years.
There are two harps in the orchestra.
Let's grab a bite after work.
Yesterday we had ćevapi downtown.

note: Colloquial, slang.

examples.en: Lift the hood so we can look at the engine.
Smoke is coming from under the hood.
The handyman fixed the front gate.
Call the handyman, the faucet is leaking.

note: Colloquial.

examples.en: We called a handyman to fix the faucet.
Our handyman is coming tomorrow.

note: Colloquial; a German loanword.

examples.en: Folk songs sing about hajduks.
The hajduk fought against the Turks.
Mom is crocheting a tablecloth.
I want to learn to crochet.

note: A German loanword.

Grandma is teaching me to crochet.

She wears black leggings and a long T-shirt.

My pen doesn't write anymore.

note: short for «хемијска оловка»

Hernia surgery takes about an hour.

Lend me the stapler, please.

I'm looking for a hatchback with an automatic transmission.

People love to hate on social media.

examples.en: Don't bash anyone if you don't know what happened.

note: Slang.

examples.en: I'm cooking buckwheat for lunch.
The store has two kinds of buckwheat.
I drink hibiscus tea.
Hibiscus blooms in summer.
Personal hygiene is very important.
Children learn about hygiene at school.
In winter the skin needs more moisture.
Drink water to keep your body well hydrated.

examples.sr: Она је веома [хѝровита] када је уморна.
examples.en: She is very moody when she is tired.
The weather is changeable today.
She was in the surgical ward.
Surgery is needed.
He is a quick and skilled worker.
The cat is a nimble hunter.

examples.en: Let's sit in the shade under the tree.

examples.en: It's pleasant in the shade, but hot in the sun.
We are sitting in the shade under the tree.
Let's go into the shade!

note: Colloquially «ладовина».

examples.en: Raspberries are kept in cold storage.
I work at a cold-storage plant near the city.
Beer gets its bitterness from hops.
Hops are grown in Vojvodina.
An octopus has eight arms.

examples.sr: Салата од [хобо̀тнице] је специјалитет на обали.
examples.en: Octopus salad is a specialty of the coast.
Grandma uses a walker in the house.
We bought a walker for Grandpa.

examples.sr: Лекар каже да ми је [холестѐрол] повишен.

The test shows high cholesterol.

Stress affects hormones.
I read my daily horoscope every morning.
Do you believe in horoscopes?
This hydrangea has blue flowers.
Hydrangeas grow best in the shade.

Birds come to the feeder in winter.
Oatmeal is nutritious.
We need a more substantial breakfast.
The old oak gives shade.
The furniture is made of oak.

examples.sr: За доручак смо јели [хрѐновке] и сенф.
examples.en: For breakfast we had frankfurters and mustard.
Buy some frankfurters at the store.

Grandpa is snoring on the couch.

It's a chronic problem.
The crust of the bread is crispy.
I like crispy French fries.

The ear is made of cartilage.

The owner takes the greyhound to a race.

We bought a hamster for the kids.
I wear warm tights under my dress.
I bought black tights.

note: Plural only.

examples.en: The police arrested several hooligans.

examples.sr: Те [ху̀лигане] треба држати даље од стадиона.
examples.en: Those hooligans must be kept away from the stadium.

note: A harsh word; not used for a child.

examples.en: The organization is sending humanitarian aid.
A charity event was held.
I saw your girl in town.
Who is that girl with you?

note: Colloquial, slang.

examples.sr: На граници смо дуго чекали на [царѝни].
examples.en: We waited a long time at customs at the border.

examples.en: You have to pay duty on this perfume.
She is a real queen of the kitchen.
You're amazing, you got everything done!

note: «Баш си цар/царица!» means "you're awesome, respect".

examples.en: Beet salad is red.
Boiled beets go well with meat.
The blossoming of the fruit trees begins in April.
I love the cherry trees in bloom.
I bought a bouquet at the flower shop.
The flower shop is next to the market.
Where are my glasses?
Put your glasses on so you can see better.

note: Colloquial.

The puppy is whimpering because it's hungry.

I love the chirping outside my window.
Birds are chirping on the branches.
Sparrows are chirping outside the window.
A cricket sings in the grass at night.
The sound of cicadas reminds me of summer.

A cloth tote replaces a plastic bag.

note: A cloth bag with long handles.

examples.en: She is squeezing a lemon for lemonade.
Strain the tea through a sieve.
Drain the pasta through a colander.
I strained the tea through a strainer.
Take a shopping bag when you go to the market.
Grandma is pulling a shopping bag on wheels.

note: Colloquial, especially in Vojvodina; «кеса» is a plastic bag.

examples.en: There is celery root in the soup too.
Celery root puree is healthy.

examples.sr: На пијаци се [це̏нкам] за сваку цену.
examples.en: At the market I haggle over every price.
I don't like to haggle.

Tenants pay for central heating by floor area.

His friends ripped his shirt.
Don't be a nitpicker, it's not that important.
Our boss is a terrible nitpicker.

note: Literally: one who splits a hair.

examples.en: You can't do winter climbing without an ice ax.
He forgot the ice ax in the car.

examples.sr: Цео разред се [цѐрека] због његове шале.
examples.en: The whole class is howling at his joke.
What are you cackling about like a madman?

note: colloquial, sometimes a bit rude

examples.sr: Не волим да се [цѐњкам] на пијаци.
examples.en: I don't like to haggle at the market.

examples.sr: Они су се дуго [цѐњкали] око цене.
examples.en: They haggled over the price for a long time.

note: Colloquial.

Cyclamen likes a cool room.
The road zigzags up the mountain.
The hare ran away in zigzags.

note: Usually «у цикцак».

examples.en: She keeps pestering me to help her.
Stop bugging me over silly things.

note: Slang.

examples.en: Don't stress, everything will be fine.

examples.sr: Нема потребе да се [ци̏мате] због тога.
examples.en: There is no need to stress about it.

note: Slang, usually in the imperative: «не цимај се».

Apples with cinnamon are my favorite.

note: Colloquial: «цимни ме» means call or text me.

note: Colloquial.

note: Usually plural.

The small intestine digests food.

note: Rude.

Old chakshire are on display in the museum.

note: Part of the traditional men's folk costume.

note: Colloquial, humorous: just a little, then it all gets eaten.

Don't be a grouch, smile a little.

note: Colloquial; a neuter noun used of anyone.

I can't find the other sock.

note: Singular «чарапа» is one sock.

The good sorceress granted the wish.

The sheet is cotton.

note: Figuratively, the townspeople and their gossip.

My grandfather was a watchmaker.

He is picking his teeth with a toothpick.

He got fried to a crisp in the sun.

note: Plural; the singular is «чварак».

Ice will reduce the bump.

note: Colloquial.

I long for the sea.

I'm happy even with a 4.

note: Grade 4 out of 5, in words «врло добар» (very good).

examples.en: Our team reached the quarterfinal.
The quarterfinal is played tomorrow evening.
I bought a new toothbrush.
Clean the floor with a stiff brush.

meanings: «чешати се» to itch, to scratch oneself

examples.en: The dog is scratching behind its ear.
I've been itching from mosquito bites all night.

note: Not to be confused with «чешљати» - to comb hair.

I always carry a comb in my bag.

I'm chopping three cloves of garlic.

The child loves her little red boots.

note: Diminutive of «чизме»; also means ankle boots.

note: Youth slang.

examples.en: Grandpa is still hale and hearty.

note: Often in the pair «чио и здрав» (hale and hearty).

I stepped on a thumbtack.

The school cleaner has already gone home.

The reader should draw the conclusion himself.
At school we read from the reader.
I bought a reader for second grade.

A death notice is pasted on the pole.

note: In Serbia they are customarily posted on poles and building entrances.

examples.en: The children's sneakers have Velcro straps.

note: «На чичак» means with Velcro.

Dude, what are you doing?

note: Vocative of «човек»; also an exclamation of emotion, not only a form of address.

examples.en: Many dream of returning from abroad.

note: Colloquially, abroad is «преко» (lit. over there).

note: Serbian has names for ancestors back to the 16th generation.

A human has five senses.

examples.en: Don't pull the cat's tail!

The dog is limping on one leg.

note: Colloquial.

Rabbits love carrots.

The carpet is very colorful.

note: A floral dress is «цветна хаљина».

note: Colloquial; ironic: «шатро је».

examples.en: He took a handful of nuts.

He has wacky ideas.

meanings: typically Serbian ways, things that happen only in Serbia

examples.en: The bus is late - typical Serbia!

note: People also say «балканска посла» for things typical of the Balkans.

meanings: a Christmas greeting; the reply is «Ваистину се роди!»

examples.en: - Christ is born! - Truly he is born!

note: To simply wish someone well, say «Срећан Божић!». Orthodox Christmas in Serbia is on January 7.

meanings: a polite closing formula for a letter

examples.sr: Хвала на пажњи. [С пошто̀вањем], Марко Петровић.
examples.en: Thank you for your attention. Sincerely, Marko Petrović.

note: For informal cards: «с љубављу».

meanings: a warm sign-off on a card or letter

examples.sr: Срећна Нова година! [С љу̀бављу], твоја Ана.
