examples.en: Happy New Year! With love, your Ana.

forms: literally: slides like a kitten down a gutter
meanings: goes smoothly, like clockwork; of a drink, goes down easily

examples.sr: Посао нам иде [ка̏о ма̏че ни̏з о̀лук].
examples.en: Our work is going like clockwork.
The rakija goes down easily.

note: Most often said of a drink that goes down without effort.

forms: literally: the circle of the two
meanings: the area of Belgrade enclosed by the loop of tram line 2

examples.en: I live inside the number 2 loop.

note: A line number is named with a feminine noun: двојка, тројка, петица, деветка. The same goes for trolleybus and bus lines.

forms: literally: you are missing one paper
meanings: a joke about bureaucracy: you're missing one more document

examples.sr: Жао ми је, [фа̏ли вам јѐдан па̀пӣр].
examples.en: I'm sorry, you're missing one more paper.

note: Abbreviated ФТЈП. You expect to hear it from the clerk at the counter when you think all the documents are collected.

examples.en: Thursday is neither here nor there.

note: People joke that Thursday is the middle of the week: «Четвртак - ни тамо ни овамо».

examples.en: He isn't easy to reach by phone.
Why didn't you call me back right away?

examples.sr: Није [глу̑п ка̏о ма̀гарац], само је ћутљив.
examples.en: He isn't stupid, he's just quiet.

note: The donkey also stands for stubbornness: «тврдоглав као магарац».

key: phr:моје срце куца само за тебе
cyr: моје срце куца само за тебе.
acc: мо̀је ср̏це ку́ца са̏мо за те̏бе.
forms: literally: my heart beats only for you

examples.sr: Љубави моја, [мо̀је ср̏це ку́ца са̏мо за те̏бе]!
examples.en: My love, my heart beats only for you!

note: Fits a card for Valentine's Day (February 14).

examples.en: I have to go, see you tomorrow!

note: Among friends, when you expect to meet soon.

meanings: talk to you later, we'll be in touch

examples.en: Thanks for the help, talk soon!

note: A very common goodbye when you want to stay in touch.

examples.en: Have a good trip, take care!

note: Concern for someone close; the polite form is «чувајте се».

examples.en: I'm going to bed, good night!

note: Also said as a farewell late in the evening.

examples.en: Have a good time at the seaside, enjoy!

note: A wish for someone who is about to do something pleasant. The polite form is «уживајте».

meanings: the relationship fell apart, the friendship is over

examples.sr: Били су другови, али је [пу̏кла ти̏ква].
examples.en: They were friends, but then it all fell apart.

note: Said when everything goes wrong after a quarrel.

meanings: I lost my patience, I snapped

examples.sr: Три сата у гужви и [пу̏као ми је фи̏лм].
examples.en: Three hours in a traffic jam, and I snapped.

note: A colloquial expression; the verb agrees with «филм».

forms: literally: to burst at the seams
meanings: to come apart at the seams, to fall apart

examples.sr: План ће [пу̏ћи по ша̀вовима] ако не нађемо решење.
examples.en: The plan will fall apart if we don't find a solution.

forms: literally: to burst like a rattle
meanings: to fall apart, to break down, also emotionally

examples.sr: Ауто је стар, једног дана ће [пу̏ћи ка̏о звѐчка].
examples.en: The car is old, one day it will fall apart.

examples.sr: У нашем крају има много паса [лу́талица].
examples.en: There are a lot of stray dogs in our neighborhood.

note: Plural: «пси луталице».

forms: literally: do you get off at the next one?
meanings: a question on public transport: are you getting off at the next stop?

examples.en: Excuse me, are you getting off at the next stop?

note: Used to ask someone to let you through to the door. Other questions: «Која је следећа станица?» (What is the next stop?), «Када полази следећи воз?» (When does the next train leave?).

forms: literally: go to three beautiful ones
meanings: get lost, go away (a mild euphemism for a rude phrase)

examples.sr: Остави ме на миру, [ѝди у три̏ лѐпе]!
examples.en: Leave me alone, get lost!

note: The last word is left out. A playful rhyming variant: «иди у три лепе шаргарепе». Not for formal settings, but you will hear it in films.

meanings: to put an end to, to wrap up

examples.sr: Време је да [ста̀вимо та̏чку] на ту причу.
examples.en: It's time to put an end to that story.

note: Similar: «ставити питање» - to ask a question, «ставити услов» - to set a condition.

examples.sr: Стигао је [у мѝнӯт до два́нае̄ст], али је стигао!
examples.en: He arrived at the last second, but he made it!

examples.sr: Пријавила сам се [у мѝнӯт до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: I registered at the very last moment.

note: Said of someone who made it in time at the very last moment.

forms: literally: to fall onto the mind
meanings: to come to mind, to occur to someone

examples.en: What were you thinking? (What came into your head?)

note: The person takes the dative, the thing that occurs is the subject.

meanings: to faint; to be in shock

examples.sr: Пала је [у не̏све̄ст] кад је сазнала вести.
examples.en: She fainted when she heard the news.

note: Figuratively: «Пали смо у несвест после тог сусрета» - we were in shock after that meeting.

forms: literally: to fall into the eyes
meanings: to catch the eye, to stand out

examples.sr: Пао ми је [у о̏чи] овај леп шешир.
examples.en: This nice hat caught my eye.

forms: literally: to fall at an exam

examples.en: The student failed the exam.
I would never fall for that.

forms: literally: to go out to a meeting

examples.en: I'm going on a date with her tonight.

note: Colloquially - «дејт».

forms: literally: to be in a connection

examples.en: They have been together for a year now.

note: Colloquially - «забављати се». To break up: «раскинути»; to end a relationship: «прекинути везу с неким».

forms: literally: to hold on to each other's hands

examples.sr: Шетају парком и [др̀же̄ се за ру̑ке].
examples.en: They walk in the park holding hands.

examples.sr: Одлучила је да [прѐкине ве́зӯ] са њим.
examples.en: She decided to break up with him.

note: A colloquial variant is «раскинути».

examples.en: Belgrade is expecting an Indian summer.

note: Named after Михољдан, October 12. The other form is «бабље лето».

meanings: said of a person whose mood and opinions change quickly

examples.sr: Не могу да га разумем, [промѐнљив је ка̏о јѐсење вре́ме].
examples.en: I can't understand him, he's as changeable as the autumn weather.

meanings: weak autumn sun that shines but gives no warmth

examples.sr: Изашло је [зу̀бато су̑нце], али дува хладан ветар.
examples.en: The sun came out, but a cold wind is blowing.

forms: literally: to get drenched to bare skin
meanings: to get soaked to the skin

examples.sr: Нисам имао кишобран, па сам [покѝснуо до го̀ле ко̏же].
examples.en: I didn't have an umbrella, so I got soaked to the skin.

forms: literally: rain falls, it would kill a mouse
meanings: it's pouring, it's raining cats and dogs

examples.sr: Види какво је време, [па̏да ки̏ша у̀би ми̏ша]!
examples.en: Look at the weather, it's pouring!

note: A rhyming expression for heavy rain.

examples.sr: Рекла сам [бѐлу ла̑ж] да га не повредим.
examples.en: I told a white lie so as not to hurt him.

meanings: a person who stands out from the others, an odd one out

examples.en: In this company I'm the odd one out.

examples.sr: Од малена је [цр̏на о́вца] у породици.
examples.en: Since childhood he has been the black sheep of the family.
The country is facing a falling birth rate.

meanings: to be pessimistic, to see the dark side

examples.sr: Не [гле̏да̄ј цр̏но], биће све у реду.
examples.en: Don't be so pessimistic, everything will be fine.

note: The opposite - «гледати бело» - means to stare blankly, not understanding anything.

meanings: a day of bad luck and misfortune; a rainy day

examples.en: You should save for a rainy day.
I'm at a crossroads in my life.

key: phr:бити као бадњи дан и божић
cyr: бити као Бадњи дан и Божић
acc: би̏ти ка̏о Ба̑дњи да̑н и Бо̀жић
forms: literally: to be like Christmas Eve and Christmas

examples.sr: Њих двоје [су ка̏о Ба̑дњи да̑н и Бо̀жић], увек заједно.
examples.en: Those two are inseparable, always together.

note: Бадњи дан is January 6, Божић is January 7, two holidays next to each other. Said of close friends.

meanings: out of turn, cutting in line

examples.sr: Извините, могу ли да уђем [пре̏ко ре̑да]?
examples.en: Excuse me, may I go in out of turn?

note: At a clinic: «Само нешто да питам» (I only have a question), «Могу ли ја пре Вас?» (May I go before you?).

forms: literally: to sway between two extremes
meanings: to swing between two extremes, to waver between opposite decisions

examples.sr: Дуго сам се [љу̀љао и̏змеђу две̑ кра́јности].
examples.en: I wavered between the two extremes for a long time.

note: Also used of an unstable situation: «политичка сцена се љуља».

meanings: the Easter greeting; the reply is «Ваистину васкрсе!»

examples.en: - Christ is risen! - Indeed He is risen!

note: This is the church form with ва-. To simply wish someone a happy Easter, say «Срећан Васкрс!» or «Срећан Ускрс!».

forms: literally: to remain in someone's shadow

examples.sr: Цео живот је [о̀стао у сѐнци] старијег брата.
examples.en: All his life he stayed in his older brother's shadow.
Don't go out, it's hell out there.

note: A colloquial expression about heat.

meanings: out of spite, to spite someone

examples.en: He did it to spite everyone.
He parked there to spite his neighbor.

note: Инат is stubbornness, the urge to do the opposite of what is expected. A very Serbian idea.

examples.en: You're lucky.
She has a talent for singing.

note: имати + genitive: имати среће, дара, разума - with a sense of «possessing» some of it.

meanings: may I join in? (a queue, a game)

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да се уба̀цим?] Нас је четворо.
examples.en: May I join in? There are four of us.

note: In a gym, this is how you ask to share a machine and take turns with someone.

meanings: what do you do (for a living or as a hobby)?

examples.en: What do you do? - I work as a programmer.

note: бавити се + instrumental. Formal: «Чиме се бавите?»

key: phr:драго ми је што смо се упознали
cyr: драго ми је што смо се упознали
acc: дра̑го ми је што̏ смо се упо̀знали

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је што̏ смо се упо̀знали.] - Такође.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. - Likewise.

note: The reply is «Такође» (likewise).

forms: literally: to come out at the end
meanings: to cope, to manage, to get the better of

examples.sr: Једва сам [иза̀шао на кра̑ј] са папирима.
examples.en: I barely managed to get through the paperwork.

examples.sr: Не могу да [ѝзађем на кра̑ј] са овом децом.
examples.en: I can't cope with these kids.

note: Usually with «са + instr.»: изаћи на крај са неким/нечим.

meanings: to take a chance, to roll the dice

examples.sr: Одлучио је да [ба̏ци ко̏цку] и отвори радњу.
examples.en: He decided to take a chance and open a shop.

note: Related: «коцка је пала» - the die is cast, the decision is made.

examples.en: The decision has been made, the die is cast.
See you at eight? - Okay!

examples.sr: Ти плаћаш кафу, а ја колаче. - [Ва́жи].
examples.en: You pay for the coffee and I'll pay for the cakes. - Deal.

note: With «ма» («ма важи») it sounds ironic: yeah, sure, right.

examples.sr: Мораш све да научиш до сутра! - [Ма̏ ва́жи].
examples.en: You have to learn it all by tomorrow! - Yeah, sure.

note: Sarcasm: the speaker has no intention of doing it.

examples.sr: Дошао је ред да и ти [одрѐшиш ке̏су].
examples.en: Now it's your turn to cough up.

note: A colloquial expression. Similar in meaning: «машити се џепа» - to reach for one's wallet.

meanings: to reach for one's wallet, to pay

examples.en: He was the first to reach for his wallet.
I prefer to pay in cash.
Can you pay by card?

note: Also: «у готовини» - in cash, «картицом» - by card.

examples.en: Slow down, there's a speed bump here.

note: Literally a «lying policeman».

examples.sr: На [кру̏жном то̀ку] скрени на другом излазу.
examples.en: At the roundabout, take the second exit.

examples.sr: Личим не на мајку, [ве̏ћ] на бабу.
examples.en: I look like my grandmother, not my mother.

examples.sr: Не [и̏дем] на посао, већ на састанак.
examples.en: I'm not going to work, but to a meeting.

note: The negation can go before the verb or before the contrasted element.

examples.en: Thank you very much for your help!

note: A polite reply is «молим лепо» (you're welcome).

examples.en: Thanks! - You're welcome.

note: «Молим» alone also covers both «please» and «you're welcome».

examples.sr: [Ле̑по сам ти ре̏као] да не касниш.
examples.en: I told you not to be late.

note: «Лепо» expresses reproach here: it was said clearly and in a friendly way.

forms: literally: it stands beautifully on you
meanings: it looks good on you, it suits you (clothes)

examples.en: This jacket looks good on you.
Good night, sweet dreams!

examples.sr: [Ле̑по је ви̏дети те] после толико времена.
examples.en: It's nice to see you after such a long time.

note: The polite form: «лепо је видети вас».

meanings: to show off, to put on airs

examples.en: Why are you putting on airs?
Who's putting on airs here?

note: Said playfully to a shy child who turns away from guests.

forms: literally: to know what you are standing on

examples.sr: Када су цене јасне, [зна̑ш на чѐму си].
examples.en: When the prices are clear, you know where you stand.
I want to know where I stand.

note: About clarity in business and relationships.

examples.en: You're right.
He's not right.

note: Not to be confused with «право» - straight ahead: «иди право».

forms: literally: to learn onto the mind
meanings: to learn by heart, to memorize

examples.en: I don't like to memorize things.

examples.sr: Желим да ми сир буде [у ко̏маду].
examples.en: I want the cheese in one piece.

note: In a shop, you say this if you don't want your cheese or cold cuts sliced.

examples.en: I'd like to order food to go.

note: Pronounced as a single unit.

examples.en: No way! Really?

note: «Ма» strengthens the emotion, «иди» is not about walking here.

meanings: I have a reservation under the name ...

examples.sr: Добар дан, [ѝма̄м резерва̀цију на и̏ме] Петровић.
examples.en: Good afternoon, I have a reservation under the name Petrović.

meanings: may I register? (may I check in?)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [мо̀гу ли да се при̏јавим]?
examples.en: Good afternoon, may I check in?

note: At a hotel: пријава means check-in.

forms: literally: fell off a pear tree
meanings: to be bewildered, to be clueless

examples.sr: Шта гледаш, јеси ли [па̏о с кру̏шке]?
examples.en: What are you staring at, did you just fall out of the sky?

note: Said of someone who is confused or unaware of something obvious.

forms: literally: from the sky and into the ribs

examples.sr: Та вест дошла је [с не̏ба па у рѐбра].
examples.en: That news came out of the blue.

forms: literally: whoever gets to the girl first, she is his girl

examples.sr: Нисам хтео да чекам - [ко̏ пре̏ дѐво̄јци, њѐгова дѐво̄јка].
examples.en: I didn't want to wait: first come, first served.

note: A proverb: the quickest one wins.

examples.en: Lend you money? Not a chance!

note: A sharp, ironic «no».

meanings: to put in order, to sort out

examples.en: I have to sort out my documents.

forms: literally: when grapes grow on a willow

examples.sr: Он ће вратити дуг [ка̏д на вр̏би ро̏ди гро̑жђе].
examples.en: He will pay back the debt when pigs fly.

forms: literally: to buy a cat in a sack
meanings: to buy a pig in a poke

examples.sr: Не волим да [ку̏пим ма̏чку у џа̏ку].
examples.en: I don't like to buy a pig in a poke.

forms: literally: to be on a horse
meanings: to be in the saddle, to be in a winning position

examples.sr: Сад си [на ко̀њу] - имаш посао и стан.
examples.en: Now you're in a good position: you have a job and an apartment.
The sooner we get home, the better.

note: On its own «што пре» means as soon as possible. Do not confuse with «брже-боље» - in a rush.

examples.en: He prepared dinner in a rush.
You passed the exam? Well done!
You're doing great with Serbian!
I'm grateful to you for everything.

note: A woman says «захвална сам ти».

forms: literally: to fall off one's feet
meanings: to drop from exhaustion, to be dead on one's feet

examples.sr: Данас сам [па̏о с но̏гу] од посла.
examples.en: Today I was dead on my feet from work.

note: Much more vivid than the plain «био је уморан».

forms: literally: it does not fall onto my mind
meanings: it wouldn't even occur to me, no way

examples.sr: Да га замолим за опроштај? [Не па̏да ми на па̏ме̄т]!
examples.en: Ask him for forgiveness? It wouldn't even occur to me!

forms: literally: to sleep like a slaughtered one

examples.en: Last night I slept like a log.

examples.sr: Он [пли̏ва у па̏рама] откако је продао фирму.
examples.en: He has been rolling in money since he sold the company.

note: A variant: «купати се у парама».

forms: literally: to turn into an ear

examples.sr: Док прича, ја се [претво̀рим у у̏во].
examples.en: When he talks, I'm all ears.

meanings: to be starving, to die of hunger

examples.en: I can't take it anymore, I'm starving.

note: Colloquial, instead of «гладан сам».

meanings: to wake up from a dream

examples.en: I woke up from a bad dream.
I had a strange dream last night.

note: A variant with a verb: «сањао сам нешто чудно».

examples.en: Help, I can't breathe!
Quick, call an ambulance!
I feel sick, I need a doctor.

note: The thing needed is the subject, the person is in the dative: треба ми лекар, треба ми лек.

examples.en: Grandpa had a heart attack.

meanings: I'd like to make an appointment (for a checkup)

examples.en: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

note: закажем - to book a time slot; термин - an appointment time.

meanings: do you have any free appointments?

examples.sr: [Да ли и̏мате сло̀бодне тѐрмине] за четвртак?
examples.en: Do you have any free appointments for Thursday?

meanings: I have a referral to a specialist

examples.en: I have a referral to a specialist.
What time suits you?

note: Often also «које време вам одговара».

examples.en: Thanks, I'm just looking.
May I try this on?

meanings: I'm buying it as a gift

examples.sr: Желим да то упакујете, [ку̀пује̄м на по̏клон].
examples.en: Please wrap it, I'm buying it as a gift.
Do you have anything cheaper?
My change, please.

examples.sr: Путовали смо месец дана, али [сву̀да по̏ђи, ку̏ћи до̀ђи].
examples.en: We traveled for a month, but there's no place like home.

forms: literally: measure three times, cut once

examples.sr: Помисли добро: [три̏ пу̏та ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: Think it over: measure twice, cut once.

key: phr:човек се учи док је жив
cyr: човек се учи док је жив
acc: чо̏век се у̏чи до̏к је жи̑в
forms: literally: a person learns as long as he lives

examples.sr: Не стиди се, [чо̀век се у̏чи до̏к је жи̑в].
examples.en: Don't be embarrassed, you live and learn.

examples.sr: Не брини, [сва̏кӣ ло̀нац на̑ђе сво̑ј по̀клопац].
examples.en: Don't worry, every pot finds its lid.

note: About everyone finding a match.

key: phr:јабука не пада далеко од стабла
cyr: јабука не пада далеко од стабла
acc: ја̏бука не па̏да далѐко од ста̏бла
meanings: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree

examples.sr: Син личи на оца - [ја̏бука не па̏да далѐко од ста̏бла].
examples.en: The son looks like his father - the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

key: phr:ко другоме јаму копа, сам у њу упада
cyr: ко другоме јаму копа, сам у њу упада
acc: ко̏ дру̏гоме ја̏му ко̏па, сам у њу̑ у̀пада
meanings: whoever digs a pit for others falls into it himself

examples.sr: [Ко̏ дру̏гоме ја̏му ко̏па, сам у њу̑ у̀пада].
examples.en: Whoever digs a pit for others falls into it himself.

key: phr:што посејеш, то ћеш и пожњети
cyr: што посејеш, то ћеш и пожњети
acc: што̏ по̀сејеш, то̑ ћеш и по̀жњети

examples.en: You reap what you sow.

meanings: the less you know, the better you sleep

examples.en: The less you know, the better you sleep.

key: phr:пала му је секира у мед
cyr: пала му је секира у мед
acc: па̏ла му је сѐкира у ме̑д
forms: literally: his axe fell into honey
meanings: to strike it lucky, to have a stroke of luck

examples.sr: Добио је посао - [па̏ла му је сѐкира у ме̑д].
examples.en: He got the job - he struck it lucky.

key: phr:вук длаку мења, али ћуд никада
cyr: вук длаку мења, али ћуд никада
acc: ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏када
forms: literally: the wolf changes its coat, but never its nature
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots

examples.sr: [Ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏када] - није се променио.
examples.en: A leopard can't change its spots - he hasn't changed.

note: The point: a person does not change at heart.

forms: literally: like a cat around hot porridge

examples.sr: Он се врти [ка̏о ма̏чка о̏ко врѐле ка̏ше].
examples.en: He keeps beating around the bush.

key: phr:ко зна зашто је то добро
cyr: ко зна зашто је то добро
acc: ко̏ зна̑ за̏што је то̑ до̀бро
forms: literally: who knows why it is good
meanings: every cloud has a silver lining, a blessing in disguise

examples.sr: Изгубио је посао, али [ко̏ зна̑ за̏што је то̑ до̀бро].
examples.en: He lost his job, but who knows, it may be a blessing in disguise.
Which Slava do you celebrate?

note: A question about which saint the family honors on that day.

examples.en: Cheers! - Cheers!
Hi, what's up?

note: A casual alternative to «како си».

meanings: who cares about you, nobody pays any attention to you

examples.sr: Он хоће да се прави важан, али [ко̏ га ши̏ша].
examples.en: He wants to act important, but who cares about him?

note: Colloquial, a bit rude: said of someone nobody notices or listens to.

examples.en: I'm late. - Never mind.

meanings: what's wrong with you?, what's your problem?

examples.en: Why are you so quiet? What's wrong with you?

note: Colloquial: asks for the reason behind someone's behavior.

examples.sr: Да ћу ја то урадити? [Не̑ма ша̏нсе].
examples.en: Me, do that? No way.

key: phr:то ти је што ти је
cyr: то ти је што ти је
acc: то̑ ти је што̏ ти је

examples.sr: Тако је како је, [то̑ ти је што̏ ти је].
examples.en: That's how it is, it is what it is.

note: Accepting a situation that cannot be changed.

meanings: not really in the mood, not really my thing

examples.sr: Данас [ни́сам ба̏ш у фа̏зону] за излазак.
examples.en: I'm not really in the mood to go out today.

note: Colloquial «фазон» - a state of mind, a mood.

examples.sr: Ја сам рекао своје, [ра̏ди ка̏ко зна̑ш и у̀ме̄ш].
examples.en: I've said my piece, do as you see fit.

meanings: oh, come on, the things you hear

examples.sr: Рекао је да не пије? [Е̏х, сва̏шта].
examples.en: He said he doesn't drink? Oh, come on.

note: Disbelief or surprise.

examples.en: Taxes are a necessary evil.

forms: literally: to carry off the cord
meanings: to win, to take the prize

examples.sr: Наш тим је [по̏нео шну̑р] у финалу.
examples.en: Our team won the final.

forms: literally: a pumpkin that puts on airs
meanings: a pretentious upstart who puts on airs

examples.en: That man is a real conceited upstart.

note: Said of someone who has recently become rich and puts on airs.

examples.en: Get lost!

note: Rude: an order to leave.

examples.sr: У њеном стану је [ка̏о у апоте́ци].
examples.en: Her apartment is spotless.
That was ages ago, before Christ.

meanings: in the middle of nowhere, very far away

examples.en: We live in the middle of nowhere.

note: Literally «behind God's back». A variant: «Богу иза ногу».

forms: literally: to not close one's mouth

examples.en: She hasn't stopped talking since morning.

forms: literally: so that you lick your fingers

examples.en: This baklava is finger-licking good.

note: Colloquially: «боли глава» - mind-blowingly delicious.

examples.en: First of all, thank you for the invitation.

examples.sr: [По мо̑м ми̏шљењу], то је добра идеја.
examples.en: In my opinion, it's a good idea.
Sorry, but I disagree.

meanings: that makes no sense, there's no point

examples.en: There's no point, you have to decide.
Let me explain what happened.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда се ни̏када не̑ће̄мо сло̀жити], али то је у реду.
examples.en: Maybe we'll never agree, but that's okay.
What are they saying? I couldn't care less.

note: «Баш ме брига» - the same, but ruder.

examples.en: Look at the room, it's like a pigsty!

forms: literally: poor as a church mouse

examples.en: He's poor as a church mouse.

examples.sr: Он ће платити [ка̏д се ро̏ди Карађо̀рђе].
examples.en: He'll pay when hell freezes over.
He'll pay the debt back on the twelfth of never.

key: phr:не зна се ко пије, а ко плаћа
cyr: не зна се ко пије, а ко плаћа
acc: не зна̑ се ко̏ пи̏је̄, а ко̏ пла́ћа
forms: literally: nobody knows who is drinking and who is paying
meanings: total chaos, nobody knows what is going on

examples.sr: На састанку [се не зна̑ ко̏ пи̏је̄, а ко̏ пла́ћа].
examples.en: The meeting was total chaos.

examples.sr: Напољу је четрдесет степени, [ску̏вао сам се].
examples.en: It's 40 degrees Celsius outside, I'm boiling.
Without a jacket I'm freezing.

forms: literally: to let out one's soul
meanings: to give up the ghost, to pass away

examples.en: Grandpa passed away in his sleep.

forms: literally: to stretch out one's hooves

examples.en: The old cow kicked the bucket.

note: Colloquial and jocular.

forms: literally: lives like a kidney in suet
meanings: to live in clover, to live in luxury

examples.en: He lives in clover.

meanings: you shouldn't have gone to the trouble

examples.sr: Тако леп поклон! [Нѝје тре̏бало да се му̏чиш].
examples.en: Such a lovely gift! You shouldn't have.

note: The polite form: «није требало да се мучите».

examples.sr: [Ба̏ш ле̑по од те̏бе] што си дошао.
examples.en: It's really nice of you to have come.

meanings: I have a little surprise for you

examples.en: I have a little surprise for you.

forms: literally: to pretend to be an Englishman
meanings: to play dumb, to pretend not to understand

examples.sr: Не [пра̏ви се Ѐнгле̄з], добро знаш о чему се ради.
examples.en: Don't play dumb, you know exactly what this is about.

forms: literally: to have no hair on one's tongue
meanings: to not mince words, to speak frankly

examples.en: He doesn't mince words.

meanings: to idle, to goof off, to gawk around

examples.en: Don't just stand around gawking, do something.

forms: literally: to give a wind in the back
meanings: to give a boost, to encourage, to support

examples.sr: Хвала што ми дајеш [ве̏тар у ле́ђа].
examples.en: Thanks for giving me a boost.

forms: literally: to drink like a snake

examples.en: He drinks like a fish.

key: phr:ко се мача лати, од мача ће и погинути
cyr: ко се мача лати, од мача ће и погинути
acc: ко̏ се ма̏ча ла̏ти, од ма̏ча ће и по̀гинути
meanings: he who lives by the sword dies by the sword

examples.sr: [Ко̏ се ма̏ча ла̏ти, од ма̏ча ће и по̀гинути].
examples.en: He who lives by the sword dies by the sword.

meanings: to make a mountain out of a molehill

examples.en: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill.

forms: literally: to have butter on one's head
meanings: to have a guilty conscience, to have something to hide

examples.sr: Он [и̏ма пу̏тер на гла́ви], зато ћути.
examples.en: He has a guilty conscience, which is why he's keeping quiet.

examples.sr: [Сре̏ћна Но̑ва го̏дина]! Нека ти донесе много среће.
examples.en: Happy New Year! May it bring you lots of luck.

key: phr:нека ти донесе много среће, здравља и љубави
cyr: нека ти донесе много среће, здравља и љубави
acc: не̏ка ти до̀несе мно̏го сре̏ће, здра̏вља и љу́бави
meanings: may it bring you lots of luck, health and love

examples.sr: Срећна Нова година! [Не̏ка ти до̀несе мно̏го сре̏ће, здра̏вља и љу́бави].
examples.en: Happy New Year! May it bring you lots of luck, health and love.

forms: literally: without three fingers there is no cross

examples.sr: Попиј и трећу, [без три̏ пр̏ста не̑ма кр̏ста].
examples.en: Have a third one too, third time's the charm.

note: In Serbia coffee is brought to a boil three times; the saying alludes to crossing oneself with three fingers.

meanings: Truly He is born! (the reply to the Christmas greeting)

examples.en: - Christ is born! - Truly He is born!
I'm sending my friends a card: Merry Christmas!

note: Christmas in Serbia is on January 7.

examples.en: We wished our neighbors a happy Christmas Eve!

note: Christmas Eve is on January 6.

examples.en: I overate today.
What, are you his self-appointed lawyer?

note: Someone who stands up for another person without being asked.

examples.en: He's totally nuts.

forms: literally: to work with full steam

examples.en: The factory is working at full steam.

examples.sr: Да је он отишао? [Пр̀ви пу̑т чу̏је̄м].
examples.en: He left? That's news to me.
I was late. - So what?

meanings: I was just thinking about that

examples.sr: [Та́ма̄н сам ми̏слио на то̑], зови га.
examples.en: I was just thinking about that, call him.

meanings: all that glitters is not gold

examples.en: Be careful, all that glitters is not gold.

key: phr:ко се последњи смеје, најслађе се смеје
cyr: ко се последњи смеје, најслађе се смеје
acc: ко̏ се по̀следњӣ смѐје̄, на̏јслађе се смѐје̄
forms: literally: whoever laughs last laughs the sweetest
meanings: he who laughs last laughs best

examples.sr: [Ко̏ се по̀следњӣ смѐје̄, на̏јслађе се смѐје̄].
examples.en: He who laughs last laughs best.

meanings: same as ever, the same old

examples.en: What's new? - Same as ever.

meanings: to look back on the past year

examples.sr: Пред Нову годину [о̀сврнемо се на про̀теклу го̀дину].
examples.en: Before New Year we look back on the past year.

meanings: I don't care about that, it's not important to me

examples.sr: Резултат ме не занима, [нѝје ми ста̏ло до то́га].
examples.en: The result doesn't interest me, I don't care about it.

note: «стало ми је до + gen.» - something matters to me, I care about it.

examples.en: I can't stand this food.

note: Stronger: «апсолутно не подносим».

examples.en: I love going to visit people.
We'll order a bottle of red wine.

note: The grapes are dark, so red wine is called «black» in Serbian. White wine is «бело вино».

examples.sr: Падала је киша, [та̀ко̄ да] нисмо ишли у парк.
examples.en: It was raining, so we didn't go to the park.

note: A conjunction of result: the main clause comes first, then the result.

examples.sr: Он је постао директор? [Ко̏ би ре̏као]!
examples.en: He became a director? Who would have thought!
I heard that you're moving.

forms: literally: to look for a hair in an egg

examples.en: He's always nitpicking.

meanings: I don't get the joke, I don't see the point

examples.en: What are they laughing at? I don't get the joke.

note: A meme with Saša Matić, a blind singer.

forms: literally: to break through the trick
meanings: to see through a trick, to catch on to someone's game

examples.en: I've seen through your trick.
Sorry for being late. - No worries.

meanings: pretty please (a request among close people)

examples.en: Open the window, pretty please!
Kisses, bye!

note: Only for warm relationships; with strangers say «молим вас».

examples.en: Please cut my hair shorter.
Please give me bangs.
Cook it on low heat.
- Sorry I'm late. - No worries.
No worries, we'll make it on time.

note: Colloquial slang. Close in meaning: «није фрка» - no big deal.

forms: literally: if it is not a panic for you

examples.sr: [А̏ко ти нѝје фр̏ка], помози ми са торбама.
examples.en: If it's no trouble, help me with the bags.

examples.sr: - Можеш ли да ме одвезеш? - [Нѝје ми фр̏ка].
examples.en: - Can you give me a ride? - No trouble.

note: An informal polite request; the reply is «није ми фрка» - no trouble for me.

meanings: get lost, get out of here

examples.en: Get out of here!
I told him to get lost.

note: Colloquial and rude; strengthened with «бре»: «носи се, бре!».

examples.en: They say ironically: the further south, the sadder.

examples.sr: Плате су све ниже, [што̏ ју̏жније, то̑ ту̏жније].
examples.en: Wages keep getting lower: the further south, the sadder.

note: A joking saying about a hard economic situation; it rhymes: «јужније - тужније».

key: phr:мени је милије поред мога илије
cyr: мени је милије поред мога Илије
acc: ме̏ни је ми̏лије по̏ред мо̑га Ѝлије
forms: literally: I like it better beside my Ilija
meanings: I'd rather be beside my beloved than in luxury

examples.sr: Не треба ми палата, [ме̏ни је ми̏лије по̏ред мо̑га Ѝлије].
examples.en: I don't need a palace, I'm happiest by my Ilija's side.

examples.sr: Могла би у град, али [ме̏ни је ми̏лије по̏ред мо̑га Ѝлије].
examples.en: I could move to the city, but I'm happiest by my Ilija's side.

note: A rhyming proverb (милије - Илије): being near a loved one beats any comfort.

examples.en: He decided to grow a beard.
He grew a beard in the winter.

meanings: leave me alone; also let go of me, let me through

examples.en: Please, leave me in peace.
Oh, forget him, he's crazy!

note: The sense depends on the situation: let go, let me through, leave alone, never mind. Example: «пусти ме да радим шта хоћу» - let me do what I want.

forms: literally: to let out a rumor

examples.sr: Неко је [пу̏стио ру̏жне гла̀сине] о њој.
examples.en: Someone spread nasty rumors about her.
Don't spread rumors without proof.

forms: literally: in love up to the ears

examples.sr: Он је [за̀љубљен до у̀шијӯ] у њу.
examples.en: He's head over heels in love with her.
I'm head over heels in love with you.

examples.sr: [О̀сећам не̏што пре̏ма те̏би], али се плашим да кажем.
examples.en: I have feelings for you, but I'm afraid to say so.
I know you have feelings for me.

examples.sr: Знам да [ти си мо̀ја дру̏га поло̀вина].
examples.en: I know that you are my other half.
For him she is the other half.

note: A man can say jokingly to a woman: «ти си моја лепша половина» - you are my better half.

meanings: I like you, I'm into you

examples.sr: [Сви̏ђаш ми се] више него што мислиш.
examples.en: I like you more than you think.
I really like you.

note: «Свиђати се» takes the dative: «ти ми се свиђаш», «свиђам му се» - he likes me.

examples.en: Look at those sparkly little eyes!
The baby has bright little eyes.

note: An affectionate, rhyming expression for a child's shining eyes.

key: phr:као да те је киша поквасила
cyr: као да те је киша поквасила
acc: ка̏о да те је ки̏ша по̀квасила
forms: literally: as if the rain had soaked you
meanings: you look washed out and tired

examples.sr: Што си такав, [ка̏о да те је ки̏ша по̀квасила]?
examples.en: Why do you look so washed out, as if you'd been caught in the rain?

examples.sr: Изгледаш [ка̏о да те је ки̏ша по̀квасила].
examples.en: You look limp and worn out.
He bought a sweater of some indeterminate color.
The wall was some murky, drab color.

forms: literally: when a dead man farts

examples.en: He'll pay you when pigs fly.

examples.sr: Тај воз ће стићи [ка̏д мр̀тав пр̏дне].
examples.en: That train will arrive when hell freezes over.

note: Colloquial and a bit rude: said of something you will never see.

examples.en: Don't stop, keep going!
A little more, keep pushing to the end!

note: A shout from Balkan weddings that went viral in 2022: keep up the pace, don't give up.

key: phr:добити тањир супе и ногу у дупе
cyr: добити тањир супе и ногу у дупе
acc: до̀бити та̏њӣр су̏пе и но̏гу у ду̏пе
forms: literally: to get a plate of soup and a kick in the backside
meanings: to get nothing for one's trouble

examples.sr: Радио је годину дана и [до̀био та̏њир су̏пе и но̏гу у ду̏пе].
examples.en: He worked for a year and ended up with nothing.

examples.sr: Није му платила, [до̀био је та̏њир су̏пе и но̏гу у ду̏пе].
examples.en: She didn't pay him: he got nothing for his trouble.

note: Colloquial and a bit rude: to get nothing in return for your work.

examples.en: I'm going to take a half-hour nap.
After lunch he took a nap.

note: A pun: «хрчак» (hamster) and «хркати» (to snore).

examples.en: Somebody let a dove out in the elevator.

examples.sr: Тихо је [пу̏стио го̏луба] и насмејао се.
examples.en: He quietly let a dove out and laughed.
There's only odds and ends in the drawer.
I didn't buy anything, just little trinkets.

note: Colloquial and playful: small, useless things.

meanings: aren't you ugly! (said fondly to a baby)

examples.en: Aren't you ugly, my little one!

examples.sr: Бака му је рекла [што̏ си га̀дан] због урока.
examples.en: Grandma told him he was ugly, to ward off the evil eye.

note: Babies are called «гадан» or «ружан» to ward off the evil eye (урок): one does not praise them directly.

examples.en: I love you, forever yours.
He signed the letter: forever yours.

note: A man writes «заувек твој».

key: phr:не могу да престанем да читам
cyr: не могу да престанем да читам
acc: не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да чи̏там

examples.sr: Књига је тако добра, [не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да чи̏там]!
examples.en: The book is so good, I can't stop reading!

examples.sr: Већ је поноћ, а [не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да чи̏там].
examples.en: It's already midnight, and I can't stop reading.

meanings: when does the next train leave?

examples.sr: Извините, [ка̀да по̀лази слѐде̄ћӣ во̑з] за Ниш?
examples.en: Excuse me, when does the next train to Niš leave?

examples.sr: Реците ми, [ка̀да по̀лази слѐде̄ћӣ во̑з] за Суботицу?
examples.en: Tell me, when does the next train to Subotica leave?

meanings: where can I leave my luggage?

examples.sr: Молим вас, [где̏ мо̀гу да о̏ставим пр̀тља̄г]?
examples.en: Excuse me, where can I leave my luggage?

examples.sr: Да ли знате [где̏ мо̀гу да о̏ставим пр̀тља̄г]?
examples.en: Do you know where I can leave my luggage?

key: phr:да ли је воз на време
cyr: да ли је воз на време
acc: да ли је во̑з на вре́ме

examples.en: Is the train on time?

examples.sr: Питам [да ли је во̑з на вре́ме].
examples.en: I'm asking whether the train is on time.
Excuse me, this seat is taken.

examples.sr: Не можете да седнете, [о̀во̄ ме̏сто је резѐрвисано].
examples.en: You can't sit here, this seat is reserved.
He has no luck in love.
No luck with the lottery today.

note: In the past tense: «није имао среће» - he was unlucky.

examples.sr: Професорка нам је [по̀желела сре̏ћу] пре испита.
examples.en: The professor wished us luck before the exam.
Everyone wished him luck.
He tried his luck at gambling.

examples.sr: Хоћу да [о̏кушам сре̏ћу] у великом граду.
examples.en: I want to try my luck in a big city.

forms: literally: to be of a lucky hand

examples.sr: Он је баш [сре̏ћне ру́ке], све му полази за руком.
examples.en: He's really lucky, everything works out for him.

examples.sr: Мој брат је [сре̏ћне ру́ке] у послу.
examples.en: My brother is lucky in business.

forms: literally: to have more luck than sense
meanings: to be more lucky than smart

examples.sr: [И̏мала сам ви̏ше сре̏ће не̏го па̏мети]: положила сам, а нисам учила.
examples.en: I was luckier than I was smart: I passed without studying.
He's luckier than he is smart.
The doctor recommends a healthy diet.
A healthy diet gives you energy.

note: Variants: «балансирана», «уравнотежена исхрана».

examples.en: I burn calories by swimming.
I want to burn off some calories after lunch.

examples.sr: Лако је [одржа́вати здра̀ву тежѝну] уз кретање.
examples.en: It's easy to maintain a healthy weight if you stay active.
I'm trying to maintain a healthy weight.

examples.sr: Лекар ми је рекао да [огра̀ничим у̏нос шѐћера].
examples.en: The doctor told me to limit my sugar intake.
One should limit sugar intake.

note: Likewise: «унос соли, масти, меса».

examples.en: He decided to quit smoking.
I want to quit smoking by summer.

forms: literally: the rain pours as if from a bucket

examples.en: It's pouring outside.

examples.sr: Не излази, [ки̏ша ли̏је̄ ка̏о из ка́бла]!
examples.en: Don't go out, it's pouring!

note: «Кабао» is a large bucket or tub.

forms: literally: I got wet to the bare skin
meanings: I got soaked to the skin

examples.sr: Без кишобрана [по̀кисао сам до го̀ле ко̏же].
examples.en: Without an umbrella, I got soaked to the skin.
We all got soaked to the skin.

meanings: to get caught in the rain

examples.sr: На путу кући [у̀хватила ме је ки̏ша].
examples.en: I got caught in the rain on the way home.

examples.sr: Узми кишобран да те не [у̏хвати ки̏ша].
examples.en: Take an umbrella so you don't get caught in the rain.
Around noon the sky clouded over.
Look, the sky is getting gloomy.

examples.sr: Изнад града [на̀вукли су се та̑мнӣ о̏бла̄ци].
examples.en: Dark clouds have rolled in over the city.

key: phr:и ја имам коња за трку
cyr: и ја имам коња за трку
acc: и ја̑ ѝма̄м ко̀ња за тр̏ку
forms: literally: I also have a horse for the race
meanings: I've got something to compete with too
I have an ace up my sleeve too

examples.sr: Не брини, [и ја̏ ѝма̄м ко̀ња за тр̏ку].
examples.en: Don't worry, I have an ace up my sleeve too.

examples.sr: Нека се они хвале, [и ја̏ ѝма̄м ко̀ња за тр̏ку].
examples.en: Let them brag, I have an ace in the hole too.

note: Quiet confidence: said by someone who has a trump card in reserve.

key: phr:упала ми је кашика у мед
cyr: упала ми је кашика у мед
acc: у̏пала ми је ка̀шика у ме̑д
forms: literally: the spoon fell into the honey for me

examples.sr: Добио сам посао - [у̏пала ми је ка̀шика у ме̑д]!
examples.en: I got the job - I hit the jackpot!

examples.sr: Нашла је стан близу посла, [у̏пала јој је ка̀шика у ме̑д].
examples.en: She found an apartment near work - she really lucked out.

note: Said when someone has had a big stroke of luck.

forms: literally: you were not born in a boat
meanings: were you born in a barn?

examples.en: Close the door, were you born in a barn!

examples.sr: Опет су врата отворена? [Ни̏си у ча̏мцу ро̏ђен]!
examples.en: The door is open again? Were you born in a barn?

note: A reproach to someone who has left a door open.

examples.en: He came home furious.
Don't go near him, he's furious.

meanings: to be silent as a fish

examples.en: He said nothing, he's keeping mum.
Promise you'll keep quiet about it.

meanings: to sleep like a lamb (quietly and peacefully)

examples.en: The baby is sleeping like a lamb.
After a walk I sleep like a baby.

examples.sr: Он [ра̏ди ка̏о ко̏њ], а нема одмора.
examples.en: He works like a horse, and there's no rest.
Mother works like a horse for the family.
Grandpa is wise as an owl.
Ask her, she's wise as an owl.
That merchant is sly as a fox.

examples.sr: Не веруј му, [лу̏кав је ка̏о лѝсица].
examples.en: Don't trust him, he's sly as a fox.
My brother is stubborn as a mule.

examples.sr: Не слуша никога, [тврдо̀глава је ка̏о ма̀гарац].
examples.en: She doesn't listen to anyone, she's stubborn as a mule.
My sister is hardworking as an ant.
He works hard, like an ant.
Today I'm slow as a snail.
Traffic is crawling like a snail.
The runner is fast as a hare.
This cat is fast as a hare.
He is loyal as a dog.
Her friend is loyal as a dog.
He's thin as a rake.

examples.sr: Откако је на дијети, [мр̏шав је ка̏о гли́ста].
examples.en: Ever since he went on a diet, he's been skinny as a rail.
The girl sings like a nightingale.
Grandma used to sing like a nightingale.
That guy is strong as an ox.
He's small, but strong as an ox.

key: phr:гледати као теле у шарена врата
cyr: гледати као теле у шарена врата
acc: гле̏дати ка̏о тѐле у ша̏рена вра́та
forms: literally: to look like a calf at a painted door

examples.sr: Шта си се загледао, [гле̏да̄ш ка̏о тѐле у ша̏рена вра́та]?
examples.en: What are you staring at, why do you look so bewildered?

examples.sr: Гледао је [ка̏о тѐле у ша̏рена вра́та], ништа није разумео.
examples.en: He stared blankly, he didn't understand a thing.

examples.sr: - Попио сам само два пива. - [Чу̑ј] два!
examples.en: - I only had two beers. - Two, yeah right!

examples.sr: - Не можеш сам да подигнеш џак. - [Чу̑ј] не могу!
examples.en: - You can't lift the sack by yourself. - Can't, my foot!

note: Put before an echo of the other person's words, in surprise or irony; literally «listen».

examples.sr: Купио сам карту за хиљаду динара, [чу̑ј ме̏не], евра!
examples.en: I bought a ticket for a thousand dinars, what am I saying, euros!

examples.sr: Стижем у два, [чу̑ј ме̏не], у три сата.
examples.en: I'll arrive at two, I mean, at three o'clock.

note: A playful quick correction after a slip of the tongue.

forms: literally: to drive poppy seeds onto a thread

examples.sr: Немој да [те̏раш ма̏к на ко̀нац], важно је да је проблем решен.
examples.en: Don't split hairs, what matters is that the problem is solved.

examples.sr: Он увек [те̏ра ма̏к на ко̀нац] око ситница.
examples.en: He's always nitpicking over trifles.

meanings: a kum (best man, godfather) can't be replaced like a button

examples.en: The godfather isn't a button, he has to be invited.

examples.sr: Не можеш га заменити, [ку̑м нѝје ду̀гме].
examples.en: You can't replace him, a kum is not a button.

note: The «кум» (best man, godfather) is a key figure in Serbian culture.

meanings: to look for a needle in a haystack

examples.sr: Тражити га у граду је као [тра́жити и̏глу у пла̏сту се̏на].
examples.en: Looking for him in the city is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

examples.sr: Не [тра̏жи и̏глу у пла̏сту се̏на], питај некога.
examples.en: Don't look for a needle in a haystack, ask somebody.

examples.sr: Потписали смо [у̏гово̄р о за̏купу] на годину дана.
examples.en: We signed a one-year lease agreement.

examples.sr: У [у̀говору о за̏купу] стоји и депозит.
examples.en: The lease agreement also mentions the deposit.
The notary prepared the sales contract.
We're signing the sales contract on Monday.
I've been waiting for my residence permit for a month.
She renewed her residence permit.

forms: literally: to hold on like a drunk to a fence
meanings: to cling on for dear life

examples.en: He clings to his job for dear life.

examples.sr: Не [др̀жи се ка̏о пѝјан пло̏та] старих навика.
examples.en: Don't cling to old habits.

note: A drunk holds on to a fence so as not to fall: to cling stubbornly to something.

forms: literally: let everything go its own course

examples.sr: Не мешај се, [не̏ка све̏ и̏де сво̀јӣм то̑ком].
examples.en: Don't interfere, let things take their course.
Leave it, let things take their course.

note: A synonym of «само полако».

meanings: to have a sense of decency
to have a sense of honor

examples.en: He's a decent man, he will never lie.
How can you have the nerve to ask for that?

note: The negative «немати образа» means to behave shamelessly.

examples.sr: Он има [чи̏ст о̀браз], увек говори истину.
examples.en: He has a spotless reputation, he always tells the truth.

examples.sr: [Чи̏ст о̀браз] му је важнији од новца.
examples.en: His good name matters more to him than money.

forms: literally: to figure out on the ace

examples.sr: Сконтао је [на ке́ца] шта му тражим.
examples.en: He understood right away what I was asking him for.
The girl caught on to everything instantly.

note: «Кец» is a Hungarian loanword: an ace, also the grade 1.

examples.sr: Није се спремао, [и̏шао је гр̏лом у ја̏годе].
examples.en: He didn't prepare, he just rushed in headlong.

examples.sr: Не иди [гр̏лом у ја̏годе], прво размисли.
examples.en: Don't rush in headlong, think first.

meanings: to poke one's nose into other people's business

examples.sr: Немој да [гу̏раш но̑с] у туђе ствари.
examples.en: Don't poke your nose into other people's business.
The neighbor is always poking her nose into everything.

meanings: to have an eye for something

examples.en: You have an eye for this kind of work.
She has an eye for beautiful things.

meanings: at the end of the world

examples.en: He lives in the middle of nowhere.
Their house is at the end of the world.

forms: literally: it burns under my heels

examples.sr: [Го̀рӣ ми под пѐтама], рок је сутра.
examples.en: I'm under heavy pressure, the deadline is tomorrow.

examples.sr: Њему [го̀рӣ под пѐтама], а он мирује.
examples.en: He's in hot water, and yet he stays calm.

forms: literally: not even up to the knee

examples.sr: Он му [ни до ко̀лена] не стиже.
examples.en: He can't hold a candle to him.
Next to her, I can't hold a candle.

examples.sr: - Могу ли да уђем? - [Ка̏ко да не]!
examples.en: - May I come in? - Of course!

examples.sr: - Биће готово за пет минута. - [Ка̏ко да не]...
examples.en: - It'll be done in five minutes. - Yeah, right...

note: The meaning depends on tone: calm means sincere agreement, a smirk or a pause means sarcasm.

examples.sr: Ма [ма̀ни се] глупости, боље хајде на кафу.
examples.en: Oh, forget that nonsense, let's go for a coffee instead.
Drop it, it's not worth the effort.

note: «манути се» + gen.: to drop something; «мани ме се» - leave me alone.

examples.sr: Киша пада, [шта̏ да ра̏дим], остајем код куће.
examples.en: It's raining, what can I do, I'm staying home.
There's no time, what can you do.
You got the job? No way!

examples.sr: [Ма̏ не̏мој] да плачеш, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Oh, don't cry, everything will be fine.

note: «немој» + «да»/infinitive is a prohibition, but this reply on its own expresses surprise.

examples.en: He's late again? Don't get me started!
Prices are crazy. - Tell me about it.

note: Agreement with feeling when the other person complains or is surprised.

examples.sr: [Где̏ си], бре, одавно те нисмо видели!
examples.en: Hey, where have you been, we haven't seen you in ages!
Hey, where are you? - Here I am!

note: A greeting between friends; colloquial variants «де си», «ђе си», often with «бре» or «брате».

examples.en: What are you doing in Belgrade?

examples.sr: Ооо, [о̀ткуд ти], нисмо се видели годинама!
examples.en: Oh, look who it is, we haven't seen each other in years!

note: Glad surprise at an unexpected meeting.

examples.en: How's it going? - Slowly but surely, getting by.
Nothing special, we're just plugging along.

note: In speech «гурати даље» means to cope, to get by as best you can.

forms: literally: to pour oil on the fire
meanings: to add fuel to the fire

examples.sr: Не [до̀ливај у̑ље на ва̏тру], причекај да се смири.
examples.en: Don't add fuel to the fire, wait for things to calm down.

examples.sr: Његови коментари само [до̀ливају у̑ље на ва̏тру].
examples.en: His comments only add fuel to the fire.

examples.sr: Имаш [гла̏дне о̏чи], напунио си тањир а ниси појео ништа.
examples.en: Your eyes are bigger than your stomach: you filled your plate and ate nothing.
He isn't hungry, his eyes are just bigger than his stomach.

meanings: to act as if one has just landed from another planet

examples.sr: Како не знаш за то? Јеси ли [па̏о с Ма̑рса]?
examples.en: How can you not know about that? Did you just land from Mars?

examples.sr: Понашаш се као да си [па̏о с Ма̑рса].
examples.en: You act as if you just landed from Mars.

forms: literally: there is no bread without a hoe

examples.sr: Ако хоћеш успех, ради: [не̑ма хле̏ба без мо̏тике].
examples.en: If you want success, work for it: no pain, no gain.
Study every day, no pain, no gain.

note: «мотика» is a hoe; colloquial «леба» for «хлеба» also occurs.

examples.sr: Код њега је живот [ме̑д и мле́ко].
examples.en: His life is all milk and honey.

examples.sr: Не очекуј да ће све бити [ме̑д и мле́ко].
examples.en: Don't expect everything to be smooth sailing.

meanings: be careful, don't do anything silly

examples.sr: Идете у град? Пазите се, [па̏ме̄т у гла̑ву]!
examples.en: Going into town? Take care, be sensible!
Going out tonight? Behave yourself!

note: A parting word from parents to children.

examples.sr: Цене у ресторанима на мору су [па̏прене].
examples.en: Prices in the seaside restaurants are sky-high.

examples.sr: За те [па̏прене це̏не] нећу ништа да купим.
examples.en: I won't buy anything at those crazy prices.

examples.sr: Нисам знао да су тротинети толико скупи. - Ма да, то је [ску̑по ка̏о о̀тров].
examples.en: I didn't know scooters were so expensive. - Yeah, they're insanely expensive.

examples.sr: Станови у центру су [ску̑пӣ ка̏о о̀тров].
examples.en: Apartments in the center are insanely expensive.

note: «као отров» intensifies any adjective in the sense of «terribly».

examples.en: A new car is just throwing money away.
Don't waste money on nonsense.

forms: literally: to cost like Saint Peter's scrambled eggs

examples.sr: Вечера овде [ко̏шта ка̏о Све̏тог Пе̏тра ка̏јгана].
examples.en: Dinner here costs a fortune.

examples.sr: Тај сат [ко̏шта ка̏о Све̏тог Пе̏тра ка̏јгана].
examples.en: That watch costs a fortune.

note: Colloquial hyperbole.

examples.sr: Таксиста нас је [о̏драо] за вожњу до аеродрома.
examples.en: The taxi driver ripped us off for the ride to the airport.
Don't go there, they'll fleece you.

note: In speech «одрао» is often shortened to «одро».

examples.en: Oh my goodness, what a crowd on the bus!
Good heavens, what have I done!

note: A mild substitute for a curse, expressing shock or surprise.

forms: literally: oh, all sorts of things

examples.sr: [Е̏, сва̏шта], то нисам очекивао од тебе.
examples.en: Well, I never, I didn't expect that from you.

examples.sr: Каже да је све било бесплатно? [Е̏, сва̏шта]!
examples.en: He says it was all free? Well, I never!

note: Reproach or disbelief; «свашта» on its own means «all sorts of things».

examples.en: Oh, all right, if that's what you say.
Well, fine, let's go then.
Where's the key? - I have no idea.
I have no idea what to do.

note: Colloquial; can be strengthened: «немам ни појма».

examples.sr: [Не сѐкирај се], стићи ћемо на време.
examples.en: Don't worry, we'll get there on time.
Just don't stress about it.

note: Close: «не брини», «немој да се оптерећујеш».

examples.en: Thanks, but there's no need.
There's no need to hurry.

note: A polite way to decline an offer; also «хвала, не треба».

examples.en: This meat is no good, it smells.
A habit like that is no good.

note: Colloquial; the opposite is «ваља» - fine, good.

examples.en: One round-trip ticket to Belgrade, please.
How much is a return ticket?

forms: literally: to give by the handful and by the capful

examples.sr: Он [да̑је ша̏ком и ка̏пом] добре оцене.
examples.en: He hands out good grades generously.

examples.sr: Ради за ту фирму и [де̏ли ша̏ком и ка̏пом].
examples.en: He works for that company and throws money around left and right.

note: Also «делити шаком и капом»; about generosity or extravagance.

examples.en: Only a handful of people came.

examples.sr: На сајму је био једва [ша̏чица] посетилаца.
examples.en: There were barely a handful of visitors at the fair.

forms: literally: to hold in one's little finger
meanings: to know like the back of one's hand

examples.sr: Он све правила [др̀жи у ма̏лом пр̏сту].
examples.en: He knows all the rules like the back of his hand.

examples.sr: Мој тата [др̀жи у ма̏лом пр̏сту] сваку улицу у граду.
examples.en: My dad knows every street in the city like the back of his hand.

forms: literally: to spin someone around the little finger
meanings: to wrap someone around one's little finger

examples.en: She has him wrapped around her little finger.

examples.sr: Не дај да те [вр̏те о̏ко ма̏лог пр̏ста].
examples.en: Don't let anyone wrap you around their little finger.

key: phr:не бити некоме ни за мали прст
cyr: не бити некоме ни за мали прст
acc: не би̏ти не̏коме ни за ма̑лӣ пр̏ст
forms: literally: not to be even worth someone's little finger
meanings: can't hold a candle to someone

examples.sr: Тај глумац јој [нѝје ни за ма̑ли пр̏ст].
examples.en: That actor can't hold a candle to her.

examples.sr: Данашњи глумци [ни́су ни за ма̑ли пр̏ст] старим мајсторима.
examples.en: Today's actors can't hold a candle to the old masters.

note: Stronger: «ни за црно испод нокта» - not worth even the dirt under a nail.

examples.en: He talks as if he knows everything.

examples.sr: Гледа ме [ка̏о да] сам му непријатељ.
examples.en: He looks at me as if I were his enemy.

note: Followed by present or past by meaning: «као да је јуче било» (as if it were yesterday).

key: phr:смејати се као луд на брашно
cyr: смејати се као луд на брашно
acc: смѐјати се ка̏о лу̑д на бра̏шно
forms: literally: to laugh like a madman at flour
meanings: to laugh like a madman for no reason

examples.sr: Шта ти је? [Смѐје̄ш се ка̏о лу̑д на бра̏шно]!
examples.en: What's wrong with you? You're laughing like a madman!

examples.sr: Целу вечеру се [сме̏јао ка̏о лу̑д на бра̏шно].
examples.en: He laughed like a madman all evening.

note: Two origins are given: a Greek flour-sprinkling rite and a Macedonian prayer-over-flour cure.

forms: literally: to look through one's fingers

examples.sr: Инспектор је [про̀гледао кроз пр̏сте] њиховим прекршајима.
examples.en: The inspector turned a blind eye to their violations.

examples.sr: Не можемо више [про̀гледати кроз пр̏сте] том проблему.
examples.en: We can't turn a blind eye to this problem any longer.
They made the deal under the table.
The money was handed over on the sly.

note: About secret, illegal deals and payments.

examples.en: The gang laundered money through companies.
He is suspected of laundering money.
I got the tickets for free.

examples.sr: Није ништа купио, све је узео [за џа̏бе].
examples.en: He didn't buy anything, he got it all for free.

note: Colloquial, a Turkish loanword.

meanings: it does no harm to keep them

examples.en: Buy that too, it won't hurt.
Let them stay, they're not in the way.

note: Said of things you can keep in reserve: they get in nobody's way.

examples.en: He wants to do it at all costs.
The children wanted to go to the cinema at all costs.

note: Colloquial; close to «по сваку цену».

forms: literally: may his nice house be far away

examples.sr: Хоће да се жали? [Далѐко му лѐпа ку̏ћа]!
examples.en: He wants to complain? To hell with him!

examples.sr: Опет је касно дошао, [далѐко му лѐпа ку̏ћа].
examples.en: He came late again, good riddance to him.

note: Expresses contempt and not wanting to see the person; a bit rude.

meanings: um, what do you call it

examples.sr: Она је, [о̀ва̄ј, ка̏ко се зо̀ве], већ завршила то.
examples.en: She, um, what's her name, has already finished that.

examples.sr: Дошао је онај, [о̀ва̄ј, ка̏ко се зо̀ве], комшија.
examples.en: That, um, what's-his-name, the neighbor, came by.

note: A filler while you search for a name or a word.

examples.sr: [Ми̏слӣм], није лоше, али сам очекивао више.
examples.en: I mean, it's not bad, but I expected more.

examples.sr: Не знам шта да ти кажем, [ми̏слӣм], нисам упућен у ситуацију.
examples.en: I don't know what to tell you, I mean, I'm not up to speed on the situation.

note: A colloquial marker; similar are «оно» and «значи».

examples.sr: Кафа је на мом рачуну, [ку̏ћа ча̏сти]!
examples.en: The coffee is on us - on the house!
Dessert is on the house.
Put your wallet away, it's my treat.
Tonight I'm buying for everyone.

note: A variant: «на мој рачун» - on me.

examples.en: Please, help yourself to the cakes.
Help yourself, no need to ask.

note: A variant: «узмите слободно» - take some, don't be shy.

examples.en: I can't wait to see you!
The kids can't wait for the vacation.

note: Literally «I barely wait», but the sense is positive: eager anticipation.

examples.en: So much work, and all for nothing.

examples.sr: Оставили су нас без одговора, [џа̏бе смо кре̏чили].
examples.en: They left us without an answer, we did it all for nothing.

note: An ironic remark when effort brought no result; also «џабе сам кречио», «џабе смо кречили».

examples.en: He won the lottery? No way!

examples.sr: [Ма̏ да̑ј], то не може бити истина.
examples.en: Come on, that can't be true.

note: A reaction to unexpected news; on its own «дај» is just «give».

forms: literally: that's how that is for you

examples.en: It didn't work out, that's how it goes.

examples.sr: Не секирај се, [та̀ко̄ ти је то̑] у животу.
examples.en: Don't worry, that's life.

note: A calm, philosophical tone: accepting the situation.

forms: literally: let go of that story
meanings: oh, come on, don't make a drama of it

examples.en: Oh, come on, it's not that bad.

examples.sr: [Ма̏ пу̑стӣ при̑чу] и дођи на кафу.
examples.en: Oh, drop it and come over for a coffee.

note: A friendly way to calm someone who is exaggerating.

examples.sr: Рекао сам ти да ће касни. [Е̏то ти]!
examples.en: I told you he'd be late. See!
There you go, it's started raining.

note: A short, convincing remark when the outcome is obvious.

examples.en: She left him? Wow!
Wow, I can't believe it!

note: A reaction to striking news or gossip, often not negative.

examples.sr: Кад устанем, [вр̏ти ми се у гла́ви].
examples.en: When I stand up, I feel dizzy.

examples.sr: Од вожње [вр̏ти ми се у гла́ви].
examples.en: Traveling makes me dizzy.
The noise makes my head split.
My head is splitting, I need a pill.
I feel sick, I have to sit down.
I'm sick of his stories.

note: «мука ми је од чега» - to be sick of something.

examples.sr: Учио сам два месеца, положићу [јѐдан кроз јѐдан].
examples.en: I studied for two months, I'll pass for sure.
The victory will be a sure thing.

note: Colloquial: a hundred percent, no two ways about it.

examples.sr: Стигли смо на станицу [у пе̑т до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: We got to the station at the last minute.

examples.sr: Он увек све ради [у пе̑т до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: He always does everything at the last minute.
The wind was blowing at full blast.

examples.sr: Радили су [све̏ у шѐснае̄ст] да заврше посао.
examples.en: They worked flat out to finish the job.

examples.sr: [Ни пе̑т ни ше̑ст], одмах јој је пришао.
examples.en: Without a second thought, he went straight up to her.

examples.sr: Одлучио је [ни пе̑т ни ше̑ст] да се исели.
examples.en: He decided on the spot to move out.

examples.sr: Закаснио си? [Ма̏ не̑ма ве̏зе], стигли смо на време.
examples.en: You're late? Never mind, we made it on time.

examples.sr: [Ма̏ не̑ма ве̏зе], нека буде како хоћеш.
examples.en: It doesn't matter, let it be as you like.

note: «нема везе» alone: never mind, it doesn't matter.

meanings: thanks for the offer, but (a polite refusal)

examples.sr: [Хва́ла на по̀нуди, а̏ли] тренутно нисам заинтересован.
examples.en: Thanks for the offer, but I'm not interested right now.

examples.sr: [Хва́ла на по̀нуди, а̏ли] мислим да ћу изабрати нешто друго.
examples.en: Thanks for the offer, but I think I'll choose something else.

key: phr:жао ми је, али имам друге планове
cyr: жао ми је, али имам друге планове
acc: жа̏о ми је, а̏ли ѝма̄м дру̑ге пла̏нове
meanings: I'm sorry, but I have other plans

examples.sr: [Жа̏о ми је, а̏ли ѝма̄м дру̑ге пла̏нове].
examples.en: I'm sorry, but I have other plans.

examples.sr: Позив је диван, [жа̏о ми је, а̏ли ѝма̄м дру̑ге пла̏нове].
examples.en: It's a lovely invitation, I'm sorry, but I have other plans.

forms: literally: it is not the right moment

examples.en: I appreciate the offer, but it's not the right moment.

examples.sr: Знам да желиш да причамо, али [нѝје пра̑вӣ трену́так].
examples.en: I know you want to talk, but it's not the right time.
Unfortunately, I can't come tonight.
Thanks, but unfortunately I can't.

note: The most universal polite refusal.

examples.sr: [Чи̏ни ми се да] имамо довољно времена.
examples.en: It seems to me that we have enough time.
It seems to me it's going to rain.

note: Less categorical than «мислим да».

examples.en: As far as I know, the meeting is tomorrow.

examples.sr: [Колѝко ја̏ зна̑м], он је у Нишу.
examples.en: As far as I know, he's in Niš.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда гре̏шим, а̏ли] мислим да је ово тачно.
examples.en: I may be wrong, but I think this is correct.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда гре̏шим, а̏ли] он је већ отишао.
examples.en: I may be wrong, but he has already left.
You're right, that's important.
I think he's right.

note: «бити у праву» - to be right; the negative is «нисам у праву».

examples.sr: [Не сла̏жем се у по̀тпуности] са твојим мишљењем.
examples.en: I don't fully agree with your opinion.

examples.sr: [Не сла̏жем се у по̀тпуности], али разумем те.
examples.en: I don't fully agree, but I understand you.

key: phr:пу, пу да те не урекнем
cyr: пу, пу да те не урекнем
acc: пу̏, пу̏ да те не у̀рекнем
meanings: touch wood, so I don't jinx you (said of a baby)

examples.sr: Јао, како си велики! [Пу̏, пу̏ да те не у̀рекнем]!
examples.en: Oh, how big you are! Touch wood, so I don't jinx you!

note: Said to avert the evil eye, with a light pretend spit.

examples.en: I lived in Kaliningrad for a whole month.
He studied guitar for exactly a year.

note: Likewise «годину дана», «недељу дана»; «за недељу дана» - in a week.

examples.en: I waited for you for a whole hour.
I've been working here for an hour.

note: «сат» + a fixed «времена»; stresses exactly one hour.

examples.en: You have to take care of your health.

note: Usually with «о» + loc.: «о здрављу», «о времену».

examples.sr: Током путовања почела је да [во̏ди дне̑внӣк].
examples.en: During the trip she started keeping a diary.
Her family originates from Russia.

note: Bookish; «порекло» means origin.

meanings: to do most of the talking
to take the lead in a conversation

examples.sr: На састанку је [во̀дио гла̏вну ре̑ч] он.
examples.en: He dominated the conversation at the meeting.
The company keeps records of working hours.

meanings: as many sparks, as much health (a Christmas blessing)

examples.sr: [Колѝко ва̏рница, толѝко̄ здра̏вља], среће и весеља!
examples.en: As many sparks, as much health, happiness and joy!

note: Said by the «положајник», the first Christmas visitor, as he stirs the fire with a twig of the Yule log.

key: phr:учини добро, не кај се; учини зло, надај се
cyr: учини добро, не кај се; учини зло, надај се
acc: у̏чини до̀бро, не ка̏ј се; у̏чини зло̏, на̏дај се
forms: literally: do good - don't repent; do evil - expect (punishment)
meanings: do good and don't regret it; do evil and expect payback

examples.sr: Не жали, [у̏чини до̀бро, не ка̏ј се; у̏чини зло̏, на̏дај се].
examples.en: Don't regret helping: do good and don't repent, do evil and expect payback.

note: A consolation for someone who helped people and got no thanks; «надај се» here means «expect payback».

key: phr:новци кад одлазе имају сто ногу, а кад долазе само две
cyr: новци кад одлазе имају сто ногу, а кад долазе само две
acc: но̑вци ка̏д о̀длазе и̏мају сто̑ но̏гу, а ка̏д до̀лазе са̏мо две̑
forms: literally: money, when it leaves, has a hundred legs, and when it comes, only two
meanings: money goes fast and comes slowly

examples.sr: Годину дана смо штедели, а за недељу дана све потрошили: [но̑вци ка̏д о̀длазе и̏мају сто̑ но̏гу, а ка̏д до̀лазе са̏мо две̑].
examples.en: We saved for a year and spent it all in a week: money has a hundred legs when it leaves and only two when it comes.

note: «новци» is a dialectal form of «новац».

key: phr:роди ме, мајко, срећног, па ме на ђубре баци
cyr: роди ме, мајко, срећног, па ме на ђубре баци
acc: ро̏ди ме, ма̏јко, сре̏ћног, па ме на ђу̏бре ба̏ци
forms: literally: bear me lucky, mother, and then throw me on the dump

examples.sr: Он је лењ, а има све: [ро̏ди ме, ма̏јко, сре̏ћног, па ме на ђу̏бре ба̏ци].
examples.en: He's lazy and yet has everything: bear me lucky, mother, then throw me on the dump.

note: Said about someone else's luck; variant: «Роди ме, мајко, без главе, само немој без среће».

examples.en: Let's not discuss it now, later, later.

note: Colloquial: a way to put off a talk or a task.

examples.sr: То ће бити готово [Бо̑г зна̑ ка̏д].
examples.en: It'll be ready God knows when.
Someday you'll understand it.

meanings: in the blink of an eye

examples.en: I'll finish this in the blink of an eye.
The repair is a quick job.

note: Literally «an hour of work»; means quick and easy.

examples.en: We'll have coffee at a leisurely pace.

note: Of Turkish origin; colloquial.

examples.en: Don't plan too much, whatever will be, will be.
No rush, we can do it later.

note: «фрка» means fuss or haste; colloquial, youth slang.

examples.en: Sooner or later you'll have to decide.
Should I lend you some money? Not a chance!

note: An ironic refusal; colloquial.

examples.en: Do you want to go? - No way!

note: «јок» is Turkish for «no»; colloquial, a flat refusal.

meanings: to have a knack for something

examples.en: He has a knack for repairs.

note: «кликер» is a glass marble; colloquial.

meanings: I like it when we're together

examples.sr: [При̏ја ми ка̏д смо за̏једно] у тишини.
examples.en: I like being together in silence.

note: «прија ми» - it feels good to me, I like it.

examples.sr: Било је лепо, [са то̏бо̄м је вре́ме пролѐтело].
examples.en: It was lovely, time flew by with you.

meanings: something is going on between us

examples.sr: Осећам да се [не̏што де̏шава и̏змеђу нас].
examples.en: I feel that something is going on between us.

meanings: we have to do this again

examples.en: That was great, we have to do this again!

examples.sr: Услови рада у тој фирми су [у на̏јмању ру̑ку] понижавајући.
examples.en: Working conditions at that company are humiliating, to say the least.

note: Bookish, often used when judging something.

examples.sr: Плата је лоша, али [а̏ко ни̏шта дру̏го], иде ти стаж.
examples.en: The pay is bad, but if nothing else, it counts toward your work record.

examples.sr: Дошао сам [чи̏сто да] видим да ли сте добро.
examples.en: I came just to check that you're all right.

examples.sr: Учим мало јапански, [те̏к да] могу да се споразумем у продавници.
examples.en: I'm studying a little Japanese, just enough to get by in a store.

examples.sr: Учио је [те̏к толѝко̄ да] положи испит.
examples.en: He studied just enough to pass the exam.

meanings: thanks, I don't need a bag

examples.en: Thanks, I don't need a bag, I have my own.
I have small change, don't worry.

note: What you tell a cashier to avoid trouble with change.

forms: literally: can you make it small

examples.en: Can you break this banknote?

note: «уситнити» literally means to make small: this is how you ask for change.

meanings: to have butterflies in one's stomach

examples.sr: Кад га види, одмах [и̏ма лѐптириће у сто̏маку].
examples.en: Whenever she sees him, she gets butterflies in her stomach right away.

examples.sr: Шта је било, [ма̏чка ти је по̀јела јѐзик]?
examples.en: What's the matter, cat got your tongue?

note: Said to someone who suddenly went quiet.

forms: literally: to mix old women and frogs

examples.sr: Не можеш то поредити, [ме̏шаш ба́бе̄ и жа̏бе]!
examples.en: You can't compare those, you're mixing apples and oranges!

meanings: I can barely keep my eyes open

examples.en: It's late, my eyes are closing.
After lunch my eyelids are heavy.
Since this morning I've been dead on my feet.
After the move I was dog-tired.

examples.sr: Дај ми кафу, [мо̏зак ми не ра̏ди].
examples.en: Give me a coffee, my brain isn't working.
Tonight I was dying of exhaustion.

note: «цркнути» is rude and normally said of animals; used jokingly of people.

meanings: it's all the same to me

examples.en: - Tea or coffee? - I don't mind.

examples.sr: Не желим да чујем, [ба̏ш ме бри̏га]!
examples.en: I don't want to hear it, I couldn't care less!

note: A bit rude; shows irritation.

examples.en: - When should we come? - I don't mind.

note: A word of Hungarian origin, used in Vojvodina even by people who don't speak Hungarian.

key: phr:све му је равно до косова
cyr: све му је равно до Косова
acc: све̏ му је ра̑вно до Ко̏сова
forms: literally: to him everything is flat all the way to Kosovo

examples.sr: Пропустио је рок, а [све̏ му је ра̑вно до Ко̏сова].
examples.en: He missed the deadline and doesn't care about anything.

note: Joking, of an indifferent person; such people supposedly live a hundred years.

key: phr:зато што сам ја тако рекла
cyr: зато што сам ја тако рекла
acc: за̀то̄ што̏ сам ја̑ та̀ко̄ ре̏кла

examples.sr: - Зашто? - [За̀то̄ што̏ сам ја̏ та̀ко̄ ре̏кла]!
examples.en: - Why? - Because I said so!

note: A classic parental line; a man says «рекао».

key: phr:видећеш кад ти отац дође кући
cyr: видећеш кад ти отац дође кући
acc: ви̏дећеш ка̑д ти о̀тац до̑ђе ку̏ћи
meanings: just wait till your father gets home

examples.en: Just wait till your father gets home!

note: A parental threat.

examples.en: Whose are you, my child? What family are you from?

note: Serbs like to ask about family and roots: this asks which family you come from.

examples.en: Everything is ready, let's go!

note: From the film «Ко то тамо пева»; a call to get started.

examples.sr: Џабе се смеје, [Ла̏кӣ је ма̏ло не̏рво̄зан].
examples.en: He's laughing for nothing, Laki is a little nervous.

note: A quote from the film «Маратонци трче почасни круг»; said when someone is furious.

examples.en: Again right at the end: less wine!

note: A quote from the film «Лажно лето 68».

key: phr:никада они не могу мене толико мало да плате колико ја могу мало да радим
cyr: никада они не могу мене толико мало да плате колико ја могу мало да радим
acc: ни̏када о̀ни не мо̀гу ме̏не толѝко̄ ма̏ло да пла̑те колѝко ја̑ мо̀гу ма̏ло да ра̏дим
meanings: however little they pay me, I can work even less

examples.sr: Знаш како кажу: [ни̏када о̀ни не мо̀гу ме̏не толѝко̄ ма̏ло да пла̑те колѝко ја̏ мо̀гу ма̏ло да ра̏дим].
examples.en: You know what they say: they can never pay me so little that I can't work even less.

note: A line from the film «Јагоде у грлу», a symbol of an attitude to work.

examples.en: Happy birthday! All the best!

note: Birthdays are usually marked by singing «Данас нам је диван дан».

examples.en: We want to surprise him.
It's urgent? Yeah, I'm running as we speak!

note: A sarcastic reply to a demand for «urgent».

examples.sr: Од данас, [за̏боље ме]! Радите шта хоћете.
examples.en: From today on, I couldn't care less! Do what you want.

note: A mild colloquial form instead of ruder variants.

examples.en: The family has preserved the tradition for centuries.

key: phr:село гори, а баба се чешља
cyr: село гори, а баба се чешља
acc: сѐло го̀рӣ, а ба̏ба се че̏шља
forms: literally: the village is on fire and the old woman is combing her hair

examples.sr: Сви причају о несрећи, а она о плановима за викенд: [сѐло го̀рӣ, а ба̏ба се че̏шља].
examples.en: Everyone is talking about the disaster, and she about her weekend plans: fiddling while Rome burns.

note: Of someone busy with trifles when an urgent problem needs solving; also the name of a Serbian TV series.

forms: literally: I don't know where I'm hitting
meanings: I don't know where to start (from being tired or busy)
I don't know which way to turn

examples.sr: Толико посла имам да [не зна̑м где̏ у̏дарам].
examples.en: I have so much work that I don't know where to start.

forms: literally: I can eat an ox

examples.sr: Од јутрос ништа нисам јео, [мо̀гу во̀ла да по̀једе̄м].
examples.en: I haven't eaten anything since this morning, I could eat a horse.

meanings: to roll on the floor laughing
to be doubled over with laughter

examples.en: We were all rolling with laughter.

meanings: my legs are about to fall off (tired after a long walk)

examples.en: After the walk my legs are about to fall off.

examples.sr: Кад сам чуо тај звук, [ср̏це ми је ста̏ло].
examples.en: When I heard that sound, my heart stopped.

examples.sr: Када је ауто закочио, [у̏мро сам од стра̑ха].
examples.en: When the car braked hard, I almost died of fear.

key: phr:смем ли да помазим вашег пса
cyr: смем ли да помазим вашег пса?
acc: сме̑м ли да по̏мазим ва̏ше̄г пса̏?

examples.en: May I pet your dog?

note: Polite way to ask the owner; the usual answer is «Може!»

key: phr:упала му је секира у мед
cyr: упала му је секира у мед
acc: у̏пала му је сѐкира у ме̑д
forms: literally: his axe fell into honey
meanings: he struck it lucky, an easy success

examples.sr: [У̏пала му је сѐкира у ме̑д], нашао је стан за мало новца.
examples.en: He got a lucky break: he found an apartment for little money.
Luck smiled on him at the exam.

meanings: God looked after him, he was lucky

examples.sr: [Бо̑г га је поглѐдао], избегао је несрећу.
examples.en: God looked after him, he avoided the accident.

meanings: things started going well for him

examples.sr: После много труда најзад [му је кре́нуло] на послу.
examples.en: After a lot of effort, things finally started going well for him at work.

examples.sr: [Посрѐћило му се] да нађе паркинг у центру.
examples.en: He got lucky and found a parking spot downtown.

forms: literally: everything fell into the water

examples.sr: Због кише [све̏ је па̏ло у во̏ду].
examples.en: Because of the rain, everything fell through.

meanings: all my ships have sunk, everything is lost

examples.sr: Кад је изгубио посао, [све̏ ла̏ђе су му пото̀нуле].
examples.en: When he lost his job, everything was lost.

examples.sr: Од јутра [је све̏ кре́нуло по злу̏].
examples.en: Everything has gone wrong since this morning.

examples.sr: Откад је остао без посла, [све̏ му је кре́нуло ни̏збрдо].
examples.en: Ever since he lost his job, everything has gone downhill for him.

key: phr:ништа ми не полази за руком
cyr: ништа ми не полази за руком
acc: ни̏шта ми не по̀лази за ру́ко̄м

examples.sr: Данас [ни̏шта ми не по̀лази за ру́ко̄м].
examples.en: Nothing is working out for me today.

key: phr:ништа ми не иде од руке
cyr: ништа ми не иде од руке
acc: ни̏шта ми не и̏де од ру́ке
meanings: everything is going wrong for me

examples.sr: Данас [ни̏шта ми не и̏де од ру́ке].
examples.en: Everything is going wrong for me today.

meanings: to get up on the wrong side of the bed

examples.sr: Изгледа да је данас [у̀стао на ле̏ву но̏гу].
examples.en: Looks like he got up on the wrong side of the bed today.
I completely flunked the exam.

note: Colloquial, for a complete failure.

examples.sr: Једна грешка и [све̏ о̏де у три̏ лѐпе].
examples.en: One mistake and everything goes down the drain.

note: A mild replacement for a vulgar expression.

examples.sr: Нама се све срушило [ка̏о ку́ла од ка̏ра̄та̄].
examples.en: Everything collapsed for us like a house of cards.
I've been trying for a long time, but I can't get it right.

meanings: it wasn't meant to be for me

examples.sr: Покушао сам, али [нѝје ми би̏ло су̏ђено].
examples.en: I tried, but it wasn't meant to be.

meanings: as if bad luck is following me

examples.sr: Шта год урадим, [ка̏о да ме пра̏ти ма̏лер].
examples.en: Whatever I do, it's as if bad luck is following me.

meanings: whoever cursed me didn't waste their time (jokingly, about a streak of bad luck)

examples.sr: Опет ми је све пошло наопако: [ко̏ ме кле̏о, нѝје да̀нгубио].
examples.en: Everything has gone wrong for me again: whoever cursed me didn't waste their time.

note: Jokey; «дангубити» means to waste time.

examples.sr: Данас [су̑нце пр̏жи] тако да је немогуће бити напољу без капе.
examples.en: The sun is so scorching today that you can't be outside without a hat.

note: Also «сунце пече»; for strong summer sun.

examples.sr: Данас сам [у фа̏зону] да не радим ништа.
examples.en: Today I'm in the mood to do nothing.

note: Colloquial.

examples.en: Take it easy, there's time, don't get nervous.

note: The main mantra of everyday life, from the bank to work meetings.

forms: literally: we lived and we saw

examples.sr: Шта ће бити? [Жи̏ви би̏ли па ви̏дели]!
examples.en: What will happen? We'll see!

meanings: be quiet, it could be worse

examples.sr: Изгубили смо новац, али [ћу̏ти, мо̏же и го̏ре].
examples.en: We lost money, but hush, it could be worse.

note: Serbian consolation: be glad it isn't worse.

examples.en: Football is not my cup of tea.

note: A calque from English.

key: phr:шта је писац хтео да каже
cyr: шта је писац хтео да каже?
acc: шта̏ је пи́сац хте̏о да ка̏же?
meanings: what did the author mean to say? (ironic, about unclear speech)

examples.sr: Остало ми није јасно: [шта̏ је пи́сац хте̏о да ка̏же]?
examples.en: The rest wasn't clear to me: what was the author trying to say?

note: A school question, repeated ironically when someone speaks unclearly.

examples.sr: Знао је истину, али је [др̏жао јѐзик за зу́бима].
