examples.en: He knew the truth, but he held his tongue.

meanings: to get the short end of the stick

examples.en: He got the short end of the stick in the argument.

meanings: to have someone in one's grip
to have someone under one's thumb

examples.sr: Зна његове тајне и [др̀жи га у ша̏ци].
examples.en: He knows his secrets and has him under his thumb.

meanings: to bang one's head against a wall
to be stubborn and push ahead regardless

examples.sr: Не слуша савете, увек [и̏де гла́во̄м кроз зи̑д].
examples.en: He doesn't listen to advice, he always charges ahead regardless.

examples.sr: [Прѐврнуо је не̏бо и зе̏мљу] да нађе решење.
examples.en: He moved heaven and earth to find a solution.

examples.sr: После грешке на послу [о̑н је на та̏нком ле̏ду].
examples.en: After the mistake at work, he's on thin ice.

examples.sr: У расправи је најбоље било [спу̀стити ло̏пту].
examples.en: In the argument, the best thing was to tone it down.

meanings: to turn a blind eye to something

examples.sr: Не треба [затва́рати о̏чи] пред очигледним проблемима.
examples.en: We shouldn't turn a blind eye to obvious problems.
Today I'm buying everyone a round.
Who's buying this round?
Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
How do I get to the city center?

note: Be polite: «Извините, молим вас...»

examples.sr: Хотел је на углу, [не мо̏жеш да про̏машиш].
examples.en: The hotel is on the corner, you can't miss it.

examples.sr: Видећеш велики натпис, [не мо̏жеш да про̏машиш].
examples.en: You'll see a big sign, you can't miss it.

examples.sr: Не брини, [јо̏ш ма̏ло па си ту̑].
examples.en: Don't worry, you're almost there.
Cross the street at the crosswalk.
There's a new crosswalk near the school.

note: Colloquially «зебра».

examples.sr: - Знаш ли ти њега? - [Чу̑ј зна̑м]! То ми је брат!
examples.en: - Do you know him? - Of course I do! He's my brother!

note: «чуј» before a verb makes an indignant «and how!» or «of course».

examples.en: We will continue regardless of the obstacles.
I'll come regardless of being tired.

examples.sr: [С о̏бзиром на] гужву, кренули смо раније.
examples.en: Given the traffic jam, we left earlier.

examples.sr: [С о̏бзиром на] време, остајемо код куће.
examples.en: Given the weather, we're staying home.
The candidate's experience should be taken into account.

examples.sr: Молим вас да [у̏зме̄те у о̏бзӣр] моје стање.
examples.en: Please take my condition into account.

forms: literally: it doesn't come into consideration

examples.en: Being late is out of the question.
Selling the house is out of the question.

note: The opposite is «долази у обзир»: it is suitable, possible.

examples.en: Be considerate toward the sick.
You should be considerate of your neighbors.

forms: literally: let it stand, it doesn't eat bread
meanings: let it sit there, it doesn't cost anything (about a spare)

examples.sr: Узми и то, [не̏ка сто̀јӣ, хле̏ба не је̏де].
examples.en: Take that too, it doesn't hurt to have it.

examples.sr: Купио сам још једну, [не̏ка сто̀јӣ, хле̏ба не је̏де].
examples.en: I bought another one, let it sit there, it doesn't cost anything to keep.

note: Said about something bought in reserve that bothers no one.

forms: literally: he has no hair on his tongue

examples.sr: Он је искрен, [не̑ма дла̏ке на јѐзику].
examples.en: He's honest, he doesn't mince words.
My aunt says everything straight to your face.

forms: literally: he looks for a hair in an egg
meanings: he splits hairs, he looks for a flaw

examples.en: The boss is always nitpicking.

examples.sr: Не [тра̏жи дла̏ку у ја̏јету], све је у реду.
examples.en: Don't nitpick, everything is fine.

examples.sr: Аутобус је прошао [за дла̏ку] поред нас.
examples.en: The bus missed us by a hair.
We avoided the accident by a hair.

key: phr:вук длаку мења, али ћуд никад
cyr: вук длаку мења, али ћуд никад
acc: ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏кад
forms: literally: the wolf changes its coat, but never its temper
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots

examples.sr: Многи кажу: [ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏кад].
examples.en: Many say: a wolf changes its coat, but never its nature.

note: «ћуд» means temper, character.

forms: literally: goes along with the fur

examples.sr: Колеге му [и̏ду ни̑з дла̏ку] да нема свађе.
examples.en: His colleagues humor him so there are no quarrels.

examples.sr: Не мораш да му [и̏деш ни̑з дла̏ку].
examples.en: You don't have to go along with everything he says.
Excuse me, what time is it?
What time is it now?

note: Colloquially also «Колико има сати?»

examples.en: See you at half past two.
Lunch is at half past twelve.

note: «пола» + the next hour: «пола пет» = 4:30

examples.en: We'll arrive at five to three.
The train leaves at ten to four.

note: Minutes «до» + the next hour: «петнаест до шест» = 5:45

examples.en: I don't want to wait.
She doesn't want to talk to me.

note: «нећу» + да + present tense: refusal, unwillingness; «нећу доћи» is a plain future: I won't come

meanings: long hair, short on brains (about a shallow person)

examples.sr: Не слушај је, [ду́га ко̀са, кра̏тка па̏ме̄т].
examples.en: Don't listen to her, long hair, short on brains.

note: A mocking and rather rude proverb; better not to say it to a woman.

examples.sr: Заборавио си кључеве у ауту? [Где̏ ти је па̏ме̄т би́ла]?
examples.en: You left the keys in the car? Where was your head?

examples.sr: [Где̏ ти је па̏ме̄т би́ла] кад си то рекао?
examples.en: What were you thinking when you said that?

forms: literally: he has more luck than sense
meanings: he's luckier than he is smart

examples.en: He's luckier than he is smart.

examples.sr: Прошао је без повреда, [и̏ма ви̏ше сре̏ће не̏го па̏мети].
examples.en: He got away without injuries, he has more luck than sense.

note: About someone who did something stupid and still got away with it.

key: phr:као да је попио сву памет света
cyr: као да је попио сву памет света
acc: ка̏о да је по̀пио сву̏ па̏ме̄т све̑та
forms: literally: as if he drank all the wisdom of the world

examples.sr: Прича [ка̏о да је по̀пио сву̏ па̏ме̄т све̑та].
examples.en: He talks as if he had all the wisdom in the world.

examples.sr: Ћути, нећеш ти [по̀пити сву̏ па̏ме̄т све̑та].
examples.en: Be quiet, you're not smarter than everyone else.

meanings: don't tell me what to do

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да ми со̏лиш па̏ме̄т], знам шта радим.
examples.en: Don't lecture me, I know what I'm doing.
My colleague is constantly lecturing me.

note: About unsolicited advice.

meanings: can you take a picture of me?

examples.sr: [Мо̏жеш ли да ме сли̏каш] испред зграде?
examples.en: Can you take a picture of me in front of the building?
Excuse me, could you take a picture of us?
Well done, you got a good shot.
Can I pay by card?
You can pay by card here.

meanings: to tap the card (on the terminal)

examples.en: Tap your card on the terminal.
Just tap your card and you're done.
My card was declined at the terminal.

meanings: to pick a fight with someone
to get into it with someone

examples.sr: Не [зака̀чи се с њи̑м], опасан је.
examples.en: Don't mess with him, he's dangerous.
He's picked a fight with someone again.

examples.sr: [Све̏ у свѐму], била је то добра одлука.
examples.en: All in all, it was a good decision.
All in all, we had a good rest.

meanings: I would like to make an appointment (with a doctor)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлела бих да за̀кажем пре́глед].
examples.en: Good afternoon, I would like to make an appointment.

examples.sr: [Жѐлео бих да за̀кажем пре́глед] за четвртак.
examples.en: I would like to make an appointment for Thursday.

note: A man says «желео бих».

examples.sr: Докторе, [не о̀сећам се до̀бро] већ три дана.
examples.en: Doctor, I haven't been feeling well for three days.
Excuse me, I don't feel well.
I'm allergic to penicillin.
She's allergic to pollen.

meanings: I find it hard to breathe

examples.sr: Од јутрос [те̑шко ми је да ди̏шем].
examples.en: I've had trouble breathing since this morning.
I find it hard to sleep.
Call an ambulance, please!
Quick, call an ambulance!
Next week I'm defending my thesis.

examples.sr: Студент је [бра̏нио ма̏стер ра̑д] пред комисијом.
examples.en: The student defended his master's thesis before the committee.

note: The defense itself is «одбрана».

examples.en: Get out of here! I didn't tell you anything.
Scram, man!

note: Very rude, from Turkish; «сиктер бре» means get lost.

forms: literally: I haven't closed an eye
meanings: I didn't get a wink of sleep

examples.en: I didn't sleep a wink all night.
Because of the heat, we didn't sleep a wink.

examples.sr: Та слика криво виси и [бо̀де о̏чи].
examples.en: That picture hangs crooked and it's an eyesore.

key: phr:не могу га очима да видим
cyr: не могу га очима да видим
acc: не мо̀гу га о̏чима да ви̏дӣм
meanings: I can't stand the sight of him

examples.sr: Од тог комшије [не мо̀гу га о̏чима да ви̏дӣм].
examples.en: I can't stand the sight of that neighbor.
I can't stand the sight of her.

note: About a woman: «не могу је очима да видим»

key: phr:далеко од очију, далеко од срца
cyr: далеко од очију, далеко од срца
acc: далѐко од о̀чијӯ, далѐко од ср̏ца
meanings: out of sight, out of mind

examples.sr: [Далѐко од о̀чијӯ, далѐко од ср̏ца], каже пословица.
examples.en: Out of sight, out of mind, as the saying goes.
I'm boiling in this bus.
Everyone is boiling at thirty degrees.
I'm melting from the heat.
What are you doing? I'm melting in the sun.

meanings: I've turned into a crackling (very sunburnt or overheated)

examples.sr: После сата на плажи [претво̀рио сам се у чва́рак].
examples.en: After an hour on the beach, I've turned into a crackling.

key: phr:није што је вруће, него што је спарина
cyr: није што је вруће, него што је спарина
acc: нѝје што̏ је вру̏ће, не̏го што̏ је спа̀рина
meanings: it's not the heat, it's the humidity

examples.sr: [Нѝје што̏ је вру̏ће, не̏го што̏ је спа̀рина], не могу да дишем.
examples.en: It's not the heat, it's the humidity, I can't breathe.

note: A summer saying-meme about muggy weather.

examples.sr: Ако изађем у подне, [до̏бӣћу то̏плотни у̏да̄р].
examples.en: If I go out at noon, I'm going to get heatstroke.

examples.sr: У овој соби [не мо̏же да се ди̏ше].
examples.en: You can't breathe in this room.

examples.sr: Напољу [не мо̏же да се ди̏ше] од врућине.
examples.en: You can't breathe outside in this heat.
Give me some water, I'm dying of heat.

note: «цркох» is a jokey aorist of «цркнути»; rather rude, colloquial.

examples.en: - See you at six? - Okay!
- Can I sit here? - Sure.

note: The most common affirmative reply in conversation.

examples.en: - Do you want to come with us? - Why not?
Coffee? Why not!

examples.sr: - Можеш ли да ми помогнеш? - [Не̑ма про̀блема].
examples.en: - Can you help me? - No problem.
No problem, I'll be there on time.
- See you tomorrow at ten. - It's a deal.

examples.sr: Његов коментар је [ди̏гао пра̀шину] на мрежама.
examples.en: His comment caused a stir on social media.
That article will cause a stir.
If you read between the lines, you'll understand the truth.
I know how to read between the lines.

meanings: the pen is mightier than the sword

examples.sr: Договорили су се мирно, [ре̑ч је ја̀ча̄ од ма̏ча].
examples.en: They settled it peacefully, words are stronger than swords.
Come over to my place!

note: In slang «гајба» means a flat or home; literally a crate (for beer).

key: phr:као да му је из ока испао
cyr: као да му је из ока испао
acc: ка̏о да му је из о̏ка ѝспао
forms: literally: as if he fell out of his eye
meanings: the spitting image of (his father, mother)

examples.sr: Син је оцу [ка̏о да му је из о̏ка ѝспао].
examples.en: The son is the spitting image of his father.

examples.sr: Ћерка је мајци [ка̏о да јој је из о̏ка испа̀ла].
examples.en: The daughter is the spitting image of her mother.

meanings: to not take one's eyes off someone
to not take one's eyes off

examples.sr: Целе вечери [нѝје ски̏дао о̏чи с ње̑].
examples.en: He didn't take his eyes off her all evening.
The mother doesn't take her eyes off the child.

examples.sr: Разговор са њом ми је [отво̀рио о̏чи].
examples.en: Talking to her opened my eyes.
I want to open your eyes.

key: phr:на једно уво уђе, на друго изађе
cyr: на једно уво уђе, на друго изађе
acc: на је̏дно у̏во у̏ђе, на дру̏го и̏зађе
meanings: it goes in one ear and out the other

examples.sr: Шта год му кажеш, [на је̏дно у̏во у̏ђе, на дру̏го и̏зађе].
examples.en: Whatever you tell him, it goes in one ear and out the other.

examples.sr: Већ два дана [ра̏збијам гла̑ву] над овим проблемом.
examples.en: I've been racking my brain over this problem for two days.
Don't rack your brain, it'll be fine.

forms: literally: it doesn't go into my head
meanings: I can't wrap my head around it
it makes no sense to me

examples.sr: [Не и̏де ми у гла̑ву] зашто је то урадио.
examples.en: I can't wrap my head around why he did that.

meanings: to have one's head in the clouds

examples.sr: На часу је стално [с гла́во̄м у о̏бла̄цима].
examples.en: He always has his head in the clouds in class.
He always has his head in the clouds.

key: phr:не кајем се због своје тетоваже
cyr: не кајем се због своје тетоваже
acc: не ка̏јем се збо̏г сво̀је тето̀важе

examples.sr: Прошло је десет година и [не ка̏јем се збо̏г сво̀је тето̀важе].
examples.en: Ten years have passed and I don't regret my tattoo.
Everyone passed the exam.
I hope I'll pass the exam.

note: «пасти на испиту» means to fail an exam.

examples.en: I would like to go to the cinema.
I would like to try this dish.

note: A man says «волео бих», a woman «волела бих»; softer than «хоћу» and «желим».

meanings: that's the first I've heard of it
I'm hearing about it for the first time

examples.en: That's the first I've heard of it!

examples.sr: Извини, [пр̀ви пу̑т чу̏је̄м за то̑] место.
examples.en: Sorry, I've never heard of that place.

examples.sr: Не питај ме, [ни́сам упу̀ћен у то̑].
examples.en: Don't ask me, I'm not in the loop.
She hasn't been told the details.

forms: literally: that's a Spanish village to me

examples.en: Math is all Greek to me.

examples.sr: То ми је [шпа̏нско сѐло], не разумем ништа.
examples.en: It's all Greek to me, I don't understand anything.
Where did he go? God only knows.
God only knows when he'll come.
Come in, make yourself at home.

examples.sr: Молим вас, [осѐћајте се ка̏о ко̏д ку̏ће].
examples.en: Please, make yourself at home.

examples.sr: - Не знам како ћу све стићи! - [Ма̏ ла̏гано]!
examples.en: - I don't know how I'll get everything done! - Come on, take it easy!
Take it easy, there's time.

examples.sr: - Морамо одмах да кренемо. - Полако, [и̏ма вре̏мена].
examples.en: - We have to leave right now. - Easy, there's time.
Don't rush, there's time.

examples.sr: - Шеф је љут на мене! - [Не ло̀жи се].
examples.en: - The boss is angry at me! - Don't get worked up.

note: Colloquial.

examples.sr: - Бојим се да нећу моћи да купим. - Ма [би̏ће].
examples.en: - I'm afraid I won't be able to buy it. - Come on, it'll work out.

note: Reassuring, without forcing events.

forms: literally: you bang like Maxim at a division

examples.sr: Не слушај га, [лу̏па ка̏о Ма̏ксим по дивѝзији].
examples.en: Don't listen to him, he's talking nonsense.

note: Максим is either a gunner or the «Maxim» machine gun.

examples.sr: Синоћ је дошао кући [пѝјан ка̏о ма̑јка].
examples.en: Last night he came home dead drunk.

note: By one version, women in labor were given rakija as a painkiller.

key: phr:као да је пао с крушке
cyr: као да је пао с крушке
acc: ка̏о да је па̏о с кру̏шке
forms: literally: as if he fell from a pear tree
meanings: as if he just dropped from the sky, clueless
as if he were born yesterday

examples.sr: Шта ме гледаш [ка̏о да си па̏о с кру̏шке]?
examples.en: Why are you looking at me like you just dropped from the sky?

examples.sr: Не [мла̏ти пра̏зну сла̏му], реци шта хоћеш.
examples.en: Don't talk nonsense, say what you want.

meanings: to pull the wool over someone's eyes

examples.sr: Он само [про̀даје ма̏глу] и ништа не ради.
examples.en: He only feeds people a line and does nothing.
Don't feed people a line.
Sorry, my connection is breaking up.
My connection is breaking up, we'll talk later.

examples.sr: [Сла̏бо те чу̏је̄м], можеш ли да поновиш?
examples.en: I can barely hear you, can you repeat that?
Sorry, I can barely hear you.

meanings: the video froze on my end

examples.en: Wait, my picture froze.
The internet went down in the whole building.

examples.sr: [Да ли ме са̏да чу̏је̄ш] и видиш?
examples.en: Can you hear and see me now?

examples.sr: Мало сам променио везу, [да ли ме са̏да чу̏је̄те]?
examples.en: I changed my connection a bit, can you hear me now?

forms: literally: to cost like Saint Petka's scrambled eggs
meanings: to cost an arm and a leg

examples.sr: Овај стан [ко̏шта ка̏о све̏те Пе̏тке ка̏јгана].
examples.en: This apartment costs a fortune.

note: Its origin is linked to religious traditions.

forms: literally: to pick a green melon patch
meanings: to come to a bad end

examples.en: If you do that, you'll be in big trouble.

forms: literally: the devil has come for his own
meanings: the day of reckoning has come
the devil has come to collect

examples.sr: Годинама је варао људе, сада је [до̏шао ђа̏во̄ по сво̀је].
examples.en: For years he deceived people, now the day of reckoning has come.

forms: literally: like a chick in tow fibers
meanings: like a chicken with its head cut off

examples.sr: Без плана сам [ка̏о пи̏ле у ку̏чине].
examples.en: Without a plan I'm completely lost.

examples.sr: Била је [ка̏о пи̏ле у ку̏чине] међу папирима.
examples.en: She was completely lost among the papers.

forms: literally: fell from a horse onto a donkey
meanings: to go from bad to worse
to come down in the world

examples.sr: Променио је посао и [па̏о с ко̀ња на ма̀гарца].
examples.en: He changed jobs and things got worse.

forms: literally: to go with one's throat into the strawberries

examples.en: Don't rush headlong, think it over.
He always rushes in headlong.

forms: literally: to be on a war footing
meanings: to be at war with each other

examples.sr: Комшије су [на ра̏тној но̀зи] због музике.
examples.en: The neighbors are at daggers drawn over the music.

examples.sr: Брат и ја смо [на ра̏тној но̀зи].
examples.en: My brother and I aren't speaking.

forms: literally: to not smell each other
meanings: to not be able to stand each other

examples.en: The Petrovićes don't get along with their neighbors.

forms: literally: to not be in love
meanings: to not be on good terms

examples.sr: Они [ни́су у љу́бави] од прошле године.
examples.en: They've been on cool terms since last year.

note: Ironic.

examples.en: Granny Mara talks and talks and never shuts her mouth!

note: Colloquial.

key: phr:први мачићи се у воду бацају
cyr: први мачићи се у воду бацају
acc: пр̀вӣ ма̀чићи се у во̏ду ба̏цају
forms: literally: the first kittens are thrown into the water
meanings: the first attempt is always the roughest

examples.sr: Не жали, [пр̀ви ма̀чићи се у во̏ду ба̏цају].
examples.en: Don't feel bad, the first attempt is always the roughest.

meanings: to be out of one's mind

examples.en: What's wrong with you, have you lost your mind?

meanings: to be on pins and needles
to sit on pins and needles

examples.sr: Чекао је резултате и [се̏део ка̏о на ѝглама].
examples.en: He was waiting for the results and sitting on pins and needles.

key: phr:као да је пао с марса
cyr: као да је пао с Марса
acc: ка̏о да је па̏о с Ма̑рса
meanings: as if he just dropped from Mars
as if he's from another planet

examples.sr: Гледа ме [ка̏о да је па̏о с Ма̑рса].
examples.en: He's looking at me as if he just dropped from Mars.

forms: literally: let me knock on wood

examples.sr: Све иде добро, [да ку̏цнем у др̏во].
examples.en: Everything is going well, knock on wood.
I'm healthy, knock on wood.

note: You knock on wood as you say it; also «да не чује зло».

forms: literally: to go like a barefoot man through thorns

examples.sr: У тој фирми сам [про̏шао ка̏о бо̑с по тр̑њу].
examples.en: I went through a lot at that company.

examples.sr: Након развода је [про̏шла ка̏о бо̑с по тр̑њу].
examples.en: After the divorce she had a hard time.

forms: literally: to enter the fairies' round dance
meanings: to get caught in a vicious circle

examples.en: The debtor got caught in a vicious circle.

note: «врзино коло» is a magic circle you can't escape from.

examples.sr: Шта је, [ма̏чка ти је по̀јела јѐзик]?
examples.en: What's the matter, cat got your tongue?

meanings: to treasure like the apple of one's eye

examples.sr: Чува ту књигу [ка̏о о̏чи у гла́ви].
examples.en: He treasures that book like the apple of his eye.

meanings: to leave someone in the lurch

examples.en: They didn't leave me in the lurch.
Don't leave me in the lurch.

key: phr:проћи поред некога као поред турског гробља
cyr: проћи поред некога као поред турског гробља
acc: про̑ћи по̏ред не̏кога ка̏о по̏ред ту̏рског гро̏бља
forms: literally: to pass someone like a Turkish cemetery
meanings: to walk right past someone without noticing them

examples.sr: Прошао је поред мене [ка̏о по̏ред ту̏рског гро̏бља].
examples.en: He walked right past me as if I weren't there.

forms: literally: to get fired up over someone
meanings: to have a huge crush on someone

examples.en: He has a huge crush on her.

note: Colloquial; «ложити се» generally means to get fired up or hooked on something.

forms: literally: to come unglued over someone
meanings: (slang) to lose one's head over someone

examples.en: I'm completely crazy about her.

note: Slang; the verb «одлепити» literally means to unstick.

examples.en: I lost my head over her.

meanings: to be taken in by someone's charm

examples.en: I totally fell for her smile.

note: Colloquial «скроз» means completely, through and through.

forms: literally: to be mad about someone

examples.en: Marko is crazy about Maša.

note: Also used for a passion: «луд сам за сладоледом» (I'm crazy about ice cream).

forms: literally: to fall in love up to the ears
meanings: to fall head over heels in love

examples.sr: [Заљу́била] се до ушију у новог колегу.
examples.en: She fell head over heels in love with the new colleague.

forms: literally: as far as it touches me

examples.en: As far as I'm concerned, we can go.
That doesn't concern you!

note: The verb «тицати се» always takes the genitive, mostly in the 3rd person: «тиче се свих нас».

meanings: to bring up a topic in passing

examples.sr: У разговору смо се [дота̀кли] теме путовања.
examples.en: In the conversation we touched on the topic of travel.

note: A topic is touched on briefly, without detail.

forms: literally: to turn off the topic

examples.sr: Мало смо [скре̏нули] с теме, вратимо се на оно што смо причали.
examples.en: We went a bit off topic, let's get back to what we were talking about.

note: Often said to bring the conversation back to the main point.

forms: literally: to shake out every topic

examples.sr: Седели смо сатима и [претрѐсли] сваку тему.
examples.en: We sat for hours and went over every topic.

forms: literally: to comb a topic lengthwise and across
meanings: to go through a topic inside out
to cover a topic from every angle

examples.sr: Ту тему смо [про̏чешљали] уздуж и попреко.
examples.en: We went through that topic inside out.

examples.sr: После толико година пријатељства рекли смо једно другом све [од А̑ до Ш].
examples.en: After so many years of friendship, we told each other everything from A to Z.

note: The Serbian Cyrillic alphabet ends in Ш, so it is «од А до Ш» where English says «from A to Z».

forms: literally: to kill two flies with one blow
meanings: to kill two birds with one stone

examples.sr: Ако стигнем у пошту на путу до посла, [у̏бићу] две муве једним ударцем.
examples.en: If I stop by the post office on my way to work, I'll kill two birds with one stone.

meanings: to have a finger in every pie

examples.sr: Он је увек [у сва̏кој чо́рбӣ] мирођија.
examples.en: He always has a finger in every pie.

note: Said about a person who interferes in everything.

examples.en: The task is easy as pie.

forms: literally: like a calf at a painted gate

examples.sr: Стоји и гледа [ка̏о] теле у шарена врата.
examples.en: He stands there staring blankly.

examples.sr: Немој да ме [фа̏рбаш], знам да лажеш.
examples.en: Don't try to fool me, I know you're lying.

note: Colloquial «фарбати некога» means to deceive or fool someone.

forms: literally: to look into someone's cup
meanings: to tell someone's fortune from coffee grounds

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми [по̀гледа̄ш] у шољу?
examples.en: Can you read my coffee grounds?

note: After Turkish coffee the grounds are flipped onto the saucer and the future is «read» in the patterns.

forms: literally: see you at the horse
meanings: see you at the Horse (the monument on Republic Square in Belgrade)

examples.en: See you at the Horse at six.

note: The monument to Prince Mihailo Obrenović on a horse is the traditional meeting place for Belgraders.

key: phr:леди ми се крв у жилама
cyr: леди ми се крв у жилама
acc: ле̏ди ми се кр̑в у жи̏лама
forms: literally: my blood freezes in my veins

examples.sr: Кад чујем тај крик, [ле̏ди] ми се крв у жилама.
examples.en: When I hear that scream, my blood runs cold.

key: phr:срце ми је сишло у пете
cyr: срце ми је сишло у пете
acc: ср̏це ми је си̏шло у пе̏те
forms: literally: my heart went down into my heels
meanings: my heart sank into my boots

examples.sr: Кад сам видео пса, [ср̏це] ми је сишло у пете.
examples.en: When I saw the dog, my heart sank into my boots.

forms: literally: to be afraid of one's own shadow
meanings: to be afraid of one's own shadow

examples.sr: После оног догађаја [пла̏ши] се сопствене сенке.
examples.en: Since that incident he's afraid of his own shadow.
I got goosebumps all over from fear.

note: A woman says «сва сам се најежила».

examples.en: Actually, I didn't know.

note: Written as two words: «у ствари». «Уствари» is a mistake.

examples.en: Come on, don't tell me!

note: Expresses surprise or disbelief.

forms: literally: to carry one's head in a bag

examples.en: A journalist risks his neck.
He writes like chicken scratch.

forms: literally: to cover oneself with one's ears
meanings: to want to sink through the floor with shame

examples.en: I wanted to sink through the floor with shame.

note: Said about intense shame.

examples.en: Come off it, don't talk nonsense!

note: «бре» is an emotional particle expressing indignation or emphasis.

forms: literally: a little beer for the nerves
meanings: a beer to calm the nerves (rhyming joke)

examples.en: Come on, let's have a little beer for the nerves!

note: A rhyming jokey phrase, like «пиће за младиће».

examples.en: This is a cool idea!

note: The word «фора» is very versatile: a gimmick, a trick, a scheme.

meanings: to be a ball of energy, to get everything done

examples.en: You're awesome!
He works like a beast.

note: Praise.

forms: literally: Đura sewed it for me

examples.sr: Шеф је рекао да ће нам платити хиљаду и по евра. - [Ши̏о] ми га Ђура!
examples.en: The boss said he'd pay us fifteen hundred euros. - Yeah, right!

note: After a Belgrade tailor named Đura. It used to mean quality, now it expresses disbelief.

forms: literally: the pleasant for the dear
meanings: to pay someone back in kind

examples.en: We'll pay them back in kind.

note: Can be used for good or for bad.

forms: literally: your dad is not a glazier
meanings: you're not made of glass, move out of the way

examples.en: Move over, your dad's not a glazier!

note: What fathers say to kids who block the TV.

forms: literally: to bring out rabid worms

examples.en: Don't listen to him, he's talking nonsense.

forms: literally: chicha-miche, the story is ready

examples.en: We signed and - that's that.

note: A jokey way to end a story.

meanings: April first - I trust no one

examples.en: April first - I trust no one!

note: A chant said in Serbia on April Fools' Day.

examples.en: I'm only taking carry-on luggage.
Show your boarding pass.
Please fasten your seat belts.

note: A phrase heard on a plane.

forms: literally: to look as if a she-bear is dancing
meanings: to gawk at someone as at a spectacle

examples.en: Everyone is gawking at him with their mouths open.
My battery is dead.
Can I charge my phone?

meanings: do you have a wine opener?

examples.en: Do you have a corkscrew?

examples.sr: Не [да̑ј] се, сад је пола посла готово!
examples.en: Don't give up, half the work is already done!

forms: literally: I have a marble for that
meanings: I have a knack for it
I know my way around it

examples.en: I have a knack for that.

note: Colloquial; «кликер» is a glass marble for playing.

examples.en: Drinks for the lads, here you go!

note: A rhyming catchphrase of waiters.

examples.en: Do you have change for twenty euros?
I care about those books.

note: The construction is «стало ми је до» + genitive.

forms: literally: even the sparrows know that
meanings: everybody knows that, it's common knowledge

examples.sr: То [и вра́пци зна̏јӯ], не мораш да објашњаваш.
examples.en: Even the sparrows know that, you don't have to explain.

examples.sr: Од среће су јој потекле [су̏зе ра̏доснице].
examples.en: Tears of joy ran down her face from happiness.

forms: literally: you were not born on a boat
meanings: close the door, were you born in a barn? (a reproach)

examples.en: Close the door, were you born in a barn!

note: A parent's reproach: a boat has no door, so there is nothing to close.

key: phr:ако сви скачу с моста, хоћеш ли и ти
cyr: ако сви скачу с моста, хоћеш ли и ти
acc: а̏ко сви̏ ска̏чу с мо̏ста, хо̏ћеш ли и ти
meanings: if everyone jumped off a bridge, would you too?

examples.sr: Ако сви [ска̏чу] с моста, хоћеш ли и ти?
examples.en: If everybody jumps off a bridge, will you jump too?

note: A parent's answer to «everybody does it».

meanings: let's go! let's do this! (excited cry)

examples.en: There's a party tonight, let's go!

note: Youth slang. Hence «гасери»: trendy people in brand-name clothes.

examples.sr: Та [жу̏та шта̑мпа] пише само о скандалима.
examples.en: That tabloid press writes only about scandals.

note: Also: жуто новинарство; cheap stories are «петпарачке приче» (five-para stories).

meanings: to drink like a fish, to drink heavily

examples.sr: Он [пи̏је̄ ка̏о сму̑к], сваке вечери је у кафани.
examples.en: He drinks like a fish, he's at the pub every evening.

note: Смук is a snake; an old belief says it drinks milk from cows' udders.

examples.sr: Био је [пѝјан ка̏о ле̏тва] и једва је стајао.
examples.en: He was drunk as a skunk and could hardly stand.

note: Летва is a lath (wooden strip); it warps when soaked, like a drunk.

examples.en: He came home dead drunk.

meanings: to drink oneself senseless, to get blind drunk

examples.en: Last night he drank himself senseless.

meanings: to act like a real man, to man up

examples.en: Man up and admit your mistake!

note: Colloq.: neuter «мушко»/«женско» mean a man/a woman: «Она је право женско».

meanings: Wednesday is a little Friday (midweek, time to relax)

examples.sr: [Сре́да је ма̑лӣ пе́так], па идемо на кафу.
examples.en: Wednesday is a little Friday, so let's go for a coffee.

forms: literally: to straighten the crooked Drina
meanings: to tilt at windmills, to attempt the impossible

examples.sr: Не трошите снагу, то је као [ѝсправљати кри̏ву Дри̏ну].
examples.en: Don't waste your energy, it's like tilting at windmills.

note: The Drina is a winding border river; it cannot be straightened.

meanings: to love wholeheartedly, to love with all one's soul

examples.en: I love you with all my heart, I don't know any other way.

note: Colloquial.

meanings: death to fascism, freedom to the people (Partisan slogan)

examples.en: Death to fascism, freedom to the people!

note: A slogan of the Yugoslav Partisans in World War II, still heard on memorial days.

meanings: is this the end of the line?

examples.en: Excuse me, is this the end of the line?

note: «је л'» is short for «је ли»; «ред» is a line, a queue.

examples.en: What a party, it's insane!

note: Colloq. exclamation; often admiring, not only critical.

meanings: what was his name again? (when trying to recall)

examples.en: What was his name again, that actor?

note: «Беше» (imperfect of «бити») is just a filler here: «Одакле си беше?» - where are you from again?

examples.sr: Он [пу̏ши ка̏о Ту̀рчин] и стално кашље.
examples.en: He smokes like a chimney and coughs all the time.
They said he drinks like a fish.

key: phr:као да је дошао из бијафре
cyr: као да је дошао из Бијафре
acc: ка̏о да је до̏шао из Би̏јафре
forms: literally: as if he came from Biafra

examples.sr: Једе као да је [до̏шао из Би̏јафре].
examples.en: He eats as if he'd been starving for a week.

note: Refers to the famine in Biafra, a secessionist region of Nigeria, in the 1960s.

meanings: something incomprehensible, all Greek to me

examples.en: This grammar is all Greek to me.

forms: literally: to dissolve like the Bulgarian parliament
meanings: to crush, to wipe out completely

examples.en: The team crushed its opponent.

meanings: up to one's ears in debt

examples.en: He's up to his ears in debt.

forms: literally: naive as a French maid
meanings: feigning naivety, a wolf in sheep's clothing

examples.en: Don't act so innocent.

meanings: well, thanks a lot (ironic reply to an unpleasant remark)

examples.sr: [Ба̏ш ти хва́ла], мама, знаш да ме обрадујеш.
examples.en: Well, thanks a lot, Mom, you really know how to cheer me up.

note: Sarcasm: «thanks» in reply to a disservice or a tactless remark.

key: phr:није срамота не знати, срамота је не питати
cyr: није срамота не знати, срамота је не питати
acc: нѝје срамо̀та не зна̏ти, срамо̀та је не пи́тати
meanings: there is no shame in not knowing, the shame is in not asking

examples.sr: Питај слободно: [нѝје срамо̀та не зна̏ти, срамо̀та је не пи̏тати].
examples.en: Feel free to ask: there is no shame in not knowing, the shame is in not asking.

meanings: to do something for the pleasure of it, for the love of it

examples.en: He sings in the choir just for the love of it.

examples.sr: Моја бака верује у [га̏тање из та̏лога].
examples.en: My grandmother believes in reading coffee grounds.

meanings: oh, drop it, don't make a big deal of it

examples.en: Oh, forget it, it's no big deal.

meanings: happy slava, host (a guest's greeting on a family's saint's day)

examples.en: Happy slava, host!

note: The hostess may offer «жито» (boiled wheat): the guest crosses himself, wishes well and eats.

meanings: have a good time, enjoy yourself

examples.en: Have a great time at the concert!

note: To several people or politely: «лепо се проведите»; the reply is often «и ти».

examples.en: Everything's going well, knock on wood.

note: Said while tapping wood, so as not to jinx things.

examples.en: Tomorrow we're driving to the seaside.

note: «кола» (car) is plural only: instr. «колима». «колом» is from «коло» (round dance).

meanings: backwater, a place where everything is badly run

examples.sr: Ово није Европа, ово је [та̑мнӣ ви̏лајет].
examples.en: This isn't Europe, this is some dark backwater.

note: A vilayet was an Ottoman province, here Bosnia. Now an ironic image of disorder and corruption.

meanings: by the book, properly, by all the rules

examples.en: Everything was done by the book.

note: ЈУС: the Yugoslav standard, like DIN in Germany. The phrase outlived Yugoslavia.

forms: literally: to knock oneself with eggs
meanings: to tap Easter eggs against each other

examples.en: Children tap eggs against each other on Easter.

note: An Easter game: two people knock their eggs together, and the one whose shell stays whole wins.

examples.en: Judging by the clouds, it's going to rain.

note: A frozen gerund; then «по» + loc.: «судећи по изгледу», «судећи по гласу».

examples.en: He stayed there on principle.

note: «Инат» is almost a national trait: acting «из ината» is a point of pride.

meanings: on St George's Day the hajduks (outlaws) gather

examples.en: They say: «On St George's Day the hajduks gather».

note: A saying: hajduks hid in winter, and on St George's Day, with the warmth, came out and formed bands.

forms: literally: how handsome you are to me
meanings: how handsome you look (said with feeling)

examples.sr: [Ка̀ка̄в си ми ле̑п] у том оделу!
examples.en: How handsome you look in that suit!

note: «Ми» is not 'to me' here but shows the speaker's feeling (ethical dative).

forms: literally: like a fly without a head
meanings: to run around like a headless chicken

examples.sr: Трчао је около [ка̏о му̀ха без гла́ве].
examples.en: He was running around like a headless chicken.

note: About a flustered person who grabs at everything and finishes nothing.

examples.en: I'm cold, close the window!

note: Impersonal, with dat.: «зима ми/ти/му је». «Зима» also means winter; cold weather: «хладно».

examples.en: - Can I help you? - I'm just looking, thanks.

note: The standard answer to a shop assistant's «Изволите?». Pattern: «да» + present.

meanings: do you have anything smaller? (smaller bills or change)

examples.sr: [Да ли и̏мате не̏што си̏тније]? Имам само хиљадарку.
examples.en: Do you have anything smaller? I only have a thousand-dinar note.

note: Asked by cashiers when given a large banknote. Answer: «Имам» or «Немам, нажалост».

meanings: that's just your horoscope (that's how it goes)

examples.sr: - Зашто увек каснимо? - [Та̀ка̄в ти је хо̏роскоп]!
examples.en: - Why are we always late? - Well, that's your horoscope!

note: A joking all-purpose answer to «why?» when there is no logical explanation.

meanings: I have an appointment (with a doctor, hairdresser)

examples.en: I have a hairdresser's appointment on Saturday.

note: «Код» + gen.: with whom: код зубара, код фризера. Booking ahead is normal.

examples.en: How much is a kilo of strawberries?

note: Colloq. variant of «колико кошта?», used for prices at a market. Also «Пошто су јагоде?».

examples.sr: На плакату пише: [пла̏ти два̑, у̀зми три̏].
examples.en: The poster says: pay for two, take three.

note: Ad slogan: buy two, get three. Nearby words: «попуст» (discount), «распродаја» (sale), «50 посто» (50 percent).

examples.en: It's just an ordinary typo.
How old are you turning this year?

note: Said to a birthday person. Plain age: «Колико година имаш?»; birth year: «Које си годиште?».

examples.en: - What year were you born? - 1975.

note: More common than «колико имаш година?» for sizing up someone's age; people compare it with their own year.

meanings: have a good time, enjoy yourselves

examples.en: Are you going to a birthday party? Have a great time!

note: A wish to people going to a party, a celebration or on vacation.

examples.sr: [Бо̏га пи̑та̄ј] где је била све време.
examples.en: God only knows where she's been all this time.

note: Said when nobody knows the answer.

examples.en: - I forgot my gloves again! - It happens!

note: A sympathetic phrase: it comforts, not judges. «Шта се дешава?» is 'what's going on?' and can sound sharp, or mean 'what's new?'.

meanings: to play dumb, to act clueless

examples.en: Don't play dumb, you know everything.

note: Likewise: «правити се блесав», «правити се паметан» (to act smart).

forms: literally: to work on one's own hand
meanings: to act on one's own, to do things one's own way, at one's own risk

examples.en: He always does things his own way.

meanings: I don't feel like working, I'm not in the mood to do something

examples.en: I don't feel like working today.

note: Pattern «не + verb + ми се»: «не спава ми се» (don't feel like sleeping), «не једе ми се».

meanings: it is about, it concerns, the point is

examples.en: This concerns a very important matter.

meanings: to make a secret of something

examples.sr: Не [пра̏ви та̏јну од] тога, сви већ знају.
examples.en: Don't make a secret of it, everybody already knows.

meanings: my hair stood on end, it gave me goosebumps

examples.sr: Када сам чуо ту причу, [најѐжила ми се ко̀са].
examples.en: When I heard that story, my hair stood on end.

note: With «најежити се» alone: «најежио сам се» - I got goosebumps.

examples.en: He fainted from the heat.

note: Synonyms: «онесвестити се», «пасти у несвест». «Доћи свести» - to come to.

examples.sr: Чуо сам за твог деду, [ба̏ш ми је жа̏о].
examples.en: I heard about your grandfather, I'm so sorry.

note: Used both for condolences and for small disappointments.

examples.en: Please accept my condolences on your loss.

note: Informal, to one person: «Прими моје саучешће».

examples.en: Leave me alone, please.

note: Polite or plural form: «Оставите ме на миру».

examples.sr: [То̑ те се не ти̑че], брини о себи.
examples.en: That's none of your business, mind your own.

note: Sounds sharp. The informal form: «То те се не тиче».

examples.en: - Who do you root for? - Red Star.

note: The same question about a club: «За који клуб навијаш?».

examples.en: You look great today!

note: Polite form: «Лепо ми изгледате». Without «ми» is also correct, but drier.

meanings: you have a really nice dress

examples.en: What a lovely dress you have!

note: Polite form: «Баш вам је лепа хаљина».

meanings: look how dressed up you are! (said to a woman)

examples.en: You're so dressed up, I'm speechless!

note: Said to a man: «скоцкао си се».

examples.en: What a slim figure you have!

note: A compliment to a woman on her slimness.

forms: literally: to show a pomegranate (the fig sign)
meanings: to turn someone down flat, to refuse rudely

examples.sr: Тражио сам помоћ, а они су ми [пока̀зали ши́пак].
examples.en: I asked for help, and they turned me down flat.

meanings: I feel sleepy, I feel like sleeping

examples.en: I've been feeling sleepy since this morning.

note: Pattern «verb + ми се»: «једе ми се», «пије ми се», «не ради ми се».

examples.en: It's pouring outside.
Thank you very much for your help.

note: Similar: «много хвала», «пуно хвала», «захваљујем».

examples.en: Thanks, all the best!

note: A typical goodbye to a taxi driver or shop assistant: «Хвала лепо, све најбоље».

examples.sr: - Могу ли да вас питам нешто? - [Са̏мо трену́так].
examples.en: - Can I ask you something? - Just a moment.

meanings: send a car to ... (ordering a taxi)

examples.sr: [Је̏дно во̀зило у] Улицу краља Петра број пет.
examples.en: One car to King Peter Street, number five.

note: Full form: «Да ли може једно возило у ...?». You give only the street, number and entrance.

examples.en: I run every other day.

meanings: a foreigner married to a Serbian woman (said of a man)

examples.sr: Кажу да је Ајнштајн био [ср̏пскӣ зе̏т].
examples.en: They say Einstein was a Serbian son-in-law.

note: Of a woman: «српска снајка» (a foreigner married to a Serb).

examples.sr: Изађи на изборе, [сва̏кӣ гла̑с је би̏тан]!
examples.en: Go and vote, every vote counts!

meanings: to go to the polls, to vote

examples.en: Most citizens went to vote.

meanings: election silence, the quiet period before an election

examples.en: The pre-election silence begins at midnight.

note: Campaigning is banned during this period.

meanings: party patronage hiring, jobs given for party loyalty

examples.en: They criticize party patronage hiring in state companies.

note: A common practice: a job in the public sector comes through the party.

meanings: what a great joke, nice trick

examples.en: That joke is really great!

note: A reaction to a good joke; on April 1: «Априлилили!» (April fool).

examples.en: That politician is a big shot.

meanings: a coincidence, a combination of circumstances

examples.sr: Све је то био само [сти̏цај при́лика].
examples.en: It was all just a coincidence.

examples.sr: Његов говор је [о̀ставио у̀тисак] на све.
examples.en: His speech made an impression on everyone.

meanings: to gain trust, to earn trust

examples.sr: Тешко је [сте̏ћи повере́ње], а лако изгубити.
examples.en: Trust is hard to earn and easy to lose.

examples.sr: [Сте̏кла сам у̀тисак да] нас не слушају.
examples.en: I got the impression that they aren't listening to us.

note: Said by a man: «Стекао сам утисак да».

meanings: between two fires, caught in the middle

examples.sr: Био је [и̏змеђу две̑ ва̏тре], не знајући кога да подржи.
examples.en: He was caught between two fires, not knowing whom to support.

note: Also the name of a children's game, dodgeball.

examples.en: Children love egg tapping at Easter.

note: Two people knock their eggs together; the one whose shell stays whole wins.

meanings: do you have anything for fasting? (no meat or animal products)

examples.sr: [Да ли и̏мате не̏што по̏сно] за ручак?
examples.en: Do you have anything for fasting for lunch?

note: Same set: «Да ли постите?» (are you fasting?), «Да ли је ово посно?».

meanings: for form's sake, just to be polite

examples.en: I asked her just to be polite.
It's your turn, roll the die.

note: Polite form: «На вас је ред».

examples.en: Check the bus timetable.
The new project is on the agenda.
First of all, we need to rest.

examples.sr: [По̏ред то́га], он је и добар глумац.
examples.en: Besides that, he's also a good actor.
Despite all the effort, I didn't succeed.

examples.sr: Он стално мења мишљење, [ча̏с о̀во̄, ча̏с о̀но].
examples.en: He keeps changing his mind, now this, now that.

note: Pattern «час... час»: «час овамо, час онамо» - now here, now there.

meanings: at the right moment, just in time

examples.en: You came just in time.

examples.sr: Не секирај се, [за ча̏с] ћемо ово урадити.
examples.en: Don't worry, we'll do this in no time.

note: Also «за часак»: «сачекај, враћам се за часак» - wait, I'll be right back.

examples.en: Get well soon and come back!

note: Informal, to one person: «Брзо оздрави!».

examples.en: Stop whining, it's nothing serious.

note: Also «немој више кукати».

examples.en: My colleague has been on sick leave since Monday.
I have a fever, I'm staying home.

note: Also «диже се температура» (the fever is rising), «не могу да спустим температуру» (I can't bring the fever down).

examples.en: My blood pressure has been high for days.

examples.sr: [Чу̑ј га], он ће да нас учи!
examples.en: Just listen to him, he's going to teach us!

meanings: I don't even want to hear about him

examples.sr: Не прича ми о њему, [не́ћу ни да га чу̏је̄м].
examples.en: Don't talk to me about him, I won't even hear of him.

meanings: to lock up, to put under lock and key

examples.en: She locked the money away.

meanings: to make someone understand, to let someone know

examples.sr: [Ста̏вио сам му до зна̏ња] да касни.
examples.en: I let him know that he was late.
He entered the room on tiptoe.

meanings: get in touch, give me a call

examples.en: Let me know when you arrive.

note: Also «цимни ме» (colloq.) - give me a buzz.

examples.en: We have to say goodbye to the host.

note: «Поздравити се» is both to greet and to say goodbye: «није се ни поздравио са мном».

meanings: don't bug me, don't distract me

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да ме ци̏маш], имам пуно посла.
examples.en: Don't bug me, I have a lot of work.

meanings: we didn't let you know we were coming

examples.en: We didn't let you know we were coming, sorry.
I swear to you, never again.

note: More formal: «Заклињем се».

meanings: to be on pins and needles

examples.en: I was on pins and needles all evening.
I don't care what they think.

note: Often in a dismissive phrase: «Ма брига нас за то!» - what do we care about that.

examples.en: Joking aside, we need to work.

meanings: I'm on the road, I'm away on a trip

examples.en: - Where are you? - I'm on the road.

note: An evasive answer: away on business, without saying where.

forms: literally: the child is on the road
meanings: a baby is on the way

examples.sr: Чула сам да [је де́те на пу̏ту].
examples.en: I heard a baby is on the way.
You got a tan!

note: A compliment after a vacation; also «баш сте поцрнели», «баш ти је леп тен».

examples.en: Come on, we're late!

note: Cheering at a match: «Ајмо, ајде сви у напад!» - everyone attack!

examples.en: Go, Serbia!

forms: literally: there is no what there is not
meanings: there's everything you can think of

examples.en: At the market there's absolutely everything.

examples.sr: Сада сам у Сокобањи, [а̏ко не̏ко не пра̏ти].
examples.en: I'm in Sokobanja now, in case anyone doesn't know.

meanings: to turn a blind eye, to overlook

examples.en: The teacher overlooks small mistakes.
At the party he drank anything and everything.

meanings: to answer for oneself, to be accountable

examples.en: He answers to no one.

note: «Полагати испит» - to take an exam.

examples.en: He whispered sweet words to her.
Freshwater fish are tasty.

meanings: storks don't bring babies (babies are born to their mothers)

examples.sr: [Бра̏ћу не доно̀се ро̏де], већ их рађају мајке.
examples.en: Storks don't bring brothers, mothers give birth to them.

note: A line from a children's song; «рода» is a stork.

meanings: to cast a line, to put out feelers

examples.en: He wants to put out feelers with the director.

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да се уба̀цујеш], знамо шта радимо.
examples.en: Don't butt in, we know what we're doing.

meanings: don't interrupt me with remarks, don't provoke me

examples.en: Don't throw in remarks while I'm talking.

meanings: give me a ride to work

examples.sr: [Одба̀ци ме до по̀сла], ако ти је узгред.
examples.en: Drop me off at work, if it's on your way.

note: Also «Да те одбацим кући?» - shall I drive you home?

examples.en: Transfer the money to my account.

meanings: I have nothing to reproach him for

examples.sr: [Не̑ма̄м шта̏ да му пре̏бацим], радио је све како треба.
examples.en: I have nothing to reproach him for, he did everything right.

meanings: what are you missing? (like 'what more do you want?')

examples.sr: Имаш посао и кућу, [шта̏ ти фа̏ли]?
examples.en: You have a job and a house, what more do you want?

examples.sr: Био је [од гла́ве до пе̏те] мокар.
examples.en: He was wet from head to toe.

key: phr:говори српски да те цео свет разуме
cyr: говори српски да те цео свет разуме
acc: гово̀ри ср̏пскӣ да те це̏о све̑т ра̏зӯме
meanings: speak Serbian so that the whole world understands you (joking saying)

examples.sr: [Гово̀ри ср̏пскӣ да те це̏о све̑т ра̏зӯме]!
examples.en: Speak Serbian so the whole world understands you!

note: A well-known joke that everyone supposedly understands Serbian.

meanings: tomato tourism (ironic: bringing your own food from home)

examples.sr: Они иду на [пара̀дајз турѝзам] у Грчку.
examples.en: They're going to Greece with their own food.

note: A term from the 1980s: people brought food from home and sliced tomatoes on the beach. Now about thrifty tourists.

key: phr:ко има пара иде на море, ко нема у сутоморе
cyr: ко има пара иде на море, ко нема у Сутоморе
acc: ко̏ и̏ма па̑ра и̏де на мо̑ре, ко̏ не̑ма у Су̏томо̄ре
meanings: whoever has money goes to the sea, whoever doesn't goes to Sutomore

examples.sr: [Ко̏ и̏ма па̑ра и̏де на мо̑ре, ко̏ не̑ма у Су̏томо̄ре].
examples.en: Those with money go to the seaside, those without go to Sutomore.

note: A joking rhyme (море / Сутоморе): Sutomore is an inexpensive Montenegrin resort.

meanings: to play «at the ear» (trumpeters play right by the ear)

examples.en: The trumpeters played right at his ear.

note: A tradition: trumpeters come up close, and are paid for it.

examples.sr: Била је то [љу́бав на пр̀ви по̏гле̄д].
examples.en: It was love at first sight.

examples.sr: Кад га видим, имам [ле̏птириће у сто̏маку].
examples.en: When I see him, I get butterflies in my stomach.

meanings: to be left breathless, to be awestruck

examples.en: I was almost left speechless by the beauty.

note: «Замало да» means 'almost'.

examples.sr: [Ни́сам мо̏гла да му одо̀лим], купила сам га.
examples.en: I couldn't resist it, so I bought it.

note: Said by a man: «нисам могао да му одолим».

meanings: all right, okay; when paying: keep the change

examples.en: - How much is it? - Two hundred. - Keep the change.
We want law and order.
It rained three days in a row.

meanings: that's how it should be, that's the custom

examples.en: That's how it's done.

meanings: to tidy up a room, to put it in order

examples.en: I have to tidy up the room before the guest comes.

note: «Средити папире» - to get documents in order.

meanings: you matter to me, I care about you

examples.sr: [Ста̏ло ми је до те̏бе], не одлази.
examples.en: I care about you, don't leave.

note: Pattern «стало ми је до» + gen.: «до њега ми је стало».

forms: literally: to look into the palm

examples.en: A fortune teller read my palm.

note: «Линија живота» - the life line.

meanings: I'm laughing, but I'd rather cry

examples.en: I'm laughing, but I'd rather cry.

note: A line from a well-known song.

meanings: to celebrate everything under the sun

examples.sr: Она [сла̏ви све̏ жи̑во] - сваки празник је њен.
examples.en: She celebrates everything under the sun - every holiday is hers.

key: phr:у малом граду све се зна
cyr: у малом граду све се зна
acc: у ма̏лом гра̀ду све̏ се зна̑
meanings: in a small town everybody knows everything

examples.sr: Не крији ништа, [у ма̏лом гра̀ду све̏ се зна̑].
examples.en: Don't hide anything, in a small town everybody knows everything.

note: From a song: «Мали је ово град, у њему све се зна».

examples.en: Don't bug me, I'm busy.

note: Slang, from «смарати» (to annoy).

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да му се у̀лизујеш], остани своја.
examples.en: Don't suck up to him, stay yourself.

meanings: rain is falling, grass is growing (children's rhyme about brushing teeth)

examples.sr: Зубе перемо овако: [ки̏ша па̏да, тра́ва ра̏сте].
examples.en: This is how we brush our teeth: rain is falling, grass is growing.

note: Brush strokes top to bottom (rain falls) and bottom to top (grass grows).

examples.en: I have a hairdresser's appointment.

note: For a hairdresser, doctor, restaurant: «код зубара», «код Милице».

meanings: if you've got money, you can do anything (the motto of the rich)

examples.sr: Његов мото је: [и̏ма се, мо̏же се].
examples.en: His motto: if you've got money, you can do anything.

note: A line from the rap song «Дивљина»; «има се» - one has the money.

examples.en: They are accused of laundering money.

meanings: Prince Charming (a prince on a white horse)

examples.sr: Свака девојчица сања о [при̏нцу на бѐлом ко̀њу].
examples.en: Every little girl dreams of Prince Charming.
Don't be a mama's boy, go and get it yourself.

meanings: we're going to a wedding (as wedding guests)

examples.en: On Saturday we're going to a wedding.

note: Also «идемо на свадбу» - the same, but more neutral.

meanings: don't be a child, act your age

examples.en: Don't be a child, decide for yourself.

forms: literally: throw the little bugs out of your head
meanings: get silly ideas out of your head

examples.en: Get those silly ideas out of your head and work.
That's a disgrace and a shame!
Don't embarrass me in front of the guests.

note: Also «немој да ме бламираш».

examples.sr: [Сра̑м те би̏ло], тако се не ради!
examples.en: Shame on you, that's not how it's done!
I'm ashamed to tell you.

note: Also «стид ме је», «стидим се».

examples.en: Your dress is awesome!

note: In youth slang «брука» means very cool.

meanings: it suits me, it's convenient for me

examples.sr: Ако ти је [зго̏дно], дођи у пет.
examples.en: If it suits you, come at five.

note: Negative: «није ми згодно».

examples.en: This time suits me.

note: Of size, price, color, time. «Таман ми је» - it fits (size only).

forms: literally: I have a hill of things
meanings: I have a ton of things

examples.en: I have a ton of things to pack.

meanings: my back is giving me trouble (colloq.)

examples.en: My back has been giving me trouble lately.

key: phr:нека вам се свака жеља оствари
cyr: нека вам се свака жеља оствари
acc: не̏ка вам се сва̏ка̄ жѐља о̀ствари
meanings: may all your wishes come true

examples.en: May all your wishes come true!

examples.sr: Још увек устајем [по на̏вици] у шест.
examples.en: I still get up at six out of habit.

forms: literally: my stomach is teasing me
meanings: my stomach is giving me trouble (colloq.)

examples.sr: Данас ме [зе̏за] желудац, не могу да једем.
examples.en: My stomach is acting up today, I can't eat.

note: Colloq.; «зезати» is to tease, to let down. Also with other body parts: «зеза ме леђа».

examples.en: My stomach is growling from hunger.

forms: literally: he drank a little more
meanings: he had a bit too much to drink

examples.sr: Јуче је [по̀пио ма̏ло ви̏ше] па је заспао у аутобусу.
examples.en: Yesterday he had a bit too much and fell asleep on the bus.

note: «баш је попио» is the same; a mild way to say someone drank a lot.

meanings: to my taste, my kind of thing

examples.sr: Овај филм је баш [по мо̑м у̏кусу].
examples.en: This movie is just my kind of thing.

note: Changes with the person: «по твом укусу», «по његовом укусу».

forms: literally: to raise hands from someone
meanings: to give up on someone, to wash one's hands of someone

examples.en: Everybody has given up on him.

note: Often about someone nobody hopes for anymore, e.g. an incorrigible person.

forms: literally: it is hateful to me to
meanings: I can't be bothered to, I'm too lazy to

examples.en: I can't be bothered to iron.

note: Impersonal: «ме» is acc., the verb is always «мрзи». Then «да» + present.

examples.sr: [Ру̑ку на ср̏це], није то лоша идеја.
examples.en: Honestly, that's not such a bad idea.
We're late, but what can you do.
He did it to spite me.

note: «Инат» is stubbornness, refusal to give in; «из ината» - out of stubbornness.

examples.en: I have nowhere to go, I'm staying here.

note: «Куд» is a short form of «куда»; usually in negation.

examples.en: Make love, not war.
I recharge my batteries in the countryside.
Tomorrow I turn thirty.
After the inheritance he's loaded.

note: «Пара» is money. At Christmas it's a joke about whoever finds the coin in the «чесница» (festive bread).

forms: literally: to give with full handfuls

examples.sr: Она [да̑је пу̏ним ша̏кама] свима око себе.
examples.en: She gives generously of herself to everyone around her.

forms: literally: to go over to the other side

examples.sr: Његов брат је [о̀тишао пре̏ко] пре десет година.
examples.en: His brother went abroad ten years ago.

note: In colloquial speech «преко» means 'abroad', especially for work and emigration.

examples.en: Look at this, I'm speechless!

meanings: to side with no one, to sit on the fence

examples.sr: Он стоји по страни, [ни на̏шӣм ни ва̏шӣм].
examples.en: He stays on the sidelines, siding with no one.

note: About a neutral position: choosing neither side.

examples.en: Excuse me, who's next?

note: The answer: «Ја сам» - I am.

examples.en: Do you have anything smaller?

note: A request for smaller bills or coins; the answer is often «Немам, извините».

key: phr:опростите, да ли бисте могли да ми помогнете
cyr: опростите, да ли бисте могли да ми помогнете
acc: опро̀стите, да ли бисте мо̏гли да ми по̀могнете
meanings: excuse me, could you help me

examples.sr: [Опро̀стите, да ли бисте мо̏гли да ми по̀могнете]?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you help me?

note: A polite request to a passer-by; «опростите» gets their attention.

meanings: I can't find my way, I'm lost

examples.sr: [Не мо̀гу да се сна̏ђем], где је станица?
examples.en: I can't find my way around, where is the station?
A bit slower, please, I don't understand.

examples.sr: Видимо се кад се вратиш - [сре̏ћан пу̑т]!
examples.en: See you when you get back - have a good trip!

forms: literally: let the devil take it

examples.en: Forget the problems, to hell with all of them!

note: «нека га ђаво носи» is the same about a person or thing; colloq.

examples.en: Call an ambulance!

note: In Serbia the emergency number is 194; often shortened to just «хитна».

examples.en: I don't feel well, I need to sit down.

note: Used to talk about how you feel; «лоше се осећам» - I feel bad.

examples.en: I've had a runny nose for two days now.

meanings: a bigger or smaller size (in a shop)

examples.en: Do you have a bigger size?

note: «број» is a shoe or clothing size; «боја» is color: «у другој боји».

forms: literally: get in touch with me
meanings: let me know, just ask (said by a shop assistant)

examples.en: If you need anything, just let me know.
Fancy a beer? My treat.

note: Said with a question intonation: «може + noun» offers something to drink or eat: «може кафа?».

forms: literally: are you for a coffee?

examples.sr: [Да ли си за ка̀фу]? Спремио сам нову.
examples.en: Want a coffee? I just made a fresh pot.

note: With «вама» (formal): «да ли сте за кафу?»

examples.sr: Нисам прошао, али [ви̏ше сре̏ће дру̏гӣ пу̑т].
examples.en: I didn't pass, but better luck next time.

forms: literally: it doesn't go for us
meanings: things aren't going well for us

examples.sr: Видим да [нам не и̏де] с овим послом.
examples.en: I can see this job isn't going well for us.

examples.sr: Да ли ти се свиђа? - [А јо̏ш ка̀ко]!
examples.en: Do you like it? - You bet!

forms: literally: to fall into the water

examples.en: Our plan fell through.

meanings: you shouldn't have (on getting a gift)

examples.en: Oh, you shouldn't have!

note: A polite reaction to a gift; also «Што сте се трошили?» - why did you go to the expense.

examples.en: You got the color just right!

note: About a gift: the size, the color, the choice itself.

forms: literally: a soul of a person
meanings: a heart of gold, a kind soul

examples.sr: Он је [ду́ша од чо̏века], свима помаже.
examples.en: He has a heart of gold, he helps everyone.

forms: literally: to be by the will

examples.en: I'm not to your liking.

note: Often negated: «ништа ми није по вољи» - nothing is to my liking.

meanings: nothing is good enough for him, he is never satisfied

examples.sr: [Ни̏шта јој нѝје до̀бро], стално се жали.
examples.en: Nothing is good enough for her, she complains all the time.

forms: literally: to put everything on the die
meanings: to put everything at stake, to risk everything

examples.sr: Дао је све на [ко̏цку] и отворио фирму.
examples.en: He risked everything and started a company.

note: «Коцка» here is a die. The idiom is close to English to stake everything.

examples.en: Wait, I'm coming!

note: Said when you have just arrived or are about to. Similar: «ето га» - here he is.

examples.en: He almost fell off the chair.
The train is about to arrive.

note: Refers to the future or the past: in the first case «any moment now», in the second «it almost happened».

examples.en: Let me help you.
Let me tell you something.

note: A polite opener when offering help. But «само да вам кажем нешто» can also lead into a lecture.

examples.sr: [Не са̏мо] да је закаснио, него је и заборавио књиге.
examples.en: Not only was he late, he also forgot the books.

note: After «него и» the verb stays in its usual form. «не само ... већ и» is also possible.

forms: literally: how are you to me
meanings: how are you, how are things

examples.en: Hi, how are you?

note: The short «ми» makes the question warmer.

examples.en: I'm bored at the lecture.

note: An impersonal construction with «ми». «Досадан си» about a person - you are annoying or boring.

forms: literally: a roof over the head
meanings: a roof over one's head, a place to live

examples.sr: Најважније је да имамо [кро̏в над гла́во̄м].
examples.en: The most important thing is that we have a roof over our heads.

meanings: I don't know, I'm not sure, who knows

examples.sr: Да ли ће доћи? [Шта̏ ја̏ зна̑м].
examples.en: Will he come? I don't know.

note: An evasive answer instead of a direct «не знам»; it sounds softer and vaguer.

examples.en: Who knows whether he'll come.

note: Said about other people's actions or an uncertain future: it is unclear how a person will behave.

forms: literally: from where do I know

examples.en: How should I know where he went?

note: Often with a touch of irritation. A variant is «како ја знам».

examples.sr: Видимо се у лето, [а̏ко Бо̑г да].
examples.en: We'll see each other in the summer, God willing.

note: Even non-believers say it about plans and hopes. It can replace a vague «не знам».

forms: literally: I'm not quite for that
meanings: I'm not really up for it

examples.sr: Да идемо на кишу? [Ни́сам ба̏ш за то̑].
examples.en: Shall we go out in the rain? I'm not really up for it.

note: A soft refusal without a direct «нећу».

meanings: let me see, let me check

examples.en: Let me see if I have any.

note: A shop assistant or anyone else buys time this way to check something.

examples.en: Shall we go? We'll see.

note: A polite way not to answer right away when you don't want to say no.

meanings: nice to meet you, pleased to meet you

examples.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Ana.

note: Said on meeting someone; «мени је драго» adds emphasis. The reply is «и мени».

meanings: what seems to be the problem

examples.en: Good afternoon, what seems to be the problem?

note: A standard question from a doctor or pharmacist.

meanings: to have blood taken for a test

examples.sr: Сутра идем да [ва̏дим кр̑в] на анализу.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to have blood taken for a test.

note: For a test it is «вадити крв»; for donating, «дати крв» is more common.

examples.en: I'll transfer you the money today.

note: Colloquial for a transfer to an account. «Паре» - money, always plural.

examples.en: We didn't want to come by car.

note: «Колима» is the instrumental of «кола». Likewise: «ићи бусом», «авионом».

examples.en: He works with a speech therapist because of a speech impediment.
The baby was born by cesarean section.

note: The name is linked to the Roman emperor, hence «царски». This is what it is called in hospitals.

forms: literally: it set off for me

examples.en: Hurry, it's started!

note: Colloquial for the start of labor. Without «ми» the phrase just means «it got going».

forms: literally: we congratulate on the addition

examples.en: Congratulations on the new arrival!

note: The standard congratulation to new parents. The construction is «честитати на + loc.».

examples.en: Happy Serbian New Year, friends!

note: A greeting on the night of January 14, when the New Year is celebrated by the Julian calendar.

forms: literally: it has stopped for me
meanings: I care, it matters to me

examples.en: I care about you.

note: The construction is «стало ми је до + gen.»: «до тебе», «до посла». Used about what someone holds dear.

examples.en: He's still a mama's boy.

note: About a child who likes to cuddle and gets spoiled. Said of an adult, it can sound like a mild reproach.

examples.en: Enough is enough! Let's go home.

note: A sharp remark when your patience has run out.

examples.en: I give up, I can't take it anymore.

note: Both about physical and emotional exhaustion.

examples.en: It's raining outside.

note: Likewise «пада снег». The verb «ићи» is not used here.

examples.en: It's already dark, let's go home.

forms: literally: it fell on my mind

examples.sr: [Па̏ло ми је на па̏ме̄т] да позовем Ану.
examples.en: It occurred to me to call Ana.

note: Negated: «није ми пало на памет» - it never even crossed my mind.

forms: literally: of my mother to me

examples.en: I saw him, I swear on my mother!

note: An oath in conversation: «мајке ми», «бога ми», «живота ми». They sound emotional, not always serious.

examples.en: Word of honor, I'll come tomorrow.
I'm one hundred percent sure.

note: Colloquial «посто» instead of «одсто»; «сто посто!» - exactly.

examples.en: I'm telling you seriously, don't go there.

note: A variant is «стварно ти кажем».

examples.en: I'm not kidding, he left.

note: Colloq. A variant is «не шалим се».

examples.en: A state of emergency has been declared in the country.
The child has chickenpox.
When it's cold, stay home.

note: The slogan of the 2020 quarantine and the title of a song.

examples.en: Don't worry, this too shall pass.
The children are watching a cartoon.

note: Colloquially «цртач». Only cartoons are dubbed in Serbia; other films have subtitles.

examples.en: Oh, you shouldn't have! Thank you so much.

note: What you say on getting a gift. Also: «што сте се трошили», «нисте морали», «баш сте погодили».

forms: literally: not even on the emergence
meanings: nowhere in sight, not on the horizon

examples.en: The end of the crisis is nowhere in sight.
A vacation is still nowhere in sight.

note: «Помол» is something just appearing over the horizon. Usually negated: «није на помолу».

forms: literally: there is no joke with him
meanings: he doesn't joke around, don't mess with him

examples.sr: Пази шта причаш, [не̑ма ша̏ле са њи̑м].
examples.en: Watch what you say, he doesn't joke around.

note: Related: «без шале» - no kidding, seriously; «шалим се» - I'm joking.

meanings: toned and fit (about a woman's figure)

examples.en: After training she is toned and fit.

note: One of the compliments to a woman; also «изгледа као авион» - looks great.

forms: literally: looks like a million dollars

examples.en: You look like a million bucks today.

meanings: a woman who does it all, superwoman

examples.sr: Ради, гради кућу и васпитава децу: права [жѐна зма̏ј].
examples.en: She works, builds a house and raises children: a real superwoman.

note: A compliment of admiration. Similar praise: «права мачка», «лепа као лутка».

examples.en: Sort it out, the sooner the better.
Come as soon as possible.

note: «Што» + a comparative or adverb gives «as ... as possible»: «што брже», «што гласније».

forms: literally: so that I don't jinx it

examples.en: Everything is going well, knock on wood.

note: A variant is «да не чује зло». Serbs knock on wood and say «пу, пу, пу».

examples.en: - Are you going to the game? - You bet!

note: «Него шта мислиш?» - what do you think? Just «Него?» - what else?

meanings: here I am (the usual answer to «Где си?»)

examples.en: - Where are you? - Here I am!
- Where are the keys? - Here they are.

note: «Где си?» is often just a greeting, not a question about place. You can answer «Где си ти?» or «Ево ме!». Same forms: ево те, ево га, ево је, ево нас, ево вас, ево их.

forms: literally: on top of the hill a willow sways
meanings: tongue twister for the syllabic R

examples.sr: Реци брзо: [на вр̏х бр̏да вр́ба мр̏да].
examples.en: Say it fast: on top of the hill a willow sways.

note: It trains the «р» between consonants: врх, брда, врба, мрда. The «р» can be stretched out like a tiger's growl.

meanings: I can't be bothered, I'm too lazy

examples.en: I can't be bothered to cook.
Today I can't be bothered to do anything.

note: «Мрзим» means I hate; «мрзи ме + да + present» is an impersonal laziness.

examples.en: Don't tell me you were late again!

note: A short reaction of surprise, like «Стварно?!» and «Озбиљно?!».

key: phr:то су за мене шпанска села
cyr: то су за мене шпанска села
acc: то̑ су за ме̏не шпа̏нска се̏ла
forms: literally: that is Spanish villages for me

examples.en: Math is all Greek to me.

note: «Шпанска села» means something incomprehensible.

forms: literally: precise as a Swiss watch

examples.en: He is as punctual as a Swiss watch.

meanings: a moment of losing one's temper

examples.sr: Ухватила га је [жу̏та мину́та] и све је разбио.
examples.en: He lost his temper and smashed everything.
Come as soon as possible.

note: «Што + comparative» means «as ... as possible»: што више, што боље, што брже.

examples.en: The faster, the better, they're waiting for us.

forms: literally: to mix grannies and frogs
meanings: to mix up unrelated things, to mix apples and oranges

examples.sr: Не [ме̑шај ба́бе̄ и жа̏бе], то су два посла.
examples.en: Don't mix apples and oranges, those are two separate jobs.

forms: literally: for every guest three days are enough
meanings: a guest soon wears out his welcome

examples.sr: [Сва̏ког го̏ста три̏ да̑на до̏ста], па су отишли.
examples.en: Three days are enough for any guest, so they left.

note: A proverb about hospitality: a guest is welcome only for a short time.

forms: literally: a kind word opens iron doors
meanings: kind words can get you far

examples.sr: [Лѐпа ре̑ч гво̀здена вра́та о̀твара], пробај љубазно.
examples.en: A kind word opens iron doors, try being polite.

key: phr:први кучићи се у воду бацају
cyr: први кучићи се у воду бацају
acc: пр̀вӣ ку̏чићи се у во̏ду ба̏цају
forms: literally: the first puppies are thrown into the water

examples.sr: Не брини, [пр̀ви ку̏чићи се у во̏ду ба̏цају].
examples.en: Don't worry, the first attempt rarely goes well.

note: A first experience is often a failure; it is made as a trial.

forms: literally: if you don't want it kindly, you'll want it by force
meanings: if you won't do it the nice way, you'll do it the hard way

examples.sr: [А̏ко не̑ће̄ш ми̏лом, хо̏ћеш си̏ло̄м], ја одлучујем.
examples.en: If you won't do it the nice way, you'll do it the hard way, I'm the one who decides.

examples.sr: Не треба [у̀зимати здра̏во за го̀тово] све што чујеш.
examples.en: You shouldn't take everything you hear for granted.

note: «Здраво за готово» - accepting something without checking it.

forms: literally: in hardship heroes are recognized
meanings: a friend in need is a friend indeed, true character shows in hard times

examples.sr: [На му̏ци се по̀знају ју̏наци], видећемо ко ће остати.
examples.en: True character shows in hard times, we'll see who stays.

meanings: ultimately, at the end of the day

examples.en: At the end of the day, the decision is yours.

forms: literally: a suit doesn't make the man

examples.sr: [Оде́ло не чи̏ни чо̏века], он је добар.
examples.en: Clothes don't make the man, he's a good guy.

meanings: very good-looking, pretty as a doll

examples.en: You look as pretty as a doll today.

note: In Serbia you can compliment a man's looks too, not only a woman's. Colloq. variant: леп ко лутка.

examples.en: You look nice today.

note: With «ми» it adds warmth: «лепо ми изгледаш». Polite form: «лепо изгледате». «Добро» can replace «лепо».

examples.sr: Каже да је његова другарица [до̀бра ри̏ба].
examples.en: He says his friend is a real catch.

note: Men's slang about a girl in the third person. A similar one is «мачка».

examples.en: May I ask a question?
I have to book an appointment with the dentist.
We have to make a decision by Friday.
The government took measures against overcrowding.
Tomorrow I'll submit a visa application.
The hotel provides an airport transfer service.

forms: literally: to lie through an illness
meanings: to get through an illness (in bed)

examples.en: He got through the flu without any medication.

note: About an illness that you sit out in bed.

meanings: to be in prison, to serve time

examples.en: He spent a long time in prison.

forms: literally: to carry off a victory

examples.en: Our team won the victory.

forms: literally: to live through a defeat

examples.en: The national team suffered a defeat.
The schoolgirl won first place.
The director will give a speech.
I've been on a diet for a month now.

forms: literally: to break through a deadline

examples.en: Unfortunately, we missed the deadline.
I've been to Serbia several times.

note: The comparative here compares nothing: it means «several», not «more».

examples.sr: Не можемо да дођемо [из ви̏ше ра́злога].
examples.en: We can't come for several reasons.

meanings: for a long time, for a longer stay

examples.en: I'm going to Russia for a long stay.
The apartment is for rent short-term.
My grandmother's hearing isn't very good.

note: A soft way to say «badly»: «мало слабије говорим српски».

examples.en: This film is relatively recent.
I'm looking for a shorter book.
Are you planning a vacation in the near future?

meanings: like a wind-up toy (about fast chatter)

examples.en: The little girl talks like a wind-up toy.

note: «Навијен» comes from «навити» (to wind a spring or a clock). The form follows the gender: «као навијена», «као навијен».

meanings: at full speed, a mile a minute

examples.en: She talks a mile a minute.

note: Often about fast speech. «Сат» is an hour, as in kilometers per hour.

examples.en: Hi, how's it going?

forms: literally: there is nothing for what

examples.en: Thank you! - You're welcome.
Achoo! - Bless you!

note: Said after a sneeze. You reply with «хвала».

examples.en: It's a deal, an agreement is an agreement.

examples.sr: [Без бри̏ге], све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
Thanks for the help, all the best!
Thanks, and the same to you!

note: Said both before a meal (enjoy your meal) and when parting. Not to be confused with «пријатно ми је» - I'm pleased.

examples.en: He is a true hero through and through.

note: An ironic, colloq. intensification of «прави».

examples.sr: Донела си ми кафу, [ти си пра̑ва]!
examples.en: You brought me coffee, you're a star!

note: To a woman after a nice, unexpected gesture; to a man: «ти си прав».

key: phr:на које име да оставим сто
cyr: на које име да оставим сто
acc: на ко̀је̄ и̏ме да о̏ставим сто̑
meanings: what name shall I put the table under?

examples.sr: Добар дан, [на ко̀је̄ и̏ме да о̏ставим сто̑]?
examples.en: Good afternoon, what name shall I put the table under?

note: A phrase of the restaurant host; the reply: «Резервисано је».

meanings: I would like to reserve a table

examples.sr: Добар дан, [хтѐла бих да резѐрвишем сто̑] за вечерас.
examples.en: Good afternoon, I would like to reserve a table for tonight.

note: A man says «хтео бих». On sunny weekends you may be left without a table if you don't book.

meanings: to get a beating, to get a hiding

examples.en: If you don't stop, you'll get a hiding.

forms: literally: am I tugging at you?
meanings: am I hurting you? (when combing hair)

examples.en: Am I hurting you?

meanings: how much do I owe you?

examples.en: Thanks, how much do I owe you?

note: A man says «колико сам вам дужан».

meanings: I would like to get my ends trimmed

examples.sr: [Хтѐла бих да о̀шишам кра̏јеве], само мало.
examples.en: I would like to get my ends trimmed, just a little.

note: A man says «хтео бих». For coloring: «хтела бих да офарбам косу».

examples.en: Let's blow-dry it into curls.

note: Other options: «на равно» (straight), «на таласе» (waves).

meanings: to hold the door for someone

examples.en: He kindly held the door for me.

note: «Врата» is neuter plural; придржим, придржиш.

examples.en: Press the button and call the elevator.
First knock on the door, then come in.

note: «Позвонити на врата» - to ring the doorbell.

examples.en: My husband is celebrating his double coming of age.

note: A joke about the age of 36: 18 times 2.

meanings: long may he live, long may she live (birthday song)

examples.en: Long may he live, long may he live, and may he be happy!
Long may she live, long may she live, and may she be happy!

note: In the song «Диван дан» the form follows the gender of the birthday person: «живео» (he), «живела» (she). Don't mix it up with «живело» - neuter.

forms: literally: that isn't good for you
meanings: that won't do you any good

examples.sr: Превише си поносан, [не ва̀ља ти то̑].
examples.en: You're too proud, that won't do you any good.
He did the job properly.

meanings: it would be a good idea to, you ought to

examples.en: You ought to change the tires.

meanings: it is proper to, it is the done thing

examples.en: We should visit our aunt, it's the done thing.

note: A social «ought»: that is how it is done, it is expected.

examples.en: It's no use, they don't want to listen.
It's cheap, it's worth a try.
Come here, sit on my lap.

note: «Крило» also means a wing; «у крилу» - on the lap.

forms: literally: as if I'm talking to a wall
meanings: it's like talking to a wall

examples.sr: [Ка̏о да при̑чам зи̏ду], никад не слуша.
