examples.en: We haven't seen each other in ages.

examples.sr: Пре [ме̏тар да́на̄] сам почео да учим српски.
examples.en: I started learning Serbian ages ago.

note: Belgrade slang, often said as a joke.

examples.sr: [У ве́зи са] вашим последњим писмом, јављамо вам се.
examples.en: Regarding your last letter, we are getting in touch with you.

note: A formal opening in letters. Followed by the instrumental: «у вези са уговором».

examples.en: Please find the necessary documents attached.

note: A polite business expression. «Прилог» is an attachment.

examples.en: Kind regards, Marko Petrović.

note: A standard sign-off of a business letter. A letter opens with «Поштовани господине...».

examples.en: Thank you in advance for your reply.

note: Feminine: «унапред захвална». Used in a business letter after a request.

examples.en: The coach is timing the runners on the track.

note: From «штоперица» - a stopwatch; a colloquial verb.

examples.sr: Донећу ти књигу сутра, [завршѐно ти је то̑].
examples.en: I'll bring you the book tomorrow, consider it done.

note: A Montenegrin phrase. It all depends on the tone: from a reliable person it means «I'll definitely do it», from a lazy one it's an excuse. «Завршено је» just means «it's finished».

examples.sr: Остала сам [без пребијѐне па̑ре] после викенда.
examples.en: I was left without a penny after the weekend.

note: «Пребијена пара» is a cracked, worthless coin. Said of having no money at all.

examples.sr: Месец је тек почео, а ја сам већ [на ну̀ли].
examples.en: The month has only just started and I'm already broke.

note: Colloquial; in slang also «без кинте», «декинтиран».

forms: literally: a cobweb in the wallet

examples.sr: Погледао сам у новчаник, а тамо је само [па̏учина].
examples.en: I looked in my wallet and there were only cobwebs.

note: A joking image: there has been no money in the wallet for so long that a cobweb has grown.

forms: literally: to drag oneself like a cow
meanings: to crawl along at a snail's pace

examples.en: Come on, you're moving at a snail's pace!

note: A reproach to a slow person. Serbs often swear with animal names: магарац (donkey, stupidity), свиња (slob, miser), змија (sly), овца (mindless follower).

examples.en: Don't be a sheep, think for yourself!

note: «Овца» is someone who follows the majority.

examples.en: - Are you coming? - Be right there!

note: Written as two words, «сад ћу», not «сају» or «sacu» - those are text-message shortcuts and look sloppy.

examples.en: How much do you sleep? - It depends.

note: Word order matters: not «кад како». Likewise «мање-више», not «више-мање».

examples.sr: Није дошао, [са̀мим ти̏м] ништа не зна.
examples.en: He didn't come, so he doesn't know anything.

note: Fixed word order: «самим тим», never «тим самим».

examples.en: The argument left a bitter taste.

note: Other variants: «остала је горчина», «остао је непријатан/нелагодан осећај», «остао је лош утисак».

meanings: blind drunk (a slang scale: «као летва», «као земља», «као бетон»)

examples.en: He came home blind drunk.

note: Slang: «летва» - drank a lot, «земља» - even more, «бетон» - can't stand at all. All three are well above average.

examples.sr: После ракије је био [пѝјан ка̏о бѐто̄н].
examples.en: After the rakija he was dead drunk.

note: The top of the three slang steps: «летва», «земља», «бетон».

key: phr:упала му је кашика у мед
cyr: упала му је кашика у мед
acc: у̏пала му је ка̀шика у ме̑д
forms: literally: the spoon fell into honey for him

examples.sr: Нашао је посао одмах, [у̏пала му је ка̀шика у ме̑д].
examples.en: He found a job right away, he got lucky.

note: Old-fashioned, sounds formal to young people. Neutral: «Посрећило му се». There are crude slang variants too.

forms: literally: mothers still give birth to Obilićs

examples.sr: Спасио је дете из ватре, [јо̏ш ра̑ђају ма̑јке О̀билиће]!
examples.en: He saved a child from a fire: heroes are not extinct!

note: Miloš Obilić is a hero of the Kosovo legend. The phrase praises a brave act.

forms: literally: come on, you figure it out

examples.en: Where did he go? Who the hell knows!

note: Not vulgar. Instead of «га» you can hear «ти» or «му».

key: phr:а шта кажеш на то што
cyr: а шта кажеш на то што
acc: а шта̏ ка̏жеш на то̑ што̏
forms: literally: and what do you say to the fact that
meanings: and what about the fact that...? (a reproach in youth slang)

examples.sr: [А шта̏ ка̏жеш на то̑ што̏] те сви сматрају лудом?
examples.en: And what do you say to the fact that everybody thinks you're crazy?
You're Sergey, right?

note: A tag question added at the end of a statement; short for «је ли да». Belgraders hear it as «елда».

meanings: a men's clipper cut with short sides

examples.en: The barber gave me a number one-three clipper cut.
Everybody on the team has the same clipper cut.

note: Named after the clipper guard numbers: «кец» (one) and «тројка» (three). Popular since the 90s as a practical cut.

examples.en: Joking aside, what do we do now?
Joking aside, this is serious.

note: Used to move from jokes to business.

key: phr:ко воли окрајак, добиће добру ташту
cyr: ко воли окрајак, добиће добру ташту
acc: ко̑ во̀ли о̏крајак, до̀биће до̀бру та̏шту
meanings: whoever likes the heel of the loaf will get a good mother-in-law

examples.sr: Увек једе окрајак: [ко̏ во̀ли о̏крајак, доби́ће до̀бру та̏шту].
examples.en: He always eats the heel of the loaf: whoever likes it will get a good mother-in-law.

note: A joking superstition about the end of a loaf. Regions have different words for «окрајак»: крајка, пупушка, попак.

examples.sr: На језеру смо видели плавог [ви̏линог ко̀њица].
examples.en: We saw a blue dragonfly at the lake.
The child is chasing a dragonfly across the meadow.

note: Literally «fairy's horse»: «вила» is a fairy from Slavic legends. It's the ordinary Serbian word for a dragonfly.

examples.sr: Узми [фра̀нцуски кљу̑ч], овај завртањ је велики.
examples.en: Take the adjustable wrench, this bolt is big.

note: Plain «кључ» is both a door key and a wrench; the adjustable one is called «француски кључ».

examples.en: Wrap the wire with electrical tape.

note: The everyday name, at home and in shops.

examples.en: I like seafood, especially squid.

note: Literally «sea fruits». Used on menus; fish is usually listed separately.

forms: literally: to speak into the wind

examples.sr: Колико год му објашњаваш, [го̀ворӣш у ве̏тар].
examples.en: No matter how much you explain to him, you're wasting your breath.

examples.sr: Нико не слуша, као да [го̀ворӣм у ве̏тар].
examples.en: Nobody is listening, it's as if I'm talking to the wind.

note: An idiom about useless words: nobody hears them.

forms: literally: to shoot into the wind

examples.en: His plans are pie in the sky.
Without money we're just spinning our wheels.

note: Effort is spent, but there is no target.

forms: literally: to fly by like the wind

examples.en: The summer flew by.
The year flew by.

note: Said of time that went by too quickly.

forms: literally: to pee against the wind
meanings: to act against one's own interest

examples.sr: Свађати се са шефом је као [пѝшати уз ве̏тар].
examples.en: Arguing with your boss is like peeing into the wind.

note: A colloquial, rather crude idiom: the result will be the opposite and unpleasant. Not for formal speech.

forms: literally: I have no slight connection

examples.en: I have no idea how it works.
I haven't got a clue about computers.

note: A colloquial, more emphatic variant of «немам појма». Here «благ» means «slightest».

meanings: agreement is what builds a home

examples.sr: [До̏гово̄р ку̏ћу гра̏ди], хајде да се договоримо.
examples.en: Agreement builds a home, so let's come to an agreement.

note: A proverb: a household stands on agreement. Related: «без збора нема договора».

forms: literally: without an assembly there is no agreement
meanings: without discussion there is no agreement

examples.sr: Сви ћемо седети и причати: [без збо̏ра не̑ма до̀говора].
examples.en: We'll all sit down and talk: without discussion there is no agreement.

note: «Збор» is an assembly, the council of a village community; the proverb says an agreement comes from talking together.

key: phr:где је слога, ту је и божји благослов
cyr: где је слога, ту је и божји благослов
acc: где̏ је сло̏га, ту̑ је и бо̏жјӣ бла̏госло̄в
meanings: where there is harmony, there is God's blessing

examples.sr: [Где̏ је сло̏га, ту̑ је и бо̏жјӣ бла̏госло̄в], зато се не свађајте.
examples.en: Where there is harmony, there is God's blessing, so don't quarrel.

note: A proverb about peace in a family and a community; in the ijekavian variant «ђе је слога». Given here in the ekavian form.

forms: literally: a dumpling in the throat

examples.sr: Кад је чуо вест, остала му је [кне́дла у гр̏лу].
examples.en: When he heard the news, he was left with a lump in his throat.
I have a lump in my throat.

note: From tears and emotion; it can also have a medical sense - difficulty swallowing. «Кнедла» is a ball of dough, a dumpling.

key: phr:трава је увек зеленија у туђем дворишту
cyr: трава је увек зеленија у туђем дворишту
acc: тра́ва је у̏ве̄к зелѐнија у ту̑ђем дво̀ришту
forms: literally: the grass is always greener in someone else's yard
meanings: the grass is always greener on the other side

examples.sr: Увек ти је [тра́ва зелѐнија у ту̑ђем дво̀ришту].
examples.en: For you, the grass is always greener on the other side.

examples.sr: Кажу да је [тра́ва зелѐнија ко̏д ко̀мшије].
examples.en: They say the grass is greener at the neighbor's.

note: The place can vary: «у комшије», «у туђој башти», «са друге стране ограде».

examples.sr: Деда је и у осамдесетој [здра̏в ка̏о дре̏н].
examples.en: Grandpa is healthy as a horse even at eighty.
After the vacation I'm fit as a fiddle.

note: «Дрен» is the cornelian cherry, a tree with very hard wood.

forms: literally: a fly without a head
meanings: like a chicken with its head cut off

examples.sr: Лута као [му̀ва без гла́ве] по граду.
examples.en: He wanders around the city like a chicken with its head cut off.

examples.sr: Радим као [му̀ва без гла́ве] и ништа не завршавам.
examples.en: I'm working like a headless chicken and finishing nothing.

note: Said of a person whose actions are chaotic and aimless; often about a beginner behind the wheel.

examples.en: Don't rush: patience pays off.

note: A proverb for situations where you can't get what you want right away. People joke that its meaning is clearest when the toilet is occupied.

forms: literally: from a needle to a locomotive
meanings: from a needle to a locomotive

examples.sr: У хипермаркету се може купити [од и̏гле до локомотѝве].
examples.en: In a hypermarket you can buy everything from a needle to a locomotive.

note: Said of a market or a store that has absolutely everything.

forms: literally: to put end to end

examples.en: I can barely make ends meet.

examples.sr: Како [саста̀вљате кра̑ј са кра̏јем] до плате?
examples.en: How do you make ends meet until payday?

note: An expression about running short of money before payday.

forms: literally: not hesitating for an hour

examples.sr: [Не ча̀сећи ни ча̏са], лисица је скочила.
examples.en: Without a moment's delay, the fox jumped.

examples.sr: [Не ча̀сећи ни ча̏са], сео је на коња.
examples.en: Without a moment's delay, he got on his horse.

note: A fairy-tale formula for instant action. Sounds bookish in conversation.

meanings: for no reason (a joking answer to a silly question)

examples.en: - Why? - Just because.

examples.sr: [Збо̏г си̑ра и во̑јне му̀зике], ништа више.
examples.en: Because of cheese and military music, and that's all.

note: A joking nonsense answer. There is also «због јотовања» (because of iotation): Serbian schoolchildren blame any illogical thing on grammar.

forms: literally: to separate the wheat from the tares
meanings: to separate the wheat from the chaff

examples.sr: Мора се знати [одва́јати жи̏то од ку̀коља].
examples.en: You have to know how to separate the wheat from the chaff.

examples.sr: Критичар [одва̀ја жи̏то од ку̀коља] у новој књизи.
examples.en: The critic separates the wheat from the chaff in the new book.

note: An image from field work; the meaning is the same as the English and biblical expression.

forms: literally: like an ace on a ten

examples.sr: То би ми дошло [ка̏о ке̑ц на де̏сет].
examples.en: That would be just what I need.

examples.sr: Аутобус је стигао [ка̏о ке̑ц на де̏сет].
examples.en: The bus arrived just in the nick of time.

note: Said of something that happens just in time: money when you need it, a bus at the door. «Кец» is an ace.

examples.sr: Ја сам [у ре̏бусу] шта да изаберем.
examples.en: I'm at a loss as to what to choose.
The whole world is baffled.

note: Colloquial: the person is tangled up as in a rebus puzzle and sees no way out.

examples.sr: Ти се загрејао, а ситуација се већ охладила - [ка̏сно па́ље̄ње].
examples.en: You got all worked up, but the situation had already cooled down - slow on the uptake.

examples.sr: Он је [ка̏сно па́ље̄ње], све схвати тек сутрадан.
examples.en: He's slow on the uptake, he only gets it the next day.

note: A joke about a slow thinker. Literally an auto mechanic's term.

examples.en: Yellow rapeseed is blooming in the field.

examples.sr: Од [у̀љане ре̏пице] прави се јестиво уље.
examples.en: Cooking oil is made from rapeseed.

note: Literally «oil turnip»; that is what rapeseed is called in Serbian.

examples.en: Today is a no-classes day at school.

examples.sr: Сутра је [ненаста̀вни да̑н], деца су код куће.
examples.en: Tomorrow is a non-teaching day, the kids are at home.

note: A day when school is closed that isn't called a vacation. «Наставни» means relating to teaching.

forms: literally: a promise to a fool - rejoicing
meanings: a promise only delights a fool

examples.en: You know what they say: a promise only delights a fool.

examples.sr: Ништа није урадио, само обећања - [обећа́ње лу̑дом ра̏дова̄ње].
examples.en: He hasn't done anything, only promises: a promise only delights a fool.

note: Empty promises please only the naive.

examples.en: My respects, Mr. Director.
Hats off, I have no words.

note: A formal greeting instead of «добар дан»; in conversation, an expression of respect for someone's deed.

forms: literally: it goes on the nerves

examples.en: That noise gets on my nerves.
His chatter gets on everybody's nerves.

note: «Живци» are nerves. Related «живцирати» - to irritate: «ја њу живцирам» - I annoy her.

forms: literally: extract from the register book of births
meanings: birth certificate (an extract from the register)

examples.sr: Треба ми [и̏звод из ма̀тичне књѝге ро̑ђених] за пасош.
examples.en: I need a birth certificate for my passport.

examples.sr: Где се издаје [и̏звод из ма̀тичне књѝге ро̑ђених]?
examples.en: Where is a birth certificate issued?

note: The official name of the document. In practice people just say «извод».

examples.sr: Дуго није смео да јој [ѝскаже љу́бав].
examples.en: For a long time he didn't dare to declare his love to her.

examples.sr: Нушић је [иска̀зао љу́бав] другарици у школи.
examples.en: Nušić declared his love to a girl at school.

note: A bookish variant; in speech more often «рећи да неког волиш». Nušić has it in his «Аутобиографија».

examples.sr: - Ти си лењ! - [Ви̏ди ко̏ се ја̏вља]!
examples.en: - You're lazy! - Look who's talking!

examples.sr: [Ви̏ди ко̏ се ја̏вља], а ни он није бољи.
examples.en: Look who's talking, he's no better himself.

note: A retort to someone who is far from perfect themselves.

examples.en: Don't be sad, it will pass.
Don't be angry with me.

note: The negative imperative is «немој да» + present: «немој да журиш» (don't hurry), «немој да се мрдаш» (don't move).

forms: literally: the more southern, the sadder
meanings: the further south, the sadder (about the poverty of the southern regions)

examples.sr: У Србији важи: [што̏ ју̑жније, то̑ ту̑жније].
examples.en: In Serbia they say: the further south, the sadder.

note: Not about the weather: a saying about the weak economy of the southern regions of Serbia. In general: the further from the center, the worse.

key: phr:ко с ђаволом тикве сади, о главу му се разбијају
cyr: ко с ђаволом тикве сади, о главу му се разбијају
acc: ко̏ с ђа̏волом ти̏кве са̏ди, о гла̑ву му се разбѝјају
forms: literally: whoever plants pumpkins with the devil, they smash against his head
meanings: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas
whoever keeps bad company suffers for it

examples.sr: Знаш шта кажу: [ко̏ с ђа̏волом ти̏кве са̏ди, о гла̑ву му се разбѝјају].
examples.en: You know what they say: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas.

note: Often only the first half is said, «ко с ђаволом тикве сади»; everyone knows the rest.

forms: literally: to blow into the same pumpkin
meanings: to sing from the same hymn sheet

examples.sr: Њих двојица одувек [ду̏вају у ѝсту ти̏кву].
examples.en: The two of them have always sung from the same hymn sheet.

forms: literally: to plant pumpkins with someone
meanings: to be in cahoots with someone
to be in the same crowd as someone

examples.sr: Не волим да [са̏дим ти̏кве] са њим.
examples.en: I don't want to be in cahoots with him.

note: Usually negative: being in dubious company. Part of the proverb about the devil.

forms: literally: a pumpkin without a root
meanings: someone with no one to stand up for them

examples.sr: Он је [ти̏ква без ко̀рена], нема ко да га брани.
examples.en: He's a nobody with no connections, there's no one to defend him.

meanings: the spitting image of one's father

examples.en: The boy is the spitting image of his father.

note: Also «пљуната мајка». The image: the parent spat and a child came out. The adjective agrees with the gender.

meanings: a stage on the way to something

examples.sr: За њих је град био само [про̀лазна ста̀ница].
examples.en: For them the city was just a stopover.

examples.sr: Живе у [ди̏вљем бра̑ку] већ десет година.
examples.en: They have been living in a common-law marriage for ten years.

note: Cohabitation without a registered marriage.

forms: literally: a wedge is knocked out with a wedge

examples.sr: Ако те боли љубав, зна се: [кли̏н се кли̑ном избѝја].
examples.en: If love hurts, you know how it goes: one nail drives out another.
Believe me, it's the honest truth, I'm not lying.

note: Strengthens the word «истина» (truth). «Правда» means justice.

examples.en: For that reason I didn't come.
For what reasons are you doing this?

forms: literally: to give the first goal

examples.sr: Тим је [да̑о пр̀ви го̑л] у првом полувремену.
examples.en: The team scored the first goal in the first half.

note: The score of a match is «резултат».

examples.en: Both teams played to a draw.
His new girlfriend dumped him.

note: A colloquial expression for a breakup initiated by one side. Rare in writing.

forms: literally: a pregnant woman's sick leave

examples.sr: Била је на [тру̑дничком боло̀вању] од јуна.
examples.en: She has been on prenatal leave since June.
I was given a book as a gift.

note: Note the preposition «на»: «дати на поклон». Compare «поклонити» (to give as a gift).

examples.sr: Желим да разговарам с вама [у чѐтири о̀ка].
examples.en: I want to talk to you in private.

forms: literally: to breathe onto the mouth

examples.en: He sleeps and breathes through his mouth.
They bought a two-story house.

note: A one-story house: «приземна кућа». «На спрат» means there is one floor above the ground floor.

examples.en: I'd like fried eggs for breakfast.

forms: literally: on the account of the house

examples.en: The drink is on the house.

meanings: to look out of the window

examples.en: The child is looking out of the window at the rain.

note: Uses «кроз» + acc. (literally "through"), not «у».

forms: literally: to be late five minutes

examples.en: The train is five minutes late.

note: No preposition: the length of the delay is in the accusative.

examples.en: Corruption is a festering sore on society.

note: Figurative: a chronic problem, e.g. corruption. Written with a hyphen.

meanings: backing, support in reaching a goal

examples.en: Parents are a tailwind for their children.

forms: literally: one hand washes the other
meanings: you scratch my back and I'll scratch yours

examples.en: You know how it is: you scratch my back, I scratch yours.

note: Like the Latin «manus manum lavat».

forms: literally: a clean account, a long love

examples.sr: Враћам ти дуг, знаш: [чи̏ст ра̀чӯн, ду́га љу́бав].
examples.en: I'm paying you back, you know: short reckonings make long friends.

forms: literally: set them at odds, then rule

examples.en: Their tactic is divide and rule.

meanings: man is a wolf to man

examples.sr: Понекад се чини да је [чо̀век чо̀веку ву̑к].
examples.en: Sometimes it seems that man is a wolf to man.

forms: literally: do not throw pearls before pigs
meanings: do not cast pearls before swine

examples.sr: Не причај им, [не ба̏цај бѝсер пред сви̑ње].
examples.en: Don't tell them anything, don't cast pearls before swine.

key: phr:како будеш посејао, тако ћеш и пожњети
cyr: како будеш посејао, тако ћеш и пожњети
acc: ка̏ко бу̏де̄ш посѐјао, та̀ко̄ ћеш и пожњѐти

examples.sr: [Ка̀ко бу̏де̄ш посѐјао, та̀ко̄ ћеш и пожњѐти].
examples.en: You reap what you sow.

key: phr:ми о вуку, а вук на врата
cyr: ми о вуку, а вук на врата
acc: ми о ву̑ку, а ву̑к на вра́та
forms: literally: we talk of the wolf, and the wolf is at the door

examples.sr: Баш смо о теби причали, [ми о ву̑ку, а ву̑к на вра́та].
examples.en: We were just talking about you, speak of the devil.

examples.sr: Пут је тежак, али [кроз тр̑ње до зве́зда].
examples.en: The road is hard, but through hardships to the stars.

meanings: everyone is the architect of their own fortune

examples.sr: Не чекај никога: [сва̏ко је ко̀ва̄ч сво̀је сре̏ће].
examples.en: Don't wait for anyone: everyone is the architect of their own fortune.

meanings: the voice of the people is the voice of God

examples.sr: Кажу да је [гла̑с на́рода бо̏жјӣ гла̑с].
examples.en: They say the voice of the people is the voice of God.

forms: literally: without a hair on the tongue

examples.sr: Он увек прича [без дла̏ке на јѐзику].
examples.en: He always speaks without mincing words.
We will not be a bargaining chip.

note: A journalistic phrase: about someone used as an object of bargaining.

forms: literally: it rushed past with the whirlwind
meanings: "Gone with the Wind" (title of the novel)

examples.en: We watched the film «Gone with the Wind».

note: прохујати is to rush past, вихор is a whirlwind.

forms: literally: there is neither a puppy nor a kitten
meanings: to be without a penny or a home

examples.sr: Купио је кућу, а сада [не̑ма ни кучѐта ни мачѐта].
examples.en: He bought a house, and now he has nothing left.

note: куче is a puppy, маче a kitten; said of someone with no property and no family.

forms: literally: to jump out of the rails

examples.en: The freight train derailed.
Two cars derailed.
The washing machine is broken.

note: Official: машина за прање веша; in everyday speech the short веш-машина.

meanings: something to eat with a spoon: soup, stew

examples.sr: Сваки дан треба да поједеш [не̏што на ка̀шику].
examples.en: Every day you should eat something with a spoon, like soup.

note: Not only soup: goulash or beans too. It implies a warm, hearty meal.

examples.sr: Угојила сам се, мораћу да [пробу̀шим ка̀шику].
examples.en: I've put on weight, I'll have to go on a diet.

note: Image: the food runs out of the leaky spoon and never reaches the mouth.

key: phr:кога је змија уједала, тај се гуштера плаши
cyr: кога је змија уједала, тај се гуштера плаши
acc: ко̀га је змѝја уједа̀ла, та̑ј се гу̏штера пла̏ши
forms: literally: whom a snake has bitten is afraid of a lizard

examples.sr: Једном су га преварили: [ко̀га је змѝја уједа̀ла, та̑ј се гу̏штера пла̏ши].
examples.en: He was cheated once: once bitten, twice shy.
Knowledge was her guiding star.

examples.sr: Хајде да [у̏даримо тѐмпо] док нисмо уморни.
examples.en: Let's pick up the pace before we get tired.

forms: literally: to switch oneself off the motorway
meanings: to take an exit off the motorway

examples.sr: Код Београда смо се [искљу̀чили са а̀утопута].
examples.en: We took the exit near Belgrade.

note: An exit from a motorway is called «искључење».

examples.en: I bought a chimney cake with walnuts.

note: A sweet spiral pastry baked around a cylinder, like kürtőskalács.

examples.sr: Ћерка има [пла̀ву ко̏су] и плаве очи.
examples.en: My daughter has blond hair and blue eyes.

note: «плав» means blue, but also a pale yellow shade: плава коса is blond hair, плавуша a blonde.

forms: literally: to sleep like a cannon

examples.en: After the mountains I sleep like a log.

examples.sr: Он има [ла̏к са̏н] и стално се буди.
examples.en: He is a light sleeper and keeps waking up.

note: The opposite is тежак сан, deep sleep.

forms: literally: by a convergence of circumstances

examples.en: We met by coincidence.

note: Bookish but neutral; стицај is a convergence, a coincidence.

examples.en: She has feelings for him.
They are made for each other.

forms: literally: the kitty will come to the little door

examples.sr: Нећеш да ми помогнеш? [До́ћи ће ма́ца на вра̀танца].
examples.en: You won't help me? You'll come crawling back to me yet.

note: A variant: «доћи ће цица на колица». Cats come to be petted when they want something. A threat or gloating aimed at someone who refuses now.

forms: literally: the link that is missing

examples.sr: Нашли су [ка̀рику ко̀ја̄ недо̀стаје] у еволуцији.
examples.en: They found the missing link in evolution.

examples.sr: Живот у пустињи је [бо̀рба за о̀пстанак].
examples.en: Life in the desert is a struggle for survival.
The government introduced emergency measures.

forms: literally: how does it stand on me
meanings: how does it look on me? (clothes)

examples.en: How does this jacket look on me?

forms: literally: a lad as if broken off a hill

examples.sr: Његов син је [мо̀мак ка̏о од бре̑га одва̀љен].
examples.en: His son is a big strapping lad.

note: Said of a tall, broad, strong young man.

examples.en: For him that's child's play.

note: Said of something easy, a small thing.

meanings: something for a cold (at a pharmacy)

examples.en: I'd like something for a cold.

examples.sr: Странка је [до̀шла на вла̑ст] после избора.
examples.en: The party came to power after the election.

examples.sr: Закон ће [сту́пити на сна̑гу] од јануара.
examples.en: The law will come into force in January.
The opposition did not recognize the results of the election.

examples.sr: Прво треба [ју́рити ве́зӯ] да добијеш посао.
examples.en: First you have to pull strings to get a job.
All he does is chase girls.

meanings: to try hard to get into a university

examples.en: She is trying hard to get into the university.
The city was hit by a natural disaster.
A wildfire threatened the village.

examples.sr: Опет [и̏нтернет ко̑че], не могу да отворим страницу.
examples.en: The internet is slow again, I can't open the page.
Can you lower the price?
Can it be cheaper? I'm buying several pieces.

note: «Јел» is short for «је ли». A colloquial bargaining formula.

examples.en: I'd like to, but that is too expensive.

key: phr:од злог оца, а од горе мајке
cyr: од злог оца, а од горе мајке
acc: од зло̑г о̀ца, а од го̏ре ма̑јке
forms: literally: from a bad father and an even worse mother
meanings: bad through and through, from a bad family

examples.sr: Он је [од зло̑г о̀ца, а од го̏ре ма̑јке].
examples.en: He is rotten to the core, just like his parents.

note: Said of things too, not only of people.

examples.sr: [Ка̀ка̄в о̀тац, та̀ка̄в си̑н], обојица воле пецање.
examples.en: Like father, like son: they both love fishing.
That is what they used to call a gay man.

note: Colloquial and derogatory.

forms: literally: it is even written on the fence

examples.sr: Знао сам да ће то бити објављено, [и на тара̀би пи̑ше̄].
examples.en: I knew it would be published, it's common knowledge.

note: тараба is a picket fence, and also the # key on a phone.

examples.en: The new president took the oath of office.
Relax, everything will be fine.

note: Often just «опуштено»: no big deal.

examples.en: Who runs this account?
You need to create a profile on the site.
I feel like a fish in water.
Come home, I'm hungry as a wolf.
She is clever as a bee.

meanings: whoever survives will tell the tale (of a situation with an unpredictable outcome)

examples.sr: Утакмица ће бити тешка, [ко̏ прѐживи при̑чаће].
examples.en: The match will be tough, whoever survives will tell the tale.

forms: literally: to go onto the nerves

examples.en: That noise gets on my nerves.
I just want to voice my opinion.
One coffee to go, please.

note: A calque of the English «coffee to go».

examples.en: The director bears responsibility for the mistake.
The children are in the extended after-school program.
The furniture for the living room is new.
I've missed you too, kafana.

note: «И» here means "also". «Жељан сам» + gen.: to long for.

examples.sr: Кад је видео оцену, био је [љу̑т ка̏о па̀прика].
examples.en: When he saw the grade, he was furious.

note: «Љут» means both "hot, spicy" (of food) and "angry".

forms: literally: when the maple bears apples

examples.sr: Позајмицу ће вратити [ка̏д ја̏во̄р ја̏букама ро̏ди].
examples.en: He'll pay back the loan when pigs fly.

note: A maple tree does not bear apples, hence "never".

meanings: opening of a reply letter: I am writing about your advertisement

examples.sr: [Ја̏вљам се на Ва̏ш о̏гла̄с] за радно место књиговође.
examples.en: I am writing in response to your advertisement for the position of bookkeeper.

note: Business style. «Ваш» is capitalized in a letter.

examples.sr: [Пози́вајӯћи се на Ва̏ш до̏пис] од првог септембра, шаљемо вам понуду.
examples.en: With reference to your letter of September 1, we are sending you an offer.

note: «Допис» is an official letter from an organization. A typical opening of a reply in business correspondence.

examples.en: We inform you that the deadline has been extended.

note: Followed by «да» + verb. Formal, addressing «Вас».

examples.sr: Молимо вас да [и̏змирите ра̀чӯн] до петка.
examples.en: Please settle the bill by Friday.

note: In business language «измирити» means to discharge an obligation in full.

examples.en: You can make the payment by card.

note: Official wording; in speech people say «платити».

examples.en: We want to settle the debt in installments.

forms: literally: there isn't even enough for medicine
meanings: to be nowhere to be found
not to be had for love or money

examples.en: There wasn't a taxi to be found.

note: Said of something that is nowhere around, although it should be.

examples.sr: [Ни̏чим и̏зазван], почео је да виче на нас.
examples.en: Out of the blue, he started shouting at us.

meanings: something that does not really exist

examples.sr: Бесплатан паркинг у центру је [ми̏саона и̏меница].
examples.en: Free parking in the center is a pipe dream.

note: Humorous: about a thing that exists only in words and dreams.

examples.sr: На пословном путу смо [спо̏јили ле̑по и ко̏рисно].
examples.en: On the business trip we combined business with pleasure.
He is, pardon my language, a real fool.

note: An apology before a rude or indecent word.

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да ме гња̑вӣш] са тим питањима.
examples.en: Don't bug me with those questions.

note: Also «немој да ме смараш». Both are colloquial.

examples.en: Get lost, I don't want to see you.

note: «Брисати» means "to wipe", but in the imperative it means "get out".

examples.en: Get out, right now!

note: «Мрш» is a categorical command, also used to shoo animals.

examples.sr: [У чѐму је фа̏зон]? Не разумем шалу.
examples.en: What's the deal? I don't get the joke.

note: Colloquial slang. Tone decides: it can be asked seriously or with irritation.

examples.en: Clubs are not my thing.

note: Colloquial slang. Also «нисам у фазону»: not in the mood.

examples.sr: Он је увек [у не̏ком сво̑м фа̏зону].
examples.en: He is always in his own world.

forms: literally: what does this look like
meanings: what is this supposed to be? (indignation)

examples.en: Look at the room, what is this supposed to be!

note: An indignant remark when something looks awful or unacceptable.

meanings: how can you not be ashamed?

examples.sr: [Ка̀ко те са̏мо нѝје срамо̀та] да лажеш!
examples.en: How can you not be ashamed to lie like that!

note: «Те» instead of «вас»: addressing one person informally.

forms: literally: is there an end to the outrage

examples.sr: [И̏ма ли кра̏ја безобра̀злуку]? Опет су повећали цене.
examples.en: When will this outrage end? They've raised prices again.

meanings: even my pigs live better (about awful conditions)

examples.sr: Погледај тај смештај, [мо̀је сви̑ње бо̏ље̄ жи̏ве].
examples.en: Look at that accommodation, even my pigs live better.

note: A sarcastic remark about poor conditions or a high price.

meanings: are you out of your mind?

examples.sr: [Да ли сте ви̑ но̏рма̄лнӣ]? Овде је забрањено пушити!
examples.en: Are you out of your mind? Smoking is forbidden here!

note: Sharp. Informal: «да ли си ти нормалан/нормална?».

examples.sr: [Сачу̀вај бо̏же] да ми се то поново деси!
examples.en: God forbid that this happens to me again!

examples.sr: Овај ресторан је [то̏пла̄ пре̏порука] за све путнике.
examples.en: I highly recommend this restaurant to all travelers.
The apartment has underfloor heating in the bathroom.

note: A literal «топли под» is not used.

forms: literally: there is no messing around

examples.en: No kidding, the deadline is tomorrow.

note: Colloquial, slang.

examples.en: Thanks for the information, we'll stay in touch.

note: A business closing. In writing, often just «на вези».

examples.en: Okay, take care!

note: A friendly goodbye.

examples.sr: [По̀здрави сво̀је] и јави се кад стигнеш.
examples.en: Say hi to your folks and let me know when you arrive.

note: «Поздрави маму»: say hi to your mom.

examples.en: We'll see each other again, God willing.

note: A ritual addition to a farewell, more common among older people.

key: phr:драго ми је било да те упознам
cyr: драго ми је било да те упознам
acc: дра̑го ми је би̏ло да те у̀познам

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је би̏ло да вас у̀познам].
examples.en: It was nice to meet you.

note: Said at the end of a meeting. At the start: «драго ми је».

meanings: I'm not in the mood for

examples.en: I'm not in the mood for jokes today.

note: Followed by the genitive: «није ми до спавања» - I'm not up to sleeping.

examples.en: The suit was made to measure.

note: «Шивење по мери» is custom tailoring; «кројачка радња» is a tailor's shop.

forms: literally: those tricks don't catch fire
meanings: that trick won't work on me

examples.en: Those tricks don't work on me.

note: Colloquial. «Фора» here is a trick, a ploy.

examples.en: Get this: I won an award!

note: Colloquial slang. Said before a funny or surprising story.

examples.en: Call us, you won't regret it!

note: An advertising phrase: «покајати се» is to regret.

examples.sr: Не жели да [ди̏же фр̏ку] око тога.
examples.en: He doesn't want to make a fuss about it.

note: Colloquial. Also «правити фрку».

examples.en: I'm stressing out before the exam.

note: Negation: «није ми фрка» - I'm not worried, it's no trouble.

examples.en: He finally told her that he loved her.
In spring we do a deep cleaning of the apartment.
On Saturdays I go shopping at the market.

note: «Набавка» is buying groceries and necessities. Synonym: «ићи у куповину».

examples.en: We sell large household appliances at good prices.

note: Refrigerators, washing machines, dishwashers, freezers.

examples.sr: Купили смо нову [маши́ну за пра́ње ве̑ша].
examples.en: We bought a new washing machine.

note: In speech often shorter: «веш машина». A dishwasher is «машина за прање посуђа» or «машина за судове».

examples.en: Astronomers observe celestial bodies.

examples.sr: [Мѐсечеве ме̏не] се понављају сваких двадесет девет дана.
examples.en: The phases of the Moon repeat every twenty-nine days.
Show me your ID card, please.

note: «Карта» is not only a ticket but also a card. It shows the ЈМБГ, a citizen's unique number.

examples.en: You need a marriage certificate for the visa.
Don't leave your health insurance card at home.
A certified copy of the diploma is required.

note: «Оверити» is to certify (at a notary, at the municipality).

examples.sr: Јуче ми се [по̀ломио зу̑б] на орасима.
examples.en: Yesterday I broke a tooth on walnuts.

note: «Поломио ми се» is reflexive: the tooth broke by itself. Broken: «зуб је поломљен».

examples.en: The car needs a minor service.

note: An oil and filter change and a fluid check; «велики сервис» is more extensive.

examples.en: I joined a hiking club.

note: Synonym: «клуб планинара». They organize «акције» - hiking trips.

examples.en: My head has been hurting for days.

note: The body part is the subject: «боли ме зуб». Plural: «боле ме леђа».

examples.sr: [Не о̀сећам се ба̏ш на̑јбоље], идем кући.
examples.en: I'm not feeling too well, I'm going home.

note: A polite way to say you feel unwell. Also: «не осећам се добро».

examples.en: - Is he conscious? - No, he isn't.

note: «Свестан је» - conscious, «није свестан» - unconscious.

key: phr:с једне стране... с друге стране
cyr: с једне стране... с друге стране
acc: с је̏дне стра́не... с дру̑ге стра́не
meanings: on the one hand... on the other hand

examples.sr: [С је̏дне стра́не] је скупо, [с друге стране] је сигурно.
examples.en: On the one hand it's expensive, on the other it's reliable.

examples.sr: [Пр̀во̄], проверите да ли је место безбедно. [Друго], позовите хитну помоћ.
examples.en: First, check that the place is safe. Second, call an ambulance.

note: Neuter ordinals used as linking words: прво, друго, треће, четврто.

examples.en: It's a pity I don't have enough time.

note: «Штета» also stands alone: «Штета!» - what a pity. After «што» comes an ordinary clause.

examples.sr: Ићи ћемо на излет, [без о̏бзира на то̑] што пада киша.
examples.en: We're going on the trip even though it's raining.

note: «Без обзира на» + acc.: «без обзира на околности». «На то што» introduces a clause.

key: phr:ругао се лонац лонцу, а оба су црна
cyr: ругао се лонац лонцу, а оба су црна
acc: ру̏гао се ло̀нац ло̀нцу, а о̏ба су цр̏на
forms: literally: one pot mocked the other, and both are black
meanings: the pot calling the kettle black

examples.sr: Он вас критикује? [Ру̏гао се ло̀нац ло̀нцу, а о̏ба су цр̏на].
examples.en: He criticizes you? The pot calling the kettle black.

note: A proverb about someone who reproaches others for what he does himself.

meanings: don't let anyone push you around

examples.sr: [Не да̑ј на се̏бе], брани своје мишљење.
examples.en: Don't let anyone push you around, defend your opinion.

note: Advice to someone who is being bullied. Also «не дај се».

examples.sr: Као деца смо [и̏шли по пѐчурке] у шуму.
examples.en: As kids we went into the woods to pick mushrooms.

note: To pick: «брати печурке»; a mushroom picker is «берач гљива».

meanings: do not cast pearls before swine

examples.sr: Не објашњавај му, [не ба̏цај би̏сере пред сви̑ње].
examples.en: Don't explain it to him, don't cast pearls before swine.
The decision has been made, the die is cast.
We need ground meat for the patties.

note: Mixed (beef and pork): «мешано млевено месо».

examples.sr: [Ра̏ди се о то̏ме] да немамо довољно новца.
examples.en: The thing is that we don't have enough money.

note: Impersonal: «ради се о» + loc. Answers the question "what is it about?".

examples.sr: [Извѝњавам се што̏ прѐкидам], али морам да кажем нешто.
examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but I have to say something.
I'm not quite sure I'll make it.

note: «Баш» softens the negation: not very, not quite.

meanings: what do you do (for a living)?

examples.en: What do you do? - I work as a doctor.

note: «Бавити се» + instr.; "what" in the instrumental is «чиме».

meanings: I was born in (said by a man)

examples.sr: [Ро̏ђен сам у] Казању, а живим у Београду.
examples.en: I was born in Kazan, and I live in Belgrade.

note: A woman says «рођена сам». Date: «рођен сам дванаестог јуна».

examples.en: I speak English fluently and understand Serbian.

note: «Читам и разумем»: I read and understand.

examples.en: I'm not married, but I have a child.

note: Married: «ожењен» (man), «удата» (woman).

examples.sr: [Ни́сам слу̏жио во̑јску] јер је обавеза укинута.
examples.en: I haven't done military service because it was abolished.

note: A woman says «нисам служила».

examples.en: I'm in charge of contacts with partners.

note: «Задужен» - assigned the responsibility for it. A woman says «задужена сам за».

meanings: do you deliver to an address?

examples.sr: [Да ли доста̀вљате на адрѐсу]? Живим ван центра.
examples.en: Do you deliver to an address? I live outside the center.

meanings: I want to cancel my order

examples.sr: [Жѐлим да о̀ткажем нару̀џбину], стигла је погрешна роба.
examples.en: I want to cancel my order, the wrong goods arrived.
One item is missing from the package.

note: «Недостајати» takes the 3rd person: «недостаје један производ», «недостају два производа».

examples.en: Don't go off topic.

note: Short form of the command: «не скрећи са теме».

examples.en: Various rumors about him are going around town.
He's looking for a serious relationship, not a fling.
We signed the contract at the notary's.

note: Written on signs; colloquially «нотар».

examples.en: Don't forget the vehicle registration in the car.

note: «Возачка дозвола» is a driver's license; «саобраћајна дозвола» is the vehicle's document.

meanings: to renew the registration (of a car)

examples.en: I want to renew my car registration.

note: «Регистрација истиче» - is expiring; «је истекла» - has expired; «важи до јуна» - valid until June.

examples.sr: [За̏што сте ме за̀уставили]? Нисам прекорачио брзину.
examples.en: Why did you stop me? I wasn't speeding.
That offense carries a fine.

meanings: to drive under the influence of alcohol

examples.en: It is forbidden to drive under the influence of alcohol.
He got a fine for illegal parking.
Stay a little longer, keep me company.

examples.sr: Хајде да [на̀правимо па̀узу] од десет минута.
examples.en: Let's take a ten-minute break.

note: Collocations with «правити»: «правити буку» (to make noise), «правити разлику» (to make a difference).

examples.en: Don't make a scene in front of everyone.
Drop it, nothing will come of it.

note: Imperative of «манути се» + gen.; plural «маните се».

forms: literally: to make oneself a cool guy
meanings: to act like a big shot

examples.en: He is showing off in front of the girls.

note: Slang. «Фрајер» generally means a guy, a bloke; with «правити се» it means a show-off.

forms: literally: to catch fire for someone

examples.en: Since when have you been into him?
Older ladies don't do it for me.

note: Slang. Takes «на» + acc.

meanings: to be slow on the uptake

examples.en: You are always slow on the uptake.

note: The image is from an engine: «касно паљење» is late ignition.

examples.en: - What time do you usually have lunch? - It depends.
It all depends.

note: A short answer. In more detail: «зависи од саобраћаја» - it depends on traffic.

forms: literally: little bugs in the head

examples.en: He has hang-ups.

note: An old expression everyone understands. Slang replacement: «пун трипова». Not «бубашваба», a real cockroach.

examples.en: He is stingy.

note: Colloquial. «Пара» is a hundredth of a dinar, a tiny coin.

forms: literally: not to have even a broken para

examples.en: I don't have a penny until payday.

note: Strengthens the negation: «пребијена пара» is a para broken in half, so not even half a coin.

key: phr:не може и јаре и паре
cyr: не може и јаре и паре
acc: не мо̏же и ја̏ре и па̏ре
forms: literally: you can't have both the kid goat and the money
meanings: you can't have your cake and eat it too

examples.sr: [Не мо̏же и ја̏ре и па̏ре], изабери једно.
examples.en: You can't have your cake and eat it too, pick one.

note: A proverb. «Јаре» (kid goat) and «паре» (money) rhyme.

forms: literally: at first glance it seems
meanings: at first glance it seems that...

examples.sr: [На пр̀ви по̏гле̄д се чи̏ни] да је лако.
examples.en: At first glance it seems easy.

note: A bookish phrase, typical of romance novels. Followed by «да» + clause.

forms: literally: the chances are small that

examples.sr: [Ма̀ле су ша̏нсе да] ће падати снег.
examples.en: It's unlikely that it will snow.

note: After «да» comes the future or a plain present verb: «да се то догоди».

examples.sr: [Саосѐћам с то̏бо̄м], знам како ти је.
examples.en: I sympathize with you, I know how you feel.

note: «Саосећати» takes «с» + instr.: «с тобом», «са њом».

examples.en: Spare me the public humiliation, please.

note: Bookish: «поштедети некога чега» - to spare someone something (gen.).

examples.en: Belgrade is known for the Victor monument.
Serbs are known for their hospitality.

note: «По» is followed by the locative: «по ракији», «по гостопримству».

examples.en: He works off the books.

note: Also «црна берза» - black market, «црна листа» - blacklist.

key: phr:дај боже здравља, остало има код кинеза
cyr: дај боже здравља, остало има код кинеза
acc: да̑ј бо̏же здра̏вља, о̀стало и̏ма ко̏д ки̏неза
forms: literally: God grant health, the rest is at the Chinese shop
meanings: health is what matters, the rest can be bought

examples.sr: [Да̑ј бо̏же здра̏вља, о̀стало и̏ма ко̏д Ки̏неза].
examples.en: Good health is the main thing, the rest we can buy.

note: A humorous saying: Serbia has many Chinese shops that sell everything.

forms: literally: if you've pulled the trigger, shoot
meanings: if you've started, see it through
in for a penny, in for a pound

examples.sr: Рекао си своје, па сад [а̏ко си по̀тегао, пу̏цај].
examples.en: You've said your piece, and since you've pulled the trigger, shoot.

note: A saying with a gun image.

key: phr:ако комшијска кућа гори, гледај у своју
cyr: ако комшијска кућа гори, гледај у своју
acc: а̏ко ко̏мшијска ку̏ћа го̀рӣ, гле̏да̄ј у сво̀ју
forms: literally: if the neighbor's house is burning, look at your own
meanings: someone else's trouble may reach you too, so stay alert

examples.sr: [А̏ко ко̏мшијска ку̏ћа го̀рӣ, гле̏да̄ј у сво̀ју]!
examples.en: If your neighbor's house is burning, watch your own!

note: A warning proverb: don't gloat over another's trouble, it may touch you too.

examples.en: Your fly is open, zip up.

note: A jokey, tactful way to say it quietly.

forms: literally: only bone and skin remained

examples.sr: После болести је остао [ко̑ст и ко̏жа].
examples.en: After the illness he was left skin and bones.

forms: literally: to get fat like a she-bear
meanings: to put on a lot of weight

examples.en: She put on a lot of weight over the winter.

note: Colloquial, often mocking; «мечка» is a she-bear.

examples.en: Goodbye, take care!

note: Became a common goodbye after the pandemic. Singular: «чувај се».

key: phr:изгубио се као магарац у магли
cyr: изгубио се као магарац у магли
acc: изгу̀био се ка̏о ма̀гарац у ма̀гли
forms: literally: lost like a donkey in the fog
meanings: lost like a donkey in the fog

examples.sr: Нови у граду, [изгу̀био се ка̏о ма̀гарац у ма̀гли].
examples.en: He's new in town and completely lost.

note: A donkey is gray like fog, so it can't be found in it.

key: phr:не зна да ли је дошао или пошао
cyr: не зна да ли је дошао или пошао
acc: не зна̑ да ли је до̏шао и̏ли по̀шао
forms: literally: doesn't know whether he has arrived or set off
meanings: not to know whether one is coming or going

examples.sr: Од среће [не зна̑ да ли је до̏шао и̏ли по̀шао].
examples.en: He's so excited he doesn't know whether he's coming or going.

note: About someone who fusses and rushes about to no purpose.

key: phr:где људи пљују, ту река тече
cyr: где људи пљују, ту река тече
acc: где̏ љу̑ди пљу̏ју, ту̑ ре́ка тѐче
forms: literally: where people spit, the river flows

examples.sr: Причало се по целом селу, [где̏ љу̑ди пљу̏ју, ту̑ ре́ка тѐче].
examples.en: The whole village was talking: word gets around.

forms: literally: the kitty has come to the little door
meanings: now he's the one who comes asking

examples.sr: Подсмевао се мени, али [до̀шла ма́ца на вра̀танца].
examples.en: He laughed at me, but now the tables have turned.

note: Said jokingly or as a threat: promising payback, or expecting the offender to come asking for help himself.

forms: literally: complain to the waterworks authority
meanings: complain all you like, no one will listen

examples.sr: Не свиђа ти се? [Жа̏ли се у̀прави водо̀вода]!
examples.en: You don't like it? Go complain to the water board!

note: A sarcastic reply to someone who complains in vain. The waterworks authority has nothing to do with it.

forms: literally: to walk rabid intestinal worms

examples.en: The child is running wild around the house.

note: Jokingly rude: about noisy, unruly behavior.

forms: literally: to come out at the end with someone

examples.sr: Не знам како [и̏злазиш на кра̑ј] са њим.
examples.en: I don't know how you cope with him.

note: «Изаћи на крај» alone means to see a job through; with «са» + instr. it means to manage a difficult person.

forms: literally: not to have even a faint connection
meanings: not to have the faintest idea

examples.sr: Он [не̑ма ни бла̀ге ве̏зе] о компјутерима.
examples.en: He hasn't the faintest idea about computers.

note: Said of someone who is completely clueless.

examples.en: All of this is nonsense.
It's kind of lame.

note: Colloquial. Not to be confused with «нема везе» - never mind.

examples.en: Last night he was dead drunk.

note: Colloquial, often said after a feast.

forms: literally: to pay into an account
meanings: to transfer money to an account
to pay money into an account

examples.en: Yesterday I transferred the money to your account.

note: A banking phrase: «уплатити» is to pay money in.

examples.en: I have impostor syndrome at my new job.

note: Same meaning: «синдром варалице». Typical thoughts: «сумњам у себе» (I doubt myself), «не заслужујем свој успех» (I don't deserve my success).

forms: literally: to take to the heart

examples.en: Don't take everything to heart.

note: Usually used in a prohibition.

examples.sr: Ту су, [и̏змеђу о̀сталог], и моје ствари.
examples.en: My things are here too, among other things.

note: An introductory phrase set off by commas.

examples.sr: Имам састанак у три. [О̏сӣм то́га], морам код лекара.
examples.en: I have a meeting at three. Besides that, I have to see the doctor.

note: An introductory phrase for adding a thought.

examples.en: In a word, it was all in vain.

note: Sums up what was said.

examples.sr: Иде ми се у ресторан. [Дру̀гим ре́чима], гладан сам.
examples.en: I feel like going to a restaurant. In other words, I'm hungry.

note: Rephrases the previous sentence.

examples.en: So, it was really tiring.

note: A filler word in conversation that sums things up.

forms: literally: to fold the eyes shut

examples.en: Just close your eyes and rest.

note: In literary language also «to die»: «склопити очи заувек».

meanings: to take someone at their word

examples.en: Take my word for it.

meanings: to give one's word, to promise

examples.sr: Дао ми је [ре̑ч], али је није одржао.
examples.en: He gave me his word, but he didn't keep it.

meanings: in words only, only in talk

examples.en: He's good only in words.

examples.sr: Поновила сам све [од ре̑чи до ре̑чи].
examples.en: I repeated everything word for word.
Those are just empty words.
Dad is doing a crossword.

meanings: in a hurry, quick and dirty

examples.en: I made lunch in a hurry.
I always have my phone at hand.

meanings: to have one's hands full, to be swamped with work

examples.en: I have my hands full today.

meanings: to go smoothly, to come easily

examples.en: Languages come easily to me.

note: Its counterpart: поћи за руком, to succeed. Often negated: «Не иде ми од руке».

meanings: to give up on something, to wash one's hands of

examples.sr: Хтела је да [ди̏гне ру̑ке од] свега.
examples.en: She wanted to give up on everything.

note: Дићи руку на некога means to raise a hand against someone, to hit them.

meanings: in one's own way, a bit eccentric

examples.en: He's a bit eccentric in his own way.

meanings: to turn down, to brush off (a suitor)

examples.en: She turned him down.

meanings: to give it one's all, to do one's best

examples.en: Give it your all and win!
I don't feel like going out today.

note: Without «ми», «не да се» + inf. means it can't be done: «Не да се замислити».

examples.en: God forbid I should be late.

meanings: to step on the gas, to speed up

examples.en: Step on the gas, we're late!
He came back home safe and sound.

meanings: all day long, the whole day

examples.en: He sits and waits all day long.

meanings: one day (in the past or the future)

examples.en: One day you will learn the truth.

meanings: these days, in the next few days, the other day

examples.en: I'll get in touch with you one of these days.

note: Past, future or present: the context tells which.

meanings: the other day, a few days ago

examples.en: I saw him the other day.

meanings: as sure as day, a given

examples.en: For us that's a given.
We still don't know that to this day.

meanings: to cry one's eyes out, to sob bitterly

examples.en: The little girl cried her eyes out.

note: Here година is archaic or dialect for «bad weather, storm»: tears pour like rain.

meanings: to set one's eye on, to have one's eye on

examples.sr: [Ба̏цио сам о̏ко на] један стан у центру.
examples.en: I've set my eye on an apartment in the center.

meanings: to look at with suspicion, to give a sidelong look

examples.en: The neighbor looks at me suspiciously.
You can't see that star with the naked eye.
I have a corn on my foot.

note: Nothing to do with sight: it is named for its look.

meanings: to keep one's fingers crossed, to wish someone luck

examples.en: I'm keeping my fingers crossed for you for the exam.
The professor is giving a geography lecture.

meanings: to teach a class, to give a lesson

examples.en: I don't give private lessons.
He always keeps his word.

meanings: to hold someone to their word

examples.en: I'm holding you to your word.

meanings: to have self-respect, to care about one's reputation

examples.sr: Ниједан човек који [др̀жи до се̏бе] то неће рећи.
examples.en: No self-respecting person would say that.
The neighbors are making noise all night.

meanings: to make a fool of someone

examples.en: Don't make a fool of me.

note: Прави од себе будалу: to make a fool of oneself.

examples.en: Tomorrow we're throwing a party at my place.
You're making the biggest mistake of your life.

key: phr:први се мачићи у воду бацају
cyr: први се мачићи у воду бацају
acc: пр̀вӣ се ма̀чићи у во̏ду ба̏цају
forms: literally: the first kittens are thrown into the water
meanings: the first attempt always goes badly

examples.sr: Не брини, [пр̀ви се ма̀чићи у во̏ду ба̏цају].
examples.en: Don't worry, the first attempt always goes badly.

examples.sr: Живе негде, [где̏ је бо̑г ре̏као ћа̑о].
examples.en: They live somewhere in the middle of nowhere.
He came home penniless.
He claims to have blue blood.

examples.sr: Ја сам човек [од кр̏ви и ме̑са].
examples.en: I'm a person of flesh and blood.

examples.sr: Од те вести [ле̏ди ми се кр̑в у жѝлама].
examples.en: That news makes my blood run cold.

examples.sr: Помогли су му, јер [кр̑в нѝје во̀да].
examples.en: They helped him, because blood is thicker than water.

meanings: at daggers drawn, to the death

examples.sr: Два клана су у рату [на кр̑в и но̑ж].
examples.en: The two clans are at war to the death.

meanings: at full steam, at full capacity

examples.en: The factory is running at full capacity.
The party was in full swing.
He's rolling in money.
There's a full moon tonight.
We can barely make ends meet.
After all, that's not a problem.

meanings: at the end of the world, in the middle of nowhere

examples.en: We live at the end of the world.

meanings: to have a loose tongue, to be a blabbermouth

examples.sr: Он [и̏ма ду̏г јѐзик], не причај му ништа.
examples.en: He has a loose tongue, so don't tell him anything.

meanings: to find common ground, to get on

examples.en: We soon found common ground.

meanings: on the tip of one's tongue

examples.sr: [На вр̏х] ми је [језика], али не могу да се сетим.
examples.en: It's on the tip of my tongue, but I can't remember.

examples.sr: [У̀гризи се за јѐзик] док не чујеш све.
examples.en: Bite your tongue until you've heard everything.

meanings: to pry words out of someone, to make someone talk

examples.en: Nobody forced him to say it.

examples.sr: [Ва̏ма и ва̏шима] желим здраву и успешну годину.
examples.en: I wish you and yours a healthy and successful year.

note: «Вашима» here means your family and loved ones. A formula for colleagues and acquaintances.

key: phr:вук длаку мења, а ћуд никада
cyr: вук длаку мења, а ћуд никада
acc: ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а ћу̑д ни̏када
forms: literally: the wolf changes its coat, but never its nature
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots

examples.sr: Није се променио: [ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а ћу̑д ни̏када].
examples.en: He hasn't changed: a leopard can't change its spots.

key: phr:крсти вука, а вук у гору
cyr: крсти вука, а вук у гору
acc: кр̏сти ву̑ка, а ву̑к у го̏ру
forms: literally: baptize the wolf, and the wolf heads for the mountain
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots

examples.sr: Сто пута сам му рекао - [кр̏сти ву̑ка, а ву̑к у го̏ру].
examples.en: I've told him a hundred times, but baptize a wolf all you like, it still heads for the hills.

key: phr:и вук сит и овце на броју
cyr: и вук сит и овце на броју
acc: и ву̑к си̏т и о̑вце на бро̑ју
meanings: to have it both ways, a win-win

examples.sr: Договор је такав да [и ву̑к си̏т и о̑вце на бро̑ју].
examples.en: The deal is such that everybody wins.

meanings: to set the fox to guard the henhouse
to put the wolf in charge of the sheep

examples.sr: Именовати га за чувара је као [по̀ставити ву̑ка за пасти́ра].
examples.en: Appointing him as a guard is like setting the fox to guard the henhouse.

forms: literally: the wolf ate the donkey
meanings: gone without a trace, nobody to blame

examples.en: The money disappeared without a trace, and nobody is to blame.

examples.sr: Изгледа фино, али је [ву̑к у ја̏гњећој ко̏жи].
examples.en: He looks nice, but he's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

meanings: this and that, and so on

examples.sr: Почели су да раде заједно, [о̀во̄ о̀но].
examples.en: They started working together, and so on and so forth.

meanings: I don't care, it's all the same to me

examples.sr: Сви ми се смеју, али [не ма̏рим].
examples.en: Everyone is laughing at me, but I don't care.

note: With an object: «не марим за» + acc.

meanings: between a rock and a hard place

examples.sr: Био је [и̏змеђу ва̏тре и во̀де] и није знао шта да ради.
examples.en: He was between a rock and a hard place and didn't know what to do.

meanings: a storm in a teacup, much ado about nothing

examples.sr: Цела свађа је била [бу̏ра у ча̏ши во̀де].
examples.en: The whole quarrel was a storm in a teacup.
He has work coming out of his ears.

note: Pattern: «има» + gen. + «као воде»: Има пара као воде.

forms: literally: to let go down the water
meanings: to leave in the lurch, to betray, to let go to waste

examples.sr: Кад му више није требао, [пу̏стио га је ни̑з во̏ду].
examples.en: When he no longer needed him, he left him in the lurch.

examples.sr: Та помоћ је [ка̏о ка̑п во̀де у мо̏ру].
examples.en: That help is a drop in the ocean.

key: phr:чувати као мало воде на длану
cyr: чувати као мало воде на длану
acc: чу́вати ка̏о ма̏ло во̀де на дла̑ну
forms: literally: to guard like a little water in the palm
meanings: to treasure like the apple of one's eye, to handle with great care

examples.sr: Он чува ту девојку [ка̏о ма̏ло во̀де на дла̑ну].
examples.en: He treasures that girl like the apple of his eye.

forms: literally: to lead a thirsty man across the water
meanings: to pull the wool over someone's eyes, to con skillfully

examples.sr: Он уме да [прѐведе жѐдног пре̏ко во̀де].
examples.en: He knows how to pull the wool over people's eyes.

forms: literally: to grow as if out of water

examples.en: The child is growing like a weed.

meanings: a return ticket to..., a round-trip ticket to...

examples.en: A round-trip ticket to Smederevo, please.

meanings: to conclude a contract, to sign a deal

examples.en: After long negotiations, we signed the contract.
The companies will sign a cooperation agreement.

examples.sr: На почетку године важно је [по̀ставити] јасне [ци́љеве].
examples.en: At the start of the year, it's important to set clear goals.
All the teams have fulfilled their obligations.

meanings: to coordinate deadlines, to agree on timing

examples.sr: Морамо да [у̀складимо ро̀кове] са другим одељењима.
examples.en: We have to coordinate the deadlines with the other departments.
He's a big-hearted man.

note: Same pattern: каменог срца, hard-hearted; мека срца, soft-hearted. All in the genitive.

examples.sr: Остао је [ка̀меног ср̏ца] и није хтео да помогне.
examples.en: He stayed hard-hearted and refused to help.
I left with a heavy heart.

meanings: with a light heart, without regret

examples.sr: [Ла̀ка ср̏ца] сам се одлучио на промену.
examples.en: I decided on the change with a light heart.
He takes all criticism to heart.

key: phr:пао ми је камен са срца
cyr: пао ми је камен са срца
acc: па̏о ми је ка̏ме̄н са ср̏ца
meanings: a weight was lifted off one's chest

examples.sr: Кад је стигла вест, [па̏о ми је ка̏ме̄н са ср̏ца].
examples.en: When the news came, it was a weight off my chest.

forms: literally: the heart went down into the heels
meanings: one's heart sinks into one's boots

examples.sr: Кад сам чуо звук, [ср̏це ми је си̏шло у пе̏те].
examples.en: When I heard the sound, my heart sank into my boots.
His leaving broke her heart.
Don't drink coffee on an empty stomach.
I'd like a glass of sparkling water.

forms: literally: the water goes to the mouth

examples.sr: [Во̀да ми и̏де на у́ста] кад видим торту.
examples.en: My mouth waters when I see a cake.

forms: literally: calm water wears away the bank

examples.sr: Пази на њега: [ти̏ха во̀да бре̑г ро̏ни].
examples.en: Watch out for him: still waters run deep.

meanings: there was, it came to (an event)

examples.en: A conflict broke out.

forms: literally: to come to the head
meanings: to cost someone dearly, to come back to bite someone

examples.sr: Једног дана ће му то [до́ћи гла́ве].
examples.en: One day it will come back to bite him.

meanings: to come into its own, to show itself

examples.en: His talent came into its own.

meanings: to come to the same thing, to amount to the same

examples.sr: Како год да урадиш, [до̑ђе ти на и̏сто].
examples.en: However you do it, it comes to the same thing.

forms: literally: the cat will come to the little door
meanings: your day will come, what goes around comes around

examples.en: Go on talking, but your day of reckoning will come.

note: The sense: things will even out, and whoever was cocky will come asking.

key: phr:не знати да ли је пошао или дошао
cyr: не знати да ли је пошао или дошао
acc: не зна̏ти да ли је по̀шао и̏ли до̏шао
forms: literally: not to know whether he left or arrived
meanings: to not know whether one is coming or going

examples.sr: Од журбе [не зна̑ да ли је по̀шао и̏ли до̏шао].
examples.en: In his rush he doesn't know whether he's coming or going.

meanings: to bring a lawsuit, to sue

examples.en: He wants to sue his neighbor.

meanings: to stir up a fuss, to cause a scandal

examples.en: His statement caused a stir.

examples.sr: У очају је хтео да [ди̏гне ру̑ку на се̏бе].
examples.en: In despair he wanted to take his own life.

note: A grave euphemism. Without «на себе»: дићи руку на некога means to hit someone.

examples.sr: Након рата град се [ди̏гао из пѐпела].
examples.en: After the war the city rose from the ashes.

meanings: to get someone back on their feet (cure)

examples.sr: Лекар га је за месец [ди̏гао на но̏ге].
examples.en: The doctor got him back on his feet within a month.
Let's square it.

key: phr:ако чељад нису бесна, кућа није тесна
cyr: ако чељад нису бесна, кућа није тесна
acc: а̏ко че̏ља̄д ни́су бѐсна, ку̏ћа нѝје те̏сна
forms: literally: if the household isn't angry, the house isn't narrow

examples.sr: Нас шесторо у две собе, али [а̏ко че̏ља̄д ни́су бѐсна, ку̏ћа нѝје те̏сна].
examples.en: The six of us live in two rooms, but as long as we get along, there's room enough.

note: A proverb: where there is no ill will, there is room for everyone. Чељад is archaic for «household».

forms: literally: one's own little house, one's own little freedom
meanings: home sweet home, my own place, my own freedom

examples.sr: Стан је мали, али [сво̀ја ку̏ћица, сво̀ја слобо̀дица].
examples.en: The apartment is small, but it's my own place, my own freedom.

note: Said with joy about having a place of one's own, especially after buying one. Слободица is an affectionate «freedom».

forms: literally: to be one's own person
meanings: to be one's own man, to be independent

examples.en: Now I have a salary, I'm my own man.

note: Here свој means «belonging to oneself»: independent financially and in spirit.

meanings: to stick to one's guns, to stand one's ground

examples.sr: Сви су га убеђивали, али је [о̀стао при̏ сво̑ме].
examples.en: Everyone tried to convince him, but he stuck to his guns.

meanings: in due time, in its own time

examples.en: Everything will come in due time.

examples.sr: Овде сам [сво̑ј на сво̑ме] и никога се не бојим.
examples.en: Here I'm master of my own house and I'm not afraid of anyone.

note: Said of someone who has every right on their own ground. Usually proud or defiant.

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да ѝма̄м] једну куглу ваниле?
examples.en: Can I have one scoop of vanilla?
Can we have the check?

note: A polite way to order at a cafe or shop.

key: phr:само ћу да вас замолим за
cyr: само ћу да вас замолим за ...
acc: са̏мо ћу да вас замо̀лим за ...

examples.sr: [Са̏мо ћу да вас замо̀лим за] салвету.
examples.en: I'll just ask you for a napkin.

note: A soft request for something small. «За» takes the accusative.

forms: literally: to lie out a prison term
meanings: to serve one's time in prison

examples.sr: Пустили су га пошто је [о̀длежао ро̀бију].
examples.en: They released him after he had served his time.

note: Serbian says people «lie» in prison: лежати у затвору. «Одлежати» is to lie until the term is over.

forms: literally: he didn't move a finger

examples.sr: Цео дан је био код куће и [ни пр̏стом нѝје мр̏днуо].
examples.en: He was home all day and didn't lift a finger.

meanings: to lay a finger on, to harm

examples.sr: Ако га [до̀такнеш пр̏стом], имаћеш посла са мном.
examples.en: If you lay a finger on him, you'll have to deal with me.

note: Often negated: «ни прстом га није дотакао», he never laid a finger on him. May mean to hit or to hurt.

meanings: to have a hand in, to meddle

examples.sr: Сумњам да је и он [у̀мешао пр̏сте] у ту ствар.
examples.en: I suspect he had a hand in that business too.

note: Usually of hidden or unwelcome meddling: «овде је ђаво умешао прсте», the devil had a hand in this.

examples.sr: После пожара остао је [го̑ ка̏о пр̏ст].
examples.en: After the fire he was left penniless.

examples.sr: Праве пријатеље можеш [и̏збројати на пр̏сте] једне руке.
examples.en: You can count your real friends on the fingers of one hand.

meanings: to know inside out, to know like the back of one's hand

examples.en: He knows the whole grammar inside out.

meanings: to lose ground, to lose one's footing

examples.sr: Влада [гу̏би тло̏ под но̀гама] пред изборе.
examples.en: The government is losing ground before the elections.

note: Both literal (feeling you are falling) and figurative: support or confidence is slipping.

meanings: to lose count, to lose track

examples.sr: Радио сам толико да сам [изгу̀био ра̀чӯн] о времену.
examples.en: I worked so much that I lost track of time.

note: Usually «изгубити рачун о времену». Рачун here is a count, not a bank account.

meanings: to lose one's cool, to lose one's temper

examples.sr: Не [гу̏би жѝвце], све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't lose your cool, everything will be fine.

meanings: to lose face, to be disgraced

examples.sr: Не жели да [и̏згуби о̀браз] пред комшијама.
examples.en: He doesn't want to lose face in front of the neighbors.

note: Образ is «cheek» and «face» in the sense of honor. Also: «имати образа», to have a conscience.

meanings: to lose sight of, to overlook

examples.sr: Не смемо [гу̀бити из ви̑да] главни циљ.
examples.en: We must not lose sight of the main goal.

meanings: up to one's ears, more than enough

examples.en: I'm up to my ears in work.

note: Often «свега ми је преко главе»: I'm sick of all of it.

meanings: to bury one's head in the sand

examples.en: Burying your head in the sand is not a solution.

forms: literally: to climb onto someone's head
meanings: to get on someone's nerves, to take advantage of someone

examples.sr: Доста више, [по̀пео ми се на гла̑ву] са тим питањима!
examples.en: Enough, he's driving me up the wall with those questions!

note: Said of someone who pesters or gets too cheeky.

forms: literally: to work on someone's head
meanings: to plot against someone, to be out to get someone

examples.en: Someone is out to get me.

note: A non-obvious phrase: радити here means «to plot». «Ради му се о глави» means he is in serious danger.

meanings: to throw up one's hands, to clutch one's head

examples.en: The investors are throwing up their hands.

key: phr:не боли ме глава за то
cyr: не боли ме глава за то
acc: не бо̀ли ме гла́ва за то̑
forms: literally: my head doesn't hurt over that

examples.sr: Нека раде шта хоће, [ме̏не не бо̀ли гла́ва за то̑].
examples.en: Let them do what they want, I don't care.

key: phr:ко нема у глави, има у ногама
cyr: ко нема у глави, има у ногама
acc: ко̏ не̑ма у гла́ви, и̏ма у но̀гама
meanings: if you don't use your head, you'll use your legs

examples.sr: Заборавио је кључеве, па се враћао два пута - [ко̏ не̑ма у гла́ви, и̏ма у но̀гама].
examples.en: He forgot his keys and had to go back twice - if you don't use your head, you use your legs.

note: A proverb: whoever doesn't think ahead ends up running back and forth.

examples.en: We arrived at just the right time.

note: Literally «the right time»: what the Greeks called kairos.

examples.en: I arrived exactly on time.

meanings: in the spirit of the times

examples.en: Their style is in the spirit of the times.

examples.sr: Звао ме је [с врѐмена на вре́ме].
examples.en: He called me from time to time.
You'll get used to it in time.
We played cards to kill time.

meanings: to gain time, to buy time

examples.sr: Морамо нешто смислити да [до̀бијемо у врѐмену].
examples.en: We have to think of something to buy time.
Don't waste time on trifles.

forms: literally: to drive a knife into the back
meanings: to stab someone in the back, to betray

examples.sr: Мислио сам да ми је пријатељ, а он ми је [за̀био но̑ж у ле́ђа].
examples.en: I thought he was my friend, but he stabbed me in the back.

examples.sr: Не волим кад људи [го̀воре ѝза ле́ђа].
examples.en: I don't like it when people talk behind my back.

examples.sr: Када је остао без новца, сви су му [о̀кренули ле́ђа].
examples.en: When he ran out of money, everyone turned their back on him.

meanings: to watch someone's back, to have someone's back

examples.sr: Ти иди напред, ја ћу ти [чу́вати ле́ђа].
examples.en: You go ahead, I'll watch your back.

meanings: to see the back of someone, to be glad to see someone go

examples.sr: Једва сам дочекао да му [ви̏дӣм ле́ђа].
examples.en: I could hardly wait to see the back of him.

note: Ironic: you are glad an unpleasant person has finally left.

meanings: to have one foot in the grave

examples.sr: Старица је већ била [јѐдно̄м но̀го̄м у гро̑бу].
examples.en: The old woman already had one foot in the grave.

note: Variant: «на ивици гроба», on the edge of the grave.

examples.en: He remained faithful to her to the grave.
I'll take my secrets to the grave.

note: Of a secret one will never tell. Compare «ћутати као гроб».

meanings: to be silent as the grave

examples.sr: Реци ми, ја ћу [ћу́тати ка̏о гро̏б].
examples.en: Tell me, and I'll be silent as the grave.

meanings: to turn over in one's grave

examples.sr: Јадни мој деда би се [прѐврнуо у гро̑бу].
examples.en: My poor grandfather would turn over in his grave.

note: Almost always in the conditional: the dead would be horrified at today's disgrace.

meanings: to drive someone to an early grave

examples.sr: [О̀тераћете ме у гро̏б] са тим бригама!
examples.en: You'll drive me to an early grave with those worries!

note: Literal or an exaggeration: to worry someone to death.

examples.sr: „[Бо̏ље̄ у гро̏б не̏го ро̏б]“ - вичу они на тргу.
examples.en: "Better the grave than slavery," they shout in the square.

note: A well-known rhyming slogan: гроб - роб. Readiness to die rather than submit.

meanings: from the cradle to the grave

examples.sr: Држава брине о њима [од ко̀ле̄вке до гро̑ба].
examples.en: The state takes care of them from the cradle to the grave.

meanings: by (doing something), in such a way that

examples.sr: Деца уче језик [та̀ко̄ што̏] слушају родитеље.
examples.en: Children learn a language by listening to their parents.

examples.sr: Можеш помоћи [та̀ко̄ што̏ ћеш о̀стати] овде.
examples.en: You can help by staying here.

note: Followed by a full clause with its own verb in the right tense.

forms: literally: to call oneself to reason

examples.sr: Надам се да ће се [до̀звати па̏мети] пре него што буде касно.
examples.en: I hope he comes to his senses before it's too late.

meanings: to knock on many doors, to go from door to door

examples.sr: Морао је [оби́јати мно̏га вра́та] док није нашао посао.
examples.en: He had to knock on many doors before he found a job.
The decision was made behind closed doors.

meanings: to find nobody home, to find the door shut

examples.sr: Стигао је касно и само је [пољу̀био вра́та].
examples.en: He arrived late and found only a closed door.

note: Said when someone arrives and nobody is home or the door is locked: all he got was the door.

examples.sr: Лакше се улази [на ма̀ла вра́та] него на велика.
examples.en: It's easier to get in through the back door than through the front.

note: To get what you want outside the official procedure, through connections. The front door is «на велика врата».

meanings: to cast a glance, to glance

examples.sr: [Ба̏цио је по̏гле̄д] на сат и наставио да ради.
examples.en: He glanced at the clock and went on working.

examples.sr: Када су га питали за грешку, [обо̀рио је по̏гле̄д].
examples.en: When they asked him about the mistake, he lowered his gaze.

meanings: to fix one's gaze, to turn one's eyes

examples.en: Everyone turned their eyes to the speaker.

examples.sr: [На пр̀ви по̏гле̄д] кућа је изгледала обично.
examples.en: At first glance the house looked ordinary.

examples.sr: То је био [у сва̑ком по̀гледу] успешан састанак.
examples.en: It was a successful meeting in every respect.

note: Поглед means both «look» and «respect, aspect». Also «у том погледу», in that respect.

examples.sr: Резервисали смо [со̏бу са по̏гле̄дом] на море.
examples.en: We booked a room with a sea view.

note: Поглед also means «view, panorama»: поглед на море.

examples.en: No man's land stretches between the borders.

examples.sr: Многи су мислили да је Америка [о̀бећана зѐмља].
examples.en: Many thought America was the promised land.

meanings: to wipe off the face of the earth

examples.sr: Поплава је скоро [збри̏сала сѐло с ли̏ца зѐмље].
examples.en: The flood almost wiped the village off the face of the earth.

meanings: may the earth rest lightly on him, may he rest in peace

examples.sr: [Ла̀ка му цр̏на зѐмља], био је добар човек.
examples.en: May the earth rest lightly on him, he was a good man.

note: Said of the dead; literally «may the black earth be light on him».

forms: literally: to step on the crazy stone
meanings: to tie the knot, to get married

examples.sr: После десет година везе, коначно је [ста̏о на лу̑дӣ ка̏ме̄н].
examples.en: After ten years together, he finally tied the knot.

note: Jocular: marriage is likened to a crazy step.

key: phr:не оставити ни камен на камену
cyr: не оставити ни камен на камену
acc: не о̀ставити ни ка̏ме̄н на ка̀мену
meanings: to leave not one stone upon another

examples.sr: Критичар [нѝје о̀ставио ни ка̏ме̄н на ка̀мену] од те представе.
examples.en: The critic tore that play to shreds.

meanings: neat and tidy, in perfect order

examples.en: Everything is tidy, everything is in perfect order.

forms: literally: to hang on a thread

examples.en: His life is hanging by a thread.

meanings: to upset someone's plans, to throw a wrench in the works

examples.en: We wanted to throw a wrench in the favorite's plans.

key: phr:држати све конце у својим рукама
cyr: држати све конце у својим рукама
acc: др̀жати све̏ ко̀нце у сво̀јӣм ру̀кама
meanings: to hold all the strings, to keep everything under control

examples.sr: Он жели да [др̀жи све̏ ко̀нце у сво̀јӣм ру̀кама].
examples.en: He wants to hold all the strings in his hands.

note: The image of a puppeteer pulling the strings.

examples.en: I heard they're raking in the money.

note: Slightly ironic: of those who earn a lot, and easily.

forms: literally: to not be worth even a split para
meanings: to not be worth a red cent

examples.sr: Његово обећање [не вре́ди ни прѐбијене па̏ре].
examples.en: His promise isn't worth a red cent.

note: Пребијена пара is a split coin worth nothing. Said of things and of deeds.

meanings: a fortune, a ridiculous amount of money

examples.sr: Дао је [гр̏дне па̏ре] за тај аутомобил.
examples.en: He paid a fortune for that car.

note: Грдан means «ugly, huge»; it stresses how big the sum is.

examples.sr: Она [ле̏жи на па̏рама], а стално се жали.
examples.en: She's rolling in money, yet she complains all the time.
What on earth is this, good heavens!

note: An exclamation of surprise or annoyance.

meanings: to beg in God's name, to implore

examples.en: I implore you, tell me the truth.

note: Usually in the form «Кумим те богом».

examples.sr: Он ће да се предомисли? [Бо̏же сачу̀вај]!
examples.en: He's going to change his mind? God forbid!

key: phr:бог је најпре себи створио браду
cyr: бог је најпре себи створио браду
acc: бо̑г је на̏јпре се̏би ство̏рио бра̑ду
forms: literally: God first made a beard for himself

examples.sr: Свако мисли на себе: [бо̑г је на̏јпре се̏би ство̏рио бра̑ду].
examples.en: Everyone thinks of themselves: charity begins at home.

key: phr:где је бог рекао лаку ноћ
cyr: где је бог рекао лаку ноћ
acc: где̏ је бо̑г ре̏као ла̀ку но̑ћ
forms: literally: where God said good night

examples.sr: Они живе [та̏мо где̏ је бо̑г ре̏као ла̀ку но̑ћ].
examples.en: They live in the middle of nowhere.

note: Synonyms: «богу иза леђа», «богу иза ногу». Said of a very remote, out-of-the-way place.

meanings: no relation at all, a complete stranger

examples.sr: Шта ме брига за тог човека, он ми је [ни ро̑д ни по̀моз бо̑г].
examples.en: Why should I care about that man, he's nothing to me.

note: Said of an outsider who is neither a relative nor a friend. Often written «ни род ни помоз' бог».

key: phr:ко није са мном, против мене је
cyr: ко није са мном, против мене је
acc: ко̏ нѝје са мно̑м, про̏тив ме̏не је
meanings: whoever is not with me is against me
