examples.sr: „[Ко̏ нѝје са мно̑м, про̏тив ме̏не је]“, рекао је вођа.
examples.en: "Whoever is not with me is against me," said the leader.

note: A biblical quotation.

key: phr:око за око, зуб за зуб
cyr: око за око, зуб за зуб
acc: о̏ко за о̏ко, зу̑б за зу̑б
meanings: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth

examples.sr: Освета по принципу „[о̏ко за о̏ко, зу̑б за зу̑б]“ не решава ништа.
examples.en: Revenge on the principle of "an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth" solves nothing.

meanings: blessed are the poor in spirit

examples.en: "Blessed are the poor in spirit," says the Scripture.

meanings: a voice crying in the wilderness

examples.sr: Његови позиви остали су [гла̑с ва̀пијућег у пу̀стињи].
examples.en: His appeals remained a voice crying in the wilderness.

note: «Вапијући» is a bookish participle, rare in modern speech.

examples.sr: „[По̀следњӣ ће би̏ти пр̀ви], а први последњи“, каже изрека.
examples.en: "The last shall be first, and the first last," says the saying.

key: phr:не живи човек о самом хлебу
cyr: не живи човек о самом хлебу
acc: не жи̏ви чо̏век о са̀мом хле̏бу
meanings: man shall not live by bread alone

examples.sr: Читање је важно: [не жи̏ви чо̀век о са̀мом хле̏бу].
examples.en: Reading is important: man shall not live by bread alone.

note: A biblical quotation.

examples.sr: Нисам јео од јутрос, [гла́дан сам ка̏о па̑с].
examples.en: I haven't eaten since this morning, I'm starving.

meanings: to fight like cats and dogs

examples.en: The neighbors fight like cats and dogs.

meanings: his bark is worse than his bite

examples.sr: Не плаши га се, [па̑с ко̀јӣ ла̏је̄ не у̀једа].
examples.en: Don't be afraid of him, his bark is worse than his bite.

forms: literally: the dog barks, the wind carries it off
meanings: pay no attention to the barking

examples.sr: Не секирај се због критика: [па̑с ла̏је̄, ве̏тар но̏си].
examples.en: Don't worry about the criticism: the dog barks, the wind carries it off.

note: The wind carries the barking away: criticism is not worth minding.

examples.sr: Он [ла̏же ка̏о па̑с], не верујем му.
examples.en: He lies through his teeth, I don't believe him.

meanings: to be left without a roof over one's head

examples.sr: После пожара многе породице су [о̀стале без кро̏ва над гла́во̄м].
examples.en: After the fire, many families were left without a roof over their heads.

examples.sr: Никоме не причај, [не̏ка то̑ о̀стане̄ ме̏ђу на̏ма].
examples.en: Don't tell anyone, let this stay between us.

examples.sr: Помогао ми је, а ја [не́ћу о̀стати ду́жан].
examples.en: He helped me, and I won't stay in his debt.

note: Can mean repaying a favor or taking revenge, depending on context.

examples.sr: Младић је био толико затечен да је [о̀стао без ре̑чи].
examples.en: The young man was so taken aback that he was left speechless.

meanings: nothing else was left for me

examples.sr: [Нѝје нам о̀стало ни̏шта дру̏го] него да чекамо.
examples.en: We have no choice but to wait.
I think we're even.

note: Used both literally (to pay back a debt) and figuratively (to end a dispute, to get even).

forms: literally: a bill without the innkeeper

examples.sr: Све сте испланирали, али [пра̀вите ра̀чӯн без кр̏чмара].
examples.en: You've planned everything, but it looks like you're counting your chickens before they hatch.

note: You cannot settle up at an inn without asking the innkeeper: counting on something without the key person. Close to «counting your chickens».

examples.sr: Сви морају да [по̀ложе ра̀чӯн] за своје поступке.
examples.en: Everyone must answer for their actions.

note: Impf. «полагати рачуне»: «теби не морам полагати рачуне» - I don't have to answer to you.

forms: literally: to hang by a hair

examples.en: His life was hanging by a thread.

forms: literally: to go against the fur

examples.sr: Не треба му [ѝћи уз дла̏ку] кад је љут.
examples.en: You shouldn't cross him when he's angry.

note: The paired expression «ићи низ длаку» means to agree with someone, to flatter.

meanings: to get someone back on their feet

examples.sr: Лекари су га после дуге болести [по̀дигли на но̏ге].
examples.en: The doctors got him back on his feet after a long illness.

examples.sr: Концерт је [по̀дигао на но̏ге] цео град.
examples.en: The concert got the whole city on its feet.
I've been on my feet all day.

examples.sr: Попио је кафу [с но̏гу] и отишао на посао.
examples.en: He drank his coffee on the go and left for work.

note: Said of quick eating and drinking when there is no time to sit down.

examples.en: I've been doing music since I was little.

examples.sr: Са свим колегама живи [на до̀број но̀зи].
examples.en: He's on good terms with all his colleagues.

forms: literally: to live on a high foot
meanings: to live high on the hog

examples.sr: Почео је да [жи̏ви на висо̀кој но̀зи].
examples.en: He started to live in grand style.

examples.sr: Грип ју је потпуно [обо̀рио с но̏гу].
examples.en: The flu completely knocked her off her feet.

examples.sr: Вест о победи га је [о̀борила с но̏гу].
examples.en: The news of the victory floored him.

meanings: a lie is soon found out

examples.sr: Не лажи, јер [у ла̏жи су кра̀тке но̏ге].
examples.en: Don't lie, because lies have short legs.

note: A deception is soon uncovered and does not get you far.

forms: literally: to hide like a snake hides its legs

examples.sr: Он [кри̏је сво̀је на̑мере ка̏о змѝја но̏ге].
examples.en: He is hiding his intentions very carefully.

note: If a snake had legs, it would hide them very skillfully.

examples.sr: Ако желиш да живиш овде, поштоваћеш [ку̏ћнӣ ре̑д].
examples.en: If you want to live here, you'll follow the house rules.

examples.sr: Она је [у пр̏вим рѐдовима] међу младим научницима.
examples.en: She is in the front ranks of the young scientists.

examples.sr: И ти ћеш [до́ћи на ре̑д], само полако.
examples.en: Your turn will come too, take it easy.

examples.sr: Афера је [ба̏цила се̏нку на] његову каријеру.
examples.en: The scandal cast a shadow on his career.
Reporters followed the actress like a shadow.

meanings: to be afraid of one's own shadow

examples.sr: Не сме ништа да уради, [пла̏ши се сво̀је се̑нке].
examples.en: He doesn't dare to do anything, he's afraid of his own shadow.

note: Variant: «бојати се властите сенке».

meanings: a shadow of one's former self

examples.sr: После болести је био само [се̑нка од чо̀века].
examples.en: After the illness he was only a shadow of a man.

examples.sr: Он је [из се̑нке] утицао на све одлуке.
examples.en: He influenced all the decisions from the shadows.

examples.sr: Кад останем сам ноћу, [хва̏та ме стра̑х].
examples.en: When I'm alone at night, I get scared.

note: Pattern «хвата ме + feeling»: носталгија, језа, грозница (nostalgia, a shiver, a fever).

examples.sr: Причао је виц и сви су [хва̏тали за сто̏ма̄к].
examples.en: He was telling a joke and everyone was holding their sides.

note: Usually «хватати се за стомак од смеха».

examples.en: It looks like you're clutching at straws.
The secretary took notes during the meeting.

examples.sr: Не [хва̏тај крѝвине], има посла за све.
examples.en: Don't shirk, there's work for everyone.

note: Colloquial: to pretend to be busy and avoid work.

examples.sr: Чим је видео полицију, [у̀хватио је ма̏глу].
examples.en: As soon as he saw the police, he ran off.

note: Colloquial. More often pf.: ухватити маглу.

meanings: to pay out of one's own pocket

examples.en: I'll have to pay out of my own pocket.

meanings: to hit someone in the wallet

examples.sr: Нова такса ће нас [у̀дарити по џѐпу].
examples.en: The new fee will hit us in the wallet.

examples.sr: Они су покушали да [и̏спразне џѐпове] верника.
examples.en: They tried to empty the believers' pockets.
He came to the city penniless.
She is looking for someone with deep pockets.
That isn't within everyone's means.

forms: literally: to know like one's own pocket
meanings: to know like the back of one's hand

examples.en: I know this place like the back of my hand.

meanings: I have a problem (opening a request to a repairman)

examples.sr: [Ѝма̄м јѐдан про̀бле̄м]. Можете ли да ми помогнете?
examples.en: I have a problem. Can you help me?

note: A calm opening with a repairman or support; then you briefly say what happened.

examples.en: The faucet in the bathroom is leaking.

note: Similar complaints: «пукла је цев» - a pipe burst; «не ради бојлер» - the water heater is out.

meanings: I would like you to ... for me (request to a repairman)

examples.en: I'd like you to replace the water heater.
I'd like you to paint the wall.

note: Polite request: after «да ми» the verb takes the plural «you» form («замените») as a sign of politeness.

meanings: I'd like to book an appointment with ...

examples.en: I'd like to book an appointment with a gynecologist.
I'd like to book an appointment with Dr. Savić.

note: On the phone, first check the office («Да ли је то стоматолошка ординација?»). «код» + gen.

examples.en: Tomorrow at 12 works for me.
This time slot doesn't work for me.

key: phr:да ли постоји могућност кућне посете
cyr: да ли постоји могућност кућне посете?
acc: да ли по̀стоји могу́ћно̄ст ку̏ћне по̀сете?
meanings: is it possible to arrange a home visit?

examples.en: Is it possible for the doctor to make a home visit?

note: A home-call service is «теренска служба»; an exam at home is «преглед на терену».

forms: literally: to circle like a cat around bacon

examples.sr: Већ сат времена [кру̀жи ка̏о ма̏чка о̏ко сла̀нине], а не усуђује се да пита.
examples.en: He's been beating around the bush for an hour and doesn't dare to ask.

forms: literally: the old woman with the cakes has passed by

examples.sr: Сада је касно, [про̏шла ба̏ба с кола̀чима].
examples.en: It's too late now, the ship has sailed.

examples.sr: За њих је сваки динар [хле̏б са се̏дам ко̑ра].
examples.en: For them every dinar is hard-earned bread.

note: Said of income that took a lot of hard work to earn.

meanings: to mess things up for someone

examples.en: Someone has messed things up for us.
You've messed things up for yourself.

note: The image of a ruined soup: the roux is burnt and cannot be fixed.

examples.sr: Његова мајка је била [ѝзван се̏бе] од бриге.
examples.en: His mother was beside herself with worry.

examples.sr: Дајем ти пар дана да [до̀ђеш к се̏би].
examples.en: I'm giving you a few days to pull yourself together.

examples.sr: Он је [прѐузео на се̏бе] сву одговорност.
examples.en: He took all the responsibility upon himself.

examples.sr: Седела је у тишини, [у̀дубљена у се̏бе].
examples.en: She sat in silence, lost in thought.

examples.sr: Током разговора [по̀вукао се у се̏бе] и ћутао.
examples.en: During the conversation he retreated into his shell and said nothing.

examples.sr: Овај проблем [сам по се̏би] није тежак.
examples.en: This problem in itself is not hard.

note: «сам» declines: сама по себи, само по себи.

examples.sr: [Ца̑рство му не̏беско], био је добар човек.
examples.en: God rest his soul, he was a good man.

note: A religious condolence formula, fitting when the other person is religious.

examples.en: God rest our grandfather's soul.

note: A religious formula said in memory of the dead. Not for non-religious listeners.

examples.en: Rest in peace, dear friend.

note: For a woman: «почивала у миру».

forms: literally: water comes to my mouth

examples.sr: Кад осетим мирис ћевапа, [и̏де ми во̀да на у́ста].
examples.en: When I smell ćevapi, my mouth waters.

meanings: to take the bread out of someone's mouth

examples.sr: Тим порезима су људима [о̀тели за̏лога̄ј из у́ста].
examples.en: Those taxes took the bread out of people's mouths.

meanings: to put words in someone's mouth

examples.sr: Немој да ми [ста̀вљаш ре̑чи у у́ста].
examples.en: Don't put words in my mouth.

key: phr:из уста си ми извадио реч
cyr: из уста си ми извадио реч
acc: из у́ста си ми ѝзвадио ре̑ч
meanings: you took the words right out of my mouth

examples.en: You took the words right out of my mouth!

examples.sr: Ставио је [пр̏ст на у́ста] да ућутимо.
examples.en: He put a finger to his lips to make us be quiet.

key: phr:из твојих уста у божје уши
cyr: из твојих уста у божје уши
acc: из тво̀јӣх у́ста у бо̏жје у̏ши
meanings: from your mouth to God's ears

examples.sr: Победићемо? - [Из тво̀јӣх у́ста у бо̏жје у̏ши]!
examples.en: Are we going to win? - From your mouth to God's ears!

note: A reply to a good hope or wish: may God hear you.

examples.sr: О томе се причало [на сва̏ у́ста].
examples.en: It was talked about openly.
He sings your praises to everyone.

meanings: to be always on someone's lips

examples.sr: Та реченица им [не сѝлази с у́ста].
examples.en: That phrase never leaves their lips.

examples.sr: Немој да [прѝказујеш све̏ цр̀ним бо̀јама], није све тако лоше.
examples.en: Don't paint everything in dark colors, it's not that bad.

meanings: to see everything through dark glasses

examples.sr: Људи у депресији [гле̏дајӯ све̑т кроз цр̀не на̏оча̄ре].
examples.en: Depressed people see the world through dark glasses.
His name is on the blacklist.

examples.sr: Радим већ двадесет година и [је̏де̄м сво̑ј хле̏б].
examples.en: I've been working for twenty years and I earn my own living.

note: Echoes the Bible: «in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread».

examples.en: I don't want to live off other people.

note: Sometimes with a hint of betrayal: he ate their bread, then turned against them.

forms: literally: lie down, bread, so I can eat you
meanings: to laze around waiting for everything to be handed over

examples.sr: Он само [ле̏зи ле̏бе да те је̏де̄м] и чека да му неко све донесе.
examples.en: He just lazes around and waits for someone to bring him everything.

note: Humorous. Hence «лезилебовић» - a lazybones. Often «леб» without «х»: common in everyday speech and writing.

forms: literally: good as a little loaf

examples.en: Her grandfather is as good as gold.
He worked for his daily bread.

note: From the Lord's Prayer: «хлеб наш насушни дај нам данас».

meanings: to welcome with bread and salt

examples.sr: Код нас се гости [дочѐкују хле̏бом и со̀љу].
examples.en: Here, guests are welcomed with bread and salt.

forms: literally: to ask for bread on top of flatbread
meanings: to want more than one needs

examples.sr: Има посао и кућу, а још [тра̏жи хле̏ба пре̏ко пога̀че].
examples.en: He has a job and a house, and he still wants more.

note: Погача is a flatbread; bread on top of it is too much. «То је хлеб преко погаче» - that is excess.

forms: literally: to go after the hand

examples.sr: Коначно ми је [по̏шло за ру́ко̄м] да положим испит.
examples.en: I finally managed to pass the exam.

note: Impersonal: person (dat.) + је пошло за руком.

forms: literally: to enter into the years

examples.sr: Мој деда је [за̀шао у го̏дине], али је и даље бодар.
examples.en: My grandfather is getting on in years, but he's still sprightly.

examples.sr: Нисам могао да [вѐрујем сво̀јӣм у̀шима] кад сам чуо вест.
examples.en: I couldn't believe my ears when I heard the news.

meanings: to hear with one's own ears

examples.sr: То сам [чу̏о сво̀јӣм у̀шима], нико ми није препричао.
examples.en: I heard that with my own ears, nobody told it to me.

meanings: to listen with half an ear

examples.sr: Он ме [слу̏ша на је̏дно у̏во] док гледа телефон.
examples.en: He listens to me with half an ear while looking at his phone.

note: Variant: «слушати са пола ува».

examples.sr: Не причај о томе овде, [и зи̏дови и̏мају у̏ши].
examples.en: Don't talk about it here, walls have ears.

meanings: to blush up to one's ears

examples.sr: Девојчица је [по̀црвенела до у̀шијӯ] кад су је похвалили.
examples.en: The little girl blushed up to her ears when they praised her.
Her accent grates on my ears.

key: phr:један плус три једнако је четири
cyr: један плус три једнако је четири
acc: јѐдан плу̑с три̑ је̏дна̄ко је чѐтири

examples.en: Five minus two equals three.
Five times two equals ten.

note: Плус, минус, пута (times), подељено са (divided by). The result comes after «једнако је».

forms: literally: to swear like a coachman

examples.sr: Кад је видео штету, [псо̀вао] је као кочијаш.
examples.en: When he saw the damage, he swore like a trooper.

key: phr:ко о чему, баба о уштипцима
cyr: ко о чему, баба о уштипцима.
acc: ко̏ о чѐму, ба̏ба о у̀штипцима.
forms: literally: each about something, the old woman about fritters

examples.sr: Опет прича о храни - [ко̏ о чѐму, ба̏ба о у̀штипцима].
examples.en: Talking about food again - some people only ever think of one thing.

note: About a person obsessed with one topic. Уштипци are fried pieces of dough.

key: phr:трла баба лан да јој прође дан
cyr: трла баба лан да јој прође дан.
acc: тр́ла ба̏ба ла̏н да јој про̀ђе да̑н.
forms: literally: the old woman beat flax to make the day pass
meanings: to fritter time away on trifles

examples.sr: Цео дан смо седели и причали - [тр́ла ба̏ба ла̏н]!
examples.en: We sat and talked all day - just killing time!

note: About an activity with no result, only to kill time.

key: phr:што је баби мило, то јој се и снило
cyr: што је баби мило, то јој се и снило.
acc: што̏ је ба̀би ми̏ло, то̑ јој се и сни̏ло.
forms: literally: what the old woman likes is what she dreams of
meanings: you see what you want to see
people dream of what is on their mind

examples.sr: Он у свему види превару - [што̏ је ба̀би ми̏ло, то̑ јој се и сни̏ло].
examples.en: He sees deception in everything - you see what's on your mind.

note: Said with a touch of folk irony.

examples.en: Don't play with fire!

forms: literally: to take chestnuts out of the fire
meanings: to pull someone's chestnuts out of the fire

examples.sr: Увек ја морам да [ва̏дим ке̏стење из ва̏тре].
examples.en: I always have to pull the chestnuts out of the fire.

note: Often about a politician who sorts out a conflict he did not start.

forms: literally: to climb to the top of the head
meanings: to get on one's last nerve

examples.sr: Та песма ми се већ [по̀пела на вр̏х гла́ве].
examples.en: I'm already sick of that song.

note: Also without a verb: «Ово ми је на врх главе» - I've had enough.

forms: literally: a meeting at the top

examples.sr: Сутра почиње [са̀станак на вр̀ху] председника држава.
examples.en: A summit of the heads of state starts tomorrow.

forms: literally: it is peeing to me

examples.sr: [Пи̏шки ми се], станимо на следећој пумпи.
examples.en: I need to pee, let's stop at the next gas station.

note: Colloquial, children's or everyday speech; the construction is like «спава ми се».

forms: literally: to move on to the matter

examples.en: Let's get to the point.

note: Imperative: «Пређи на ствар!»

forms: literally: smeared with all the colors

examples.sr: Не верујем му, он је [прѐмазан сви̑м бо̀јама].
examples.en: I don't trust him, he's a sly old fox.

note: The image of a chameleon: a person who changes color to suit the situation.

forms: literally: to show in a pink color
meanings: to put in a rosy light

examples.sr: Он увек [прика̀зује ства̑ри у ру̀жичастој бо̀ји].
examples.en: He always paints a rosy picture of things.

note: The paired phrase is «приказати у црној боји».

forms: literally: to see in black colors

examples.en: You see everything in black.

note: Also «приказати у црној боји» - to portray in a gloomy light.

examples.sr: Кад је чула шалу, [пра̀сла је у сме̑х].
examples.en: When she heard the joke, she burst out laughing.

note: About sudden, unexpected laughter; can add «против воље» - against one's will.

forms: literally: to pour from the hollow into the empty

examples.sr: Цео састанак су [прѐсипали из шу̏пљег у пра̑зно].
examples.en: They spent the whole meeting spinning their wheels.

note: About people who look busy but achieve nothing.

forms: literally: to build towers in the air
meanings: to build castles in the air

examples.sr: Не [зи̑да̄ј ку̀ле у ва̀здуху], већ почни да радиш.
examples.en: Don't build castles in the air, get to work.

note: Suggests groundless dreams and plans with no basis.

forms: literally: to do the work of Sisyphus

examples.sr: Чистимо, а деца све растуре - [ра̀димо Си̏зифов по̀сао].
examples.en: We clean and the kids scatter everything again - it's a Sisyphean task.

note: From the Greek myth; often «То је Сизифов посао».

forms: literally: to come to the ready-made
meanings: to have everything handed to one on a plate

examples.sr: Он очекује да ће [до́ћи на го̀тово].
examples.en: He expects to have everything handed to him on a plate.

examples.sr: Одлука је пала, то је већ [го̀това ства̑р].
examples.en: The decision has been made, it's already a done deal.

note: «Готов» here means finished.

meanings: can I try it on? (in a shop)

examples.sr: Свиђа ми се ова јакна. [Мо̀гу ли да је про̑бам]?
examples.en: I like this jacket. Can I try it on?

note: A must-have phrase in a clothes shop; a fitting room is «кабина за пробу».

examples.en: On weekdays I get up at six.

note: «викендом» (on weekends) and «празницима» (on holidays) are built the same way, in the instrumental: a regular action.

examples.sr: У нашој фирми има [сло̏бодно ра̑дно ме̏сто].
examples.en: There is a job opening at our company.

note: For remote work people say «рад од куће» or «посао од куће».

forms: literally: don't count it as a fault

examples.en: Don't hold it against me, I was nervous.

note: Polite form: «не замерите». Smooths over a small awkwardness.

examples.en: My mistake, I didn't understand correctly.

note: Fuller: «грешка је моја». Admits responsibility.

forms: literally: I didn't want to offend you
meanings: I didn't mean to offend you

examples.en: I didn't mean to offend you, sorry.

note: A woman says «нисам хтела». Stresses that the words were not meant badly.

examples.en: We waited and waited in line.

note: The prefix «на-» and «се» show that the wait dragged on and was tiring.

examples.en: Shopping online saves time.

note: Also «штедети новац, енергију» (save money, energy).

examples.en: I don't like waiting in line.

key: phr:питати за савет у вези са
cyr: питати за савет у вези са
acc: пи́тати за са́вет у ве́зи са
forms: literally: to ask for advice in connection with

examples.sr: Желим да [пи̑та̄м за са́вет у ве́зи са] возовима.
examples.en: I want to ask for advice about trains.

note: «у вези са» + instr. means 'regarding, in connection with'.

examples.en: Which are your favorite seasons?

note: «доба» is neuter (pl. «доба»). The seasons: пролеће, лето, јесен, зима.

examples.sr: Тамо не бих ишао [ни по ко̀јӯ цѐну].
examples.en: I wouldn't go there for anything.

note: An emphatic refusal. More jokingly: «ни под тачком разно» (under no circumstances).

examples.sr: Позајмити му новац? [Ни под та̏чком ра̏зно]!
examples.en: Lend him money? Not on your life!

note: From meeting agendas, where «разно» is the last item (any other business). Sounds more ironic than «никако».

examples.sr: Сутра је [не̏радни да̑н], продавнице не раде.
examples.en: Tomorrow is a day off, the shops are closed.

note: A notice on a door. One's own day off is «слободан дан»; a holiday is «празник».

examples.sr: Овај лек се издаје само [на рѐцепт].
examples.en: This medicine is dispensed only on prescription.

note: Without a prescription: «без рецепта».

examples.en: They have good draft beer here.

note: From «точити» - to pour. Dark beer is «тамно», light is «светло».

forms: literally: whoever sings thinks no evil
meanings: he who sings means no harm

examples.sr: Увек пева, па [ко̏ пе̏ва, зло̏ не ми̏сли].
examples.en: He's always singing, and he who sings means no harm.

meanings: history is the teacher of life

examples.sr: [Ѝсто̄рија је учитѐљица живо̀та], али ђаци су лоши.
examples.en: History is the teacher of life, but the pupils are bad.

meanings: Where can I park my car?

examples.en: Excuse me, where can I park my car?

note: A possible answer: «Недалеко одавде имате паркинг» - there is a parking lot not far from here.

examples.en: You're doing great work, keep it up!

meanings: I'd like to open an account.

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлео бих да о̀творим ра̀чӯн].
examples.en: Good afternoon, I'd like to open an account.

note: A woman says «желела бих».

examples.sr: Где је мењачница? [Тре́ба да про̀меним но̀вац].
examples.en: Where is the exchange office? I need to exchange money.
Please give me small bills.
Please sign on the back.

forms: literally: the train ran away from me

examples.sr: [По̀бегао ми је во̑з], па чекам следећи.
examples.en: I missed my train, so I'm waiting for the next one.

key: phr:да ли је ово седиште заузето
cyr: да ли је ово седиште заузето?
acc: да ли је о̀во̄ се̏дӣште за̀узето?

examples.sr: Извините, [да ли је о̀во̄ се̏дӣште за̀узето]?
examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?

key: phr:на којој станици треба да сиђем
cyr: на којој станици треба да сиђем?
acc: на ко̀јо̄ј ста̀ници тре́ба да сѝђем?
meanings: Which stop should I get off at?

examples.sr: [На ко̀јо̄ј ста̀ници тре́ба да сѝђем] за музеј?
examples.en: Which stop should I get off at for the museum?
Turn left at the corner, then go straight.
Not in a hurry? Make haste slowly, there's plenty of time.

note: A proverb: rushing does not help the job.

key: phr:добар глас далеко иде, а зао још даље
cyr: добар глас далеко иде, а зао још даље.
acc: до̏бар гла̑с далѐко и̏де, а за̏о јо̏ш да̏ље̄.
meanings: A good name travels far, a bad one even farther.

examples.sr: Пази шта причаш, [до̏бар гла̑с далѐко и̏де, а за̏о јо̏ш да̏ље̄].
examples.en: Watch what you say: a good name travels far, and a bad one even farther.

examples.sr: Станите на ивицу и [у̀кључите сва̏ чѐтири].
examples.en: Pull over to the side and turn on your hazard lights.

note: Colloquial name for the hazard lights: all four turn signals.

forms: literally: I don't even have a broken para

examples.en: I don't have a penny until payday.

examples.sr: [Ка̀ква је прогно́за за су̏тра]? Хоће ли бити киша?
examples.en: What's the forecast for tomorrow? Will it rain?
It's raining outside, take an umbrella.

note: Likewise: «пада снег» (it's snowing).

examples.en: It's hot today, isn't it?

note: «зар не» is a colloquial «isn't it».

examples.en: I play sports three times a week.

note: «бавити се» takes the instrumental: бавити се музиком, фотографијом.

key: phr:он је мирођија у свакој чорби
cyr: он је мирођија у свакој чорби.
acc: о̑н је миро̀ђија у сва̀кој чо́рбӣ.
forms: literally: he is the dill in every soup
meanings: He pokes his nose into everything.

examples.sr: Он увек коментарише, [миро̀ђија у сва̀кој чо́рбӣ].
examples.en: He always has a comment, he pokes his nose into everything.

note: About a person who meddles in everything.

key: phr:нека ти нова година донесе све о чему машташ
cyr: нека ти Нова година донесе све о чему машташ.
acc: не̏ка ти Но̑ва го̏дина до̀несе све̏ о чѐму ма̏шташ.
meanings: May the New Year bring you everything you dream of.

examples.sr: [Не̏ка ти Но̑ва го̏дина до̀несе све̏ о чѐму ма̏шташ]!
examples.en: May the New Year bring you everything you dream of!

note: It usually goes on: «и нека ти се оствари све што пожелиш» - and may everything you wish come true.

examples.sr: Размисли пре одлуке: [се̏дам пу̏та ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: Think before you decide: measure twice, cut once.

key: phr:у свакој шали има пола истине
cyr: у свакој шали има пола истине.
acc: у сва̀кој ша̀ли и̏ма по́ла и̏стине.
meanings: There is some truth in every joke.

examples.sr: Смејали су се, али [у сва̀кој ша̀ли и̏ма по́ла и̏стине].
examples.en: They laughed, but there is some truth in every joke.

meanings: When choosing a wife, look at her mother.

examples.en: Grandpa says: look at the mother, choose the daughter.

note: Advice to a groom: the mother shows what the future wife will be like.

key: phr:она је метар и шумска јагода
cyr: она је метар и шумска јагода.
acc: о̀на је ме̏тар и шу̏мска ја̏года.
forms: literally: she is a meter and a wild strawberry

examples.sr: Мала је, [о̀на је ме̏тар и шу̏мска ја̏года].
examples.en: She's tiny, pint-sized.

note: A joking way to speak of a short woman.

examples.en: Say hi to Mom for me!

note: «поздравити» + acc.

meanings: the sky and the earth merged (awful weather)

examples.sr: Док смо возили, [са̀ставило се не̏бо са зѐмљо̄м].
examples.en: While we were driving, the heavens opened.
Parking is prohibited here.

note: Signs often leave out «је»: «Забрањено паркирање».

meanings: no matter what I do (it won't work)

examples.sr: Хоћу визу, али [цр̀кни, пу̏кни], не иде.
examples.en: I want a visa, but no matter what I do, it won't work.

note: Not a swear word: it expresses frustration when something won't work out.

examples.sr: Које је расе? [Мо̀гу ли да га по̀мазим]?
examples.en: What breed is he? Can I pet him?
Excuse me, does your dog bite?
- He moved to another country. - What?!

note: Also 'please', 'hello?' (answering the phone) and 'you're welcome' in reply to «хвала».

examples.en: Shall I bring you a coffee? - Yeah, right, I'm on my way!

note: A sarcastic refusal.

examples.en: Milica says hi.

meanings: How do you say it in Serbian?

examples.en: How do you say «thank you» in Serbian?
Excuse me, I'm a foreigner, please speak slowly.
What does this word mean?

examples.sr: Не осећам мирис, [но̑с ми је за̀пушен].
examples.en: I can't smell anything, my nose is blocked.

examples.sr: Не идем на посао, [ѝма̄м висо̀ку температу́ру].
examples.en: I'm not going to work, I have a high fever.
My throat hurts this morning.

note: «боли ме» + subject: боли ме глава, боле ме леђа (pl.).

examples.en: Always the same thing, I'm fed up!

meanings: I've had it up to here!

examples.en: I've had it up to here with this crowd!

note: A variant of «Пун ми је куфер»; «капа» is feminine.

examples.en: Darn it, I'm late again!

note: A mild substitute for a rude swear word.

examples.en: You have beautiful eyes and a lovely smile.
You look wonderful in that suit.

meanings: You have a good sense of humor.

examples.sr: [И̏маш до̏бар сми̑сао за ху̀мор], волим да се смејем.
examples.en: You have a good sense of humor, I love to laugh.

examples.sr: Хвала на поруци, [у̀лепшала си ми да̑н]!
examples.en: Thanks for the message, you made my day!

note: To a woman: «улепшала си ми дан».

examples.en: Neighbor, come over for coffee on Sunday!

note: A common invitation to neighbors.

key: phr:драго ми је што смо комшије
cyr: драго ми је што смо комшије!
acc: дра̑го ми је што̏ смо ко̀мшије!

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је што̏ смо ко̀мшије], зови ако треба помоћ.
examples.en: I'm glad we're neighbors, call if you need help.
Excuse me, can I help you?

meanings: Give me half a kilo of apples.

examples.sr: Молим вас, [да̑јте ми по́ла ки̏лограма ја̏бука].
examples.en: Please give me half a kilo of apples.

note: After a quantity, the genitive: пола килограма јабука.

examples.en: Thanks, I'll pay by card.
Excuse me, do you have change?
What's the shelf life of this cheese?

key: phr:да ли овај аутобус иде на аеродром
cyr: да ли овај аутобус иде на аеродром?
acc: да ли о̀ва̄ј ауто́бус и̏де на аеро̀дром?
meanings: Does this bus go to the airport?

examples.sr: [Да ли о̀ва̄ј ауто́бус и̏де на аеро̀дром]?
examples.en: Does this bus go to the airport?

meanings: Where do I need to change?

examples.en: Where do I change to get to the center?

examples.sr: Помогао си ми око селидбе, [ба̏ш си ца̏р]!
examples.en: You helped me with the move, you're the man!

note: To a woman: «Баш си царица!».

forms: literally: you're hammering like a Maxim gun at a division

examples.sr: Земља је равна? [Лу̑паш ко̏ Ма̏ксим по дивѝзији]!
examples.en: The Earth is flat? You're talking nonsense!

note: A joking reply to nonsense; «лупати» also means to talk rubbish. Maxim is a machine gun.

examples.sr: Тај кандидат ми је [ка̏о ку̏вана но̀га].
examples.en: That candidate leaves me cold.

note: About a person with no spark and no opinion.

key: phr:ко се чува, и бог га чува
cyr: ко се чува, и Бог га чува.
acc: ко̏ се чу̏ва, и Бо̑г га чу̏ва.

examples.sr: Понеси кишобран, [ко̏ се чу̏ва, и Бо̑г га чу̏ва].
examples.en: Take an umbrella, better safe than sorry.

meanings: winter is nothing to fear when there is ajvar

examples.sr: Спремио сам теглице, [не̑ма зи́ме ка̑д и̏ма ајва́ра].
examples.en: I've prepared the jars, winter is nothing to fear when there is ajvar.

note: A humorous saying: pepper preserves make for a well-fed winter. Ајвар is a roasted red pepper spread.

examples.en: Stay still, don't move, we're taking an X-ray of your tooth.

note: Often heard at the dentist.

examples.en: I'm lucky, I found parking right away.

note: «Немам среће» - I'm out of luck.

examples.en: Don't be afraid, fortune favors the brave.

key: phr:три ствари се не могу сакрити: љубав, сиромаштво и кашаљ
cyr: три ствари се не могу сакрити: љубав, сиромаштво и кашаљ.
acc: три̑ ства̑ри се не мо̀гу са̀крити: љу́бав, сирома́штво и ка̏шаљ.
meanings: Three things cannot be hidden: love, poverty and a cough.

examples.sr: Како је рекао Андрић, [три̑ ства̑ри се не мо̀гу са̀крити: љу́бав, сирома́штво и ка̏шаљ].
examples.en: As Andrić said, three things cannot be hidden: love, poverty and a cough.

note: A thought of Ivo Andrić, the Nobel Prize-winning writer.

examples.sr: Када је видео рачун, [у̀хватио се за гла̑ву].
examples.en: When he saw the bill, he clutched his head.

note: More often shows great surprise or shock, not only despair.

key: phr:волим те до месеца и назад
cyr: волим те до месеца и назад.
acc: во̏лӣм те до ме̏сеца и на̏за̄д.
meanings: I love you to the moon and back.

examples.en: I love you to the moon and back!

key: phr:срце ми куца само за тебе
cyr: срце ми куца само за тебе.
acc: ср̏це ми ку́ца са̏мо за те̏бе.
meanings: My heart beats only for you.

examples.en: My heart beats only for you.
There's a blizzard outside, stay home.
Put on your coat, it's freezing!

meanings: I wish you all the best!

examples.en: Happy birthday, I wish you all the best!

key: phr:нека ти се све жеље остваре
cyr: нека ти се све жеље остваре!
acc: не̏ка ти се све̏ же̏ље о̀стваре!
meanings: May all your wishes come true!

examples.sr: [Не̏ка ти се све̏ же̏ље о̀стваре] у новој години!
examples.en: May all your wishes come true in the new year!
The cake is good, right?
The weather is nice today, isn't it?

note: Short for «је ли да». Goes at the end of a sentence. Also «јел' да».

forms: literally: the drop that made the cup overflow

examples.sr: Његово кашњење била је [ка̑п ко̀ја̄ је прѐлила ча̏шу].
examples.en: His lateness was the last straw.

examples.sr: Та увреда је била [ка̑п ко̀ја̄ је прѐлила ча̏шу].
examples.en: That insult was the last straw.

forms: literally: an idle priest even baptizes kids

examples.sr: Целог дана преуређује полице - [до̀кон по̏п и јарѝће кр̏сти].
examples.en: He spends all day rearranging the shelves - idle hands find work.

examples.sr: Није имао посла, па је опрао и гаражу: [до̀кон по̏п и јарѝће кр̏сти].
examples.en: He had nothing to do, so he even washed the garage: idle hands find work.

note: Proverb about idleness: a bored priest even baptizes kid goats (јарић - young goat).

examples.sr: Заборавио сам хлеб! - [Не̑маш бри̏ге], већ сам купила.
examples.en: I forgot the bread! - Don't worry, I already bought some.
Don't worry, I'll sort it out.

note: A softer alternative: «не брини».

examples.sr: Шта је са пројектом? - [Све̏ је под контро́лом].
examples.en: - What's going on with the project? - Everything is under control.
Don't worry, everything is under control.

examples.sr: Чула сам да си болестан. [Оздра̀ви бр̑зо]!
examples.en: I heard you were sick. Get well soon!
Get well soon and get in touch.

note: A warm wish to friends and colleagues. A neutral, more formal option: «брз опоравак» (a speedy recovery).

examples.sr: Не журим са куповином: [два́пут ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: I'm in no hurry to buy: measure twice, cut once.

examples.sr: Пре одлуке се сети: [два́пут ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: Before you decide, remember: measure twice, cut once.

meanings: a busybody, someone who sticks their nose into everything

examples.sr: Увек се меша у све, права [миро̀ђија у сва̀кој чо́рбӣ].
examples.en: He always meddles in everything, a real busybody.
Don't be a busybody.

note: Мирођија is dill, чорба is a thick soup. Like English "a finger in every pie".

meanings: to rip people off, to charge sky-high prices

examples.sr: Нећу тамо да купујем, [де̏ру ко̏жу с ле́ђа]!
examples.en: I won't shop there, they rip you off!

examples.sr: У центру [де̏ру ко̏жу с ле́ђа] туристима.
examples.en: In the center they fleece the tourists.

note: Said of sellers who inflate prices a lot. The noun «драње» means a rip-off.

forms: literally: he pretends to be an Englishman
meanings: to play dumb, to pretend not to understand

examples.sr: Кад га питам за дуг, [пра̑вӣ се Ѐнгле̄з].
examples.en: When I ask him about the debt, he plays dumb.

examples.sr: Не [пра̑вӣ се Ѐнгле̄з], добро знаш о чему причам.
examples.en: Don't play dumb, you know very well what I'm talking about.

note: Said of someone who feigns not understanding to dodge responsibility or an awkward conversation.

forms: literally: let him rest in peace
meanings: may he rest in peace (said of the deceased)

examples.sr: Наш деда је отишао, [не̏ка по̀чива у ми̏ру].
examples.en: Our grandfather is gone, may he rest in peace.

examples.sr: [Не̏ка по̀чива у ми̏ру] и нека му је лака земља.
examples.en: May he rest in peace, and may the earth lie lightly on him.

note: A condolence phrase. Others: «моје искрено саучешће» (my sincere condolences), «саосећам са тобом» (I feel for you).

examples.sr: [Мо̀је и̏скрено са̀учешће] вама и вашој породици.
examples.en: My sincere condolences to you and your family.
I want to express my sincere condolences.

note: A fixed formula. Verb: изјавити саучешће (to offer condolences). For "I'm sorry" use «жао ми је».

forms: literally: eternal to him glory and thanks
meanings: eternal glory and thanks to him (said of the fallen)

examples.sr: Погинуо је као херој, [ве̏чна му сла̏ва и хва́ла].
examples.en: He died a hero, eternal glory and thanks to him.

examples.sr: [Ве̏чна јој сла̏ва и хва́ла]! - Слава јој!
examples.en: Eternal glory and thanks to her! - Glory to her!

note: For a woman: «вечна јој». Reply: «слава му» or «слава јој».

forms: literally: behind Mira a hundred devils peek out
meanings: a person who seems quiet and good-natured but is actually sly and treacherous

examples.sr: Изгледа мирно, али [ѝза Ми̏ре сто̑ ђа̏вола ви̏ре].
examples.en: She looks calm, but she's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

examples.sr: Не веруј јој, [ѝза Ми̏ре сто̑ ђа̏вола ви̏ре].
examples.en: Don't trust her, she's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

note: The name Мира sounds like «мир» (peace, calm), which is the joke.

forms: literally: don't mix grannies and frogs

examples.sr: Једно је посао, друго приватни живот - [не ме̑шај ба́ке и жа̏бе].
examples.en: Work is one thing, private life is another - don't mix apples and oranges.

note: A rhyming idiom: don't lump together things of a different nature.

forms: literally: for taking or for here
meanings: to go or to eat here? (asked at a bakery or café)

examples.sr: - Један бурек, молим. - [За по̀нети и̏ли за о́вде]?
examples.en: - One burek, please. - To go or to eat here?

note: A typical question at a bakery or café. Answer: «За понети» or «За овде».

examples.en: Here's your bill. Card or cash?

note: A question at the register. Short answers: «Картицом» or «Кеш».

examples.en: - Anything else? - That's all, thank you.

note: A reply to «Још нешто?» in a shop. Colloquial variant: «то је то».

examples.en: Bus rides make me nauseous.

note: «Мука ми је» also means nausea, but «мука ми је од...» also means "I'm sick of...".

forms: literally: I need something without a prescription
meanings: I need something over the counter (at a pharmacy)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [тре́ба ми не̏што без рѐцепта] за прехладу.
examples.en: Hello, I need something over the counter for a cold.

note: Greet first, then «Треба ми...» and the product or symptom: «нешто за прехладу».

forms: literally: before or after a meal

examples.sr: Овај лек пијем [пре̏ и̏ли по̏сле је̏ла]?
examples.en: Do I take this medicine before or after meals?

note: A common question to a pharmacist. Also useful: «Колико пута дневно?» (how many times a day?).

examples.en: Damn it, I'm late again!

note: One of the best-known Serbian exclamations of annoyance or surprise. It sounds like a curse but is much milder.

meanings: to look gloomy and listless, to be in low spirits

examples.sr: Данас сам [ко̏ по̀кисао ма̀гарац], ништа ми не иде.
examples.en: I'm feeling down today, nothing is going right.

note: A colloquial answer to «Како си?» when you're sad or worn out. In more bookish speech: «као» instead of «ко».

meanings: to run around like a headless chicken

examples.en: I'm running around town like a headless chicken.

note: Said of someone in a flurry who dashes about and does everything wrong.

forms: literally: come on, it will be good

examples.en: Don't worry, come on, it'll be fine!

note: A favorite calming catchphrase that shows a relaxed attitude to difficulties.

meanings: to rain down, to pour in (of things arriving in large numbers)

examples.en: Failing grades rained down.
The journalists' questions poured in.

examples.sr: После објаве позиви су [пљу̀штали ка̏о ки̏ша].
examples.en: After the announcement, calls poured in one after another.

related.en: a one, the lowest school grade

note: School grades run 1-5, and јединица is a fail. The verb agrees with the subject: јединице су пљуштале, питања су пљуштала.

key: phr:могу ли нешто да вас питам
cyr: могу ли нешто да вас питам?
acc: мо̀гу ли не̏што да вас пи̑та̄м?
forms: literally: can I ask you something

examples.sr: Извините, [мо̀гу ли не̏што да вас пи̑та̄м]?
examples.en: Excuse me, may I ask you something?

examples.sr: Добар дан, [мо̀гу ли не̏што да вас пи̑та̄м]? Који трамвај иде до Славије?
examples.en: Hello, may I ask you something? Which tram goes to Slavija?

note: A polite opener before asking a stranger a question. It uses the formal «вас».

key: phr:можете ли да ми кажете где је
cyr: можете ли да ми кажете где је ...?
acc: мо̏жете ли да ми ка̀жете где̏ је ...?
meanings: could you tell me where ... is?

examples.sr: [Мо̏жете ли да ми ка̀жете] где се овде налази благајна?
examples.en: Could you tell me where the ticket office is here?

examples.sr: Извините, [мо̏жете ли да ми ка̀жете] колико је сати?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you tell me what time it is?

note: A polite request: «можете ли» + да + present tense.

examples.sr: [Да ли зна́те мо̀жда] где могу да купим књиге на енглеском?
examples.en: Do you happen to know where I can buy books in English?

examples.sr: Извините, [да ли зна́те мо̀жда] где је најближа апотека?
examples.en: Excuse me, do you happen to know where the nearest pharmacy is?

note: «Можда» softens the question: "maybe you know?"

key: phr:не знам да ли ћу моћи
cyr: не знам да ли ћу моћи.
acc: не зна̑м да ли ћу мо̏ћи.
forms: literally: I don't know whether I will be able
meanings: I don't know if I'll be able to
I'm not sure it will work out

examples.sr: Долазиш вечерас? - [Не зна̑м да ли ћу мо̏ћи].
examples.en: - Are you coming tonight? - I don't know if I'll be able to.

examples.sr: [Не зна̑м да ли ћу мо̏ћи] да дођем на славу.
examples.en: I don't know if I'll be able to come to the slava celebration.

note: A neutral reply: it can be real doubt or a soft refusal. Intonation decides.

examples.sr: Покушаћу да дођем, али [ни̏шта не обѐћавам].
examples.en: I'll try to come, but I'm not promising anything.
I'll ask the boss, but no promises.

note: Usually means "don't count on me", without a flat no.

key: phr:јавићу ти ако се нешто промени
cyr: јавићу ти ако се нешто промени.
acc: ја̀вићу ти а̏ко се не̏што про̀мени.
forms: literally: I'll give you word if something changes
meanings: I'll let you know if anything changes

examples.sr: Сад не могу, али [ја̀вићу ти а̏ко се не̏што про̀мени].
examples.en: I can't right now, but I'll let you know if anything changes.

examples.sr: Хвала на позиву, [ја̀вићу вам а̏ко се не̏што про̀мени].
examples.en: Thank you for the invitation, I'll let you know if anything changes.

note: Most often means "not now", but leaves a small chance.

examples.sr: Све си сам завршио за сат времена? [Зма̏ј си]!
examples.en: You finished it all yourself in an hour? You're a legend!
She's an amazing woman!

note: Praise, not an insult: змај is a mythical dragon (a snake is змија). Said of someone who works hard or did brilliantly.

meanings: easy as pie, and it's done
just like that, and that's that

examples.sr: Мало соли, мало бибера, [чи̏ча-ми̏ча, го̀това при̑ча].
examples.en: A little salt, a little pepper, and presto, it's done.
You press the button and bam, it's done.

note: A rhyming catchphrase that sums up something done quickly and easily.

examples.en: The new T-shirts sold like hotcakes.

note: Of goods, tickets, treats: everything is snapped up fast. Also «ићи као халва».

forms: literally: it neither stinks nor smells
meanings: neither fish nor fowl, nothing special

examples.sr: Предлог није лош, али [ни̑т' смр̏ди, ни̑т' ми̏рише].
examples.en: The proposal isn't bad, but it's neither fish nor fowl.

note: Of a person or thing with nothing distinctive; colloq.

forms: literally: in every grain field there are weeds
meanings: there's a bad apple in every bunch

examples.sr: Не суди све по једном, [у сва̀ком жѝту и̏ма ку̀коља].
examples.en: Don't judge everyone by one person: there's a bad apple in every bunch.

note: A proverb. Кукољ is a weed in wheat.

examples.sr: - Научио сам српски за месец дана. - [Ѝди бѐгај]!
examples.en: - I learned Serbian in a month. - Yeah, right!

note: Colloq.; said when you don't believe someone.

forms: literally: to beat up like an ox in cabbage
meanings: to beat someone to a pulp

examples.sr: Ако то урадиш, [прѐбиће те ка̏о во̀ла у купу̀су].
examples.en: If you do that, they'll beat you to a pulp.

note: Colloq., rude.

examples.en: On Black Friday I'll buy a new phone.

note: Borrowed word for word from English.

examples.en: I'll get a croissant, just to tide me over.

examples.sr: Цео дан сам ишла [та̏мо-а̑мо] по граду.
examples.en: I walked around the city back and forth all day.

note: There is also the variant «тамо-вамо».

examples.en: Turn off the light before you go out.

examples.sr: [Пре̏ не̏го што̏] смо кренули, позвао сам маму.
examples.en: Before we set off, I called my mom.

note: After this conjunction the verb is in an ordinary tense, with no «да».

examples.en: Basically, everything is fine.

note: An introductory phrase, usually at the start of a sentence.

examples.sr: [У прѝнципу] могу да дођем и у суботу.
examples.en: In principle, I can come on Saturday too.

note: An introductory phrase that softens an agreement.

examples.sr: [Рѐцимо да] данас кренемо раније, шта онда?
examples.en: Let's say we leave earlier today, then what?

note: After «да» the verb is in the present tense.

examples.sr: [Да бу̏де̄м и̏скрен], нисам очекивао толико људи.
examples.en: To be honest, I didn't expect so many people.

note: A woman says «да будем искрена».

meanings: to cut a long story short

examples.sr: [Да скра̀тим при̑чу], остали смо без аута.
examples.en: Long story short, we ended up without a car.

key: phr:не знам шта да ти кажем
cyr: не знам шта да ти кажем
acc: не зна̑м шта̏ да ти ка̏жем
forms: literally: I don't know what to say to you
meanings: I don't know what to tell you

examples.sr: [Не зна̑м шта̏ да ти ка̏жем], стварно ми је жао.
examples.en: I don't know what to tell you, I'm really sorry.

note: Formal: «не знам шта да вам кажем».

forms: literally: from where do I know

examples.en: - Where's the key? - How should I know!

note: Colloq.; close to «шта ја знам» (what do I know).

forms: literally: so that we understand each other

examples.sr: [Да се разу̀мемо], ја те нисам звао.
examples.en: Let's get one thing straight: I didn't call you.

note: Put before an important clarification.

examples.en: I'm going to Spain in a week.
She was sick for a whole week.

note: Same pattern as годину дана, месец дана: used for exactly one unit, with no number.

forms: literally: this heat is killing me

examples.sr: [О̀ва̄ врућѝна ме у̀бија], идем под туш.
examples.en: This heat is killing me, I'm going to take a shower.

forms: literally: to take shelter in the shade
meanings: to get out of the sun into the shade

examples.sr: Хајде да се [скло̀нимо у хла̑д], превише пече.
examples.en: Let's get into the shade, it's too hot.
Just asking, do you have a girlfriend?

note: A girl is asked «имаш ли момка?» (do you have a boyfriend?).

key: phr:могу ли да добијем твој број телефона
cyr: могу ли да добијем твој број телефона?
acc: мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем тво̑ј бро̑ј телефо̀на?
meanings: can I have your phone number?

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем тво̑ј бро̑ј телефо̀на]?
examples.en: Can I have your phone number?

key: phr:не могу да живим без тебе
cyr: не могу да живим без тебе
acc: не мо̀гу да жи́вӣм без те̏бе

examples.sr: Волим те, [не мо̀гу да жи́вӣм без те̏бе].
examples.en: I love you, I can't live without you.

forms: literally: I dreamed you last night
meanings: I dreamed about you last night

examples.sr: [Са́њао сам те но̀ћас], био си на мору.
examples.en: I dreamed about you last night, you were at the seaside.

note: «Сањати» takes the accusative: «сањао сам те» is literally "I dreamed you".

key: phr:не могу да престанем да мислим на тебе
cyr: не могу да престанем да мислим на тебе
acc: не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да ми̏слӣм на те̏бе
meanings: I can't stop thinking about you

examples.sr: Од јуче [не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да ми̏слӣм на те̏бе].
examples.en: Since yesterday I can't stop thinking about you.

note: «Мислити на» + acc.

forms: literally: we are not one for the other
meanings: we're not right for each other

examples.sr: Схватили смо да [ни́смо је̏дно за дру̏го].
examples.en: We realized that we're not right for each other.

note: Opposite: «створени једно за друго» (made for each other).

forms: literally: I need a little space

examples.sr: Не љутим се, само [ми тре́ба ма̏ло про̀стора].
examples.en: I'm not angry, I just need some space.

note: For time: «треба ми времена» (I need time).

forms: literally: I'm not for a relationship at the moment
meanings: I'm not up for a relationship right now

examples.sr: Супер си, али [ни́сам тре̏нӯтно за ве́зӯ].
examples.en: You're great, but I'm not up for a relationship right now.

forms: literally: a relationship for one night

examples.en: I'm not looking for a one-night stand.

note: Opposite: «дугорочна веза» (a long-term relationship).

forms: literally: to make the first step

examples.sr: Чекала је да он [на̀прави пр̑ви ко̏ра̄к].
examples.en: She waited for him to make the first move.

forms: literally: that sets me on fire

examples.en: I'm really into this music.

note: Negative: «то ме не пали» (it does nothing for me).

examples.sr: Дете је прехлађено и стално [ду̀ва но̑с].
examples.en: The child has a cold and keeps blowing his nose.

examples.sr: Шта радиш вечерас? - [Ни̏шта спе̑ц], гледам филм.
examples.en: - What are you doing tonight? - Nothing special, watching a movie.

examples.sr: Како је било на предавању? - [Ни̏шта спе̑ц].
examples.en: - How was the lecture? - Nothing special.

note: A colloquial shortening of «ништа специјално». It can also answer a question about quality: so-so.

examples.en: It's late, I'm off home.
See you tomorrow, I'm off!

note: A colloquial form of «отићи», used when leaving a group. Usually with «ја»: одох ја.

forms: literally: how does it go for you
meanings: how are you getting on with ...?

examples.en: How's the new job going?
How's your Serbian coming along?

note: Asks about progress in something specific. Answer: «иде некако» (it's going okay).

forms: literally: it doesn't go like that

examples.sr: [Не и̏де то̑ та̀ко̄], морамо да се договоримо.
examples.en: That won't do, we have to come to an agreement.

examples.sr: Хоћеш да ме оставиш без ручка? [Не и̏де то̑ та̀ко̄]!
examples.en: You want to leave me without lunch? That's not how it works!

note: A mild objection, not a harsh one.

examples.sr: Не заборави да [у̀гасиш све̏тло] када излазиш.
examples.en: Don't forget to turn off the light when you leave.

examples.sr: [У̀гаси све̏тло], молим те, идемо на спавање.
examples.en: Turn off the light, please, we're going to sleep.

note: Opposite: «упалити светло» (turn on the light).

examples.en: I change the bedding on Sundays.
Guests are coming, I have to change the bedding.

note: Impf. «мењати постељину» (change it regularly), pf. «променити» (change it once).

forms: literally: to be left without text

examples.sr: Кад сам видела поклон, [о̀стала сам без те̏кста].
examples.en: When I saw the gift, I was speechless.

examples.sr: Он је [о̀стао без те̏кста] на испиту.
examples.en: He was lost for words at the exam.

note: A colloquial variant: «остати без речи»: you don't know what to say.

forms: literally: if only the neighbor's cow would drop dead
meanings: as long as the neighbor does worse

examples.sr: Код нас важи [са̏мо да ко̀мшији цр̀кне кра̏ва].
examples.en: Around here the rule is: all that matters is that the neighbor does worse.

examples.sr: Не буди од оних што мисле [са̏мо да ко̀мшији цр̀кне кра̏ва].
examples.en: Don't be one of those who only care that the neighbor does worse.

note: A formula of envy: what matters is that the neighbor fares worse, not that you do well. Said with bitter irony.

key: phr:не бира се кућа него комшија
cyr: не бира се кућа него комшија
acc: не бѝра се ку̏ћа не̏го ко̀мшија
forms: literally: you don't choose the house but the neighbor
meanings: you choose the neighbors, not the house

examples.sr: Стан је леп, али [не бѝра се ку̏ћа не̏го ко̀мшија].
examples.en: The apartment is nice, but you choose the neighbors, not the house.

examples.sr: Пре куповине упознај суседе: [не бѝра се ку̏ћа не̏го ко̀мшија].
examples.en: Meet the neighbors before you buy: you choose the neighbors, not the house.

note: Good neighbors matter more than the home itself.

key: phr:боље добар комшија него далека родбина
cyr: боље добар комшија него далека родбина
acc: бо̏ље̄ до̏бар ко̀мшија не̏го далѐка ро̏дбина
forms: literally: better a good neighbor than distant kin
meanings: a good neighbor is better than distant relatives

examples.sr: Кад сам се разболео, прва је дошла комшиница: [бо̏ље̄ до̏бар ко̀мшија не̏го далѐка ро̏дбина].
examples.en: When I got sick, the neighbor came first: a good neighbor is better than a distant relative.

examples.sr: Рођаци су далеко, а комшије близу, [бо̏ље̄ до̏бар ко̀мшија не̏го далѐка ро̏дбина].
examples.en: My relatives are far away and my neighbors are near: a good neighbor is better than distant relatives.

note: A neighbor will come to help sooner than a relative.

forms: literally: an evil neighbor is worse than a snake
meanings: a bad neighbor is worse than a snake

examples.sr: Годинама се свађам са суседом: [зла̏ ко̀мшија го̏ра од зми̏је].
examples.en: I've been feuding with my neighbor for years: a bad neighbor is worse than a snake.

examples.sr: Са таквим суседом знаш да је [зла̏ ко̀мшија го̏ра од зми̏је].
examples.en: With a neighbor like that you see that a bad neighbor is worse than a snake.

note: A proverb about feuds between neighbors.

examples.sr: Код нас у улици [комшѝлук је по́ла фамѝлије].
examples.en: On our street, neighbors are half the family.

examples.sr: Увек помогнемо једни другима, [комшѝлук је по́ла фамѝлије].
examples.en: We always help each other, neighbors are half the family.

note: Praises close, friendly neighbors who are like relatives.

examples.sr: Вечерас правим [кро̀мпӣр у га̏ћама] у рерни.
examples.en: Tonight I'm making baked potatoes in their skins in the oven.

examples.sr: Мало соли, мало уља и [кро̀мпӣр у га̏ћама] је готов.
examples.en: A little salt, a little oil, and the baked potatoes are ready.

note: A playful name for potatoes baked in their skins, usually halved, with oil and salt.

examples.sr: Хоћеш ли стићи до осам? - [Те̑шко, бо̏гами].
examples.en: - Will you make it by eight? - Hardly, to be honest.
- Will he agree? - Hardly.

note: A politely evasive refusal. Close in meaning: «ваљда не», «вероватно не» (probably not).

examples.sr: Ти ћеш да поправиш ауто? [Ма̏ да, на́равно]!
examples.en: You're going to fix the car? Yeah, sure!

examples.sr: Рекао је да ће платити? [Ма̏ да, на́равно].
examples.en: He said he'd pay? Yeah, right.

note: Without irony «наравно» simply means "of course". Here the tone and «ма да» show doubt.

meanings: a long weekend (extended to Thursday or Friday)

examples.sr: Отишли смо на [про̀дужени вѝкенд] у Будимпешту.
examples.en: We went to Budapest for a long weekend.
Because of the holiday we have a long weekend.

note: Used when a trip covers not only Saturday and Sunday but also Friday or even Thursday.

meanings: the cream of the crop, the elite

examples.sr: На пријему се окупио [кре̑м де̏ ла̑ кре̑м] града.
examples.en: The city's elite gathered at the reception.

examples.sr: Они мисле да су [кре̑м де̏ ла̑ кре̑м] друштва.
examples.en: They think they're the cream of society.

note: From French.

examples.sr: [Ба̏ш си по̀ранила] данас, тек је шест сати.
examples.en: You're up really early today, it's only six o'clock.
- You're here already? - Yes, I came early.

note: To a man: «баш си поранио». Short form: «поранила си!». A comment that someone got up or set out unusually early.

examples.sr: Банка ми је дала потврду о [га̀шењу рачу́на].
examples.en: The bank gave me a certificate of account closure.
I'm requesting account closure because of a move.

note: Official wording in documents. In everyday speech also «затварање рачуна». Гасити is to put out, to switch off.

examples.sr: - Узела сам ти џемпер без питања. - [Не̏ка си], не смета.
examples.en: - I took your sweater without asking. - It's fine, it doesn't bother me.

examples.sr: - Узео сам и твоју оловку. - [Не̏ка си].
examples.en: - I took your pen too. - Help yourself.

note: A reply when someone did or took something without asking and you don't mind.

examples.en: - I'll beat you tomorrow. - Yeah, yeah!

examples.sr: [Не̏ка, не̏ка], оставите дете да се игра.
examples.en: Let it be, let it be, let the child play.

note: Jokingly or as a threat: "yeah, yeah, I'll remember that". Also generous: «нека», let it be, no harm done.

forms: literally: I have something to ask you
meanings: I need to ask you something

examples.en: Excuse me, I need to ask you something.

examples.sr: [И̏ма не̏што да ми ка̏же], али се стиди.
examples.en: He has something to tell me, but he's shy.

note: «Имати» + да + present expresses a wish or intention to say or do something. Not obligation: «има да идеш» means "you have to go".

meanings: I'll get in touch (call or write)

examples.en: I'm in a hurry now, I'll get in touch this evening.
When I get home, I'll let you know.

note: A typical way to end a conversation. Similar: «чујемо се» (we'll talk), «зовем те» (I'll call you), «на вези смо» (we're in touch).

meanings: I'll call you (present instead of future)

examples.sr: Сад не могу да причам, [зо̀вем те] касније.
examples.en: I can't talk now, I'll call you later.
Thanks, I'll call you tomorrow.

note: A phone goodbye. The request the other way: «Назови ме» or «Јави ми се» (call me, get in touch).

key: phr:назови ме кад будеш имао прилику
cyr: назови ме кад будеш имао прилику
acc: на̀зови ме ка̑д бу̏де̄ш и̏мао прѝлику
forms: literally: call me when you have an opportunity
meanings: call me when you get a chance

examples.sr: Нисам стигао да те чујем. [На̀зови ме ка̑д бу̏де̄ш и̏мао прѝлику].
examples.en: I didn't get a chance to talk to you. Call me when you can.

examples.sr: Ако ти је згодно, [на̀зови ме ка̑д бу̏де̄ш и̏мала врѐмена].
examples.en: If it suits you, call me when you have time.

note: It sounds gentle, but the listener will understand that it matters to you that he calls back.

examples.sr: Зовем је већ сат времена, [ни̏ко се не ја̏вља].
examples.en: I've been calling her for an hour, nobody answers.

examples.sr: Звао сам кући, али [ни̏ко се нѝје ја̏вио].
examples.en: I called home, but nobody answered.

note: «Јавити се» is to answer a call and make contact. To call is «звати».

forms: literally: much has stood for me
meanings: it matters a lot to me
I care a lot about it

examples.sr: [Мно̏го ми је ста̏ло] до овог пројекта.
examples.en: This project matters a lot to me.

examples.sr: Знам да [му је мно̏го ста̏ло] до породице.
examples.en: I know his family means a lot to him.

note: The construction is «стало ми је до» + gen.: до тебе, до посла, до тога.

examples.en: Excuse me, my husband doesn't speak Russian.

examples.sr: Моја свекрва [не при̑ча ру̏ски], али понешто разуме.
examples.en: My mother-in-law doesn't speak Russian, but she understands a few things.

note: In colloquial speech «причати» simply means "to speak". More neutral: «не говори руски».

examples.en: I don't feel well, I'm going home.

examples.sr: Од јутрос [ни́сам до̀бро], мислим да имам температуру.
examples.en: Since this morning I haven't felt well, I think I have a fever.

note: Also «није ми добро» and «не осећам се добро».

examples.sr: Нисам хтела да закасним, [та̀ко̄ је ѝспало].
examples.en: I didn't want to be late, that's how it turned out.
It wasn't planned, it just turned out that way.

note: A short excuse. «Испасти» also means "to fall out" and "to turn out".

forms: literally: it interests me a lot

examples.en: I'm very interested in your job.

examples.sr: [Ја̑ко ме за̀нима] како си то урадио.
examples.en: I'm very curious how you did that.

note: The person who is interested is in the accusative: ме, те, га, је.

meanings: to cancel an appointment (with a doctor, a stylist)

examples.en: I have to cancel my dentist appointment.
Cancel the appointment, we won't make it.

note: «Термин» is an appointed time. To book: «заказати термин», to reschedule: «померити термин».

meanings: come on in, join us (no ceremony)

examples.en: We're in the garden, come on in!
The door is open, come on in.

note: A casual invitation to simply join the group.

examples.en: Enough already, stop shouting!
Enough of this talk already!

note: «Више» here adds irritation and means "already": likewise «умукни више» (shut up already), «ајде више».

examples.en: Come on already, we'll be late!
Come on, say already what you want.

note: An impatient "come on already". Without «више», «ајде» is a plain "come on".

examples.sr: Уговор не важи у случају [ви̏ше сѝле].
examples.en: The contract does not apply in case of force majeure.
The delay was caused by force majeure.

note: A legal term found in contracts and insurance terms.

examples.en: Drink as much water as possible.
Try to learn as many words as possible.

note: «Што» + comparative gives "as ... as possible": што пре (as soon as possible), што боље (as well as possible).

examples.en: I feel awkward that I'm late.

examples.sr: [О̀сећам се не̏прија̄тно] када ме сви гледају.
examples.en: I feel awkward when everyone looks at me.

note: «Непријатно» is for social awkwardness. Physical discomfort is «неудобно».

examples.en: There's no more bread, it's all sold out.
There are no more tickets for the concert.

note: Also: «ништа више» (nothing more), «никад више» (never again).

examples.en: - Anything else? - Nothing else, thanks.
I didn't want to say anything more.

note: Often heard as a customer's answer to «Још нешто?».

examples.en: I'll never go there again.

examples.sr: Обећај да то [ни̏кад ви̏ше] нећеш урадити.
examples.en: Promise you'll never do that again.

note: Double negation: никад + нећу, никад + нећеш.

examples.en: So, where were we?
I don't remember where we left off.

note: Asked about a conversation or about a route. «Стати» means to stop.

examples.en: Please, help me with the bag.
Help me, I lost my passport!

note: A loud cry for help: «У помоћ!». Informal: «помози ми».

examples.en: I can't wait, it's urgent.
Call him right away, it's urgent.

note: Useful in an emergency: «Хитно је!» makes the other person react.

examples.sr: Данас је [ле̑по вре́ме], идемо у парк.
examples.en: The weather is nice today, we're going to the park.
The weather will be nice tomorrow.

note: Weather is praised with «лепо», not «добро»: лепо време, ружно време (bad weather).

examples.en: Which way is the main square?

examples.sr: [У ко̑м пра́вцу] треба ићи до станице?
examples.en: Which way do I go to get to the station?

note: The case after «у» is the locative: у ком правцу, у правцу центра.

examples.en: Wait, I took a wrong turn.

examples.sr: [По̀грешно сам скре́нула] и сад сам изгубљена.
examples.en: I took a wrong turn and now I'm lost.

note: A woman says «скренула». To clarify directions: «Где је лево?» (where is left?), «Иди право» (go straight).

forms: literally: I'm calling in connection with

examples.sr: [Зо̀вем у ве́зи са] огласом за стан.
examples.en: I'm calling about the apartment ad.

examples.sr: [Зо̀вем у ве́зи са] послом који сте објавили.
examples.en: I'm calling about the job you posted.

note: It is usual to state the reason for the call right away. Variant: «јављам се у вези са...».

examples.sr: Имала сам [про̀пуштен по́зив] с овог броја.
examples.en: I had a missed call from this number.
I see a missed call from you.

note: A way to open the conversation when you call back an unknown number.

meanings: this is ... speaking (a way to introduce yourself on the phone)

examples.en: Hello, this is Marija.

examples.sr: Станко [је на телефо̀ну], потребан ми је термин.
examples.en: This is Stanko, I need an appointment.

note: A Serb names himself in the third person. Then comes the request: «Могу ли да добијем...?»

meanings: may I speak to ...? (on the phone)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем] Стефана?
examples.en: Hello, may I speak to Stefan?
May I speak to Mr. Petrović?

note: Answer: «Можете, наравно. Само тренутак» (Of course. Just a moment).

forms: literally: a package has arrived to you
meanings: a package has arrived for you

examples.en: A package has arrived for you, sign here.

examples.sr: Курир каже да [вам је сти̏гао па̀ке̄т].
examples.en: The courier says a package has arrived for you.

note: The verb agrees with «пакет» (masc.). Another word for a parcel: «пошиљка».

examples.en: Let's take a taxi, we're running late.
It's raining, let's take a taxi.

note: «Узети» is to take, «наручити» to order: желим да наручим такси (I want to order a taxi).

forms: literally: which sport do you occupy yourself with

examples.en: What sport do you do?
And you, what sport do you do?

note: «Бавити се» + instr.: бавим се спортом, бавим се музиком (I do sports, I'm into music).

examples.en: We need a table for two.

examples.sr: Имате ли [сто̑ за дво̏је] у осам?
examples.en: Do you have a table for two at eight?

note: «За двоје» is for a mixed pair, «за двојицу» for two men.

examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?

examples.sr: [Да ли је о́вде сло̏бодно]? Могу ли да седнем?
examples.en: Is this seat free? May I sit down?

note: A polite question about a seat at a table or on transport.

examples.sr: Касним јер [ми се гу̏ма про̀бушила] на аутопуту.
examples.en: I'm late because I got a flat tire on the highway.

note: «Гума» is a tire, «точак» the whole wheel; «пробушити» is to puncture.

examples.sr: Извините, [где̏ мо̀гу да на̀ђем] кесе за смеће?
examples.en: Excuse me, where can I find trash bags?

examples.sr: Реците ми, [где̏ мо̀гу да на̀ђем] млеко?
examples.en: Tell me, where can I find the milk?

note: A shop assistant's answer: «Налази се у пролазу 3, са леве стране» (It's in aisle 3, on the left).

meanings: how much would you like? (a shop assistant's question)

examples.en: How much would you like? - Three hundred grams, please.

note: «Измерити» is to weigh out goods in a shop.

examples.en: Give me a kilo of apples. - Anything else?

note: The standard question from a shop assistant at the register.

examples.en: Are you paying cash? Do you need a receipt?

note: «Рачун» means both a bill and a receipt.

examples.sr: [Жѐлим да вра̀тим] ове ципеле, мале су ми.
examples.en: I want to return these shoes, they're too small.

examples.sr: [Жѐлим да вра̀тим] блузу и добијем новац назад.
examples.en: I want to return the blouse and get my money back.

note: «Вратити» is to return goods or money.

meanings: I'd like to book a room

examples.sr: [Жѐлео бих да резѐрвишем со̏бу] за две особе на пет ноћи.
examples.en: I'd like to book a room for two people for five nights.

examples.sr: [Жѐлела бих да резѐрвишем со̏бу] са погледом на море.
examples.en: I'd like to book a room with a sea view.

note: A woman says «желела бих».

key: phr:да ли су дозвољени кућни љубимци
cyr: да ли су дозвољени кућни љубимци
acc: да ли су дозво̀љени ку̏ћнӣ љу̏бимци

examples.sr: [Да ли су дозво̀љени ку̏ћнӣ љу̏бимци] у вашем хотелу?
examples.en: Are pets allowed in your hotel?

note: A shorter way: «Могу ли да дођем са псом?» (can I come with a dog?).

key: phr:до када морамо да напустимо собу
cyr: до када морамо да напустимо собу
acc: до ка̀да мо̑ра̄мо да на̀пустимо со̏бу
meanings: what time do we have to check out of the room?

examples.sr: Извините, [до ка̀да мо̑ра̄мо да на̀пустимо со̏бу]?
examples.en: Excuse me, what time do we have to vacate the room?

key: phr:да ли треба да уплатим аванс
cyr: да ли треба да уплатим аванс
acc: да ли тре́ба да у̀платим а̀ванс
meanings: do I need to pay a deposit?

examples.sr: [Да ли тре́ба да у̀платим а̀ванс] за резервацију?
examples.en: Do I need to pay a deposit for the reservation?

note: «Аванс» is an advance payment; «уплатити» is to pay money in.

key: phr:желим да уплатим новац на свој рачун
cyr: желим да уплатим новац на свој рачун
acc: жѐлим да у̀платим но̀вац на сво̑ј ра̀чӯн
meanings: I want to deposit money into my account

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлим да у̀платим но̀вац на сво̑ј ра̀чӯн].
examples.en: Hello, I want to deposit money into my account.

note: «Уплатити» is to pay in, «исплатити» to pay out.

key: phr:желим фризуру као на овој слици
cyr: желим фризуру као на овој слици
acc: жѐлим фризу́ру ка̏о на о̀вој сли̏ци
meanings: I want a haircut like in this picture

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлим фризу́ру ка̏о на о̀вој сли̏ци].
examples.en: Hello, I want a haircut like in this picture.

note: «Слика» is a picture: it can be a painting or a photo.

key: phr:желео бих да те позовем на вечеру
cyr: желео бих да те позовем на вечеру
acc: жѐлео бих да те по̀зовем на вѐчеру
meanings: I'd like to invite you to dinner

examples.sr: [Жѐлео бих да те по̀зовем на вѐчеру] у петак.
examples.en: I'd like to invite you to dinner on Friday.

note: A woman says «желела бих».

meanings: let's take a walk in the park

examples.en: Let's take a walk in the park after work!

note: A route takes the instrumental with no preposition: шетати парком, ићи улицом.

key: phr:надам се да ће ти се свидети
cyr: надам се да ће ти се свидети
acc: на̏дам се да ће ти се сви̏дети

examples.sr: Ово је за тебе, [на̏дам се да ће ти се сви̏дети]!
examples.en: This is for you, I hope you'll like it!

note: Said when handing over a gift.

key: phr:ово је управо оно што сам желела
cyr: ово је управо оно што сам желела
acc: о̀во̄ је у̏право о̀но што̏ сам жѐлела
meanings: this is exactly what I wanted

examples.sr: Вау, [о̀во̄ је у̏право о̀но што̏ сам жѐлела]!
examples.en: Wow, this is exactly what I wanted!

note: A man says «желео».

key: phr:ова књига ме је расплакала и насмејала
cyr: ова књига ме је расплакала и насмејала
acc: о̀ва̄ књи̏га ме је ра̀сплакала и на̀смејала
meanings: this book made me cry and laugh

examples.sr: [О̀ва̄ књи̏га ме је ра̀сплакала и на̀смејала].
examples.en: This book made me cry and laugh.

note: The participle agrees with the subject: књига - расплакала; роман - расплакао.

examples.en: I highly recommend this movie.

note: «Топло» is literally "warmly", here meaning "wholeheartedly".

examples.sr: [Ра́дња се о̀двија] у Русији деветнаестог века.
examples.en: The story is set in nineteenth-century Russia.

note: «Радња» is the plot or action of a story; it also means a small shop.

meanings: to share the internet (from a phone)

examples.sr: Можеш ли, молим те, [да по̀делиш и̏нтернет] са телефона?
examples.en: Can you please share the internet from your phone?

note: «Поделити» means both "to divide" and "to share out".

examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?

note: «Сметати» means to disturb: literally "does it bother you?"

examples.en: Take a picture of me in front of the monument, please.

note: «Сликати» means both to paint and to take photos.

examples.sr: Реци ми, молим те, [ши̏фру од ва̀јфаја].
examples.en: Tell me the Wi-Fi password, please.

note: «Шифра» is a password, and so is «лозинка». It is also written «Wi-Fi» in Latin letters.

examples.sr: [Не разу̀мем зада́так]. Можете ли да га објасните?
examples.en: I don't understand the assignment. Can you explain it?
I didn't hear, please repeat that.

note: Informal: «молим те, понови».

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the post office?

note: «Налазити се» means to be located.

examples.en: On the right here, please.

note: Said to a taxi driver. Left is «лево».

examples.sr: [По̀зовите, мо̏лӣм вас, та̀кси] за сутра у седам.
examples.en: Please call a taxi for tomorrow at seven.
Happy Valentine's Day, my love!

note: February 14.

key: phr:желимо вам пуно здравља, среће и весеља
cyr: желимо вам пуно здравља, среће и весеља
acc: жѐлимо вам пу̏но здра̏вља, сре̏ће и вѐсеља
meanings: we wish you lots of health, happiness and joy

examples.sr: [Жѐлимо вам пу̏но здра̏вља, сре̏ће и вѐсеља] у новој години!
examples.en: We wish you lots of health, happiness and joy in the new year!

note: A greeting for New Year and Christmas.

meanings: a sound mind in a sound body

examples.sr: Зато трчим сваког јутра: [здра̏в ду̏х у здра̀вом тѐлу].
examples.en: That's why I run every morning: a sound mind in a sound body.

note: A proverb.

key: phr:боље слеп очима него слеп памећу
cyr: боље слеп очима него слеп памећу
acc: бо̏ље̄ сле̑п о̀чима не̏го сле̑п па̏ме̄ћу
meanings: better blind in the eyes than blind in the mind

examples.sr: Учи, јер [бо̏ље̄ сле̑п о̀чима не̏го сле̑п па̏ме̄ћу].
examples.en: Study, because it's better to be blind in the eyes than blind in the mind.

note: A proverb about the value of knowledge.

key: phr:у срећу се узда луд, а паметан у свој труд
cyr: у срећу се узда луд, а паметан у свој труд
acc: у сре̏ћу се у̀зда лу̑д, а па̏метан у сво̑ј тру̑д
meanings: the fool relies on luck, the wise on his own effort

examples.sr: Не чекај срећу: [у сре̏ћу се у̀зда лу̑д, а па̏метан у сво̑ј тру̑д].
examples.en: Don't wait for luck: the fool relies on luck, the wise on his own effort.

note: A proverb. «Уздати се» is to rely on, to trust.

key: phr:благо ономе ко зна да не зна, а хоће да зна
cyr: благо ономе ко зна да не зна, а хоће да зна
acc: бла̑го о̀но̄ме ко̏ зна̑ да не зна̑, а хо̀ће да зна̑
meanings: blessed is he who knows that he doesn't know and wants to know

examples.sr: [Бла̑го о̀но̄ме ко̏ зна̑ да не зна̑, а хо̀ће да зна̑]: он ће научити.
examples.en: Blessed is he who knows that he doesn't know and wants to know: he will learn.

note: A proverb. «Благо» here means "happy, blessed".

meanings: a book is useless where there is no sense

examples.sr: Знање се не добија само читањем: [за̏луд књи̏га где̏ па̏мети не̑ма].
examples.en: Knowledge doesn't come from reading alone: a book is useless where there is no sense.

note: A proverb. «Залуд» means "in vain".

forms: literally: spends like a Russian vehicle

examples.en: My other half spends money like water.

note: A joking comparison. Colloquially «као» becomes «ко».

forms: literally: to carry oneself with stress

examples.sr: Како се [но̏сӣш] са стресом на послу?
examples.en: How do you cope with stress at work?

examples.sr: Научила је да се [но̏си] са притиском.
examples.en: She learned to cope with pressure.

note: «Носити се са» + instr. means to cope with (a difficulty, a loss). «Како се носиш?» asks how someone is getting through a hard time.

examples.en: It's okay to seek help.
There's no shame in seeking help from a professional.

note: A fixed collocation: «потражити помоћ код некога» (to turn to someone for help). The perfective suits a decision already made.

examples.en: The greenhouse effect is warming the planet.
Carbon dioxide strengthens the greenhouse effect.

note: A greenhouse is a «стаклена башта» (literally "glass garden"), hence the name. A plastic-sheet greenhouse is a «пластеник».

examples.sr: На зиду виси [мр̏тва при́рода] са воћем.
examples.en: A still life with fruit hangs on the wall.
He painted only still lifes.

note: A calque of French «nature morte».

examples.sr: Жене су после рата добиле [пра́во гла̀са].
examples.en: Women got the right to vote after the war.
Minors have no right to vote.

note: «Гласати» is to vote, «глас» is both a voice and a vote. Elections: «избори».

examples.en: Come on, our team! We believe in you!
The whole stand shouted: Go, our team!

note: A fans' cheer. Nearby: «Навијамо за наш тим!» (We're rooting for our team!).

meanings: to keep passing by (of something long awaited)

examples.sr: Помоћ нам иде [ка̏о ки̏ша о̏ко Кра̀гујевца].
examples.en: Help keeps passing us by, like rain around Kragujevac.

examples.sr: Плата ми стиже [ка̏о ки̏ша о̏ко Кра̀гујевца].
examples.en: My pay arrives like rain around Kragujevac: it never reaches me.

note: By the saying, rain supposedly always bypassed Kragujevac: clouds but no rain. A joke about what is promised but never arrives.

examples.en: We saw a shark in the sea.
A shark rarely attacks.

note: A synonym of «ајкула». «Морски пас» is heard more in Croatia, but it is also understood in Serbia and Montenegro.

examples.sr: Кад чујем ту песму, [ду́ша ме бо̀ли].
examples.en: When I hear that song, my heart aches.
I ache inside because of him.

note: Built like «боли ме»: боли ме глава, боли ме грло (my head hurts, my throat hurts). With «душа» it is about feelings, not the body.

examples.sr: Кад видим те очи, [ср̏це ми се цѐпа].
examples.en: When I see those eyes, my heart breaks.
My heart is breaking with pity.

note: Of very strong pity or pain. Also: «срце ми је стало» (my heart stopped, from fright).

forms: literally: a room with a view of the sea
meanings: a room with a sea view

examples.sr: Треба ми [со̀ба са по̏гле̄дом на мо̑ре].
examples.en: I need a room with a sea view.

examples.sr: Да ли имате [со̏бу са по̏гле̄дом на рѐку]?
examples.en: Do you have a room with a river view?

note: Also: са погледом на парк. Same pattern for beds: соба са брачним креветом (a room with a double bed).

forms: literally: like a chicken without a head
meanings: to run around in a flap

examples.sr: Цео дан трчим [ка̏о ко̀кошка без гла́ве].
examples.en: I've been running around all day like a headless chicken.

examples.sr: Не трчи [ка̏о ко̀кошка без гла́ве], смири се.
examples.en: Don't run around like a headless chicken, calm down.

forms: literally: to fall from a pear tree

examples.sr: Зар си [па̏о с кру̏шке]? Сви то знају.
examples.en: Were you born yesterday? Everybody knows that.

examples.sr: Не прави се да си [па̏о с кру̏шке].
examples.en: Don't pretend you were born yesterday.

note: Also said of a naive person who is easy to fool.

forms: literally: to drop in for someone
meanings: to swing by to pick someone up

examples.en: I'll swing by to pick you up at seven.

examples.sr: Хоћеш ли [свра́тити по ње̏га] после посла?
examples.en: Will you pick him up after work?

note: «Свратити» is to drop in on the way. «По» + acc. is to fetch a person or thing; «до» + gen. is to visit: «свратићу до тебе».
