note: From Italian via slang; the verb «капирати» - to get, to understand. Informal only, with equals.

meanings: like, sort of; in the style of

examples.sr: Рекао је нешто [у фа̀зону] „ма, није то ништа”.
examples.en: He said something like "oh, it's nothing".
He dressed eighties-style.

note: Colloquial. «Фазон» is a manner or style, and also a joke or gag.

forms: literally: let me tell you honestly

examples.sr: [Да ти ка̏жем и̏скрено], не свиђа ми се тај план.
examples.en: To be honest, I don't like that plan.

examples.sr: [Да ти ка̏жем и̏скрено], нисам очекивао толико људи.
examples.en: Frankly, I didn't expect so many people.

note: An intro to an honest opinion, between people on «ти» terms. Polite form: «Да вам кажем искрено».

forms: literally: well I think, you know
meanings: I mean, like, you know (filler words)

examples.sr: [Па ми̏слӣм, зна̑ш], није то баш лако.
examples.en: I mean, you know, it's not exactly easy.

examples.sr: Ја, [па ми̏слӣм, зна̑ш], не знам шта да кажем.
examples.en: I, like, don't know what to say.

note: A pause filler while you look for words. Not needed in writing.

examples.en: The child's nose is running, give him a tissue.
My nose has been running since this morning.

note: «цурити» - to trickle in a thin stream; also said of a leaking tap: «Цури славина».

meanings: tooth fairy (takes away a fallen baby tooth)

examples.sr: Остави зуб под јастук, доћи ће [зу̀бић ви̏ла].
examples.en: Put the tooth under your pillow, the tooth fairy will come.

note: «Зубић» is a diminutive of «зуб»; «вила» is a fairy or woodland nymph from folk tales.

forms: literally: to puff out the lips
meanings: to purse one's lips (duck face); to pout

examples.en: She purses her lips in every photo.
The child started to pout.

note: The verb «пућити»: пућим, пућиш, пући; perfective «напућити». Also said of sulking.

forms: literally: I did not hear well

examples.sr: Извините, [ни́сам до̀бро чу̏о], можете ли поновити?
examples.en: Excuse me, I didn't catch that, could you repeat it?
I didn't catch your name.

note: A polite request to repeat. You can add «Молим?» or «Како, молим?».

forms: literally: the roller shutter falls on me
meanings: to lose it, to snap from anger

examples.sr: Кад чујем ту причу, [па̑дне ми ролѐтна].
examples.en: When I hear that story, I just snap with anger.

examples.sr: Само да ми не [па̑дне ролѐтна] пред шефом.
examples.en: I just hope I don't lose it in front of the boss.

note: A colloquial image: as if a shutter comes down inside and reason switches off.

examples.en: The kids ask for cotton candy at the fair.
I bought my daughter pink cotton candy.

note: «Вуна» is wool: the candy looks like a ball of wool.

examples.en: The child caught measles.
There is a vaccine against measles.

note: «Богиње» - pox, «мале богиње» - measles, «овчије богиње» - chickenpox. The singular «богиња» is a goddess.

meanings: that's how things stand, that's the situation

examples.sr: Не волим то да кажем, али [та̀ко̄ сто̀је̄ ства̑ри].
examples.en: I don't like to say it, but that's how things stand.
The project is late, that's how things are.

note: Sums up a conversation.

forms: literally: every day is a holiday

examples.sr: Кад си међу пријатељима, [сва̏кӣ да̑н је пра̑знӣк].
examples.en: When you're among friends, every day is a holiday.

examples.sr: Мом деди је [сва̏кӣ да̑н пра̑знӣк] у башти.
examples.en: For my grandpa every day in the garden is a holiday.

note: A slogan-wish: treat ordinary days as a reason to be glad.

examples.en: We spent the summer on the Côte d'Azur.
The Côte d'Azur is expensive for us.

note: The name of a region in France, written «Азурна обала» with capitals. «Азурни» means azure, sky blue.

meanings: God help me! (when everything is falling apart or you have no strength)

examples.en: The flight is canceled again, God help me!

examples.sr: Погледај колики је ово хаос, [помо̀зи, Бо̏же]!
examples.en: Look what a mess this is, good Lord!

note: A half-joking exclamation of tiredness or bewilderment, not necessarily religious.

forms: literally: let a message go to me
meanings: leave me a message, text me

examples.en: I can't talk now, text me.
If you get there earlier, drop me a message.

note: A message is «пустити» (let go), as if sent on its way; also «оставити поруку».

meanings: you're a sweetheart, you're a gem (affectionate, thankful)

examples.en: Thanks for coming, you're a sweetheart!
You brought me coffee, you're a darling!

note: Colloquial praise to a close person; said to a woman or a man.

forms: literally: I hold figs for you
meanings: I'm keeping my fingers crossed for you

examples.sr: Сутра ти је испит, [др̀жӣм ти фи̏ге]!
examples.en: You have an exam tomorrow, fingers crossed for you!
We're keeping our fingers crossed for you at the interview.

note: Serbs hold «фиге» (a fist with the thumb between two fingers) rather than crossing their fingers.

meanings: let life go on, life goes on

examples.sr: Било је тешко, али [не̏к и̏де жѝвот]!
examples.en: It was hard, but life goes on!
Don't worry, life goes on!

note: A cheerful motto of staying calm about trouble; «нек» is colloquial for «нека».

examples.en: Surely it's not going to rain again!

examples.sr: Он [нѐће ва̀љда] да дође без позива?
examples.en: Surely he won't come without an invitation?

note: «Ва̀љда» means "probably, I suppose". With a negation it voices surprise and the hope that it is not so. Likewise «Ниси ваљда!» - you didn't, did you?

meanings: no way, not by any means

examples.sr: Да ли ћеш му позајмити новац? — [Ни слу̏ча̄јно]!
examples.en: Will you lend him money? - No way!

examples.sr: Таква грешка [ни слу̏ча̄јно] не сме да се понови.
examples.en: Such a mistake must under no circumstances happen again.

note: A sharp refusal; the gesture is crossed arms.

meanings: I'll go crazy (from noise, tiredness, anger)

examples.en: This crowd is unbearable, I'll go crazy!
If this goes on for another hour, I'll go nuts.

note: Future of «полудети». Not strong: also said of minor annoyances.

examples.en: It's already eight, you're late!
You're late for work again.

note: «Касни(ти)» - to be late or slow: «касни воз», «сат касни».

examples.en: Call me when you arrive!
If you need anything, call me.

note: In colloquial speech «назвати некога» means to phone someone; «позвати» is also used.

forms: literally: oh, what did I do
meanings: oh no, what have I done?!

examples.sr: Пребацила сам новац погрешном човеку. [Јо̑ј! Шта̏ сам у̀радила?!]
examples.en: I sent the money to the wrong person. Oh no, what have I done?!

examples.sr: Заборавила сам кључеве у стану, [јо̑ј, шта̏ сам у̀радила]!
examples.en: I forgot the keys in the apartment, oh no, what have I done!

note: Feminine form «урадила»; a man says «урадио». «Јој» is an interjection of distress.

examples.en: The bus has left, so now what?
We've finished everything. What next?

note: Longer variants: «шта сад да радимо?», «и шта сад?».

examples.sr: Фотографија је лоша, на њој сам [ру́жан ка̏о ло́пов].
examples.en: The photo is bad, I look hideous in it.

examples.sr: Он је [ру́жан ка̏о ло́пов], али има добро срце.
examples.en: He's ugly as sin, but he has a good heart.

note: A set comparison: «ружан» changes by gender (ружна као лопов), «лопов» stays. Jocular and a bit rude; not said to someone's face.

examples.sr: Значи, сви долазе у суботу? — [Та̀ко̄ је].
examples.en: So everyone is coming on Saturday? - Exactly.

examples.sr: Цена је превисока. — [Та̀ко̄ је], слажем се.
examples.en: The price is too high. - That's right, I agree.

note: A short confirmation or agreement; at speeches and meetings it is often shouted in support.

forms: literally: to take off the list
meanings: to cross off the list, to take off the list

examples.sr: Купио сам хлеб, [ски̏ни] га са списка.
examples.en: I bought the bread, take it off the list.

examples.sr: Ако не можеш да дођеш, [ски̏ни] се са списка.
examples.en: If you can't come, take yourself off the list.

note: Seen on signs and in apps («Скините са списка»); on paper also «прецртати».

examples.en: A pile-up happened on the highway.

examples.sr: У магли је дошло до [ла̏нчаног су̏дара] осам возила.
examples.en: In the fog, eight vehicles collided in a pile-up.

note: based on «ланац» - chain

examples.en: I'm sending the parcel by express mail.
Express mail arrives in two days.

note: written on parcels when fast delivery is needed

examples.en: The pedestrian path goes this way.

examples.sr: Бицикли не смеју на [ста̏зу за пѐшаке].
examples.en: Bicycles are not allowed on the pedestrian path.

note: a sign near summer terraces and in parks; «стаза» - path, trail

meanings: registration sticker: a hologram sticker on the windshield showing the car's registration is valid for a year

examples.en: The new registration sticker is valid for a year.
I stuck the registration sticker on the windshield.

note: In Serbia you get it after the technical inspection and the renewal of the car's registration («регистрација»).

forms: literally: it is not all the same
meanings: it matters, it makes a difference

examples.en: It matters to me what he will say.

examples.sr: Када се ради о здрављу, [нѝје свејѐдно] шта једеш.
examples.en: When it comes to health, it matters what you eat.

note: a slogan on a juice package: the choice matters; «свеједно» - all the same, no difference

examples.en: Here we are, we made it!
Hi, here we are at the party.

note: modeled on «ево ме» (here I am); «ево вас» - here you are

meanings: watch your head (a warning at a low ceiling or beam)

examples.en: There's a low beam here, watch your head!

examples.sr: На степеницама је плафон низак, [па̏зи ву̏гла].
examples.en: The ceiling on the stairs is low, watch your head.

note: A sign on the stairs of a café in Novi Sad. «Вугла» is slang for head, a reshaping of «глава» in the style of «шатровачки» slang (syllable play). Jocular, colloquial.

meanings: let's move on, let's go on (in a story, a trip, a program)

examples.en: We're done with this, let's move on.
Thanks for the question, let's move on.

note: Works for a literal journey (we drive on) and for moving to the next topic.

examples.en: Throw the paper in the trash can.

note: On the street this is the litter bin; at home more often «канта за смеће».

examples.en: Where is the fitting room?

note: A phrase for a clothing store; politely: «Могу ли да пробам?» (May I try it on?).

examples.en: The escalator isn't working.

note: The word «ескалатор» is understood too, but signs usually say «покретне степенице».

examples.en: I'd like a slice of rye bread with butter.

note: dark bread in general is «црни хлеб», white bread «бели хлеб»

examples.sr: Дајте ми један [ро̑л ви̏ршла] и јогурт.
examples.en: Give me one sausage roll and a yogurt.

note: a typical bakery snack, grabbed on the go; «виршла» - a wiener, frankfurter

forms: literally: without a mountain of money
meanings: without a ton of money; when there is not enough money at all

examples.sr: Тешко је живети [без бр̏да па̑ра] у великом граду.
examples.en: It's hard to live in a big city without a ton of money.

examples.sr: Да имам [бр̏до па̑ра], не бих радио.
examples.en: If I had a ton of money, I wouldn't work.

note: «брдо» in colloquial speech means «a pile, a lot»: «брдо пара» - loads of money, «брдо ствари» - a mountain of things.

meanings: to withdraw money from a card or account
to take money off an account (of a bank)

examples.sr: Са рачуна су ми [ски̏нули па̑ре] за рату кредита.
examples.en: They took the loan installment off my account.
I need to withdraw money from my card.

note: Colloquial; in formal speech more often «подићи новац».

meanings: special offer, sale (on a price tag or banner)

examples.sr: Ове недеље траје [спе̏ција̄лна по̏нуда] на све кишобране.
examples.en: This week there's a special offer on all umbrellas.

examples.sr: Видела сам [спѐцијалну по̏нуду] у радњи поред куће.
examples.en: I saw a special offer in the shop next to my house.

note: Next to it on signs you see «попуст» (discount) and «распродаја» (sale).

meanings: you rock, you're killing it, that came out great

examples.en: You rock! You played really well.
Bro, you're killing it on stage!

note: slang praise: someone does something at the top level. Said to friends, jokingly or seriously.

examples.sr: Молим вас, две [ко̏цке ше̏ћера] у чај.
examples.en: Two sugar cubes in my tea, please.

examples.sr: Обично не стављам [ко̏цку ше̏ћера] у кафу.
examples.en: I usually don't put a sugar cube in my coffee.

note: In Serbia sugar is often served in cubes with coffee and tea; counted as «коцке».

forms: literally: how long does the procedure last
meanings: how long does the treatment take?

examples.en: How long does a facial treatment take?

examples.sr: Реците ми, [колѝко тра̑је трѐтма̄н] и колико кошта.
examples.en: Tell me, how long does the treatment take and how much does it cost?

note: «траје» - from «трајати» (to last).

forms: literally: how often do the buses go
meanings: how often do the buses run?

examples.en: How often do buses run to the center?

examples.sr: Не знам [колѝко че̑сто и̑ду а̀утобуси] викендом.
examples.en: I don't know how often the buses run on weekends.

note: «ред вожње» - timetable.

forms: literally: when will we already finally ...
meanings: when are we finally going to (start ...)?

examples.sr: [Ка̏да ћемо ве̏ћ јѐдно̄м] почети да носимо летњу одећу?
examples.en: When will we finally start wearing summer clothes?

examples.sr: [Ка̏да ћемо ве̏ћ јѐдно̄м] отићи на море?
examples.en: When will we finally go to the seaside?

note: «већ једном» - finally, at last: impatience or a joking complaint; the verb is in the future tense.

key: phr:можеш ли ми показати како се ради ова вежба
cyr: можеш ли ми показати како се ради ова вежба?
acc: мо̀жеш ли ми пока́зати ка̏ко се ра̏ди о̀ва̄ вѐжба?
forms: literally: can you show me how this exercise is done
meanings: can you show me how to do this exercise?

examples.sr: [Мо̀жеш ли ми пока́зати ка̏ко се ра̑ди о̀ва̄ вѐжба]?
examples.en: Can you show me how to do this exercise?

examples.sr: Тренеру, [мо̀жете ли ми пока́зати ка̏ко се ра̑ди] чучањ?
examples.en: Coach, can you show me how to do a squat?

note: «радити вежбу» - to do an exercise (not «правити»).

key: phr:дајте му овај лек два пута дневно
cyr: дајте му овај лек два пута дневно.
acc: да̑јте му о̀ва̄ј ле̑к два̑ пу̑та дне̑вно.
forms: literally: give him this medicine two times daily
meanings: give him this medicine twice a day

examples.sr: [Да̑јте му о̀ва̄ј ле̑к два̑ пу̑та дне̑вно] после јела.
examples.en: Give him this medicine twice a day after meals.

examples.sr: Ветеринар каже: [да̑јте му о̀ва̄ј ле̑к два̑ пу̑та дне̑вно].
examples.en: The vet says: give him this medicine twice a day.

note: «пута» after numbers: «два пута, три пута»; «дневно» - daily.

forms: literally: summer is a state of mind
meanings: summer is a state of mind

examples.sr: За мене [ле̏то је ста́ње у̑ма], чак и у новембру.
examples.en: For me summer is a state of mind, even in November.
Don't rush, summer is a state of mind.

note: A caption on a greeting card. «Стање ума» - a state of mind or mood.

forms: literally: I gather moments, and not things

examples.sr: Путујем лако: [са̀купљам трену́тке, а не ства̑ри].
examples.en: I travel light: I collect moments, not things.

examples.sr: Мој мото је [са̀купљам трену́тке, а не ства̑ри].
examples.en: My motto is: I collect moments, not things.

note: A nice caption for a vacation photo; «ствари» - things.

forms: literally: the coffee will not drink itself
meanings: the coffee won't drink itself (time to get going, come to the table)

examples.en: Sit down, the coffee won't drink itself.

examples.sr: [Ше́тња се нѐће са̀ма о̀бавити], хајде да идемо.
examples.en: The walk won't take itself, let's go.

note: A joking card phrase: «X се неће сам(а) Y» - X won't get done by itself, time to start. Seen on «Добро јутро» cards.

examples.en: Call any number from the list.
Take any book.

note: only «који» declines: било ког, било коме; stress on «било» and «који». For people there is «било ко» (anyone).

forms: literally: death does not exist, there is migration
meanings: there is no death, there is only a passage (a soul or a people moves on)

examples.sr: Писац је рекао: [смр̏ти не̑ма, и̑ма сѐоба].
examples.en: The writer said: there is no death, only migration.
I'm reading «Migrations», a novel about the great migration of the Serbs.

note: A quote from the writer Miloš Crnjanski (the novel «Сеобе»). «Сеоба» - migration, exodus; the word often speaks of a people's fate.

key: phr:са природом се споји, свој живот кроји
cyr: са природом се споји, свој живот кроји.
acc: са при̏родом се спо̀ји, сво̑ј жѝвот кро̑ји.
forms: literally: unite with nature, cut your life
meanings: unite with nature and tailor your own life (slogan of an eco brochure)

examples.en: I want to shape my own life.

examples.sr: Викендом се [спа̑јам са при̏родом] на планини.
examples.en: On weekends I merge with nature in the mountains.

note: A rhymed call (споји - кроји). «Кројити живот» - literally to tailor: to arrange your fate as you wish.

meanings: are you out of your mind? (about odd, inappropriate behavior)

examples.sr: [Је̑ л' си је̏о бу̀нике]? Не можеш тако да вичеш!
examples.en: Are you out of your mind? You can't shout like that!
What are you doing, have you lost your mind?

note: «Бунике» - henbane, a poisonous plant: whoever eats it acts mad. «Је л'» is a colloquial short form of «јеси ли».

forms: literally: excuse me, I am a foreigner
meanings: Excuse me, I'm a foreigner (when you did not understand)

examples.sr: Извините, ја сам [стра́нац], можете ли да говорите спорије?
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm a foreigner, could you speak more slowly?

note: A polite way to ask for help or for slower speech.

meanings: I wouldn't; no thanks (a soft refusal)

examples.en: I wouldn't do anything like that.

examples.sr: Да сам на твом месту, [не бих] ишао.
examples.en: If I were you, I wouldn't go.

note: The conditional: бих + participle. Sounds softer than «нећу».

meanings: forget it; don't even think about it (a sharp refusal)

examples.en: A new car? Forget it, we have no money.

note: A colloquial refusal; in the same row: «нема шансе» and «не бих».

meanings: no open fires, making fires is prohibited

examples.en: Making fires is prohibited in the forest.

note: A typical sign in forests and parks. The verb «ложити» here means to light, to kindle.

key: phr:могу ли да добијем једну кафу, молим вас
cyr: могу ли да добијем једну кафу, молим вас?
acc: мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем јѐдну ка̏фу, мо̏лим вас?
forms: literally: can I get one coffee, please
meanings: a polite request for a coffee in a café

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем јѐдну ка̏фу], молим вас?
examples.en: Can I have a coffee, please?

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да до̀бијем ка̏фу] са млеком?
examples.en: Can I have a coffee with milk?

note: Shorter and more usual: «Једну кафу, молим.» «Могу ли да замолим…» is even more polite.

key: phr:можете ли ми додати мало шећера
cyr: можете ли ми додати мало шећера?
acc: мо̀жете ли ми до̀дати ма̏ло ше̏ћера?
forms: literally: can you add me a little sugar
meanings: a request to add a little sugar

examples.sr: [Мо̀жете ли ми до̀дати ма̏ло ше̏ћера], молим вас?
examples.en: Could you add a little sugar, please?

examples.sr: [Мо̀жете ли ми до̀не̄ти] још једну кафу?
examples.en: Could you bring me another coffee?

note: «Можете ли ми» + infinitive is a universal polite request; «мало» is followed by the genitive.

forms: literally: do you have decaffeinated coffee

examples.en: Do you have decaf coffee?

examples.sr: [Да ли и̑мате] соје млеко за капућино?
examples.en: Do you have soy milk for a cappuccino?

note: «Да ли имате…?» is the standard question about availability; decaf isn't found everywhere in Serbia.

examples.en: The airbag deployed in the collision.
This car has six airbags.

note: The same «јастук» as an ordinary pillow for sleeping.

examples.sr: [Мѐра̄ч го̀рива] показује да је резервоар скоро празан.
examples.en: The fuel gauge shows the tank is almost empty.
Look at the fuel gauge before the trip.

note: The pattern «мерач» + genitive: «мерач температуре» - temperature gauge.

forms: literally: little lever of the gearbox

examples.sr: Ухватио је [ру̀чицу мења́ча] и пребацио у другу.
examples.en: He grabbed the gear lever and shifted into second.
The gear lever moves stiffly.
Buy toothpaste and soap.

examples.sr: Ова [па̏ста за зу̑бе] има укус нане.
examples.en: This toothpaste tastes of mint.

note: The pattern «за» + accusative plural: «за зубе» (for teeth).

examples.en: I have a business meeting at nine.
The business meeting has been moved to tomorrow.
I need a formal suit for the wedding.
Everyone came in formal wear.
I forgot my toothbrush.

examples.sr: Ова [че̏ткица за зу̑бе] је превише тврда.
examples.en: This toothbrush is too hard.

note: Plain «четка» is a brush for clothes or hair.

examples.en: The referee showed the forward a yellow card.

examples.sr: Добио је други [жу̑тӣ ка̀рто̄н] и црвени.
examples.en: He got a second yellow card and then a red one.

note: «Картон» is cardboard; a bank card is «картица».

examples.en: The referee awarded a free kick.
He scored a goal from a free kick.

examples.sr: Где је [да̀љӣнскӣ]? Опет сам га изгубила.
examples.en: Where's the remote? I lost it again.
Bring me the remote control from the table.

note: In speech people almost always say just «даљински».

meanings: The cake is awesome! («топ» is a slang word of praise)

examples.en: The cake is awesome!
The concert was great.

note: «Топ», «врх» and «екстра» are slang words of praise: «Време је врх!», «Изгледаш екстра!».

forms: literally: the weather is the top

examples.en: The weather is great today!
You look great!

note: «Врх» means a peak; in speech it means "top-notch". «Екстра» and «топ» are similar praise.

meanings: Where is the nearest bus stop?

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the nearest bus stop?

note: Handy in town: you can ask the same about «трамвајска» and «железничка станица».

meanings: on the right side, on the right

examples.en: The bank is on the right side of the street.
The pharmacy is on the left.

note: Directions: «са леве стране» on the left, «право» straight ahead, «десно» to the right.

examples.en: Go straight to the traffic light.
Then turn left at the bakery.

note: To a taxi driver: «право» straight ahead, «лево» left, «десно» right.

meanings: to go get bread (go and bring it back)

examples.en: I'm going to get bread, I'll be right back.
He went to the store to get bread.

note: «по» + acc. means going somewhere to fetch something: «ићи по хлеб».

examples.en: We signed a contract with the client.

examples.sr: Наш [до̏гово̄р] је био да поделимо трошкове.
examples.en: Our agreement was to split the costs.

related.en: contract — a written document: employment, lease, with a client
agreement, arrangement — made in words between people

meanings: how to say «to meet»: састати се, срести, наићи, дочекати

examples.en: We often meet after work.
Yesterday I ran into my neighbor on the stairs.

examples.sr: Јуче сам [на̏ишао] на њу у продавници.
examples.en: Yesterday I came across her at the store.
We rang in the New Year with our family.

related.en: to meet (by arrangement) — a planned business or friendly meeting
to meet, to run into — the general verb: planned and chance meetings alike
to come across, to run into — to meet by chance
to welcome, to see in — guests, a holiday, an event

note: After наи́ћи always comes на + acc.: наи́ћи на њу̑.

meanings: how to say «to call»: звонити, позвати, јавити се, телефонирати

examples.en: The phone is ringing.
Call me tomorrow at eight o'clock.
I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.
She phones her mother every evening.

related.en: to ring — only when a bell or phone rings: «Телефон звони»
to call (someone) — the basic verb for phoning a person
to get in touch, to call back — broader: to contact, to answer a call
to phone, to call — biaspectual, neutral, slightly bookish

note: По̀звати also means «to invite»: позвали су ме на рођендан. And ја́вити се also means «to answer the phone»: јави се на телефон.

examples.en: Here is the school timetable.
Look at the train timetable.
The festival schedule has been published.

related.en: hour-by-hour schedule — a conference, a festival, a working day

note: For flights, ре̑д ле́то̄ва̄ is used, not ред вожње.

meanings: how to say goodbye: довиђења, ћао, збогом, видимо се

examples.en: Goodbye, Director!
Bye, see you tomorrow!
Farewell, and thanks for everything.
See you on Friday!

related.en: goodbye — neutral and polite: with colleagues, people you barely know
bye, hi — with people you are on first-name terms with
see you — to friends, when you will meet soon

note: Ћа̑о is said both when meeting and when parting. There is also чу̏је̄мо се - «we'll talk» (by phone).

cyr: пас · псић · псето · куче · штене · кер · џукела
acc: па̏с · пси̏ћ · псе̏то · ку̏че · штѐне · ке̑р · џу̀кела
meanings: words for a dog: пас, псето, куче, штене, кер, џукела

examples.en: I've had a dog for five years.
Look at that little doggy!
Get that mutt away from me!
What a cute little dog!

examples.sr: Наше [штѐне] још учи да хода на поводцу.
examples.en: Our puppy is still learning to walk on a leash.
Some mutt barked all night.
Careful, that cur bites!

related.en: doggy, little dog — diminutive, often a puppy too
doggie, pooch — affectionate, also for a grown dog
cur, mongrel — rude; also used of a nasty person

note:
How to choose:
• neutral - па̏с
• affectionate - пси̏ћ, ку̏че
• rude - псе̏то, ке̑р, џу̀кела
• a young dog - штѐне

examples.sr: Тешко ми је [одлу́чити] шта да обучем.
examples.en: It's hard for me to decide what to wear.
We have to solve this problem.

related.en: to decide, to make a decision — to choose, to make a choice
to solve — first of all to resolve a problem or a task

note: «To solve a problem» is only ре́шити: ре́шити зада́так. «To make a decision» is одлу́чити or донети одлуку.

meanings: how to say «to go» by vehicle: ићи, возити се, путовати

examples.en: I'm going home by bus.
I like riding my bike.
We're going to Montenegro by train.

related.en: to go (on foot or by vehicle) — the simplest option
to ride, to go for a ride — on transport, often regularly or for pleasure
to travel, to be on the way — a trip or a journey

note: Ѝћи means both «to go on foot» and «to go by vehicle». «To drive a car» is во̀зити without се: возим аутомобил.

examples.en: This year we're spending the summer at the seaside.
They are flying to Podgorica.

related.en: to spend the summer, to vacation in summer
to fly — to move through the air

note: Лѐтовати is about the summer, not about flying. The two verbs conjugate differently: летујем, but лѐтӣм.

examples.en: We have a small house in the countryside.

examples.sr: Живимо у новој [згра̏ди] на Новом Београду.
examples.en: We live in a new apartment building in New Belgrade.
Welcome to my home!

related.en: house — a detached house of one or two floors
building, apartment block — a multistory building
home, hearth — one's own home; in names of institutions: дом здравља - health center, студентски дом - dormitory

note: Ко̑д ку̏ће means «at home» wherever you live: in a ку̏ћа or in a згра̏да.

examples.en: I study Serbian every day.
She is getting her education in Belgrade.
I'm studying medicine in Belgrade.

related.en: to learn, to study — the most general word
to be educated, to go to school — over several years: school, college, university
to study at university — to study a particular field

note: A schoolchild does not студира: he иде у школу or учи.

examples.sr: Влада је уложила много [но́вца] у пројекат.
examples.en: The government invested a lot of money in the project.
I don't have enough money to buy it.

related.en: money — neutral and official; singular only
money — colloquial; plural only, from Turkish

note: Genitive: нема новца, нема пара. Па̏ра in the singular means «steam»: пара из чајника.

meanings: how to say «to gather, to collect»: скупљати, окупљати, склапати, брати, паковати

examples.en: I collect postcards from different countries.
We're collecting signatures for the petition.
We get together with friends at the café.
He's been putting the wardrobe together for two hours.
We picked mushrooms in the forest.
I'm still packing my suitcase for the trip.

related.en: to collect, to gather — data, things, people, a collection
to gather people — only of people; окупљати се - to get together
to assemble — from parts: furniture, a model kit; close to састављати
to pick — to harvest: mushrooms, flowers, fruit
to pack — things, luggage for a trip

note: Serbian uses a different verb for each kind of object: people, parts, harvest or things for a trip.

examples.en: Every morning we go out for a run.
He always runs away from problems.

related.en: to run — physical running: sport, a jog, hurrying
to flee, to run away — also figuratively: to run from problems

examples.sr: Сутра морам да [сре̏дим] овај хаос у ормару.
examples.en: Tomorrow I have to sort out this mess in the wardrobe.
The trip threw off my daily routine.

related.en: to put in order, to sort out — things, papers, thoughts
to disrupt, to upset — order, routine, plans

note: Imperfective forms: сређи́вати and рѐметити.

meanings: verbs of payment: платити, уплатити, исплатити, наплатити

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
Yesterday I paid the loan installment.
The bank will pay the owner a dividend.
The taxi driver charged me four thousand.

related.en: to pay — to pay for a purchase or a bill
to pay in, to transfer — money into an account or toward a payment
to pay out — to hand over a sum: salary, dividends
to charge, to collect payment — said of the one who receives the money: a taxi driver, a seller

note: Nouns: у̀плата (payment in) and и̏сплата (payout). На̀платити also means «to collect (a debt)»: на̀платити ду̏г.

meanings: how to say «to hurt, to be ill»: болети, бити болестан, боловати

examples.en: My throat hurts.
My cat is sick.
He suffers from a serious illness.

related.en: to hurt, to ache (of a body part)
to be ill — the state right now
to be ill for a long time — a serious illness; «боловати од» + gen.

note: With бо̀лети the sore spot is the subject and the person is in the acc.: боли ме грло, бо̑ле ме ле́ђа.

meanings: how to say «tour, excursion»: обилазак, тура, излет, екскурзија

examples.en: The tour of the fortress lasted two hours.

examples.sr: Водич нас је повео на [ту̏ру] по старом граду.
examples.en: The guide took us on a tour of the old town.
We organize trips to Montenegro.
The pupils are going on a school trip.

related.en: sightseeing visit, tour — a visit to a place or to sights
short guided tour — brief, with a guide
outing, day trip — a trip to the countryside: picnic, walk, a trip to another town
organized trip — for a group, more often a school one

note: A sightseeing tour of a city is an оби́лазак or ту̑ра, not an екску̀рзија.

meanings: how to say «owner, landlord, host»: власник, станодавац, газда, домаћин

examples.en: Who is the owner of this dog?
The landlord comes for the rent every month.
The owner closed the café.
The host offered the guests rakija.

related.en: owner — a broad word: legal and colloquial
landlord — the one who rents out housing
boss, owner — informal: the owner of a café, a workshop
host — the master of the house, who receives guests

note: A landlord of a rented apartment is a станода̀вац: вла̑снӣк is closer to «owner». Female forms: вла̑сница, станодавка, дома̀ћица.

meanings: how to say «shade, shadow»: хлад, хладовина, сенка

examples.en: We took shelter in the shade.
It's really hot, let's go into the shade!
There is the shadow of a tree on the wall.

related.en: shade, coolness — shelter from the heat
shade, a cool spot — a shady corner
shadow (silhouette) — the shadow cast by an object

note: Се̑нка is also used figuratively: сенка сумње - «a shadow of a doubt».

meanings: words for heat: врућина, жега, спарина, припека

examples.en: It's really hot today.
The heat is unbearable.
The muggy heat is awful.
Don't go out into the blazing sun without a hat.

note: Спа̀рина has a synonym: оморина.

cyr: сунчати се · поцрнети · добити боју · препланути
acc: су̀нчати се · поцр̀нети · до̀бити бо̀ју · препла̀нути
meanings: to get a tan: сунчати се, поцрнети, препланути, добити боју

examples.en: We spend all day sunbathing on the beach.
Everyone got a tan at the seaside.

examples.sr: Ако не желите да [до̀бијете бо̀ју], користите крему.
examples.en: If you don't want to get a tan, use sunscreen.

examples.sr: Ја сам [препла̀нула] јер сам била на мору.
examples.en: I'm tanned because I was at the seaside.

related.en: to sunbathe (the process) — to lie in the sun
to get tanned — literally «to turn black»
to get a tan — literally «to get color»

note: A tanned person: препланео (m.), препланула (f.). Су̀нчати се is the process, the others the result.

examples.en: Well, I don't know.
Come on, how should I know!
Oh, come on! I don't believe it!

related.en: well, so, because — links replies, explains, continues a thought
oh come on, no way — emotional: disbelief, irritation, brushing something off

note: Па softly opens a reply: па до̀бро - «well, all right». Ма̏ is sharper: ма̏ јо̏к! - «no way!»

examples.en: Life is beautiful.
My stomach hurts.
Sweets make my belly grow.

related.en: life — not a part of the body
stomach, tummy — when it hurts after eating

note: «My stomach hurts» is боли ме стомак, not жѝвот, which is «life».

examples.en: I've done only one task, nothing more.
I've done just one task so far, and I'll continue.
It worked only on the fifth attempt.

related.en: only — a limit: nothing more, a total
only, just, not until — the start of a process or a late moment; «тек сад» - «only now»

note: Са̏мо што̏ also means «just now»: само што је стигао - «he has only just arrived».

meanings: come on, let's, don't: ајде, ајмо, немој, немојмо

examples.en: Come on, get out of here!
Let's go to the gym!
Don't be late.
Let's not argue.

related.en: come on, go on — urging the listener
let's go — a suggestion to do something together
don't — a prohibition; -те for the polite form and the plural
let's not — giving up an action together with the speaker

note: А̀јде and не̏мој address the listener, а̀јмо and не̏мојмо include the speaker. After не̏мој comes да + present or the infinitive: не̏мој да пи̑ше̄ш, не̏мој пи́сати - «don't write».

examples.en: I always pay by card.
I'm crying with happiness!

related.en: to cry — плачем, плачеш, плаче (к changes to ч)

note: Плаћам is with money, плачем is with tears.

examples.en: I put a spoonful of sour cream in the soup.
There's some mileram in the fridge.
Buy sweet cream for the cake.

related.en: thick sour cream — a bit richer, sold as a separate product

note: Whipping cream is слатка павлака.

examples.sr: Већ три месеца [ре̏до̄вно] идем на пливање.
examples.en: I've been going swimming regularly for three months now.
I don't have regular working hours.

related.en: regular, steady — happens in order: habits, visitors
proper, normal, by the rules — meets the norm

note: The regular price, without a discount, is редовна цена.

meanings: to understand: разумети, схватити, сконтати, скапирати

examples.en: I didn't understand you very well.

examples.sr: Коначно сам [схва̀тио] у чему је проблем.
examples.en: I finally figured out what the problem is.

examples.sr: Коначно сам [ско̀нтао] како ради ова апликација.
examples.en: I finally got how this app works.
I realized right away that it was a trap.

related.en: to grasp — to catch the point quickly, mostly in the past
to figure out — colloquial, after some thought
to get it, to catch on — colloquial, everyday speech, a sudden realization

note: The colloquial «got it?» is капираш? (from скапѝрати).

examples.en: Add one tablespoon of flour.
Put a teaspoon of sugar in the coffee.

note: The spoons are named after the dishes: супена - for soup, кафена - for coffee. Plain ка̀шика is a spoon in general.

examples.sr: [По̀следњӣ] филм који сам гледао био је добар.
examples.en: The last movie I watched was good.
The final deadline is Friday.

related.en: last — at the end of a series: the last film, the last task
final, ultimate — at the very edge or limit: the final deadline, the last stop

note: «Last» meaning «previous» is not по̀следњӣ: прошле недеље - «last week».

examples.sr: Моје [ми̏шље̄ње] је да је филм одличан.
examples.en: My opinion is that the film is excellent.
Thinking about the future motivates me.

related.en: opinion — the result of thinking, a position
thinking, reflection — the process of pondering

note: The verbs are ми̏слити and разми́шљати. «In my opinion» is по мом мишљењу.

examples.en: The road is temporarily closed.
He's busy at the moment.

related.en: temporarily — for a limited time: «привремено затворен»

note: The adjective is прѝвремен: прѝвременӣ по̀сао - «a temporary job».

meanings: to make, to do: правити, радити, чинити

examples.en: I'm making a cake for the birthday.
I'm doing my homework.
You're doing a good deed.

related.en: to make, to create — material things: a cake, noise
to do, to work — work and activities
to do, to commit — deeds and abstract things

note: «What are you doing?» is шта радиш?. Пра̏вити се means «to pretend»: прави се да не зна.

meanings: to know, to be able to: знати, умети, моћи

examples.en: I know where the store is.
I can cook.
I can come tomorrow.

related.en: to know how to — a skill, an ability
can, to be able to — possibility, permission

note: «To know how to swim» can be умем да пливам or знам да пливам.

examples.en: He drank as many as three glasses of wine.
I need at least five minutes.

related.en: even, as many as — emphasis, more than expected
at least — a minimum, the lower limit

note: Ча̏к и - «even»: ча̏к и дѐца зна̏јӯ - «even children know».

examples.en: I'm renting a furnished apartment.
I'm renting out a furnished apartment.

related.en: to rent (as a tenant), to hire — the one who pays
to rent out, to let — the owner, the one who lets it

note: Изна́јмити sometimes means «to rent out» too, so only издајем is unambiguously «I rent out». «To rent» can also be узети под кирију.

meanings: to flirt, to hang around: мувати, мувати се, смувати се

examples.en: Luka is hitting on the waitress.
He's always hanging around the house.

examples.sr: Милош и Маја су се [сму̀вали] прошлог лета.
examples.en: Miloš and Maja got together last summer.

related.en: to hit on, to flirt with someone
to hang around, to wander aimlessly
to start going out — the moment a relationship begins

note: Милош и Маја се мувају means that they are flirting with each other.

meanings: also, the same, similar: такође, исто, слично

examples.en: Marko is coming, and Ana too.
We have the same opinion.
This city is similar to Belgrade.

note: И̏сто ми је - «I don't care».

cyr: потребно је / потребни су · треба да
acc: по̀требно је / по̏требнӣ су · тре́ба да

examples.en: New textbooks are needed.
You should study every day.

related.en: needed, necessary — the stress is on things: «потребно је време» - «time is needed»
need to, should — the stress is on an action: «треба да учиш» - «you should study»

note: Тре́ба ми + nominative also means «I need»: тре́ба ми по̏мо̄ћ - «I need help».

examples.en: The next step is to fill out the form.
We're planning the project for the coming weeks.

related.en: next, upcoming — more formal, mostly about plans and deadlines

note: Слѐде̄ћӣ is also «next in line»: слѐде̄ћӣ, мо̏лим! - «next, please!»

meanings: to remember, to forget: сећати се, сетити се, заборавити

examples.sr: [Се̏ћам се] свог првог дана у школи.
examples.en: I remember my first day at school.

examples.sr: [Сѐтио сам се] да сам заборавио кључ.
examples.en: I remembered that I had forgotten the key.
I forgot where I left my phone.

related.en: to remember (impf.) — to have something in memory: «сећам се свог првог дана у школи»
to recall, to think of (pf.) — «сетио сам се да...»

note: Се̏ћати се and се̏тити се take the genitive: сећам се њега. Забо̀равити takes the accusative: заборавио сам кључ.

examples.en: I agree with you.
I'm putting the T-shirts in the closet.
I lied to him.

related.en: to agree — always with «се»: «слажем се» - «I agree»
to put away, to stack — without «се» + accusative: «слажем дрва» - «I stack the firewood»
to lie, to tell a lie (pf.) — perfective of «лагати»: «слагао сам га» - «I lied to him»

note: «I agree» is always слажем се: without се it is a different verb, e.g. слажем мајице - «I fold T-shirts».

examples.en: I know where the library is.
I found out where the library is.

related.en: to know (impf.) — to have the information
to find out, to learn (pf.) — to get new information

note: «To recognize» is препо̀знати: нисам га препознао - «I didn't recognize him».

examples.en: I remember my childhood.
I remembered her name.

related.en: to recall, to think of (pf.) — a flash of memory at a specific moment

note: Both take the genitive: сећам се детињства, сетио сам се имена.

examples.en: I keep old photographs.
I saved all the messages.

related.en: to keep, to look after, to guard (impf.) — the process
to save, to preserve (pf.) — the result

note: Чу́вати де̏цу - «to look after children». Чувај се! - «take care of yourself».

examples.en: I'm starting to learn Serbian.

examples.sr: [По̀чео] сам да учим српски прошле године.
examples.en: I started learning Serbian last year.

related.en: to begin (impf.) — a process or a regular action

note: Both also mean «to start» without се: филм почиње у осам - «the film starts at eight».

examples.en: Tell me what you think.
I think that you're right.
We know that you were here.

related.en: what (question word) — in direct and indirect questions: «шта хоћеш?», «не разумем шта кажеш»
that (conjunction) — joins two clauses: «мислим да си у праву»

note: Unlike English «that», да cannot be left out: мислим да сте у праву.

key: cmp:за + вин. п.-кроз + вин. п.-преко + род. п.
cyr: преко + род. п. · кроз + вин. п. · за + вин. п.
acc: пре̏ко + ро̑д. п. · кроз + ви̑н. п. · за + ви̑н. п.
meanings: across, through, in: преко + gen., кроз + acc., за + acc.

examples.en: I'm crossing the bridge.
We went through the forest.
The train arrives in ten minutes.

related.en: across, over (a surface, an obstacle) — a street, a bridge: «прећи преко улице»
through (inside something) — a forest, a crowd, an opening: «проћи кроз шуму»
in (of time) — after a period of time: «за годину дана» - «in a year»

note: Пре̏ко is also used figuratively: преко интернета - «over the internet», преко пријатеља - «through friends».

meanings: to manage, to make it: успети, стићи

examples.en: I didn't manage to finish my homework.
I managed to solve the problem.
Will you make it to the train?

related.en: to manage, to succeed — it worked out: «успео сам да решим» (impf. успе́вати)
to make it in time; to arrive; to catch up (impf. сти̏зати)

note: Trap: «to make the train» is сти̏ћи на во̑з, not успети. У̀спети is about success: успео сам у животу - «I've succeeded in life».

examples.en: What are you doing?

examples.sr: Не могу да идем [за̀то̄ што̏] имам обавезе.
examples.en: I can't go because I have things to do.
That's the reason I didn't come.

related.en: what (question word) — in a question and an indirect question: «шта радиш?», «не знам шта да радим»
because, that (conjunction) — a reason: «зато што», «разлог што»

note: Што̏ is also «that» after све̏, оно: све̏ што̏ зна̑м. Colloquially it can mean «why»: што плачеш?

examples.en: I found money on the street by chance.
I finally found a job!
The police found the stolen car.

related.en: to find — to discover, also by chance: «морам да нађем кључ»
to find after effort — a long search, a valuable find

note: На́ћи се also means «to meet»: нађимо се у осам - «let's meet at eight».

examples.en: Last night I dreamed that I was flying.
He dreams of becoming a doctor.
I dream of a house by the sea.

related.en: to dream (in sleep); to dream of a goal — dreams in sleep are only сањати
to daydream, to fantasize — pleasant thoughts, real or not

meanings: to say, to speak, to talk: казати, рећи, причати, разговарати, говорити

examples.sr: Он [ка̏же] да те је срео јуче.
examples.en: He says that he met you yesterday.
I said everything I knew.
People are talking about you.
I need to talk to you.
He speaks three languages fluently.

related.en: to say, to tell — has a present tense: «он каже да...»
to say, to tell — perfective only: «рекла сам», «реците»
to tell, to chat, to talk — everyday, informal
to talk, to converse — a serious conversation with someone
to speak, to express oneself, to know a language

note: Ре̏ћи has no present tense, ка́зати takes its place: он каже - «he says», but он је рекао - «he said».

meanings: flower, flowers, blossoms: цвет, цвеће, цветови

examples.en: I have one flower in a pot.
I like planting flowers in the garden.
The first blossoms have opened on the tree.

related.en: a flower — a single one: «имам један цвет у саксији»
flowers (collective) — flowers in general, a bouquet, a flower bed
blossoms, individual flowers — on a tree or a stem, when the number matters

note: Цве̑ће is neuter singular: цве̑ће је ле̑по - «flowers are beautiful».

examples.sr: Дао ми је [на̑знаку] да му се свиђам.
examples.en: He gave me a hint that he likes me.
His look was a sign of trouble.

examples.sr: Изјава је била [а̀лӯзија] на прошли догађај.
examples.en: The statement was an allusion to a past event.

related.en: hint, sign — the closest to «a hint»
warning sign, veiled signal — foreshadows something: «наговештај невоље»
allusion — a cultural or ironic reference to an event or topic

note: Verbs: нагове́стити (impf. наговешта́вати), алуди́рати.

examples.en: I can't hear you, the microphone is off.

examples.sr: Волим да [слу̀шам] аудио књиге у превозу.
examples.en: I like listening to audiobooks on public transport.
He never listened to his parents' advice.

related.en: to hear — to perceive a sound without special attention: «не чујем те»
to listen — attentively, with concentration; also «to obey»

note: Чу̏ти за - «to hear of someone»: чуо сам за њега. Чу̏ти се - «to be in touch (by phone)».

examples.en: I go to work every day.
He went home.
I got home.

related.en: to go, to walk — movement in progress or a habit: «идем у школу»
to leave, to go away — left a place and is no longer there: «отишао је кући»
to come, to arrive — arrival at a destination: «дошао сам кући»

note: Оти́ћи and до́ћи have no present tense for «I'm leaving» and «I'm coming»: it is одлазим and долазим.

cyr: треба да + глагол · морам да + глагол
acc: тре́ба да + гла̏гол · мо̑ра̄м да + гла̏гол

examples.en: You should get some rest.
I have to go.
I don't have to work today.

related.en: should, ought to — advice, a recommendation or an outside necessity: «треба да учим»
must, have to — a personal obligation: «морам да идем»

note: With a negation the meaning splits: не мо̑ра̄м да - «I don't have to», не тре́ба да - «I shouldn't».

examples.en: My house is bigger than yours.
It's easier said than done.

examples.sr: Он је виши [не̏го што̏] сам мислио.
examples.en: He is taller than I thought.

related.en: than — comparing nouns and pronouns: «већа од твоје», «паметнији од мене»
than — comparing actions, states, parts of a sentence: «боље је учити него губити време»

note: With numerals only од: ви̏ше̄ од де̏сет. Tip: «than» between two nouns is од, between two actions it is не̏го.

examples.en: He is a strong man.
I drink strong coffee.
He took a powerful blow.

related.en: strong, hard — having strength and intensity
powerful, mighty — a display of strength: an action, a machine, will

note:
Typical combinations:
• ја̑к чо̏век, јака кафа, ја̑к ве̏тар
• сна́жан у̀дарац, сна́жан мо̀то̄р, снажна воља

examples.sr: На крају састанка прешли смо на [ра̀зно].
examples.en: At the end of the meeting we moved on to any other business.
People react to stress differently.
Belgrade has a varied architecture.

related.en: miscellaneous, various — a set of unrelated things; the agenda item «any other business»
varied, diverse — a wealth of kinds, forms, flavors

note: Close in meaning to разнолико: разно̀врстан, шаро̀лик.

examples.en: This is a difficult question.
Here's the bus, hurry up.
Here I am, I've arrived!

related.en: here is, here comes (particle) — does not decline; the thing named goes in the genitive

note: With е̏во the short pronoun forms are used: е̏во ме, е̏во га - «here I am», «here he is».

examples.sr: Запамтио сам сваку [ре̑ч] из ове песме.
examples.en: I memorized every word of this song.
This letter is hard to write.

examples.sr: Његов [го̏во̄р] на конференцији био је инспиративан.
examples.en: His speech at the conference was inspiring.

related.en: word — a single word of a language: «тачна реч»
letter — a sign of the alphabet
speech, dialect — a talk, a manner of speaking, a local dialect

note: Do not mix them up: сло̏во is a letter of the alphabet, and the word for «word» is ре̑ч.

examples.en: My stomach hurts.
Life is full of surprises.

related.en: life — not a part of the body
stomach, belly — where it hurts after a meal

note: «My stomach hurts» is боли ме стомак. The outer belly, the paunch, is тр̀бух.

examples.en: My country is very beautiful.
Serbia is a small country.
Look at the other side of the paper.

related.en: country, land — a territory; also soil and the planet
side, page — the side of something, or a page of a book

note: «Country» is зѐмља or др̀жава; стра́на means «side» or «page».

meanings: драго ми је or задовољан сам?

examples.en: I'm satisfied with my job.

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је] што си добио посао!
examples.en: I'm glad you got the job!

related.en: I'm satisfied — lasting satisfaction: with a job, a grade, a result
I'm glad, I'm pleased — a reaction to news or an event; with «да» or «што»

note: Дра̑го ми је also means «nice to meet you». A woman says задовољна сам.

examples.en: I told him the truth.
Can I say something?
He speaks three languages.
We chatted all night.

related.en: to say, to tell — a short, specific statement; perfective
to say, to tell — the same as «рећи», but it has a present tense: «кажем»
to speak, to talk — the process of speaking, giving a speech, knowing a language
to tell, to chat — informal conversation

note: Ре̏ћи has no present tense: кажем is used instead. «To tell (a story)» is испри́чати.

examples.sr: Београд ми је [до̏м] већ десет година.
examples.en: Belgrade has been my home for ten years now.
We bought a house and two apartments.

examples.sr: Живим у малом [ста̑ну] на петом спрату.
examples.en: I live in a small apartment on the fifth floor.

related.en: home, hearth, homeland — a broader and warmer notion
apartment, flat — a dwelling in an apartment building

note: До̏м also means an institution: дом здравља is a «health center», дом за старе a «nursing home». «At home» is код куће.

examples.en: My arm hurts.
He took a full handful of walnuts.

related.en: arm, hand — the whole arm from shoulder to fingers; the general word
hand, handful — only the hand itself; also a measure, a handful

note: «To shake hands» is ру̏ковати се.

examples.en: I don't know how to explain it.
I saw him running.
She is as beautiful as an angel.
He works as a teacher.

related.en: how, in what way — in questions and after verbs of speech and perception
like (comparison), as (a role) — comparison, a role, a profession

note: With да it means «as if»: као да спава. And ка̏ко after «see» or «hear» introduces a clause: чуо сам како пева.

cyr: умрети · преминути · упокојити се · угинути · цркнути
acc: у̀мрети · прѐминути · упо̀којити се · у̀гинути · цр̀кнути
meanings: умрети, преминути, упокојити се, угинути or цркнути?

examples.en: He died after a long illness.
A well-known actor passed away yesterday.
The Patriarch passed away at the age of ninety.
The dog died of old age.
My phone has died.

related.en: to pass away — official: news, obituaries
to pass away, to repose — church style
to die, to perish — of animals
to croak, to kick the bucket — rude; jokingly of gadgets

note: Said of a person, цр̏кнути sounds like an insult, and у̀гинути as if the person were an animal.

examples.en: Turn on the light, it's dark.
Plug the phone into the charger.
He joined the discussion.

related.en: to turn on, to light — to start up: a light, a TV, an engine
to plug in, to include — into a network, a discussion

note: The opposites: уга́сити is the opposite of упа́лити, искљу́чити of укљу́чити.

examples.en: I want a coffee!
I'd like a coffee.
I wish you luck.

related.en: to want — a momentary wish, a decision
to wish, to want — softer and more polite, a longer-lasting wish

note: The short forms ћу, ћеш, ће come from хте̏ти and form the future tense: ја̑ ћу до́ћи.

examples.sr: Он је [јѐдӣнӣ] који је дошао на састанак.
examples.en: He is the only one who came to the meeting.
This car has a unique design.

related.en: only, sole — numerical exclusivity: one among many
unique — a quality: like nothing else, one of a kind

note: Једѝнствен also means «unified»: једѝнствено тр̏жӣште is a «single market».

examples.en: I like that song.
Fresh air does me good.
A cold juice is just what I need in this heat.

related.en: to like — taste and sympathy: «свиђа ми се песма», «свиђаш ми се»
to be pleasant, to do good — effect and well-being: «чај ми прија»

note: From прѝјати comes при̏ја̄тно! - «enjoy your meal». With both verbs the person who likes stands in the dative: ми, ти, му.

examples.en: All the people came.
It rained the whole day.
The whole city was decorated.

related.en: all, the whole (the entire body of things) — all the elements, the whole mass: «сав народ», «сва деца»
whole, entire, intact — wholeness or a full period: «читав дан», «читава књига»
whole, entire — a close synonym of «читав», common in speech: «цео град»

note: «Everyone» of people is сви̏, «everything» of things is све̏: сви су дошли, све је у реду.

examples.en: I'm going home.
I come every Saturday.
I came yesterday.
He went abroad.

related.en: to go — the basic verb of motion, on foot or by vehicle
to leave, to go away (impf. / pf.)

note: До̀лазити and о̀длазити are imperfective, до́ћи and оти́ћи perfective: долазим сваке суботе, but дошао сам јуче.

examples.en: She is sitting alone in the room.
I did it myself.
I just wanted to ask.

related.en: alone, by oneself (сама, само, сами); also «I am», from «бити»

note: A trap: са̏мо is also the neuter of сам: де́те је са̏мо - «the child is alone».

examples.en: That is very important.
I like it a lot.
How nice it is!

related.en: very — bookish: writing, news, formal style
very, a lot — the universal word in speech

note: With a noun мно̏го requires the genitive: мно̏го љу̑ди. Ба̏ш adds emotion: ба̏ш је хла́дно - «it's really cold!»

examples.en: You're late again.
Read it once more.
They started over.

related.en: again — neutral: something happened once more
once more, again — to repeat the same action
anew, from scratch — a new start

note: If in doubt, use о̏пе̄т: it fits almost always.

examples.en: I'm not tired, I'm hungry.
I've already had lunch.
He is taller than you think.

related.en: already; but, rather (after a negation): «не ја, већ он»
than; but, rather (after a negation): a comparison and «not A but B»

note: In «not A but B» both work: нѝје о̑н, ве̏ћ ја̑ = нѝје о̑н, не̏го ја̑. In a comparison «than» is only не̏го.

examples.en: I just arrived.
I only have five minutes.
I barely made it.

related.en: just now; not until — about time: «тек сам стигао»
only, just — a limit on quantity

note: Једва чекам - «I can't wait». Те̏к у де̏вет - «not until nine».

examples.en: The driver was injured in the accident.
The screen is damaged.
The TV is broken.

related.en: injured, hurt — only of people: a physical or emotional wound
damaged — of things, when it is unclear how
broken, spoiled — not working, food gone bad; also of corrupt people

note: Verbs: ра̀збити - to smash, сло̀мити - to break, напу̀кнути - to crack.

cyr: спавати · заспати · одспавати · наспавати се · преспавати
acc: спа̀вати · за̀спати · одспа̀вати · на̀спавати се · прѐспавати
meanings: спавати, заспати, одспавати, наспавати се or преспавати?

examples.en: The baby is sleeping in the stroller.
I fell asleep quickly.
I'm going to take a half-hour nap.
I haven't had enough sleep.
I slept through the whole day.

related.en: to sleep — the process of sleeping (impf.)
to fall asleep — the moment of dozing off
to take a nap, to sleep a little
to get enough sleep — to sleep your fill
to oversleep (a stretch of time); to sleep over

note: Преспа́вати also means «to stay the night»: можеш да преспаваш код нас - «you can stay the night at our place».

examples.en: Maybe I'll come.
He will probably arrive on time.
I hope the rain stops by evening.

related.en: maybe, perhaps — the chances are about even; neutral, any style
I suppose, hopefully — colloquial, with hope or doubt

note: Ва̀љда often expresses hope: Ва̀љда ће би̏ти бо̏ље̄ - «hopefully it will get better».

examples.en: We became friends.
A buddy from school called me.
He is just an acquaintance to me.
He has been my mate since childhood.

related.en: friend, close friend — the closest circle
buddy, pal, comrade — a good acquaintance who may become a пријатељ
mate, buddy — a colloquial, warm word for a close friend

note: A group of friends is дру́штво or еки́па. «To become friends» is спријатѐљити се.

examples.en: I want a different drink.
Do it differently.
It was a completely different movie.

related.en: other, another — a different thing or person, a choice among several
differently, otherwise (adv.) — the manner of an action

note: Дру̏гӣ also means «second» in order: дру̏гӣ пу̑т - «the second time».

examples.en: Oh, I forgot!
Ow, my leg hurts!
Oh no, what now?
Phew, it's finally Friday!

related.en: oh, oops — soft and human: surprise, sympathy, embarrassment
ow, oh — sharp: pain, fear, shock
oh dear, woe — drama, panic, often ironic
phew, ugh — tiredness, relief, a sigh

note: The meaning depends a lot on intonation. A ready phrase: ку̏кӯ мѐнӣ! - «woe is me!»

examples.en: Many cultures exist in the world.
I want to become a doctor.

related.en: to exist, to be — there is, there exists
to become, to turn into — a change of state or profession

note: По̀стати is perfective, its imperfective is по̀стајати. Посто̀јати exists only as an imperfective.

examples.en: Come here!

examples.sr: Хоћеш ли да идемо [о̀на̄мо], код реке?
examples.en: Do you want us to go over there, to the river?
Yesterday I passed that way.
Go that way, the exit is there.

related.en: here, this way — direction toward the speaker
there, over there — toward a distant place
that way — along a familiar route
that way over there — a distant route off to the side

note:
Ту̀да̄ means «that way», not «to there»; «to there» is о̀на̄мо or та̏мо.

Three questions:
• о́вде, та̏мо - «where?»
• о̀ва̄мо, о̀на̄мо - «to where?»
• о̀вуда, ту̀да̄, о̀нуда - «by which way?»

cyr: минимум / минимално · најмање · бар / барем · макар
acc: мѝнимум / ми̏нима̄лно · на̏јмање · ба̑р / ба̀рем · ма̀кар

examples.en: At least half a kilogram of meat is needed.
At least twenty people are coming to the party.
At least come for a coffee.
Drop by for at least half an hour.

related.en: at least, a minimum of — an exact quantity: «минимум пола килограма»
at least — of a number of people or things
at least — if nothing more: «бар повтори лекцију»
at least, even if — a concession: «сврати макар на пола сата»

note: Ма̀кар also means «even if»: ма̀кар и ка̏сно - «even if late».

examples.sr: Желим да се [извѝним] што сам закаснио.
examples.en: I want to apologize for being late.
The river wound through the valley.

related.en: to apologize — to ask for forgiveness
to bend, to wind — of objects: a tree, a river, a branch

note: Even native speakers often mix them up. In speech the imperfective извињавам се is more common, and извини and извините are simply «sorry» and «excuse me».

examples.en: Pick up your things and go!
Pick up your stuff and get lost!

examples.sr: Спаковала је све своје [пи̏нкле] и отишла.
examples.en: She packed all her belongings and left.
Kids, pick up your toys from the playground!

related.en: belongings, junk — colloquial, plural only, often of children's toys

note: Ства̏ри is neutral; the other three are colloquial and used only in the plural.

examples.en: The child has started to walk.
I walked five kilometers.
We're strolling around the city.

related.en: to walk — the way of moving itself
to go on foot — a long way, or instead of transport
to stroll, to take a walk — aimless, for pleasure

note: «To go to school» is ићи у школу: хо́дати describes only the act of walking.

examples.en: I love flowers.
The blossoms have bloomed.

related.en: flowers (in general) — collective: plants or a bouquet
blossoms, individual flowers — countable, on a plant

note: Цве̑ће is a singular neuter noun: it has no plural.

examples.en: Here are your books.
Here he is, he came!
There they are on the table.

related.en: here is — an object near the speaker
here is — an object near the listener; «here he is» when someone was awaited
there is, over there — far from both

note: With a pronoun the short form is used: е̏во га, е̏то га, е̏но га.

examples.en: I saw him just now.
I arrived a little before you.

related.en: just now — one word: a recent moment in the past
a little earlier — a comparison in time, usually with something

note: After ма̏ло пре̏ comes the genitive: ма̏ло пре̏ по́дне, ма̏ло пре̏ те̏бе.

examples.sr: [И̏ако] је био уморан, наставио је да ради.
examples.en: Although he was tired, he kept working.

examples.sr: [И а̏ко] буде падала киша, ићи ћемо.
examples.en: Even if it rains, we'll go.

related.en: although — a concessive conjunction, written as one word
even if — «и» plus the conditional «ако», written as two words

note: И̏ако can be replaced by ма̏да: ма̏да је би̏о у̏мо̄ран.

examples.en: He learned the poem by heart.
It never occurred to me.

related.en: by heart — an adverb, written as one word
to mind, into one's head — a preposition plus a noun

note:
Set expressions:
• па̏сти на па̏ме̄т, до́ћи на па̏ме̄т - «to come to mind»
• зна̏ти на̏паме̄т - «to know by heart»

examples.en: It was a nice afternoon.
I'll come after noon.

related.en: after noon — an expression of time, two words

note: A synonym of the adverb is попо́дне: до́ћи ћу попо́дне - «I'll come in the afternoon».

examples.en: Clothes are cheap in this store.
I found an apartment at a good price.
Prices in small shops are affordable.

related.en: cheap — simply a low price, sometimes hinting at quality
favorable, good-value — the price is right and the terms are good
affordable — a price a person can afford

note: The opposite is ску̑п («expensive»).

examples.en: I'm late because there's a traffic jam.
Are you hungry?

related.en: because — a causal conjunction; can be replaced by «зато што»
question particle — a colloquial form of «је ли»

note: They cannot be swapped. You often hear јел тако? - «isn't that so?»

examples.en: Send me a picture from the wedding.
This photograph was taken in 1990.

related.en: picture, painting, photo — the broad word
photograph — a picture taken with a camera

note: Every фотогра̀фија is a сли̏ка, but not the other way round. «To take a photo of» is сли̏кати or фотогра̀фисати: сликај ме - «take my picture».

examples.en: Paying money into the account is free.
Salary is paid on the fifth of the month.

related.en: payment in, deposit — money is put in
payment out, payout — money is handed out: salary, pension

note: The verbs are у̀платити and испла́тити. «To withdraw money from an account» is по̀дићи но̀вац.

examples.en: I hung a picture on the wall.
They fell out for no reason.
Don't pick a fight with him.

related.en: to hang up — to hang or attach on purpose: a picture, a poster
to hang, to hook — also: to snag, to catch an illness, to pick a quarrel

note: Зака̏чити фа̑јл - «to attach a file». In the sense «to hang» the two verbs are almost interchangeable, and ока̏чити has no other meanings.

examples.en: This is her book.
This is for her.
I love her.
He saw her.

related.en: her, hers (possessive) — changes with gender and number: «њена књига»
her (full accusative form) — after a preposition, at the start of a phrase, for emphasis
her (short accusative form) — the usual unstressed clitic, in second position
her (clitic before «је») — replaces «је» next to the auxiliary «је»

note: «To her» (dat.): the short form is јој, the full form њо̑ј.

cyr: немој · не смеш · не мораш · не треба
acc: не̏мој · не сме̑ш · не мо̑ра̄ш · не тре́ба
meanings: немој, не смеш, не мораш or не треба?

examples.sr: [Не̏мојте] бринути, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
You can't park here.
You don't have to pay right away.

examples.sr: [Не тре́ба] да купујеш хлеб, имамо га.
examples.en: You don't need to buy bread, we have some.

related.en: don't — a direct prohibition or request; «немојте» is the polite form and the plural
you must not, you're not allowed — a taboo, a rule, the law
you don't have to — you may skip it
no need to — there is no point or necessity

note: As in English, «must not» and «don't have to» differ: не мо̑ра̄ш - «you don't have to», не сме̑ш - «you must not».

cyr: смејати се · насмејати се · осмехнути се · смешити се
acc: смѐјати се · насмѐјати се · осмѐхнути се · сме́шити се
meanings: смејати се, насмејати се, осмехнути се or смешити се?

examples.en: The kids are laughing loudly in the yard.

examples.sr: Сви су се [насмѐјали] кад је испричао виц.
examples.en: Everyone burst out laughing when he told the joke.
She just smiled and walked past.
He has been smiling mysteriously all day.

related.en: to laugh — loudly and for a long time
to burst out laughing — the start of laughter, a reaction to a joke
to smile (once) — quickly, without a sound
to smile (for a while) — to keep a smile on one's face

note: Nouns: сме̑х - «laughter», о̏сме̄х - «smile».

examples.en: Put the book on the table.
Put the bag down on the floor.
I passed the exam yesterday.

related.en: to put, to place, to put on — the universal verb
to lower, to put down — downward movement
to pass (an exam), to lay — formal

note: Поло̀жити has the imperfective пола́гати: пола́гати ѝспит - «to take an exam».

examples.en: I ordered a pizza.
Tell him to wait for me.
Can you recommend a restaurant?
I need to book a doctor's appointment.

related.en: to order (goods, a service) — the main verb for ordering: food, shoes online
to tell, to send word, to entrust — «поручи му да...»
to recommend — to suggest a film, a restaurant, a book
to schedule, to book — an appointment, a meeting

note: A table is reserved like this: резѐрвисати сто̑.

examples.en: May I open the window?

examples.sr: Не [мо̀гу] да отворим прозор, заглављен је.
examples.en: I can't open the window, it's stuck.

examples.sr: Нико није [смѐо] да јој каже истину.
examples.en: Nobody dared to tell her the truth.

related.en: to be allowed, to dare — permission, rules, etiquette, courage
can, to be able to — physical possibility, ability

note: In a polite request both work: могу ли да седнем? and смем ли да седнем? The difference is clear in the negative: не сме̑м - «I'm not allowed», не мо̀гу - «I can't (it doesn't work)».

examples.en: The dog is man's best friend.
Whose dog is this?
Give this meat to your doggie.
Look what a cute puppy!

related.en: doggie, pup — affectionate, also of an adult dog

note: A puppy is штѐне. Ку̏чка is a «bitch», with a rude shade.

meanings: близу, недалеко од, поред or око?

examples.en: The house is near the school.
The hotel is not far from the center.
The pharmacy is next to the post office.
The children are running around the table.

related.en: not far from — almost the same as «близу»; «од» is required
next to, beside — right next to: «поред прозора»
around; about — around something or approximately: «око стола», «око сат времена»

note: Поред тога - «besides that, in addition».

examples.en: I have enough time for work.
I have quite a lot of time.
Enough!

related.en: enough (for a purpose) — whether there is enough for something: «имам довољно времена»
a lot, quite a lot; enough — quantity

note: Compare: до̏ста до̀бро - «quite good», до̏во̄љно до̀бро - «good enough» for the job.

examples.en: Do you understand Spanish?

examples.sr: Управо сам [схва̀тио] где сам оставио кључеве.
examples.en: I just realized where I left my keys.

related.en: to understand — a process: a deep understanding of a language, logic, feelings
to grasp, to realize — in a moment, a sudden realization; perfective

note: Схва̏тити also means «to take, to perceive»: схва̏тити о̏збӣљно - «to take seriously».

examples.en: I did it myself.
He just wanted to ask.
A man walked into the post office.

related.en: «I am» (from «бити») / alone, by oneself — an auxiliary verb and an adjective
only, just — an adverb, does not change
one; a, a certain — a numeral and an indefinite «some»: «једна», «једно»

note: Сам occurs twice: in урадио сам то сам the first is «I am», the second «myself».

examples.en: Buy anything, I'm hungry.

examples.sr: [Шта̏ го̏д] да се деси, остани миран.
examples.en: Whatever happens, stay calm.

related.en: anyone, anything, any — it does not matter which
whoever, whatever — a concession or a generalization

note: Било goes before the question word: било где, било како. Го̏д goes after: где̏ го̏д, кад год.

examples.en: Are you coming tomorrow?
They gave me a book.

related.en: question particle «ли» — always two words in questions

note: A question can also be asked without да ли: долазиш ли сутра?

examples.en: This year we're going to the book fair.
At the New Year's fair we drink mulled wine.

related.en: fair, exhibition (trade) — business: buying and selling, presentations, forums
fair (funfair) — for fun: cotton candy, carousels, souvenirs

note:
Typical combinations:
• са́јам књи̏га - book fair, сајам аутомобила - car show
• новогодишњи вашар - New Year's fair

examples.en: Where are you traveling from?
Where did you get the money?

related.en: where from (cause, source) — colloquial, with a touch of surprise
where from (from which place) — neutral, about a place

note: О̀ткуд is common in short questions: о̀ткуд зна̑ш? - «how do you know?», о̀ткуд ти о́вде? - «what are you doing here?»

examples.en: Give me a piece of the cake.
We bought three items of clothing.

related.en: piece, item — an object as a unit: «комад сапуна»
piece, slice — a cut-off part of a whole: «парче торте», «парче пице»

note: Ко̀ма̄д also means «a stage play»: позоришни комад. The rule is not strict.

examples.en: She opened a jar of ajvar.
Open a can of beans.
I drank a can of Coke.

note: A bottle is фла̏ша or бо̏ца.

examples.en: Let's get out of the sun, into the shade.
His shadow could be seen on the wall.

related.en: shade — a cool spot out of the sun: «у хладу»
shadow (silhouette) — the dark image of an object on a surface

note: Се̑нка is also used figuratively: сенка сумње - «a shadow of doubt».

examples.en: My uncle on my mother's side lives in Belgrade.
My uncle on my father's side brought me a present.
The man at the kiosk sells newspapers.

related.en: uncle, mister — not a relative, a way to address an adult man

note:
Uncles and aunts by marriage:
• wife of ујак - у̏јна
• wife of стриц - стри̑на
• husband of an aunt - те́так or те̏ча

cyr: промислити · размислити · смислити · измислити · осмислити · замислити
acc: про̀мислити · размѝслити · смѝслити · измѝслити · осмѝслити · замѝслити

examples.en: Think it over carefully before you decide.
I'll think about it.
I came up with a nickname for the dog.
Who invented the telephone?
They devised a new advertising campaign.
Just imagine we were millionaires!

related.en: to think over, think through — weigh something in advance
to come up with — find an idea
to make up, invent; to lie
to devise, work out — think through in detail

note: One more verb of this family: предо̀мислити се - to change one's mind.

examples.en: Which juice do you want?
What is this juice like?

related.en: what kind of, what ... like — the quality of a thing

note: Ка̀ка̄в is also used in exclamations: ка̀ка̄в да̑н! - «what a day!»

meanings: пријатељ, друг, познаник, ортак or бураз?

examples.en: He's my best friend.
A friend of mine gave me this book.
He's just an acquaintance.
Buddy, come over for coffee!
Hey, bro, where have you been?

related.en: friend, close friend — a long-standing, close person
friend, pal (друг m., другарица f.) — a good acquaintance who may become a пријатељ
buddy, partner — colloquial: a mate or a friend
bro, buddy — an informal way to address a friend

note: A group of friends is дру́штво or еки́па. To become friends is спријатѐљити се.

cyr: зато · зато што · јер · због тога што · пошто
acc: за̀то̄ · за̀то̄ што̏ · је̏р · збо̏г то́га што̏ · по̏што
meanings: зато, зато што, јер or пошто?

examples.en: It's late, so I'm going home.
I'm not going because I'm sick.
I'm going home because it's late.

examples.sr: [Збо̏г то́га што̏] је падала киша, утакмица је отказана.
examples.en: Because it was raining, the match was canceled.
Since it's late, I'm going home.

related.en: so, that's why — the result after the cause
because — the cause after the result
because, for — neutral, with a hint of «since»
because of the fact that — more formal
since, as — the cause stands at the beginning of the sentence

note: Trap: по̏што in a question means «how much»: по̏што је си̏р? - «how much is the cheese?»

examples.en: We like to talk over coffee.
We like to chat over coffee.
Don't babble so much.
The bishop addressed the faithful.

related.en: to chat — a pleasant unhurried conversation
to babble, chatter — a lot and without much meaning, colloquial
to give a talk, address — bookish, solemn, rare

note:
Related words:
• бѐседа - a formal speech, sermon
• брбљѝвац - chatterbox

key: cmp:зајебавам се-зезам се-спрдам се-шалим се / шајем се
cyr: шалим се / шајем се · зезам се · спрдам се · зајебавам се
acc: ша̏лим се / ша̏јем се · зе̏зам се · спр̏дам се · зајѐбавам се

examples.en: I'm joking, don't be angry.
I'm just kidding.

examples.sr: Не [спр̏дај] се с њим, осетљив је.
examples.en: Don't make fun of him, he's sensitive.
Are you kidding me?

related.en: to kid, joke around — colloquial, friendly tone
to tease, mock — a bit rude

note: Ша́ла - «a joke, a jest», ви̏ц - «a joke (a funny story)».

meanings: «Be quiet» in Serbian: ћути, утишај се, умукни

examples.en: Be quiet, please, I'm trying to study.
Kids, quiet down, the baby is sleeping.
Shut up, I didn't ask you!

related.en: to be silent — neutral, both a request and a statement
to quiet down, speak more quietly — about volume: noisy kids, a too-loud argument
to shut up — rude; not said to elders or people you barely know

note:
Утишати се asks to lower the noise, not to stop talking.

У̀мукнути easily causes a conflict; with «бре» it sounds even more aggressive.

cyr: оговорити · надговорити · наговорити · уговорити · одговорити · изговорити · приговорити · договорити се
acc: ого̀ворити · надго̀ворити · наго̀ворити · уго̀ворити · одго̀ворити · изго̀ворити · прѝговорити · до̀говорити се

examples.en: Someone badmouthed me to the boss.

examples.sr: Никад га нећеш [надго̀ворити], увек има последњу реч.
examples.en: You'll never outtalk him, he always has the last word.

examples.sr: Пријатељи су ме [наго̀ворили] да пробам рафтинг.
examples.en: My friends talked me into trying rafting.
We arranged a meeting for Monday.
I didn't know what to answer.

examples.sr: Тешко ми је да [изго̀ворим] ово име.
examples.en: It's hard for me to pronounce this name.
Nobody dared to talk back to the director.

examples.sr: [Догово̀рили] смо се да почнемо у осам.
examples.en: We agreed to start at eight.

related.en: to badmouth, gossip — speak ill of a person behind their back
to outtalk — get the upper hand in an argument, speak more convincingly or longer
to talk into — persuade someone to do something
to arrange, agree on — a date, a price, a meeting
to answer — give an answer to a question
to pronounce — a word, a name
to object, talk back — make a remark
to agree, come to an agreement

note:
The prefix changes the meaning completely. Do not mix up нагово̀рити («to talk into», persuade) and угово̀рити («to arrange»).

Догово̀рити without «се» means to finish saying something.

examples.en: - Thanks! - You're welcome!
A glass of water, please.
- Masha! - Yes?
Here you are, your water.
Please, have a seat.

related.en: please; you're welcome; yes? / pardon? — in reply to thanks and to a call, to begin a request, to ask someone to repeat
here you are, please — when offering or inviting

note: Изволите is said by the one who offers; in a shop the customer replies: «са̏мо да по̀гледа̄м» («I'm just looking»).

examples.en: What did you eat for breakfast?
Lunch will be ready at two.
I'll take an apple for a snack.
Tonight we're having dinner at Grandma's.

related.en: snack, afternoon snack — an apple, a banana; the verb ужинати means «to have a snack»

note:
Main trap: у̏жина is not dinner but a light snack between lunch and dinner. Dinner is вѐчера.

Colloquial: кло́па - food, кло́пати - to chow down.

examples.en: Which letter is missing?
«Mama» is a word of four letters.
There is cool shade under the old beech.

note:
сло̏во means a letter and ре̑ч a word, while бу̏ква is a beech tree.

A handy phrase to remember: «Ма̏ма је ре̑ч од чѐтири сло̑ва̄».

examples.en: Mom does the laundry every week.
Dad is peeling potatoes for lunch.
She wipes the dust every day.
I have to scrub the bathtub.

related.en: to wash — dishes, hands, hair, laundry, windows, a car
to clean; to peel — an apartment, a room, shoes, vegetables
to wipe — dust, a floor, a table

note:
Teeth are «washed»: пра̏ти зу̑бе (to brush one's teeth). Shoes are «cleaned»: чистити обућу.

To tidy up a room is спре́мати со̏бу.

meanings: чаша, бокал, шоља or кригла: which vessel?

examples.en: Bring me a glass of wine.
The waiter brought a jug of water.
I'll have another cup of coffee.
We ordered two mugs of beer.

related.en: glass (wine glass, tumbler, shot glass) — named after the drink: чаша вина, чаша воде, чаша ракије
jug, pitcher, carafe — for water, juice or wine on the table
cup, mug with a handle — tea, coffee

note: A glass of wine is ча̏ша вина, while бо̀ка̄л вина is a whole jug of wine.

examples.en: I'm making lunch for the guests.
What are you doing tonight?
She works as a secretary.

related.en: to make, create, cook — when something comes into being as a result
to do, work — be busy with something

note: Something comes into being - пра̏вити: coffee, lunch, cakes, noise, problems. An activity or a job - ра́дити: homework, work.

examples.en: I'll try to pass the exam.
I'll make an effort to come on time.

related.en: to try, attempt — the result is unclear
to make an effort, try hard — the stress is on the effort

note: Both are usually followed by «да» and the present tense: по̀кушати да, потру́дити се да.

examples.en: I bought two tickets to Belgrade.
A museum ticket costs five hundred dinars.

related.en: ticket — for transport and for events; also a map or a playing card
admission ticket — for a concert, a match, a museum

note: For transport only ка̑рта is used, for example повратна карта - a round-trip ticket. For a concert or a museum both ка̑рта and у̀лазница work.

examples.en: He is the only son in the family.
