It's a unique opportunity!
The child has a room of his own.

related.en: only, sole — једини син «only son», једина си ми «you're all I have»
united, single; unique — јединствена држава «a united country»
separate; special — посебна соба «a separate room», посебне потребе «special needs»

note: Common mistake: for «only» use јѐдӣнӣ; једѝнствен is closer to «united» or «unique».

examples.en: - Would you like some coffee? - Yes, thank you.
- Would you like some coffee? - No, thank you.

related.en: thank you, yes — accepting an offer
thank you, no — a polite refusal, or thanks for something

note: This is the rule taught at school. In practice many people do not follow it, and the meaning is clear from the intonation.

examples.en: I have a dog at home.
I'm going for a walk with the dog.
Our doggy loves to play.
We have a puppy at home.

note: Forms: па̏с, gen. пса̏; ку̏че, gen. кучета; ку́ца, acc. куцу. Па̀шче is a rare word.

examples.en: The film made a good impression.

examples.sr: Твоје мишљење има велики [у̏тица̄ј] на њега.
examples.en: Your opinion has a big influence on him.

related.en: impression; imprint — оставити утисак, стећи утисак «to make an impression, to get an impression»
influence — имати утицај на некога «to have an influence on someone»

note: They sound alike. У̀тисак is what stays in your mind, у̏тица̄ј is an effect on someone or something. У̏тица̄ј is followed by «на» with the accusative: утицај на одлуку.

examples.en: The kids dye eggs for Easter.
I'm afraid of dogs.

related.en: to paint, dye, color — eggs, hair
to be afraid — with the genitive

note: In the present tense the forms look alike: бојим - «I dye», бојим се - «I'm afraid». Only «се» tells them apart.

examples.en: What time does class start?
What time is it now?
I've been waiting for him for a whole hour.

related.en: class, lesson; moment; o'clock — in formal time-telling
clock, watch; hour — as a length of time

note: The time is usually asked with са̑т: колико је сати? («what time is it?»). Ча̏с in a precise time is formal: у 22 ча̏са и 15 мину́та.

examples.en: I didn't hear well.

examples.sr: Он само [ћу̏ти] и гледа кроз прозор.
examples.en: He just keeps quiet and looks out of the window.
Look after the child until I come back.

related.en: to hear — ништа не чујем «I can't hear anything»
to keep, guard, look after — пас чува кућу «the dog guards the house»

note: They sound alike but mean different things. Easy to mix up: чуо - «heard» and чувао - «kept, looked after».

key: cmp:изути / изувати-обути / обувати-обући / облачити-скинути / скидати-ставити / стављати
cyr: обући / облачити · обути / обувати · ставити / стављати · скинути / скидати · изути / изувати
acc: обу́ћи / обла́чити · о̀бути / обу́вати · ста̏вити / ста́вљати · ски̏нути / ски́дати · ѝзути / изу́вати

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
Put on your shoes, we're in a hurry.
Put on a hat, it's snowing.
Take off those wet socks.
Please take off your shoes at the entrance.

related.en: to put on clothes; to dress someone — a jacket, a sweater, a T-shirt
to put on shoes — shoes, sneakers, heels
to put on an accessory; to put, place — glasses, a hat, a ring, a watch, lipstick
to take off — clothes, glasses, a hat; to undress

note: Clothes - обу́ћи, shoes - о̀бути, jewelry and headwear - ста̏вити. Any item can be taken off with ски̏нути, and shoes also with ѝзути.

examples.en: Joking aside!
Open your book to page thirty.

examples.sr: Он је [стра́нац], али добро говори српски.
examples.en: He's a foreigner, but he speaks Serbian well.
Clients are received from 12 to 2 p.m.
Serbia is a small country.

related.en: side; page; flank — са стране «from the side», на све стране «on all sides»
page — of a book, a website
political party; client, visitor of an office

note: A country is зѐмља, not стра́на: стра́на зѐмља - «a foreign country», страни језик - «a foreign language».

examples.en: She got a nice tan at the seaside.
Wow, you're so tanned!
You really got a tan at the seaside!

related.en: to get tanned — the neutral word
to get dark, get very tanned — colloquial
to get a tan (literally «to get color») — as a compliment

note: Поцр̀нети literally means «to turn black» and is colloquial. Добити боју is most often said after a vacation.

cyr: бацити · набацити · убацити · избацити · пребацити · одбацити
acc: ба́цити · наба́цити · уба́цити · изба́цити · преба́цити · одба́цити

examples.en: He threw the ball over the fence.
Over the winter I put on a few kilos.
Insert the card into the ATM.
They kicked him out of the club.
Transfer the money to my account.
Drop me off at work, please.

related.en: to throw on; to put on (weight)
to put in, insert; to throw in
to throw out, kick out; to dispense (of an ATM)
to throw over; to transfer (money); to reproach
to throw away, reject; to give someone a lift

note:
The prefix gives the direction:
• на- - on top of something
• «у-» - inside
• из- - out
• пре- - across, to another place
• од- - away, aside

examples.en: The little boy lost his ball.
My boyfriend works at a bank.
That young man is a medical student.
That guy is my neighbor.

note: «Boyfriend» is де̏чко or мо̀мак, «girlfriend» is дѐво̄јка.

examples.en: My family lives in Niš.
The whole extended family comes to the slava.

related.en: family — parents and children, the close circle
relatives, extended family — grandparents, aunts, cousins

note: A family name (surname) is прѐзиме, not фамилија.

examples.en: My uncle on my father's side lives in Novi Sad.
My uncle on my mother's side is a doctor.

related.en: uncle on the father's side, father's brother
uncle on the mother's side, mother's brother

note: The wife of стриц is стри̑на, the wife of ујак is у̏јна.

examples.en: On Saturday there's a wedding ceremony at the church.
I was at a friend's wedding.
We're going to the best man's wedding.

related.en: wedding ceremony; marriage — church or civil
wedding guests; wedding — идемо у сватове «we're going to a wedding»

note: Венча́ње is only the ceremony. The whole celebration is сва̀дба, and сва̑тови are also the guests on the groom's side.

meanings: брдо, брег, планина, стена or зид?

examples.en: We live at the foot of a hill.
The house stands on a hill.
We'll spend the summer in the mountains.

examples.sr: Пењачи су се попели уз стрму [сте̑ну].
examples.en: The climbers scaled a steep rock face.
We hung a picture on the wall.

related.en: hill, small mountain — a modest elevation; брдо ствари «a heap of things»
mountain — a big one, often forested
wall — of a building, a fence

note: A wall is зи̑д, while сте́на is a rock. A shore is о̏бала; бре̑г is a hill, not a bank.

examples.en: What a disgrace!
Aren't you ashamed to lie?
I blushed with shame.
We made a complete fool of ourselves at the match.

related.en: disgrace, shame — verbs брукати, обрукати се
shame — the feeling; стидим се «I'm ashamed», стидљив «shy»

note: Срамо̀та is shame about an action, сти̑д is only the feeling. Бру̏ка and блама́жа are more colloquial.

key: cmp:згодно ми је-одговара ми-таман ми је
cyr: одговара ми · таман ми је · згодно ми је
acc: одго̀вара ми · та́ма̄н ми је · зго̏дно ми је

examples.en: The size doesn't suit me.
This dress fits me just right.

examples.sr: Да ли ти је [зго̏дно] у четири?
examples.en: Is four o'clock convenient for you?

related.en: it suits me — size, color, price, time
it fits me just right — only about size
it's convenient for me — in time and place

note: Зго̏дан said of a person means «good-looking»: згодна девојка. It is not said that way about a dress.

examples.en: We bought a kilo of plums at the market.
Grandpa drinks plum brandy after lunch.
The neighbor makes grape brandy.

examples.sr: Најбоља је [ви̏шњевача] коју прави моја тетка.
examples.en: The best is the cherry brandy my aunt makes.

related.en: plum — the fruit; sometimes the brandy too
plum brandy — the classic rakija made from plums

note: Rakija is often named after the fruit. Ка̀јсија (apricot), ду̏ња (quince), кру̏шка (pear) are both the fruit and the rakija: «попићемо кајсију» - we'll have some apricot rakija. Rakija from Williams pears is виљамовка.

examples.en: I love you.
Kiss me!
Okay, bye, kisses!

related.en: to love, like — a person, a thing, food
to kiss — љубити се means «to kiss each other»
kisses, I kiss you — a fond goodbye; not a declaration of love

note: Trap: «to love» is во̀лети, while љу́бити is first of all «to kiss».

examples.en: Next Wednesday we're going to the movies.
Last Friday I was in Niš.
Next week we're going to the seaside.
My future husband is from Niš.

related.en: future — about a distant or abstract future

note: A day of the week or a period goes into the genitive without a preposition: претходне среде, наредног петка.

examples.en: Poor mother of mine, she works all day.
That is a poor family.

related.en: pitiful, poor (unfortunate) — someone to be pitied; јадница «poor thing»

note: Only сиро̀машан is used about poverty. Јадна is easily understood as «she is in a bad way», not «she has no money».

examples.en: I paid property tax.
The bank received a payment order.
I read a good review of that book.
The traffic officer gave me a fine.

related.en: order, instruction; account — налог за плаћање «payment order», налог на сајту «account on a website»
presentation, review — приказ књиге «a book review»
punishment, fine — новчана казна «a monetary fine»

note: Tax is по̀рез; на́лог is an order or an account. При́каз means a presentation or review, ка̏зна a punishment or fine.

cyr: само · тек · само што · само што није
acc: са̏мо · те̏к · са̏мо што̏ · са̏мо што̏ нѝје

examples.en: I did only one task.
I've done only one task so far.
I had just got home.
He's just about to leave.

related.en: only, just — and nothing more: a limitation, an exception
only, just; just now — so far only this stage has been reached
just now — about a recent event

note: Са̏мо јѐдан зада́так - one and nothing more. Те̏к јѐдан зада́так - only one so far, more to come.

key: cmp:недостајеш ми-ужелео сам те се-фалиш ми-чезнем за тобом
cyr: недостајеш ми · фалиш ми · ужелео сам те се · чезнем за тобом
acc: недо̀стајеш ми · фа̏лиш ми · ужѐлео сам те се · че̏знем за то̏бо̄м

examples.en: I miss you so much.
I miss you.
How I've missed you!
I long for you every day.

related.en: I miss you, I'm missing you — neutral and the most common
I've missed you — after a long separation
I long for you — bookish, strong yearning

note: The sentence is built the other way round: the subject is the person who is missed. Недостајеш ми literally means «you are lacking to me».

examples.en: We bought a pumpkin for the soup.
Grandma wears a new fur coat.
Grandpa wears a fur hat when it's cold.

note: They sound alike, so keep them apart: a fur coat is бу̑нда, while шу̀бара is a hat.

examples.en: He is good at doing math in his head.
The kids are counting apples.
I'm counting on him.

related.en: to calculate, do sums in your head; to count on — рачунати на некога «to count on someone»
to count objects, list — броји до десет «count to ten», наброј градове «name some cities»

note: Рачу̀нати comes from ра̀чӯн (account, calculation), бро̀јати from бро̑ј (number). Related words: рачу̀на̄р - computer, рачуново̀дство - accounting, бројаница - rosary.

examples.en: Thank you very much!
- Would you like some coffee? - Yes, thank you.
- Would you like some coffee? - No, thank you.
I'm grateful to you.

related.en: thank you, yes — as a rule, accepting an offer
thank you, no — as a rule, a polite refusal

note: You can strengthen хва́ла like this: хва́ла ле̑по, хвала најлепше, пу̏но хва́ла. Not everyone keeps the distinction between захваљујем and захваљујем се.

examples.en: This is my new car.
The wheel fell off the bicycle.

related.en: car — plural only, neuter: ова кола «this car»
wheel — a single one; pl. точкови

examples.en: He plays chess with his grandfather.
I like to dance at weddings.
The children are playing with a ball.
Today we're playing store.

related.en: to play (a game, a sport); to dance; to act (a role)
to dance — sounds less common than играти
to play, frolic — with a toy, in a children's game

note: Ѝграти without «се» is used for sports, cards, chess, a role, and also for a dance: ѝграти ко̏ло. With «се» it is children's games and fun: и̏гра̄мо се ра́та - we're playing war.

examples.sr: То је била само [ша́ла], не љути се.
examples.en: It was just a joke, don't be angry.
A real crush started in front of the stage.

examples.sr: Ово је био јак [шу̏т] ка голу.
examples.en: That was a strong shot at the goal.

related.en: joke — the ordinary word: без шале «no kidding», шалити се «to joke»
crush, shoving in front of the stage at a rock concert — slang
kick at the ball, shot — шутирати, шутнути «to shoot, to kick»

note: The ordinary word for a joke is ша́ла. Шу̏тка is a different word.

examples.en: Last night we talked for a long time.
Tonight we're going to Grandma's.
I didn't sleep well last night.

related.en: tonight, last night — the night just past or the one coming

note: The line between evening and night is fuzzy, and even Serbs struggle to say when но̀ћас is. It is simpler to use си̏но̄ћ for the past and вечѐрас for the future.

meanings: обићи, посетити, свратити or наћи се?

examples.sr: [О̀бишла] сам баку и донела јој лекове.
examples.en: I went to see Grandma and brought her medicine.
We'll visit you on Saturday.
Yesterday I dropped by Grandma's.

examples.sr: [На̏шла] сам се са баком у граду.
examples.en: I met Grandma in town.

related.en: to check in on, look in on — make sure everything is fine; to walk around
to visit, pay a visit — neutral or formal
to drop by — briefly, on the way, without a plan

note: All four mean some kind of visiting or meeting, but they differ in the plan: свра́тити - no plan, на́ћи се - only by arrangement.

examples.sr: Ја сам гладна, [а] Игор је жедан.
examples.en: I'm hungry, and Igor is thirsty.
I didn't see it, I heard it.
She is taller than Svetlana.

related.en: and, but — contrast after a positive statement

note: After a negative use не̏го instead of «а»: нисам гладна, него уморна - «I'm not hungry, but tired». A memory aid: «минус, него плус».

key: cmp:не хоће да знају-неће да знају-неће знати
cyr: неће да знају · неће знати · не хоће да знају
acc: не̏ће да зна̏јӯ · не̏ће зна̏ти · не хо̀ће да зна̏јӯ
meanings: неће да знају or неће знати?

examples.en: He doesn't want to go to Moscow.
They won't know the answer.
I don't want to know anything about it.

related.en: they don't want to know — refusal, unwillingness
a mistake — not said this way in Serbian

note: The negative of хте̏ти is written as one word: не́ћу, неће. «Doesn't want to do» takes неће да with the present tense, while неће with an infinitive means «will not do».

examples.en: We put the shelf in the corner of the room.
I buy cigarettes at the kiosk on the corner.
We made a play corner.

related.en: corner, angle — neutral, also in geometry

note: Ћо̀шак is most often the corner of a street or room in everyday speech. Ку́так is less common, usually with a purpose: ку́так за и̏гру - a play corner.

examples.en: We're flying to Rome via Frankfurt.
The technician ran the cable through the hallway.

related.en: across, over; via an intermediate point

note: Different cases follow: пре̏ко takes the genitive, кроз the accusative.

examples.en: I have to wash the floor.
Mom is scrubbing the bathtub.
Every morning she wipes the dust off the shelves.
Every morning I mop the hall.

related.en: to wash — the general verb: a floor, dishes
to scrub — thoroughly, with a brush or cloth
to wipe — with a damp or dry cloth

note: Nearby: усиса́вати - to vacuum, метлати - to sweep a yard or garage.

examples.en: You could at least have let me know.
Come for a short while at least.
She didn't even look at me.

related.en: at least — the minimum that could be expected
at least, even if — a concession, a minimal condition

note: Ба̑р often sounds like a reproach: «you could at least have said so».

meanings: иако, упркос or без обзира на?

examples.sr: Све је прошло одлично, [и̏ако] смо очекивали најгоре.
examples.en: Everything went great, although we expected the worst.
He recovered quickly in spite of the doctor's prognosis.

examples.sr: Воз је стигао на време [без о̏бзира на] кашњење.
examples.en: The train arrived on time despite the delay.

note: И̏ако introduces a clause. У̏пркос takes the dative: упркос прогнози. Без о̀бзира на takes the accusative: без обзира на кашњење.

meanings: више or виши? боље or бољи?

examples.en: I like tea more than coffee.
He is taller than his brother.
I feel better today.
He is a better student than I am.
Dragan is the tallest in the class.
He is the one I love most.

related.en: taller, higher — adjective from «висок»; највиши - tallest
better — adjective from «добар»; најбољи - the best

note: Ви̏ше̄ and бо̏ље̄ are adverbs, ви̏шӣ and бо̏љӣ are adjectives. Do not mix up ви̏ше̄ (more) and ви̏шӣ (taller).

examples.en: The child picked a flower.
I have to tidy up the room.

related.en: to pick, to gather — flowers, fruit; убрати шљиве
to tidy up, to put in order; to prepare — спремити собу, спремити ручак

note: У̀брати is to pick or gather a crop, not to tidy up: for that use спре́мити.

examples.en: I bought a pair of shoes.
Steam is coming out of the pot.
I don't have the money for that.
Smoke is coming out of the chimney.

related.en: pair; a couple, a few — брачни пар, пар дана

note: The plural па̏ре «money» has the genitive пара: немам пара - «I have no money».

cyr: предлагати / предложити · нудити / понудити · понудити некога нечим
acc: предла́гати / предло̀жити · ну̏дити / по̀нудити · по̀нудити не̏кога не̏чим

examples.sr: Марко ми је [предло̀жио] да идемо на планину.
examples.en: Marko suggested that we go to the mountains.
They offered me a good job.
She treated us to cakes.

related.en: to suggest, to propose — an idea, advice, a candidate
to offer something concrete — a job, help, a price, marriage
to offer someone food or drink — понудити госта колачем

note: To offer coffee or a treat is по̀нудити, not предло̀жити, and the thing offered is in the instrumental: по̀нудити не̏кога не̏чим.

cyr: прав, права, право · прави · право · право
acc: пра̏в, пра̀ва, пра́во · пра̑вӣ · пра́во · пра́во

examples.en: Draw a straight line.
He is a true friend.
He is studying law in Belgrade.
Go straight to the traffic light.

related.en: law; right (noun) — студирати право, имати право

note: One form, many meanings: the context decides. Trap: пра̑вӣ means «real», not «correct»: a correct answer is та̏чан о̏дгово̄р.

examples.sr: Он је [љу̏бомо̄ран] јер му жена прича са колегом.
examples.en: He is jealous because his wife is chatting with a colleague.
He looks at her with envy.

related.en: jealousy — of a person, in love; љубоморан је на брата
envy — of someone else's things, success; завидети некоме

note: Strictly, љубо̀мора is jealousy and за́вист is envy, but in speech љу̏бомо̄ран is often said of envy too.

examples.en: This milk is good until tomorrow.
It's no use, you can't get through.
We'll have coffee on Saturday, okay?

related.en: to be good, fit for use; ought to — ово млеко ваља до сутра
to be worth; to be of use — овај прстен вреди 200 евра
to be valid, in force; okay, deal — пасош важи до...

note: Ваља also means «should»: ваљало би, ваља се. Не ваља is «no good»: не ваља ти то. Не вреди is «no use, pointless».

examples.en: The customer is satisfied.
There are a lot of swimmers at the beach.
I bought a new swimsuit.

note: If the diacritics are dropped in Latin spelling, ку́пац and ку̀па̄ч look the same, and so do купачи and ку̀па̄ћӣ. Context tells them apart.

key: cmp:досадан-досадило ми је-досадно ми је-криво ми је-штета
cyr: досадно ми је · досадило ми је · досадан · штета · криво ми је
acc: до̏са̄дно ми је · до̀садило ми је · до̏са̄дан · ште̏та · кри̑во ми је
meanings: досадно, досадило, штета or криво ми је?

examples.en: I'm bored in class.
I'm tired of waiting.
This movie is boring.
It's a pity you can't come.

examples.sr: [Кри̑во] ми је што ниси могла да дођеш.
examples.en: I'm sorry you couldn't come.

related.en: I'm sick of it, I've had enough
boring; annoying — досадан филм, не буди досадан
I'm sorry, I feel bad about it

meanings: comfortable or convenient: удобан, одговара or згодно?

examples.en: This chair is very comfortable.

examples.sr: Да ли ти [одго̀вара] да се видимо у девет?
examples.en: Does it suit you to meet at nine?

examples.sr: Да ли ти је [зго̏дно] да се видимо сутра?
examples.en: Is it convenient for you to meet tomorrow?

related.en: it suits me, it's convenient for me — of time, conditions
it's convenient, it suits — of time, place

note: У̀добан is only about physical comfort. «Awkward, uncomfortable» in the social sense is не̏прија̄тно: осећам се непријатно.

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је] што смо се упознали.
examples.en: I'm very glad we met.
Thank you, and the same to you (enjoy your meal).

related.en: nice to meet you, glad — when being introduced
enjoy your meal; all the best — at the table, when parting

note: При̏ја̄тно is not said when meeting someone: «nice to meet you» is дра̑го ми је.

examples.en: What kind of clothes do you wear?
What is your favorite color?
Whose decision is it?

related.en: what kind of — by quality, properties
which, what — from a known set

note: All three decline like adjectives: by gender, number and case.

examples.en: What size are you?
Do you have size 39?

examples.sr: Ручни пртљаг не сме да прелази дозвољене [димѐнзије].
examples.en: Carry-on luggage must not exceed the permitted dimensions.

related.en: size in general — of clothes, things
size as a number; shoe size — број ципела

note: Димензије means only the dimensions of an object, not a clothing size.

cyr: зато што · јер · због тога што · зато · због
acc: за̀то̄ што̏ · је̏р · збо̏г то́га што̏ · за̀то̄ · збо̏г
meanings: зато што, јер, због тога што or зато?

examples.sr: Нисам те звао, [за̀то̄ што̏] је било касно.
examples.en: I didn't call you because it was late.
I didn't come because I was sick.

examples.sr: Закаснили смо [збо̏г то́га што̏] је била гужва.
examples.en: We were late because there was a traffic jam.
He was sick, so he didn't come.
We were late because of the traffic jam.

related.en: because, since — shorter, more common in speech

note: За̀то̄ means «so, that's why», not a conjunction of cause. Збо̏г is a preposition, због тога што a conjunction. More formal: по̏што, у̏след.

examples.en: The series is over.
Are you ready to go?
Lunch is ready, sit down.

related.en: done, finished — the process is complete, the result is in front of us
ready to start — everything is prepared for the action

note: Го̀тово also means «almost»: го̀тово бѐсплатно. Of lunch, both го̀тов and спре̏ман are used.

examples.en: The boss is on a business trip.
I'll take a week of vacation.
We're going on a summer vacation to Montenegro.
We're going on a winter vacation to Kopaonik.
The trip to Zagreb takes four hours.

related.en: vacation, time off; rest — узети одмор, бити на одмору
summer vacation — usually at the seaside
winter vacation — usually in the mountains, skiing

note: A business trip is a separate set phrase: слу̏жбенӣ пу̑т.

cyr: ујутру · преподне · у подне · поподне · послеподне · синоћ / вечерас / ноћас
acc: у̏јутру · препо́дне · у по́дне · попо́дне · послепо́дне · си̏но̄ћ / вечѐрас / но̀ћас
meanings: parts of the day: ујутру, преподне, подне, поподне, послеподне

examples.en: I drink coffee on the balcony in the morning.
The doctor sees patients only in the late morning.
We have lunch at exactly noon.
See you in the afternoon.
The kids come home from school in the late afternoon.
We were at the theater last night.

related.en: in the morning, roughly 3-9 a.m. — јуче ујутру
in the late morning, 9 a.m.-12 — no longer early morning
in the afternoon, 12-3 p.m. — right after noon
in the late afternoon, 3-6 p.m. — closer to evening
last night, yesterday evening / this evening / tonight

note: The hour boundaries are approximate. Trap: су̏тра means «tomorrow», not «in the morning»: «in the morning» is у̀јутру.

examples.sr: Како се зове она [ства̑р] за брисање пода?
examples.en: What's that thing for mopping the floor called?
This appliance makes shakes.

related.en: thing, item — any object; colloquially also «a song»

note: A mop or a coffee pot is not an у̏ређа̄ј: it is a ства̑р.

examples.en: Our driver is waiting in front of the hotel.
The guide showed us the fortress.
The TV host announced the guest.
I passed my driving test on the first try.

related.en: driver's license — short for возачка дозвола

note: The driver of a vehicle is во̀за̄ч, while во̀дитељ is the host of a program.

examples.en: I love you.
They kiss as they say goodbye.
I like you.

related.en: to love — a person, a thing, food
to kiss — љубити се means «to kiss each other»

note: Trap: «to love» is во̀лети, not љу́бити, which means «to kiss». With сви́ђати се, the person who likes is in the dative: свиђа ми се.

examples.en: The kids bop to the music.
We danced the kolo until morning.
They are dancing a waltz.

related.en: to dance — colloquial; on the spot, in time with fast music, of children
to dance — freely; a circle dance; fast couple dances
to dance — with choreography; slow couple dances

note: All three mean «to dance». Ѝграти and пле́сати are often interchangeable: Serbs themselves hardly distinguish the nuances.

cyr: викенд · слободан дан · празник · нерадни дан
acc: вѝкенд · сло̏бодан да̑н · пра̑знӣк · не̏радни да̑н
meanings: days off: викенд, слободан дан, празник or нерадни дан?

examples.en: We're going to the seaside for the weekend.

examples.sr: Не радим уторком, тада имам [сло̏бодан да̑н].
examples.en: I don't work on Tuesdays, that's my day off.

examples.sr: У уторак не радимо јер је државни [пра̑знӣк].
examples.en: We don't work on Tuesday because it's a public holiday.

examples.sr: Петак нам је [не̏радни да̑н] због празника.
examples.en: Friday is a non-working day for us because of the holiday.

related.en: weekend, Saturday and Sunday — за викенд, продужени викенд
a personal day off — even if it falls on a Wednesday
non-working day — official, usually because of a holiday

note: Вѝкенд is only Saturday and Sunday; the other words depend on the reason for the day off.

examples.en: At school the kids eat a snack.
I made a delicious dinner.

related.en: snack, afternoon snack — at school, between meals

note: У̏жина is a snack, not dinner: dinner is вѐчера.

examples.en: Draw it in pencil, then erase it.
Sign it with a ballpoint pen.

related.en: pencil — in conversation adults also use it for a pen

note: Strictly, о̀ло̄вка is a pencil, but someone who asks for an о̀ло̄вка often means a pen. If you need a pen, ask for a хемијска.

cyr: црно вино · бело вино · црвено вино
acc: цр̏но ви́но · бѐло ви́но · цр̏вено ви́но

examples.en: I drink red wine with meat.
White wine is better with fish.
Give us a bottle of red wine.

related.en: red wine — the more usual name, literally «black wine»
red wine — also understood, but less common

note: Serbs often call red wine literally «black»: црно вино.

examples.en: The flight to Belgrade takes two hours.
This summer we're going to the seaside.

note: The genitive of both words is лета; only the context tells them apart.

examples.en: We swam in the warm sea.
At night an awful nightmare tormented her.

note: The plural of мо̏ра is spelled like мо̑ре: моје море can mean «my nightmares».

examples.en: Our teacher is very patient.
The math teacher is strict.

note: Feminine forms: учитѐљица, на́ста̄вница.

examples.en: The city assembly approved the budget.

examples.sr: У [о̏пштини] се издају изводи из матичне књиге.
examples.en: Birth and marriage certificates are issued at the municipality office.
The local community council is organizing a meeting of residents.

related.en: municipality — also where marriages and births are registered
local community council — self-government of the residents of a neighborhood

note: Without any qualification, ску̏пштина usually means the national parliament, while скупштина града is the city assembly.

examples.en: My car is in the garage.
Your cola is cold.
They danced the kolo until midnight.
The second round is the hardest.

related.en: car; the drink cola — n. pl. or f. sg.
kolo, a circle folk dance; round — n.

note: Agreement shows the meaning: ко̏ла су но̑ва - the car (pl.), кола је хладна - the drink (sg.).

key: cmp:пудер у камену-пудер у праху-течни пудер
cyr: пудер у праху · пудер у камену · течни пудер
acc: пу́дер у пра̏ху · пу́дер у ка̀мену · те̏чнӣ пу́дер

examples.en: I apply loose powder with a big brush.

examples.sr: Увек носим [пу́дер у ка̀мену] у торбици.
examples.en: I always carry pressed powder in my purse.
I need liquid foundation for my face.

related.en: liquid foundation — in everyday speech often just «пудер»

note: In conversation, plain пу́дер often means foundation, not powder. To be exact, add у праху or у камену.

examples.en: Hit the brakes!
You're so clumsy!

related.en: brake — of a car or bicycle
clumsy, dopey — of an absent-minded, awkward person

note: Slowness is also described as као успорени снимак - «like slow motion».

examples.sr: Какав ти је то [фа̏зон]? Обећаш па не дођеш.
examples.en: What kind of behavior is that? You promise and then you don't show up.
What's the catch?

related.en: cut, style (of clothes); manner, way of doing things; a gag, a joke
a head start (in a game); a trick; a joke, a gag

note: They overlap only in the sense of «a joke»: «Ба̏ш је фо̏ра!» - «That's a good one!». «У свом фазону» - «true to form, in his usual style».

examples.en: He is a good man.
She is a very kind person.

related.en: man, person; more often, a man

note: Чо̏век often means «man». For a woman, or to be neutral, о̏соба is more usual: она је оптимистична особа.

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
Every morning I dress the kids for kindergarten.
Put your shoes on.
I don't like putting on new shoes.

related.en: to put on, to dress (pf.) — clothes
to put on, to dress (impf.) — clothes

note: Clothes take обући and облачити, shoes take обути and обувати. The imperatives о̏буци! and обуј! look alike but are not interchangeable.

meanings: чекати, сачекати, причекати, очекивати or дочекати?

examples.en: I waited for you for a long time in front of the school.
Wait for me until I finish.
Wait for me a little.
I didn't expect a gift.
They gave us a warm welcome.

related.en: to wait for, to wait until (pf.)
to expect, to count on something
to welcome guests; to live to see

note: Че̏кати, са̀чекати and прѝчекати are almost interchangeable. До̀чекати is either to receive guests or to finally live to see something: дочек Нове године - ringing in the New Year.

examples.en: Thank you for coming.
I think she is a good person.
I know what you're doing.

related.en: that, because — in set phrases: зато што, пре него што, све што
that — after opinions, feelings, knowledge: сматрам да, бојим се да

note: Rule of thumb: if you can insert «because», use што̏, if not, use да. As a question, што̏? means «why?» and шта̏? means «what?».

meanings: баш, јако, како or што in a compliment?

examples.en: You are very beautiful.
Wow, what a good-looking guy!
How beautiful you are!
How beautiful you are today!

related.en: how, what a — an exclamation, close to «како»

note: Ка̏ко and што̏ open an exclamation: како си лепа!, што си лепа!. Ја̑ко and ба̏ш stand next to the adjective itself.

examples.en: Every morning I make breakfast for the kids.
For breakfast I cook porridge and eggs.

related.en: to prepare, to make — a universal word for any kind of food
to boil, to cook in a pot — only what is boiled

note: «To make breakfast» is usually спре́мати до̀ручак. For something that is boiled, ку̏вати fits: кувам чорбу.

examples.en: I have to submit a visa application.

examples.sr: Потписао је [и̏зјаву] да ништа није видео.
examples.en: He signed a statement that he had seen nothing.

related.en: application, request — filed to get something
statement — a person officially confirms something

note: An application is submitted: по̀дне̄ти за́хтев. A statement is given: дати изјаву.

meanings: рачун, признаница or уплатница: bill and receipt

examples.en: Give me the bill, please.
Keep the receipt in case you need it.

examples.sr: Попунила сам [у̀платницу] и платила у пошти.
examples.en: I filled out the payment slip and paid at the post office.

related.en: bill, check; cash register receipt — an amount to pay or a payment made
payment slip — for paying at a bank or post office

note: Ра̀чӯн is also a «bank account»: рачун у банци.

examples.en: Almost everyone has already left.
I got back from the seaside recently.
See you soon!
I'll come soon.

related.en: soon, shortly — about the near future

note: Trap: «soon» is у̏скоро, not ско̀ро, which means «almost» or «recently».

meanings: зашто, зато што or јер: why and because

examples.en: Why didn't you come?
I'm late because there is a traffic jam.
I didn't come because I was sick.

note: You ask with за̏што and answer with за̀то̄ што̏ or је̏р. Је̏р is shorter and more common in writing.

examples.en: Where are you going tonight?
Where is the library?

note: In conversation где̏ is often used instead of ку̀да: где идеш?. The standard form is ку̀да.

examples.en: I see your shadow on the wall.
In summer we look for shade.

related.en: shadow, silhouette — the general word; сенка за очи - eye shadow
cool shade — where you can hide from the heat

note: Хладо̀вина comes from хла́дан, «cool». Deep shade is дебела хладовина.

examples.en: I study the Serbian language at the university.
I learn Serbian at home.

related.en: to study at a university; to study a subject as a student
to learn, to study — on one's own, in courses, at school

note: A schoolchild does not студира: he учи or goes у школу.

examples.en: He is a painter and does portraits.
She is an artist: she sings and acts.

note: Both can be translated as «artist», but сли̏ка̄р is only a painter, while у̀метнӣк is broader.

examples.en: He paints in oil on canvas.
I photographed the mountain from the top.
The child is drawing a house with a pencil.

related.en: to paint; in everyday speech, to take photos
to photograph — neutral, the standard word
to draw — in pencil, pen: lines, sketches, plans

note: From сли̏кати comes сли̏ка̄р, from цр̏тати comes цр́теж, a drawing. In everyday speech «take a picture of me» is сликај ме.

examples.en: I wash my hands before eating.
I have been following this series for years.

related.en: to follow, to keep track of; to accompany — пратити вести, пратити некога

note: They sound alike, but the present tense forms differ: перем and пратим.

examples.en: I feel better today.
I remember that summer.

related.en: to feel (well, bad, etc.) — how one feels

note: Both have «се», but the meaning differs. After се̏ћати се comes the genitive: сећам се тог дана.

examples.en: I ask him where he lives.
I drink tea without sugar.

note: The present tense forms differ: пи̑та̄м and пи̏је̄м.

examples.en: I like her idea.
The brothers often quarrel.

related.en: to like, to be pleasing — свиђа ми се овај град
to quarrel — они се стално свађају

note: The one who likes is in the dative: свиђа ми се. To quarrel «with someone» takes «с» and the instrumental: свађам се с братом.

examples.en: I'm sending you a message.
We're celebrating the birthday on Saturday.

related.en: to celebrate, to honor — славити рођендан

note: The present tense forms differ: ша̏ље̄м and славим. «To send off» is also по̀слати.

examples.en: I waited for half an hour.
The trip takes an hour and a half.

related.en: half — before a noun: пола јабуке
and a half — after a numeral

note: Пола goes before the noun, «и по» after the numeral: по́ла са̑та, са̑т и по, два̑ и по са̑та.

examples.en: I'm sorry I was late.
It's a pity you can't come.

related.en: a pity, too bad — an assessment of the situation; damage

note: Жа̏о ми је also works as an apology: жао ми је што касним. Ште̏та also means «damage»: материјална штета.

meanings: преко, кроз or за: «across, through, in»

examples.en: We're crossing the bridge.
We're going through the forest.
I'll be there in five minutes.

related.en: across, over — on top of, on the other side: bridge, river, street

note: «In five minutes» is за пе̑т мину́та. Кроз пе̑т мину́та also occurs, but less often.

examples.en: Maybe I'll come tomorrow.
He can swim.
Shall we go for coffee? - Sure!

related.en: maybe, perhaps — probability, does not change
can; may; okay — a form of the verb моћи, or agreement

note: «Maybe» is мо̀жда; ability, permission and agreement are може.

examples.en: I drive a bus every day.
Mom drives the kids to school.
I take the bus every day.

related.en: to drive; to give a ride — to operate a vehicle or carry someone
to ride; to go for a ride — as a passenger or for fun

note: Without «се» you are at the wheel, with «се» you are just riding. The vehicle is in the instrumental with no preposition: аутобусом, возом, колима.

examples.en: I toil in the garden the whole weekend.

examples.sr: Сваки дан [шља̏кам] од осам до пет.
examples.en: I work like a dog from eight to five every day.
He slogged away in the mine all his life.

examples.sr: Моја мајка [р̏мбачи] од јутра до мрака.
examples.en: My mother works her fingers to the bone from morning till night.

related.en: to slave away, to toil — hard, monotonous work, often for little pay
to grind, to work hard — the most common of the four
to work like a horse — until exhausted
to slog, to keep at it — stubbornly and for long hours

note: All four verbs are colloquial and almost interchangeable. The neutral verb is ра́дити.

examples.en: Let's meet at the kafana after work.
Beer is cheap at the dive.
We had dinner at a nice mehana.

examples.sr: Стара [кр̏чма] на путу ради и данас.
examples.en: The old inn on the road is still open today.

related.en: tavern-café — a place with food, beer, rakija and music
dive, cheap pub — a simple, inexpensive place
inn, tavern — an old word, sounds bookish

note: The neutral word is кафа̀на. Бѝртија sounds jokingly dismissive, while меха̀на and кр̏чма evoke the old days.

examples.en: This bread is hard.
He has a strong character.

related.en: hard — about consistency: тврдо дрво, тврда подлога
firm, sturdy — чврст мост, чврст карактер

note: Тврда вода is hard water. The solid state of matter is чвр̑сто ста́ње.

examples.en: We bought a cake for the birthday.
We tie the tomatoes to a stake.

related.en: cake, pastry, cookie — sweet baked goods
stake, pole — a wooden stick driven into the ground

note: The words differ only in the last letter, and in Latin script without diacritics (kolac, kolac) they are identical.

examples.en: The baby is sucking milk.
The barber has been cutting my hair for years.

related.en: to cut hair; шишати се - to get a haircut

note: Without diacritics in Latin script both verbs are spelled the same (sisati), so they are easy to mix up in chat. Cyrillic has no such problem.

examples.en: The money is in the bank.
We have a jar of pickles.

related.en: glass jar — for jam, pickles, ajvar

note: A jar of jam is a те́гла. A tin can is лѝме̄нка.

examples.en: Do you have anything fasting-friendly?

examples.sr: Данас је [мр̏сан] ручак: пита са месом.
examples.en: Today's lunch is not for fasting: meat pie.

related.en: lenten, fasting food — without meat, dairy or eggs
non-fasting food — meat and dairy, when fasting is not observed

note: Посна храна is food allowed during a fast, мрсна храна is ordinary food with meat and dairy.

cyr: црни лук · бели лук · медвеђи лук
acc: цр̑нӣ лу̏к · бе̑лӣ лу̏к · мѐдвеђӣ лу̏к
meanings: црни лук, бели лук or медвеђи лук?

examples.en: Chop an onion for the salad.
Garlic goes into the dish.

examples.sr: У пролеће берем [мѐдвеђӣ лу̏к] у шуми.
examples.en: In spring I pick wild garlic in the woods.

related.en: ramsons, wild garlic — a wild spring onion; also сремуш

note: The color is no guide: цр̑нӣ лу̏к (literally black onion) is just an ordinary onion, and бе̑лӣ лу̏к (white onion) is garlic.

cyr: претворити се · правити се · остваривати се
acc: претво̀рити се · пра̏вити се · оствари́вати се
meanings: претворити се, правити се or остваривати се?

examples.en: Love turned into hatred.
He pretends to be sorry.
My dream is coming true.

related.en: to turn into — to change into another state
to pretend, to act as if
to come true, to be realized — a dream, a plan

examples.en: There are big differences between them.
I didn't leave for that reason.

note: One vowel changes the meaning.

examples.en: He got a good grade in math.
It is hard to give an assessment of the situation.

related.en: grade, mark, rating — a school grade, an evaluation of work
assessment, estimate — an assessment of a situation

note: The verbs: оце́нити ра̑д - to evaluate work, проценити ситуацију - to assess the situation.

examples.en: Fill in the sentences with the appropriate forms.
This place is suitable for a vacation.

related.en: corresponding, appropriate — fitting a form or requirement
suitable, convenient — for a purpose, place or moment

note: По̏годан usually goes with «за»: по̏годан за о̀дмор.

examples.en: That was the first attempt.
There was an assassination attempt on the president.

related.en: assassination, attack — on the life of a well-known person

note: An attempt on someone's life is an атѐнта̄т, not a по̏куша̄ј.

examples.en: Tell me the truth.
We are seeking justice for everyone.

related.en: truth — what corresponds to the facts
justice, fairness — by law and morality

note: In everyday speech «the truth» is и̏стина, while пра̑вда is justice.

meanings: отворити рачун or дати први гол?

examples.en: Yesterday I opened an account at the bank.

examples.sr: Домаћини су [да̏ли пр̑ви го̑л] у петом минуту.
examples.en: The home team scored the opening goal in the fifth minute.

related.en: to open a bank account — only at a bank
to score the first goal — to open the scoring in a game

note: «To open the scoring» is not translated literally. The score of a game is резу̀лта̄т, a draw is не̏решено.

cyr: даривати некога поклонима · поклонити некоме поклон
acc: дари́вати не̏кога по̀клонима · покло̀нити не̏коме по̀клон

examples.en: He showers the children with toys.
He gave Mom flowers.

related.en: to give someone gifts, to shower with gifts

note: Same meaning, different government: дари́вати takes the accusative and the instrumental, покло̀нити the dative and the accusative.

examples.en: We buy food at the market.
Everyone has their own lot, their own bread to earn.

related.en: fated sustenance, daily bread — a bookish word

note: Нафака is a Turkism from a religious context: the sustenance destined for a person. You will not hear it in a shop.

examples.en: I'm slicing carrots for the salad.
Carrots are good for your eyesight.

related.en: carrot — a synonym, also a standard word

note: There is no difference in meaning: Serbian allows parallel standard words. The same goes for бу̀ндева and ти̏ква (pumpkin), су́сед and ко̀мшија (neighbor).

examples.en: I like boiled rice.
I bought a bag of rice.

related.en: rice — the variant used in neighboring regions

note: They are synonyms: ри́жа is the variant of neighboring regions, such as Croatia.

examples.en: We're going to the vineyard for the grape harvest.
I bought sweet grapes.

related.en: vineyard — the place, not the fruit

note: Serbian вѝногра̄д is the place where grapes grow, while the fruit itself is гро̑жђе.

examples.en: The gardener is buying fertilizer.
Don't throw trash in the street.

related.en: garbage, trash — also a rude insult

note: Said of a person, ђу̏бре is a rude insult: «scum».

examples.en: I can't run, my leg hurts.
What are you running away from?
The police are chasing the thief through the city.

related.en: to run — on foot; sports, jogging
to flee, to run away — from someone or out of a country
to chase, to race — after someone or something; to pursue

note: Any running on foot is тр̀чати, while бѐжати always means to flee or run away.

examples.en: I got an answer.
Yesterday I received your message.
She made a lot of friends.
We got tickets for the concert.

related.en: to get, to receive — the most general word
to receive, to accept — a message, signal, letter, salary
to acquire, to gain — non-material things: experience, friends, recognition
to get hold of, to procure — things: tickets, weapons

note: До̀бити works almost everywhere, even for unpleasant things: добити корпу - to be turned down.

examples.en: What is the capacity of this pitcher?
The circumference of the head is fifty-eight centimeters.
This shampoo gives hair volume.

related.en: circumference, girth; scope — waist, head; scale of work
volume, fullness — of hair; loudness of sound

note: English «volume» is split here into three words: capacity, length of an outline, and fullness.

examples.en: Which movie are you watching?
What kind of movies do you like?
How much is your salary?

related.en: which — a choice from a known set: a title, number, day
what kind of — by quality: properties, genre, type
how big, how much — size, amount

note: Quantity and price are asked with колико: Колико кошта? - «How much does it cost?»

examples.sr: Умотај колач у [та̏бак] папира за печење.
examples.en: Wrap the cake in a sheet of baking paper.
It is written on paper.
He sold securities.
My grandfather grows tobacco.

related.en: sheet of paper — a single or printed sheet
paper — the material and the general word; documents
paper — formal: securities, a scrap of paper
tobacco for smoking — the plant and the raw material

note:
Don't be misled by the look: tobacco is ду̀ва̄н, while та̏бак is a sheet of paper.

Папири in the plural means «documents», тоалетни папир is toilet paper.

examples.en: I'm drinking hot chocolate.
Give me a glass of lukewarm water.
The tea is too hot.

related.en: very hot — scalding tea, hot weather

note: То̏пао is wider than English «warm»: it is also used for hot dishes and drinks, for example то̏пла̄ чокола́да.

examples.en: I don't know a single word.
He neither drinks nor smokes.
I'll come too.

related.en: not even, no — strengthens a negation
nor, neither — joins negative parts: нити ... нити
and, also, too — in an affirmative statement

note: «Me too» is usually «и ја̑», not «ја такође».

examples.sr: Имам [о̏сећа̄ј] да нешто није у реду.
examples.en: I have a feeling that something is wrong.
She showed her feelings.
Emotions influence thinking.

related.en: sensation, hunch — of cold, of guilt
feeling — a lasting emotional experience, often in the plural
emotion — more often in psychology and science

note: О̏сећа̄ј is what you feel right now, or a vague hunch. О̀сећа̄ње is deeper. The line is loose and the words often overlap.

examples.en: Some mushrooms are poisonous.

examples.sr: Лекар је рекао да је то [гљѝвица].
examples.en: The doctor said it's a fungal infection.
We're going mushroom picking in the morning.

related.en: mushroom, fungus — the neutral, scientific word; edible and poisonous
small mushroom; fungal infection — a diminutive or a disease
mushroom — the everyday word: forest, kitchen, picking

note: Пѐчӯрка sounds more everyday, гљи̏ва more bookish, and гљивица most often means a fungal infection.

examples.en: The worker accepted our offer.

examples.sr: Она жели развод, али ја не [прѝстајем].
examples.en: She wants a divorce, but I don't agree.
I agree with you.

related.en: to accept, to agree to — an offer, rules, an idea
to agree to, to consent to — a condition, an action
to agree with — a person or an opinion

note: Government: прѝстати на + acc., сло̀жити се са + instr.

examples.en: Did you throw out the trash?
Quit smoking, it's harmful.
I'll be leaving the city soon.

related.en: to throw, to throw away — an object: trash, a coin
to leave, to quit — a habit or a person
to leave, to abandon — a place or a person

note: О̀ставити also means simply «to leave somewhere»: Оставио сам телефон код куће.

cyr: срести (се) · састати се · видети се · наћи се · окупити се
acc: сре̏сти (се) · са̀стати се · ви̏дети се · на́ћи се · о̀купити се
meanings: to meet: срести (се), састати се, видети се, наћи се, окупити се

examples.en: I ran into him in town by chance.
Tonight we're meeting with our colleagues.
See you tomorrow!
Where shall we meet?
The citizens gathered in the square.

related.en: to meet, to run into — by chance, an unexpected meeting
to meet — by arrangement, a business or planned meeting
to see each other — to keep in touch
to meet — at an agreed place
to gather — many people in one place

note: «See you!» in Serbian is видимо се.

cyr: упознати · дочекати · забављати се · наићи (на) · јавити се
acc: упо̀знати · до̀чекати · за̀бављати се · наи́ћи (на) · ја́вити се
meanings: to meet: упознати, дочекати, забављати се, наићи (на), јавити се

examples.sr: У Србији сам [упо̀знао] много занимљивих људи.
examples.en: In Serbia I met many interesting people.
Will you meet me at the airport?
Luka is dating the pharmacist.

examples.sr: [На̏ишао] сам на ову реч у уџбенику.
examples.en: I came across this word in a textbook.
This illness occurs in children.

related.en: to get to know, to meet for the first time — a new acquaintance
to meet, to welcome — an arriving person; to wait for, to live to see
to date, to go out — a relationship
to come across, to stumble upon — to find by chance
to occur, to appear — of phenomena

note:
There are other meanings:
• ја́вити се - «to get in touch»: Јави ми се кад стигнеш
• за̀бављати се - «to have fun»

cyr: сместити се · уклопити се · снаћи се · запослити се
acc: сме̏стити се · укло̀пити се · сна̀ћи се · запо̀слити се
meanings: to settle in: сместити се, уклопити се, снаћи се, запослити се

examples.en: Make yourselves more comfortable.

examples.sr: Како ћу се [укло̀пити] у нову средину?
examples.en: How will I fit into the new environment?
I found my feet in the new place.
I got a job at a shop.

related.en: to settle in, to get accommodated — in a place, in housing
to fit in — with a group, an environment, an interior
to find one's feet, to manage — to cope on your own

note: English «to settle in» has no single Serbian verb: it depends on what is being settled - housing, a place in a group, affairs or a job.

meanings: to take: узети, понети, изабрати, брати

examples.en: Take what you want.
Take the documents with you.
Which dress did you choose?
We were picking mushrooms in the forest.

related.en: to take — by hand, to buy, to take medicine
to choose, to pick — from several
to pick, to gather — fruit, flowers, mushrooms

note: In a café you order like this: У̀зе̄ћу јо̀гурт - «I'll have a yogurt». Coffee to go: по̀нети.

examples.en: I am asking for a pardon.
He is asking for a raise.
I beg you not to interrupt me.
The man asked what had happened.

related.en: to ask for, to demand; to look for
to ask, to beg — politely: please, to ask Dad for something

note: Trap: пи́тати means only «to ask a question», never «to ask for something». For a request use мо̀лити or тра́жити.

meanings: сећати се, осећати or осећати се?

examples.en: I don't remember what his name is.
Do plants feel pain?
How are you feeling today?

related.en: to feel something — pain, a smell
to feel (a certain way) — how you feel

note: The words differ by one letter and only sound alike. Се̏ћати се takes the genitive: сећам се његовог имена.

examples.sr: Не [мо̑ра̄ш] да радиш ако не желиш.
examples.en: You don't have to work if you don't want to.
You are not allowed to smoke here.
You have to work, you have no choice.

related.en: may, to be allowed to — permission

note: In the negative the meaning differs: не мо̑ра̄ш - «you don't have to», не сме̑ш - «you must not».

examples.en: I'll call you later.
The phone is ringing, answer it.
Ring the doorbell.

related.en: to call, to phone someone — + acc.

note: Зва̏ти takes the accusative: зовем брата. Зво̀нити is about a sound: a phone, a doorbell, a bell.

examples.en: I think it's important.
I was counting money.
I was counting on your help.

related.en: to consider, to think — an opinion
to calculate, to count on — arithmetic, a calculation

note: Рачу̀нати на + acc. - «to count on, to rely on»: рачунам на тебе.

meanings: to communicate: дружити се, причати, комуницирати

examples.en: We've been hanging out lately.
Go, have a chat with your uncle.

examples.sr: Важно је да редовно [комунѝцираш] са клијентима.
examples.en: It is important to communicate with clients regularly.

related.en: to hang out, to socialize — friendly relations
to talk, to have a chat — to discuss something
to communicate, to be in touch — business or informational contact

note: Trap: better not to use општити for «to communicate»: to Serbs it can sound like an awkward hint of sexual intimacy.

meanings: to need, to demand: требати, захтевати, тражити

examples.en: I need new shoes.
The workers are demanding higher wages.
Friendship takes effort.

related.en: to be needed, to need — does not mean «to demand»
to demand, to insist; to imply — firmly
to ask for, to demand, to look for — softer than захтевати

note: Trap: тре̏бати does not mean «to require». Захте́вати is a firm demand, тра́жити is a request or a search.

meanings: to cook, to make: кувати, спремати, правити

examples.en: Mom cooks wonderfully.
Today we're having a barbecue.
I prepared a light dinner.

related.en: to cook, to boil — soup, potatoes, coffee, goulash
to prepare, to get ready — food, a wedding, a talk
to make — a dish, by its name

note: Pancakes, salad and grilled food are not «boiled»: say правити палачинке, направити салату.

examples.en: Look out the window.
We have free appointment slots tomorrow at 12.
I have a gap in my schedule from three to six.

examples.sr: Службеница на [ша̀лтеру] број 3 је задужена за то.
examples.en: The clerk at counter number 3 is in charge of that.

related.en: window — an opening in a wall
appointment slot — a booked time with a doctor, a stylist
gap, break — free time between classes
counter, service window — at a bank, a post office, an office

note: You book an appointment like this: зака́зати тѐрмӣн.

meanings: to live, to stay: живети, становати, одсести

examples.en: Where do you live?
Have you been living here long?
In Belgrade we stayed at a hotel.

related.en: to reside — with a place given
to stay, to put up — temporarily: at a hotel, with acquaintances

note: You stay at a hotel with одсѐсти, while жи́вети implies a permanent home.

meanings: to carry, to bear, to postpone, to move: носити/преносити, подносити, одлагати, померати

examples.en: Mosquitoes carry diseases.
I can't stand the heat.
We have already postponed the meeting twice.

examples.sr: Можемо ли да [помѐримо] час за пола сата?
examples.en: Can we move the class by half an hour?

related.en: to carry, to transfer; to transmit — things, diseases
to bear, to stand — heat, stress, pain
to postpone, to put off — a meeting, a flight
to move, to shift — a time or a place

note: Но̀сити also means «to wear (clothes)»: Носи наочаре.

meanings: to do, to study: бавити се, учити, проучавати, радити

examples.en: What sport do you do?
I'm studying in the library.
Scientists are studying climate change.
What do you do after work?

related.en: to be engaged in, to do — a hobby, work, science
to learn, to study — lessons, a language
to study, to research — in depth, in science
to do, to work — what you are occupied with

note: Ба̏вити се is not used without a complement: say what with (instr.): бавим се спортом.

key: cmp:примати-туширати се, купати се, сунчати се-узимати
cyr: примати · узимати · туширати се, купати се, сунчати се
acc: при́мати · у̀зимати · туши́рати се, ку́пати се, су̀нчати се
meanings: to take: примати, узимати, туширати се

examples.en: We don't receive visitors.

examples.sr: Лекар је препоручио да [узѝмам] таблете два пута дневно.
examples.en: The doctor recommended that I take the pills twice a day.
I take a shower several times a day.

related.en: to receive, to accept — gifts, guests, visitors
to take — medicine; to take into account

related.sr: туширати се, купати се, сунчати се
related.en: to take a shower, a bath, a sunbath — reflexive verbs
related.acc: туши́рати се, ку́пати се, су̀нчати се

note: «To take part» is у̀чествовати, not при́мати.

key: cmp:донети одлуку-положити заклетву-предузети мере-прихватити понуду-усвојити закон
cyr: усвојити закон · донети одлуку · предузети мере · прихватити понуду · положити заклетву
acc: усво̀јити за́кон · до̀не̄ти о̏длуку · преду̀зе̄ти ме̏ре · прѝхватити по̀нуду · поло̀жити за̀клетву
meanings: to pass, to make, to take, to accept in set phrases

examples.en: Parliament passed a new law.
We made the decision on our own.
I am taking every precaution.
I accept your offer.
The new judge took the oath.

related.en: to pass a law — parliament, a document
to accept an offer — to agree
to take an oath — on taking office

note: In these phrases the verb is not при́мати: learn each phrase as a whole.

meanings: to undress: свући се, скинути се, раскомотити се

examples.sr: Сад се [сву̀ци] и легни на леђа.
examples.en: Now undress and lie on your back.
Just take off your hat.
Come in, make yourself comfortable.

related.en: to take off, to undress — literally «to pull off»
to take off extra clothes and settle in — what you offer to guests

note: Do not say скини се to a guest: it sounds like «get undressed». To invite them to take off their coat and settle in, say раскомоти се.

examples.en: Open the door.

examples.sr: [О̀ткрио] сам да мој пријатељ има канал.
examples.en: I found out that my friend has a channel.
I can't unlock my phone.

related.en: to open something closed; to begin — a door, a window, a session
to discover, to reveal — to uncover the unknown
to unlock — with a key; a lock, a screen

note: О̀ткрити also means «to unveil» a monument: о̀ткрити спо̏менӣк.

examples.en: I don't know how to play chess.
When did you learn to play the guitar?
Who acted in that movie?

related.en: to play — a game, a sport; to dance
to play an instrument; to sound — of music
to act, to play a role — in theater, film; to pretend

note: Ѝграти ко̏ло - «to dance the kolo».

examples.en: I closed the window.

examples.sr: Не сећам се да сам [закљу̀чао] врата.
examples.en: I don't remember locking the door.
Put the lid on the pot.

related.en: to close — a window, a book, a door without locking
to cover, to put a lid on — a pot, eyes with a palm

note: The opposites: отво̀рити - «to open», откљу̏чати - «to unlock».

examples.en: The boy broke his arm.
Who broke the toy?
The elevator broke down yesterday.

related.en: to break, to crush — a bone, a will, a heart
to break, to spoil — a toy, a device

note: The noun is ква̑р: Лифт је у квару - «the elevator is out of order».

meanings: to clean up, to remove: склонити, уклонити, спремити, очистити

examples.en: Move the camera away.
We removed the spam from the site.
I tidied up the room.
How can I remove limescale?

related.en: to put away, to move aside — out of sight, to the side
to remove, to get rid of — for good: spam, an obstacle
to tidy up, to put in order; to prepare — a room, an apartment
to clean, to clear off dirt — limescale, a yard, vegetables

note: Спре́мити also means «to prepare, to pack»: спре́мити ру́чак, спремити ствари.

examples.en: Some mushrooms are poisonous.
There are a lot of mushrooms in the forest.
I bought a cream for fungal infections.

related.en: mushrooms, fungi — the broadest word, any kind
mushrooms — with cap and stem, edible and poisonous

note: At a pharmacy ask for a cream against гљивица: «крем за печурке» would not be understood.

examples.sr: Хтео сам нешто да ти кажем, [за̀то̄] сам те звао.
examples.en: I wanted to tell you something, that's why I called.

examples.sr: Кућа је без намештаја, али [за̀то̄] пуна књига.
examples.en: The house has no furniture, but it is full of books instead.
The elevator is out of order, so we are taking the stairs.

related.en: therefore, that's why; but on the other hand — neutral, much more common in speech

note: Only за̀то̄ has the second meaning: «but in return».

cyr: јако · веома · врло · баш · много · пуно
acc: ја̑ко · вѐома · вр̏ло · ба̏ш · мно̏го · пу̏но
meanings: very: јако, веома, врло, баш, много, пуно

examples.en: I'm very sorry.
That is very important.
He is very kind.

examples.sr: Нашла сам [ба̏ш] оно што сам тражила.
examples.en: I found exactly what I was looking for.
I like this city a lot.
I love you a lot.

related.en: very — more often in writing, with adjectives and adverbs
a lot; very — quantity, degree, strength of action
a lot — quantity; not with adjectives

note:
For «very» with an adjective use вѐома, вр̏ло, ја̑ко, мно̏го, but not пу̏но: you don't say пу̏но до̏бар.

Ба̏ш before a noun means «exactly this»: ба̏ш о̀во̄.

examples.en: The jacket is hanging on the coat rack.
I'll put the blouse on a hanger.
The phone is on a stand.

related.en: coat rack, hook rail — a stand or a strip with hooks for jackets and coats
clothes hanger — holds a garment by the shoulders in a wardrobe
stand — for a phone, a flower, shoes

examples.en: See you in five minutes.
Turn right in a hundred meters.

examples.sr: На збору је било [пре̏ко] пет стотина људи.
examples.en: There were over five hundred people at the meeting.

related.en: across, over, on the other side of; more than; by means of
in (so much time or distance from now)

note: Пре̏ко means «across» or «more than», never «in (so long)»: пре̏ко мо̏ста, преко пријатеља. «In five minutes, in a hundred meters» is за.

examples.en: I'm thirty-five years old.
I was born in '83.
The car is a 2013 model.

related.en: year, age — with a number: пет година
year of birth, model year — neuter

note: Adults are usually asked Ко̀је̄ си го̀диште?, while Колико имаш година? sounds more like a question to a child.

examples.en: The teacher wrote the grade in the class register.
Bring the pupil's record book to the parent-teacher meeting.

related.en: class register — the teacher's record book
pupil's record book — with the pupil's grades

note: Дне̑внӣк is also a personal diary and a news bulletin.

examples.en: The bus driver stopped at the station.
The guide showed us the old town.
The news presenter announced the guest.

related.en: driver — of a car, a bus
guide, tour guide — shows a city to tourists
TV host, presenter, announcer — hosts a show

note: A driver at the wheel is only во̀за̄ч.

examples.en: What are you doing tonight?
Grandma is making pancakes.
Mom is cooking lunch.
I'm preparing dinner for the guests.

related.en: to make, create, produce — pancakes, a house
to do, to work — the process and the occupation
to prepare, get ready — including setting the table

note:
For «to cook lunch» ку̏вати, спре́мати and пра̏вити ру́чак all work, but ку̏вати means specifically to boil.

Ра́дити asks about the activity, пра̏вити about the result.

examples.en: I have to look after my sister.

examples.sr: Ништа не могу да [чу̏је̄м] због буке.
examples.en: I can't hear anything because of the noise.

related.en: to keep, protect, guard, look after

note:
They sound alike but conjugate differently:
• чу́вати - чувам, чувају, past participle чувао
• чу̏ти - чу̏је̄м, чу̏јӯ, past participle чуо, чула

examples.en: He is an imaginative storyteller.
Our designer is very creative.

related.en: creative — makes new things, including by hand

note: Машто̀вит comes from ма̀шта, «imagination».

meanings: крзно, длака, коса - which is which?

examples.en: The cat has soft fur.
There is dog hair everywhere.
She has long dark hair.

related.en: fur — an animal's thick coat, and fur as a material
hair, coat — a single hair, or an animal's hair; on animals and people

examples.sr: Одлучила сам да [о̀фарбам] косу у црно.
examples.en: I decided to dye my hair black.
Children love to color pictures.

related.en: to paint, dye — hair, walls, a room
to color, tint — a picture, an object; also figuratively

note: If unsure, use о̀фа̄рбати for hair and walls.

meanings: напунити, наточити, сипати - how to pour and fill

examples.en: Fill the glass to the brim.
Pour me a little water.
Pour the flour into the bowl.

related.en: to fill — to the brim, to full capacity
to pour out a liquid — wine, water, fuel
to pour — the most general: both liquids and loose material

note: На̀пунити is about the result, нато̏чити and си̏пати about the pouring itself. When in doubt, use си̏пати.

cyr: опрости(те) · извини(те) · извињавам се · жао ми је
acc: опро̀сти(те) · извѝни(те) · извѝњавам се · жа̏о ми је
meanings: опрости, извини, извињавам се - how to apologize

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't hear you.
Excuse me, I have to go.
I apologize for being late.
I'm sorry I'm late.

related.en: sorry, forgive me — a small slip, friendly tone
excuse me, sorry — all-purpose: among friends and politely to strangers
I apologize — formal, in writing, at work
I'm sorry — regret and sympathy, not necessarily guilt

note: For a small awkwardness there is also «не замери» (no offense).

cyr: какав · овакав · онакав · такав · некакав · икакав · никакав · било какав
acc: ка̀ка̄в · ова̀ка̄в · она̀ка̄в · та̀ка̄в · не̏какав · и̏какав · ни̏какав · би̏ло ка̀ка̄в
meanings: какав, овакав, онакав, такав, некакав, икакав, никакав

examples.en: What kind of movie is it?
I've never seen a crowd like this.

examples.sr: Хоћу [она̀ка̄в] ауто као што има комшија.
examples.en: I want a car like the one the neighbor has.
I don't like movies like that.
Some man from the bank is calling you.
Is there any point in waiting at all?
I have no plan for the weekend.
Bring any book.

related.en: what kind of — asks about quality
this kind of — like this one, here and now
that kind of — like that one, far away or earlier
such, that kind of — already mentioned
any at all — questions and conditions
no ... at all — with a negation

note: All of them decline like adjectives: ка̀ка̄в, каква, какво.

examples.sr: Један [хра́бар] пас је скочио у воду.
examples.en: A brave dog jumped into the water.
Our brave dog guards the yard.

related.en: brave, definite form — for a specific, known one: «овај», «наш», a name

note:
It is one adjective: the short form introduces something or stands in the predicate, the long one singles out a specific one.

The difference exists only in the masc. sg. nominative, in other cases the forms are the same.

examples.sr: Ово није само кућа, ово је наш [до̏м].
examples.en: This is not just a building, this is our home.
We bought a big house in the country.

related.en: home, hearth, place of origin; an institution: Дом здравља (health center)

note: «Going home» is кући: идем кући, «at home» is код куће.

examples.en: I'm going to wash the dishes.
First wipe the dust off the shelves.

related.en: to wash — with water: dishes, laundry, hands
to wipe, dust, erase — without immersing: a floor, dust, a table

note: «To do the laundry» is пра̏ти ве̏ш, «to delete a file» is бри̏сати.

examples.en: He sat among the guests.
The restaurant is between two buildings.

related.en: among — inside a group or a multitude
between — two things, at an exact spot

note: И̏змеђу takes the genitive, ме̏ђу the instrumental: и̏змеђу згра̏да, међу зградама.

examples.en: Could I have a glass of white wine?
Bring us a carafe of wine for the table.

related.en: carafe, pitcher — for the table, with wine or water
glass — an individual serving: чаша вина

note: Ask for бо̀ка̄л and you will get a whole carafe of wine.

examples.en: I always kiss my husband goodbye.
I love ćevapi and pljeskavica.

related.en: to kiss — «Љубим те»: «Love, ...» at the end of a letter or text
to love, like — people, food, activities: «Волим те»

note: Љу́бити means only «to kiss». Љубим ћевапе would mean «I kiss the ćevapi».

examples.en: Say hi to Mom for me.
Congratulations on your birthday!

related.en: to give regards, greet, say goodbye
to congratulate on something — a holiday, a birthday

note: По̏здра̄в! is also a plain «hi», with no occasion.

examples.en: In the evening I like to read a book.

examples.sr: Када је учитељ ушао, сви су [ћу̀тали].
examples.en: When the teacher came in, everyone fell silent.

note: They sound alike but mean different things: чѝтати is to read, ћу́тати is to be silent.

examples.en: My son is a third-grader.
He is a medical student.

related.en: pupil, schoolchild — primary and secondary school

note: At a university you say студирам, at school - учим. A female student is сту̀денткиња.

examples.en: Chicken soup is light and warm.

examples.sr: Рибља [чо́рба] је довољна за цео ручак.
examples.en: Fish čorba is enough for a whole lunch.

related.en: clear, light soup, broth — often with vegetables and homemade noodles
thick, hearty soup — big pieces of meat or fish, vegetables, potatoes

note: Чо́рба is almost a dish of its own, while су̏па is more of a first course.

examples.en: Shall we go for coffee? - Sure!
I agree with the content of the contract.

related.en: I agree — everyday: at home, in a café, with colleagues

note: In conversation use слажем се, otherwise you will sound like you are at a committee meeting. A woman says сагласна сам.

examples.en: Do you want to try this cake?

examples.sr: Ја ћу [по̀кушати] да објасним граматику једноставно.
examples.en: I will try to explain the grammar simply.

related.en: to try, try on, test — with any object
to attempt — only before an action, usually «да» + verb

note: If a noun follows the verb, only про́бати works. When in doubt, про́бати is safer.

examples.en: You're really talented!
I don't like foreign food.
It's really strange that he didn't come.

note: A trap: «strange» is чу̏дно, while стра̑но means «foreign, unfamiliar»: стра́на хра́на is foreign food.

meanings: ући, изаћи, отићи, скокнути - go in, out, away

examples.en: I went into the house.
I left the house at eight.
I left work at five.
I'll pop over to the store.

related.en: to leave, go away — leave a place
to pop over, nip out — for a short while: «до продавнице»

examples.en: After school we go to the cinema.
After dinner they went for a walk.

related.en: after, afterwards — colloquial; can stand without a noun: «идемо после»
after, following — formal: only with a noun

note: Before a whole clause на̀кон needs што̏: након што је завршио посао.

examples.en: I'll pay for the coffee.

examples.sr: [Напла̀тила] је двадесет евра за час српског.
examples.en: She charged twenty euros for a Serbian lesson.

related.en: to pay — the money leaves you: coffee, rent
to charge, collect payment — the money comes to you

note: На̀платити is not the perfective of пла́тити, it is a different verb.

examples.en: Do you have an ID card?
Can I pay by card?

related.en: map, ticket, card — a world map, a ski pass (возна карта), an ID card (лична карта)
small card — a bank card, a SIM card, a greeting card

note: Ка̑рта is also a playing card: играти карте.

examples.en: A bag? - No, thanks.
You do not need to come in person.

related.en: no need, no thanks — colloquial: in a shop, at a market
it is not necessary — formal: a bank, business correspondence

note: In daily speech people say не тре́ба. Није потребно in conversation sounds too ceremonious, like a letter from a ministry.

examples.en: I'm going to the doctor about my throat.
In the stories the healer treated people with herbs.

related.en: healer, witch doctor, sorcerer — treats with herbs and spells

examples.en: Where did you park the car?
The car is in front of the building.
You have to get the vehicle inspected.

note:
Ко̏ла is a neuter plural even though there is one car: Ко̏ла су но̑ва.

Во̀зило is a word from documents, in daily speech it sounds like «footwear» instead of «shoes».

examples.en: What are you studying?
What kind of vegetable is this?
What is this cucumber like?

related.en: what — a general question when nothing is known
which, what — a choice among several
what kind of, what ... like — by quality: a property, an opinion

note: A question about an unknown thing starts with шта̏, and then you narrow it down with ко̀јӣ or ка̀ка̄в.

examples.en: I find it hard to remember dates.

examples.sr: [Се̏ћаш] ли се кад смо путовали у Нови Сад?
examples.en: Do you remember when we traveled to Novi Sad?

related.en: to memorize, remember — put into memory: numbers, dates, passwords
to remember, recall — take out of memory: the past

note: Се̏ћати се takes the genitive: сећам се града.

examples.en: I can lift that, I'm strong.
He is a mighty ruler.

related.en: mighty, powerful — bookish: epics, fairy tales, a ruler

note: For ordinary strength use ја̑к: ја̑ко де́те, not си̑лно де́те.

examples.sr: Хајде на кафу? - Може, треба ми добар [ра̏згово̄р].
examples.en: Shall we go for coffee? - Sure, I need a good talk.

examples.sr: Његова [бѐседа] на конференцији била је дирљива.
examples.en: His speech at the conference was moving.

related.en: conversation, talk — an ordinary live conversation
speech, sermon — a bookish, solemn address

note: Бѐседа sounds bookish and old-fashioned, like a word from a stage or a church. The verb for ра̏згово̄р is разгова́рати.

examples.en: I like to cook, but I have no time.
This is not a glass but a cup.

examples.sr: Не зато што нећу, [ве̏ћ] зато што не могу.
examples.en: Not because I don't want to, but because I can't.

related.en: but rather — after a negation; also «than»
but rather — after a negation, more bookish than него

note:
Не̏го and ве̏ћ are used only after a negation, in the sense «but rather».

Не̏го is also «than» in a comparison: ве̏ћӣ не̏го ја̑.

examples.en: Could I have a glass of white wine?
Bring a carafe of water to the table.

related.en: glass of wine — a single serving in a glass

note: If you ask for бо̀ка̄л, a whole carafe is brought.

examples.en: I fell and I have a knee injury.

examples.sr: После тог догађаја остала је велика [тра̀ума].
examples.en: A great trauma remained after that event.

related.en: injury, damage — physical: a bruise, sprain, fracture
psychological trauma — shock, stress, an emotional mark

note: For a broken finger people say only по̏вреда, not тра̀ума.

examples.sr: [А̏ко] данас буде лепо време, идемо на Аду.
examples.en: If the weather is nice today, we'll go to Ada.

examples.sr: [Уколѝко̄] не платите рачун, услуга ће бити обустављена.
examples.en: If you do not pay the bill, the service will be suspended.

related.en: in case, if — formal: instructions, contracts, notices

note: With a friend уколѝко̄ would sound like a letter from a bank.

examples.sr: Ишли смо право, [о̏нда̄] смо скренули лево.
examples.en: We went straight, then we turned left.

examples.sr: Најпре смо пили кафу, [по̀то̄м] смо шетали парком.
examples.en: First we had coffee, then we walked in the park.

related.en: then, afterwards — more bookish: a story, a report

note: О̏нда̄ is also «then, in that case»: Ако хоћеш, онда иди.

examples.en: I love holidays because that is when I travel.
I love holidays because I get to rest.
I love holidays because of the gifts.

related.en: because — followed by a whole clause with a verb
because — shorter, also introduces a whole clause
because of — followed by a noun or pronoun in the genitive

note: Збо̏г takes only a noun: због кише. A whole clause is introduced by је̏р and за̀то̄ што̏.

examples.en: He speaks as if he were a Serb.
Do it the way I told you.

related.en: as if, as though — it seems so, but in fact it may be otherwise

note: «Such as» is ка̏о што̏ су: воће као што су јагоде и брескве.

meanings: јутрос, вечерас, ноћас, синоћ, прексиноћ - when exactly

examples.en: I had coffee this morning.
We're going to the theater tonight.
I didn't sleep last night.
We watched a movie last night.
We were at a restaurant the night before last.

related.en: tonight or last night — depending on context

note: One word replaces a whole phrase: си̏но̄ћ instead of «yesterday evening».

cyr: може · важи · у реду · договорено · слажем се · наравно · како да не
acc: мо̏же · ва́жи · у ре̏ду · договорѐно · сла̏жем се · на́равно · ка̏ко да не

examples.en: See you at six? - Works for me.
Talk tomorrow. - Deal.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да сачекаш пет минута? - [У ре̏ду].
examples.en: Can you wait five minutes? - All right.
So, Wednesday at eight? - It's settled!

examples.sr: То је добра идеја. - [Сла̏жем се], одлична је!
examples.en: That's a good idea. - I agree, it's great!
Will you come to lunch? - Of course!

examples.sr: Можеш ли ми позајмити књигу? - [Ка̏ко да не]!
examples.en: Can you lend me a book? - Sure thing!

related.en: works for me, sure — agreeing to a suggestion
all right, fine — accepting a request or a situation
of course — without a shadow of doubt
sure thing, of course — willingly, with feeling

note: Ка̏ко да не said in an ironic tone can also mean «no way».

examples.en: We're preparing a celebration for Mom's birthday.

examples.sr: После победе у граду је почело велико [сла̑вље].
examples.en: After the victory, a big celebration began in the city.

examples.sr: Послао сам јој [че̏ститку] за Нову годину.
examples.en: I sent her a card for the New Year.

related.en: jubilation, festive merrymaking — joy, often spontaneous
greeting, greeting card — what is written or said on a holiday

note: To congratulate someone on a holiday is чести́тати.

meanings: платити with prefixes: доплатити, преплатити, потплатити, отплатити, уплатити

examples.sr: За пртљаг сам морала да [допла̀тим] двадесет евра.
examples.en: I had to pay twenty euros extra for my luggage.

examples.sr: Не желим да [препла̀тим] карту за концерт.
examples.en: I don't want to overpay for a concert ticket.
He tried to bribe the policeman.
We have been paying off the loan for seven years.
Today I paid the electricity bill.

related.en: to pay extra — pay the missing part or a fee for an additional service
to overpay — pay more than it is worth
to pay off, repay — settle a debt in installments; also «to repay a kindness»
to pay in, make a payment — pay a bill, transfer money to an account

note: Отплатити and потпла́тити are easy to confuse: the first means to repay a debt, the second to give a bribe.

meanings: ћаскати, брбљати, ћућорити, беседити: ways of talking

examples.en: The neighbors were chatting in front of the building.
Stop babbling and listen!
The pupils are whispering at the back desk.
The professor gave a speech in front of a full hall.

related.en: to chat — lightly, in a friendly way, about nothing
to babble, prattle — a lot and out of place
to whisper to each other — under one's breath, e.g. in class
to hold forth, give a speech — solemn, bookish; jokingly of long stories

note: Бр̀бљати sounds reproachful, while ћа̏скати is warm and inoffensive.

cyr: кад / када · док · пре него што
acc: ка̏д / ка̀да · до̏к · пре̏ не̏го што̏
meanings: кад, док or пре него што?

examples.en: When you arrive, let me know.
While everyone is talking, I'm making coffee.
Call me before you set off.

related.en: when — a moment or an event
while, as — two actions go on at the same time
before — an action that happens earlier than another

note: With a negation до̏к means «until»: чекај док не дођем - «wait until I come».

examples.en: I'm looking for a used phone up to a hundred euros.

examples.sr: Лекар је објаснио како делују [по̏лни] хормони.
examples.en: The doctor explained how sex hormones work.

related.en: sexual, of sex — related to sex (gender): полни хормони, полни органи

note: Not to be confused with пу̏н - «full».

examples.sr: У [нѐдељу] идемо на ручак код баке.
examples.en: On Sunday we're going to Grandma's for lunch.
This week was hard for me.
