To pick up a parcel is подићи пошиљку; a notice of arrival, извештај о приспећу, is left in the mailbox. Also useful: бро̑ј за пра̏ће̄ње, пакомат.

The courier calls:
• Ево ме испред зграде
• Има ли ко да сиђе?
• Имате откупнину

Replies:
• Силазим одмах
• Не ради интерфон, отворићу вам
• Можете ли оставити код комшије?
• Имате ли ситно? - Ѝма̄м са̏мо кру̏пно

To pay on delivery is платити поузећем.

At the first football World Cup in Uruguay (1930) the Yugoslav team reached the semifinal, beating Brazil.

The cult film Монтевидео, бог те видео! was made about this trip, about ordinary Belgrade guys: the cobbler Tirke and the society man Moša.

The title plays on a rhyme: Монтевидео - "God saw you".

Football words: у̀такмица, навѝја̄ч, шутѝрати.

A band, a performance, a rehearsal, a tour: бе̏нд, на́ступ, про́ба, турне́ја.

On stage: поја̀чало, бу̏бњеви, електрична гитара, ба̏с гита́ра. The person behind the drums is бу̀бња̄р.

At a festival: главна бина, фа̑н зо́на, кемп зона, у̀лаз, и̏зла̄з.

Also: волонтери, про̀грам, у̀лазница, пу̀блика, сви̑рка у̏жӣво.

related.en: to eat a snack on the sly

note:
School memories:
• задња клупа - the back desk, where students copy answers during a ко̀нтролни (class test); краљ задње клупе - the one who comes just to sit through the lessons
• ћа̏ска̄ње на часу - whispering and chatting during a lesson
• дробити ужину - to eat a snack on the sly under the desk
• брисање табле - an excuse to leave the room to wet the cloth
• кривити се од смеха - to double over with laughter
• пу̏шкица - a cheat sheet
• вѐликӣ о̀дмор - the long break

cyr: At the gas station: what people say

related.en: What can I fill up for you?

related.sr: Наточите, молим вас, двадесет литара дизела.
related.en: Please fill it up with twenty liters of diesel.
related.acc: Нато̀чите, мо̏лим вас, два́десет лита́ра ди̏зела.

related.en: Where can I pump up my tires?

note:
The attendant asks: Шта да вам наточим?

Answer: Наточите, молим вас, двадесет литара дизела or Пу̏н резерво̀а̄р.

To ask for the total: Колѝко сам ду́жан? - Ка̀са је у̀нӯтра.

About air for the tires: Где могу да напумпам гуме? - Е̏во та̏мо.

An offer to wash the windshield: Да вам оперем предња стакла? - Хва́ла, ја̑ сам.

О̏дма̄х means «right away, immediately».

cyr: Paying for parking with a ticket

related.en: I want to pay for parking.

related.sr: Заокружите данашњи датум и време паркирања.
related.en: Circle today's date and the time you started parking.
related.acc: Заокру̀жите да̀нашњӣ да́тум и вре́ме паркѝрања.

related.sr: Морате се испаркирати до десет и петнаест, иначе плаћате казну.
related.en: You must leave by 10:15, otherwise you pay a fine.
related.acc: Мо̑ра̄те се испаркѝрати до де̏сет и пѐтнае̄ст, и̏на̄че пла̀ћате ка̏зну.

note:
How to pay:
1. Say: «Желим да платим паркинг».
2. The attendant names the amount («два сата, четири евра») and gives you a та̏лон.
3. On the ticket, circle the date and the time you started parking: «Заокружите данашњи датум и време паркирања».
4. Put the ticket in the car so that it can be seen from outside.

You must leave on time: «Морате се испаркирати до десет и петнаест, иначе плаћате казну».

cyr: At the border: talking to the customs officer

related.sr: Куда путујете и колико времена планирате да останете у Србији?
related.en: Where are you traveling and how long do you plan to stay in Serbia?
related.acc: Ку̀да пу̀тујете и колѝко врѐмена планѝрате да о̀стане̄те у Ср̀бији?

related.en: Do you have anything to declare?
You must pay the duty at the cash desk.

related.sr: Желим вам угодан боравак у Србији.
related.en: I wish you a pleasant stay in Serbia.
related.acc: Жѐлим вам у̏годан бо̀равак у Ср̀бији.

note:
The border officer asks for your document: До̏бар да̑н, па̑сош, мо̏лим вас.

He asks the purpose and length of your stay: Куда путујете и колико времена планирате да останете у Србији?

Then: Имате ли нешто за пријављивање?

If your things exceed the allowance, he asks for a receipt (рачун за торбу) and says: Морате платити царину на каси.

You may be asked to open the trunk: Отворите пртљажник.

Farewell: Желим вам угодан боравак у Србији.

The main points: се̏вер, ју̏г, ѝсток, за̑пад.

The intermediate points are written as one word: североза́пад, североѝсток, југоза́пад, југоѝсток.

To the question «Где?» (where?) you answer with the locative and the preposition на: на северу, на истоку, на западу, на југозападу.

Practice with a map: Где̏ је светио̀нӣк? - На југозападу; Где̏ је ву̀лка̄н? - На истоку.

cyr: Describing a person: looks and clothes
note:
Height and build: вѝсок, ни̏зак, средње висине, мр̏шав, дѐбео, кру́пан, сѝтан, спо̏ртскӣ ти̑п.

Hair and face: ће̏лав, кратка коса, црна коврџава коса, бр̑кови и бра́да, кукаст нос, зелене очи.

Clothes: the verb носи + accusative: носи жуту јакну, зѐленӣ са̀ко̄, љубичасту дуксерицу, фармерице, шортс, ста̏рке, зѐленӣ ка̀чке̄т, црвену кравату, сунчане наочаре.

Positive traits:
• о̏збӣљан, му́дар, и̏скрен, вре́дан
• па̀жљив, стр̀пљив, саосѐћајан, хра́бар
• кре̏атӣван, дружељу̀бив, сми̑рен

A self-confident person is called самоу̀верен or самопо̀узда̄н.

States: сре̏ћан, ту́жан, за̀бринӯт, за̀љӯбљен, не̏рво̄зан, љу̑т.

Negative traits: тврдо̀глав, песимѝстичан.

cyr: Duško Radović on the Serbian language

related.sr: Волите српски језик свакога дана помало.
related.en: Love the Serbian language a little every day.
related.acc: Во̀лите ср̏пскӣ јѐзик сва̏кога да̑на по̀мало.

related.sr: Српски језик нема никога другог осим нас.
related.en: The Serbian language has no one else but us.
related.acc: Ср̏пскӣ јѐзик не̑ма ни̏кога дру̀гог о̏сӣм нас.

note:
The writer Duško Radović left a motto for everyone who studies the language: Волите српски језик свакога дана помало. Српски језик нема никога другог осим нас.

Let's take the words apart:
• по̀мало - a little at a time
• свакога дана - every day
• о̏сӣм + genitive - «except, apart from»

cyr: Vukovica and gajevica: the two alphabets
note:
Two alphabets are in use in Serbia, and each has its own name:
• вуковица - the Cyrillic alphabet, after Vuk Karadžić, the reformer of the script
• гајевица - the Latin alphabet, after Ljudevit Gaj, whose Latin script became the basis of the modern one

For official documents ћирѝлица is used, while in everyday life латѝница is more common.

Each alphabet has 30 letters.

cyr: One of the longest words: престолонаследниковица

related.en: wife of the heir to the throne

note:
Among the candidates for the longest Serbian word is престолонаследниковица - the wife of the heir to the throne.

It has 22 letters: the stem престолона́следнӣк plus the feminine suffix -овица.

The word is almost never used in real life, since Serbia has no monarchy, but it is good practice for reading long compound words.

cyr: Writing a letter in Serbian, and why Viber is better

related.en: Dear (to a man or an organization)

related.sr: Још увек лоше говорим српски, волела бих да пишемо преко Вибера
related.en: I still speak Serbian badly, I would like us to write on Viber
related.acc: Јо̏ш у̏ве̄к ло̏ше го̀ворӣм ср̏пскӣ, во̀лела бих да пи̑ше̄мо пре̏ко Ви̏бера

note:
In a business letter, address the person as «Ви» with a capital letter.

Opening and closing:
• «Поштовани» / «Поштована» - Dear (to a man / to a woman)
• «С поштовањем» - Yours sincerely
• «Срдачан поздрав» - Kind regards

If your email goes unanswered, it is not rudeness: in Serbia people rarely use email and write to each other on Viber. They may also call you back.

If you are afraid of a phone call, write: «Још увек лоше говорим српски, волела бих да пишемо преко Вибера».

Grades are on a five-point scale, 5 being the highest. Each has a name and a colloquial name:
• 5 - «одличан», «петица»
• 4 - «врло добар», «четворка»
• 3 - «добар», «тројка»
• 2 - «довољан», «двојка»
• 1 - «недовољан», «јединица»

There is also a separate conduct grade, «оцена из владања»: «узорно», «врло добро», «добро», «лоше».

The grade point average is «просек», absences are «изостанци»: «оправдани» (excused) or «неоправдани» (unexcused).

cyr: The school year: semesters, breaks, shifts
note:
The year is divided into two semesters: «прво полугодиште» and «друго полугодиште». A division into three «тромесечја» also exists.

School breaks are «распуст»: «летњи», «зимски», «пролећни».

Classes run in two shifts: «прва смена» and «друга смена». Ordinary lessons are called «редовна настава».

cyr: At the doctor: the papers you will get
note:
File and insurance:
• «картон» - the patient file
• «здравствена књижица» - the health insurance booklet
• «осигурање» - insurance

After the visit:
• «упут» - a referral to a specialist
• «налаз» - a test result
• «потврда» - a certificate or note
• «рецепт» - a prescription
• «дијагноза» - a diagnosis

An appointment is a «термин»: «имам заказан термин». In test results you will see «нормално», «повишено» or «снижено».

cyr: A recipe step by step: kitchen verbs

related.en: Crack three eggs into a bowl
Whisk the eggs with a mixer
Add the yogurt and a little oil
Pour the mixture into a baking pan

note:
In a recipe the verbs are in the imperative, one per step:
1. «Разбиј три јаја у чинију» - crack three eggs into a bowl
2. «Умути јаја миксером» - whisk the eggs with a mixer
3. «Додај јогурт и мало уља» - add the yogurt and a little oil
4. «Умрви сир рукама» - crumble the cheese by hand
5. «Сипај смесу у плех» - pour the mixture into a baking pan
6. «Пеци на двеста степени» - bake at two hundred degrees
7. «Послужи уз јогурт» - serve with yogurt

cyr: Telling about a vacation: a six-step plan

related.sr: Била сам ове године у Шпанији
related.en: This year I was in Spain
related.acc: Би́ла сам о̀ве̄ го̏дине у Шпа̀нији

related.sr: Провели смо седам дана на мору
related.en: We spent seven days at the seaside
related.acc: Про̀вели смо се̏дам да̑на на мо̏ру

related.sr: Били смо моја сестра, мој брат и ја
related.en: There were three of us: my sister, my brother and me
related.acc: Би̏ли смо мо̀ја сѐстра, мо̑ј бра̏т и ја̑

related.sr: Ујутро смо пили кафу и шетали градом
related.en: In the morning we drank coffee and walked around the city
related.acc: У̏јутро смо пѝли ка̀фу и ше̏тали гра̀дом

related.sr: Смештај је био удобан и чист
related.en: The accommodation was comfortable and clean
related.acc: Сме̏шта̄ј је би̏о у̀добан и чи̏ст

note:
1. Where: «Била сам ове године у Шпанији» - this year I was in Spain
2. How long: «Провели смо седам дана на мору» - we spent seven days at the seaside
3. Who with: «Били смо моја сестра, мој брат и ја» - there were three of us: my sister, my brother and me
4. What you did: «Ујутро смо пили кафу и шетали градом» - in the morning we drank coffee and walked around the city
5. Accommodation: «Смештај је био удобан и чист» - the accommodation was comfortable and clean
6. Summing up: «Био је миран одмор» - it was a peaceful vacation

cyr: How to say «I feel like»: иде ми се

related.en: I want to go to the sea
I feel like going to the sea

note:
To state an intention, say «желим да идем на море» (I want to go to the sea). For a mood or an urge, a native speaker says «иде ми се на море» (I feel like going to the sea).

The formula: verb + dative pronoun + се.

• ми се - me
• ти се - you
• му се - him
• јој се - her
• нам се - us
• вам се - you (pl., formal)
• им се - them

Negation: не goes before the verb: «не иде ми се».

cyr: «I feel like» in practice: пије ми се, једе ми се

related.en: I feel like going for a walk
we feel like having ice cream

note:
The most common phrases with «се»:

• иде ми се - I feel like going
• пије ми се - I feel like drinking
• једе ми се - I feel like eating
• спава ми се - I feel like sleeping
• ради ми се - I feel like working
• шета ми се - I feel like going for a walk

If you feel like a particular dish, it stays in the nominative: «пије јој се кафа», «једе нам се сладолед».

cyr: Mika Antić - a poet who gets quoted

related.en: Not every noise is a conversation

note:
Mika Antić (1932-1986) is a beloved Serbian poet, writer, journalist and director. He is known for poems about love, freedom, youth and sincerity.

His books are read at school, his quotes have turned into aphorisms, and many of his lines have become part of everyday speech. One of them: «Није свака бука разговор».

cyr: Sports in Serbia: what Serbs talk about
note:
Sports are a favorite topic of light conversation. The names of the sports and some facts about them:

• тенис - popular thanks to Novak Djokovic
• кошарка - the Serbian school is famous worldwide, with courts in almost every neighborhood
• ватерполо - the national team often wins championships and the Olympics
• фудбал - the most emotional; the main match is «Црвена звезда» against «Партизан»
• одбојка - the women's national team is strong
• баскет 3×3 - Serbs are strong in tournaments

To start a thought, native speakers say:

• па... - well...
• дакле... - so...
• знаш... - you know...
• па добро... - well, okay...
• у ствари... - actually...
• мислим... - I mean...
• искрено... - honestly...

While you think about what to say:

• како да кажем... - how should I put it...
• чекај да размислим... - let me think...
• само тренутак... - just a moment...
• не знам баш... - I don't really know...
• па овако... - well, look...
• хм... - hm...
• заборавио сам реч... - I forgot the word...

To clarify what you have said:

• односно... - that is, in other words
• другим речима... - in other words
• тачније... - more precisely
• хоћу да кажем... - I mean to say...
• мислим на то да... - I mean that...
• у ствари... - actually
• заправо... - in fact

To structure a story:

• пре свега... - first of all
• прво... - firstly
• друго... - secondly
• затим... - then
• на крају... - in the end
• за крај... - finally
• укратко... - in short

To set thoughts against each other:

• али... - but
• међутим... - however
• с друге стране... - on the other hand
• истовремено... - at the same time
• док... - whereas, while
• иако... - although
• слично томе... - similarly

cyr: «Како сте?» and small talk in Serbian
note:
When a Serb asks «Како сте?», they rarely expect a detailed report on how things are.

A short answer is enough:
• «Добро, хвала. А ви?» - fine, thanks, and you?

Small talk about nothing in particular is not empty chatter but part of the local culture. If you want to fit in, join it.

It is easy to take Serbian politeness as a sign that your Serbian is already very good.

cyr: «Ајде на кафу» is not an invitation with a date

related.en: Let's go for coffee! Let's get together sometime

related.sr: Ајде на кафу у уторак у пет?
related.en: Let's go for coffee on Tuesday at five?
related.acc: А̀јде на ка̀фу у у́торак у пе̑т?

note:
«Ајде на кафу!» often just means «let's get together sometime», not an arrangement for a particular day and time.

If you actually want to meet, name the time and place yourself:
• «Ајде на кафу у уторак у пет?» - let's go for coffee on Tuesday at five?

What may differ from what you expect:
• September 1 is an ordinary school day: there is no assembly of all the classes, and people do not bring flowers or gifts for teachers.
• Gifts on other holidays are decided by each class: the parents arrange it among themselves.
• Collections for classroom needs, such as curtains, depend on the school. There is the «ђачки динар» (or «школски динар») - an annual parents' contribution to the school's needs. It is officially voluntary, and the school has no right to make schooling conditional on it.
• After the summer holidays, the longest break is the winter one (распуст), plus several short breaks; many days off are tied to Christmas and Easter.
• There is no cloakroom in the usual sense: children take jackets and belongings into the classroom, and primary schools sometimes have lockers (ормарићи).

cyr: In Serbia it is better to call than to write
note:
The main rule of life in Serbia: don't write - call!

A phone call is considered a more natural way to settle things than a long exchange of messages.

That is why people often say:
• «Назови ме» - call me
• «Позови их» - call them

related.en: Banat (a region in the north of Serbia)

note:
«Ветар» is any wind, while «кошава» is one specific, famous east wind: cold, gusty and strong.

Where it blows: the Danube, Belgrade, southern Banat and Vojvodina.

According to folk belief, the кошава cleans away evil and «blows the old year out of your bones».
A pigeon says «гу-гу-гу», a sparrow «жив-жив», a mouse «цију» or «цију-цију», a hen «ко-ко-да», a duck «ква» or «ква-ква», a frog «кре-кре». A cat in the street is called with «мац-мац».

cyr: Nadimak: how a name turns into a nickname
note: Serbian names have short informal versions, and they don't always look like the full name: Александар - Аца, Валентина - Вања, Марко - Маре, Горан - Гоки. When you meet someone, don't be surprised if in conversation they answer to a completely different word.

Licitar (in Serbia more often «лицидерске») cookies are bright red honey gingerbread decorated with icing. The best-known shape is a heart with a small mirror in the middle; a name may be written on it. They are given as gifts and hung as decorations at Christmas, weddings and fairs. The craft is known in Croatia, Slovenia and Serbia (especially in Vojvodina).

cyr: Voice of the streets: wall writing
Serbian slang: getting drunk by degrees
note: A series of cards about verbs of getting drunk, with the Serbian reflexive «се». Mild: «учиркати се» - to get slightly tipsy. Just drunk: «налокати се», «налити се» (literally "to pour oneself full"). Stronger: «урољати се» (plastered), «летвосати се» (absolutely wasted). All colloquial.

cyr: Lively Serbian expressions instead of plain ones

related.en: to go well, to come easily
we blew it, it all went wrong

note: A «wrong / the Serbian way» series. Instead of the neutral «знам да то радим добро» people say «иде ми то од руке» (I'm good at it). Instead of «било је ужасно» - «обрали смо бостан» (we really blew it). «То је то» is replaced by «чича-миче и готова прича» (and that's that), «он је лењ» by «лезилебовић» (lazybones), «доста је» by «таман» (that's enough, just right), «шта то причаш» by «лупаш» (you're talking nonsense).

The suits are called: треф (clubs), каро or ромб (diamonds), херц or срце (hearts), пик (spades). Diamonds and hearts each have two names: a foreign one and a Serbian one. The words come in handy when talking about cards and gambling.

cyr: Ala: a monster from folk belief
note: In Serbian mythology the ала (or аждаја) is a monster said to cause eclipses by swallowing the sun or the moon. The image often merges with the dragon slain by Saint George on icons. The word «ала» is also familiar as an exclamation like "wow!": that is a different word, but it sounds the same.

cyr: Greek words in Serbian: лампа and фењер
note: Many Serbian words came from Greek, sometimes through Turkish or Italian. «Лампа» comes from the Greek «лампа» (a light), «фењер» from the Greek «фанари» (a lantern). The sound changed: Greek «фан-» became Serbian «фењ-».

cyr: Serbian TV series instead of American ones

related.en: women from Dedinje (a district of Belgrade)

cyr: Male types in slang: фрајер, шмекер, фаца, зверка

note: Serbia has three short emergency numbers: 192 - police, 193 - firefighters and rescuers, 194 - ambulance. It's useful to know them as words: that's how signs in shops and offices are labeled.

Serbs name the half hour like this: «пола осам» is 7:30, literally "half to eight". It's easy to get wrong and think of 8:30 (compare British "half eight", which does mean 8:30). Other formats: «седам сати и пет минута» is 7:05, «пет минута до седам» is 6:55. The morning starts after midnight: 1 a.m. is «један сат ујутру».

Films in Serbia often run under their own titles: «Сам у кући» - Home Alone, «У ствари, љубав» - Love Actually, «Карневалска ноћ» - the Soviet film Carnival Night, «Како је Гринч украо Божић» - How the Grinch Stole Christmas. Useful for searching listings and subtitles.

cyr: Serbian films: titles and English names
note: A selection for those who want to watch Serbian cinema: «Подземље» (Underground, 1995), «Скупљачи перја» (I Even Met Happy Gypsies, 1967), «Ко то тамо пева?» (Who's Singin' Over There?, 1980), «Балкански шпијун» (Balkan Spy), «Национална класа» (National Class), «Маратонци трче почасни круг» (The Marathon Family; literally "The marathon runners run a lap of honor"), «Варљиво лето 68» (The Elusive Summer of '68).

cyr: How to dictate an e-mail address in Serbian
note:
Offices often ask for an e-mail address, so you need to name the characters.

• @ — «мајмунче» (little monkey)
• . — «тачка» (dot)
• - — «цртица» (hyphen)
• _ — «доња црта» (underscore)

Example: ana.petrovic@pošta.rs is read «ана тачка петровић мајмунче пошта тачка рс».

cyr: «У» and «на»: fixed combinations to learn whole
note: Choosing «у» (in, into) or «на» (on, onto) isn't always what an English speaker would expect, so learn these combinations whole. With «на»: на факултет (to the university), на интернет (on the internet), на путовање (on a trip). With «у»: у кујну (to the kitchen), у пошту (to the post office), у куповину (shopping), у шетњу (for a walk), у природу (out into nature), у пензију (into retirement), у иностранство (abroad).

In Serbian a syllable can be built around «р», and then the stress falls on that consonant. It happens in the words «хркати» (to snore), «срце», «прст», «врт», «крв». It's unusual for an English speaker: there is no vowel in the syllable, but the «р» is held like a vowel.
